nombre: Active Period End Date and Time
definicion: The date and, optionally, time of the end of the active period of an object.
descripcion: For example, the end of the active period of a seasonal object such as a buoy. Midnight is understood to be 00:00:00 (the beginning of a day); when the time is not specified then midnight in the local time zone is typically implied.

datatype.nombre: Active Period End Date and Time Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying an active period end date and time.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.4.1, Combinations of date and time of day - Complete representation - Extended format, a calendar date and time representation, as a single data element comprising up to twenty characters, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, [hh] the ordinal number of an hour within the calendar day, [mm] the ordinal number of a minute within the hour, [ss] the ordinal number of a second within the minute, and an optional 'Z' when the time is according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12' for 12 April 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412T114520Z').

definicion: The time interval of the active period of an object, consisting of a pair of dates and, optionally, times.
descripcion: For example, the active period of a seasonal object such as a buoy. Midnight is understood to be 00:00:00 (the beginning of a day); when the time is not specified then midnight in the local time zone is typically implied.

datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.5.4.1, Representation of time-intervals identified by start and end - Extended format, as a single data element comprising up to forty-one characters, using an expression in accordance with 5.5.2 combining any two date and time of the day representations as defined in 5.4.1, as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ/YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z/1985-07-01T08:23:50Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985 through 8 hours, 23 minutes and 50 seconds UTC on 1 July 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12/1985-07-01' for 12 April 1985 through 1 July 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412/19850701'). Either of the dates may be left unspecified by the use of '--------' (for example: '19850412/--------' for 12 April 1985 through an unspecified ending date).

definicion: The official alternate name of an aerodrome as designated by the operating agency or by the official publications of the country in which the aerodrome is located.
descripcion: A name other than the official selected name which on occasion continues to be used (for example: in aeronautical information publications, NOTAMS, or aeronautical charts) will be identified as an alternate name.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of aerodrome lighting system providing visual guidance during the final segment leg of an approach procedure.

datatype.nombre: Aerodrome Approach Lighting System Type Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aerodrome approach lighting system type.

dominio.etiqueta: Approach Lighting with Sequenced Flashing Lights (ALSF) Category 1
dominio.definicion: A high-intensity approach lighting system including sequenced flashing lights in a Precision Approach ILS Category I configuration.
dominio.observaciones: The variable intensity approach lights extend a total of 720 metres (2400 feet), and possibly up to 900 metres (3000 feet) when permitted by the terrain, from the runway threshold.

dominio.etiqueta: Short Approach Lighting System (SALS) with Sequenced Flashing Lights
dominio.definicion: A high-intensity approach lighting system that is similar to the ALSF Category 1 but extends only 1500 feet from the runway threshold.
A high-intensity approach lighting system that is similar to the ALSF Category 1 but extends only 1500 feet from the runway threshold and does not include sequential flashing lights.

dominio.etiqueta: Approach Lighting with Sequenced Flashing Lights (ALSF) Category 2
dominio.definicion: A high-intensity approach lighting system including sequenced flashing lights in a Precision Approach ILS Category II configuration.
dominio.observaciones: The variable intensity approach lights extend a total of 720 metres (2400 feet), and possibly up to 900 metres (3000 feet) when permitted by the terrain, from the runway threshold. This approach lighting system may operate as a Short Simplified Approach Lighting (SSAL) System with Runway Alignment Indicator Lights (RAIL) when weather conditions permit by selectively disabling a subset of lights (for example: white main bars and/or red side row bars) in the pattern.

dominio.etiqueta: Short Simplified Approach Lighting (SSAL) System with Runway Alignment Indicator Lights (RAIL)
dominio.definicion: A high-intensity approach lighting system that is similar to the ALSF Category 2 but excludes the red side row bars and has a reduced number of white main bars.
dominio.observaciones: The variable intensity approach lights extend a total of 720 metres (2400 feet), and possibly up to 900 metres (3000 feet) when permitted by the terrain, from the runway threshold.

dominio.etiqueta: Medium-intensity Approach Lighting System (MALS) with Runway Alignment Indicator Lights (RAIL)
dominio.definicion: A medium-intensity approach lighting system consisting of seven bars of white variable intensity lights spaced 60 metres (200 feet) apart for 420 metres (1400 feet) commencing at 60 metres (200 feet) from the runway threshold and which is preceeded by Runway Alignment Indicator Lights (RAIL).
dominio.observaciones: The variable intensity approach lights extend a total of 720 metres (2400 feet) from the runway threshold.

dominio.etiqueta: Medium-intensity Approach Lighting System (MALS) with Sequenced Flashing Lights
dominio.definicion: A medium-intensity approach lighting system consisting of seven bars of white variable intensity lights spaced 60 metres (200 feet) apart for 420 metres (1400 feet) commencing at 60 metres (200 feet) from the runway threshold, where the three bars farthest away from the runway threshold also contain a sequenced flashing light unit.
dominio.observaciones: The variable intensity approach lights extend a total of 420 metres (1400 feet) from the runway threshold.

dominio.definicion: An approach lighting system consisting of seven omnidirectional flashing lights located in the approach area of a nonprecision runway.
dominio.observaciones: Five lights are located on the runway centerline extended with the first light located 90 metres (300 feet) from the runway threshold and extending at equal intervals up to 450 metres (1500 feet) from the runway threshold. The other two lights are located, one on each side of the runway runway threshold, at a lateral distance of 40 feet from the runway edge, or 75 feet from the runway edge when installed on a runway equipped with a VASI.

dominio.definicion: An approach lighting system including sequenced flashing lights that are located along the extended runway centreline.
dominio.observaciones: Runway alignment indicator lights are installed only in combination with other lighting systems (for example: that indicate distance from the runway threshold).

dominio.definicion: An approach lighting system consisting of six bars of white variable intensity lights spaced 150 metres (500 feet) apart for 900 metres (3000 feet) commencing at 150 metres (500 feet) from the runway threshold and accompanied by single lights along the extended runway centreline for the initial 300 metres (1000 feet) from the runway threshold and then double lights along the extended runway centreline for the second 300 metres (1000 feet) and then triple lights along the extended runway centreline for the final 300 metres (1000 feet).
dominio.observaciones: The variable intensity approach lights extend a total of 900 metres (3000 feet) from the runway threshold. Note that sequenced flashing lights may be present.

dominio.definicion: The NATO standard approach lighting system consisting of five bars of white variable intensity lights spaced 150 metres (500 feet) apart for 750 metres (2500 feet) commencing at 150 metres (500 feet) from the runway threshold and accompanied by single lights along the extended runway centreline for the initial 450 metres (1500 feet) from the runway threshold and then double lights along the extended runway centreline for the final 450 metres (1500 feet).
dominio.observaciones: The variable intensity approach lights extend a total of 900 metres (3000 feet) from the runway threshold. Note that sequenced flashing lights may not be present.

dominio.definicion: A medium-intensity approach lighting system consisting of seven bars of white variable intensity lights spaced 60 metres (200 feet) apart for 420 metres (1400 feet) commencing at 60 metres (200 feet) from the runway threshold.
dominio.observaciones: The variable intensity approach lights extend a total of 420 metres (1400 feet) from the runway threshold.

dominio.definicion: A low-intensity approach lighting system consisting of twin aviation yellow fixed intensity light units spaced at 60 metre (200 foot) intervals commencing 60 metres (200 feet) from the runway threshold and extending back for a distance of 900 metres (3000 feet), terrain permitting.
dominio.observaciones: This system is provided on non-precision approach runways.

dominio.etiqueta: High Intensity Approach Lighting (HIAL) System Category I
dominio.definicion: A high-intensity approach lighting system in an ILS Category I configuration.
dominio.observaciones: This system consists of bars of five white variable intensity lights spaced at intervals of 30 metres (100 feet) commencing 90 metres (300 feet) from the runway threshold and extending for a distance of 900 metres (3000 feet) when permitted by the terrain.

dominio.etiqueta: High Intensity Approach Lighting (HIAL) System Category II
dominio.definicion: A high-intensity approach lighting system in an ILS Category II configuration.
dominio.observaciones: This system consists of bars of five white variable intensity lights spaced at intervals of 30 metres (100 feet) commencing 30 metres (100 feet) from the runway threshold and extending for a distance of 720 metres (2400 feet).

dominio.definicion: A lead-in lighting system consisting of one or more series of flashing lights installed at or near ground level that provides positive visual guidance along an approach path, either curving or straight, where special problems exist with hazardous terrain, obstructions, or noise abatement procedures.
An overrun lighting system used by the U.S. Air Force consisting of red side row lights, three on the left and one on the right, terminated by a bar of green lights.

The former NATO standard approach lighting system consisting of five bars of white variable intensity lights spaced 150 metres (500 feet) apart for 750 metres (2500 feet) commencing at 150 metres (600 feet) from the runway threshold and accompanied by single lights along the extended runway centreline between 300 and 450 metres (1000 and 1500 feet) from the runway threshold and then double lights along the extended runway centreline for the final 450 metres (1500 feet), with the initial 300 metres (1000 feet) being free of centreline lights and bars as the white bars are laterally displaced and accompanied by red side rows (double on the left; single on the right).
dominio.observaciones: The variable intensity approach lights extend a total of 900 metres (3000 feet) from the runway threshold. Note that sequenced flashing lights may not be present.

dominio.definicion: A simple approach lighting system consisting of single white lights located along the extended runway centreline with a bar of green lights located at the runway threshold.

A low-intensity approach lighting system consisting of single aviation yellow fixed intensity lights spaced at 90 metre (300 foot) intervals commencing 90 metres (300 feet) from the runway threshold and aligned left of the extended runway centerline.

An approach lighting system consisting of two series of red side row lights, a single light to each side, spaced at intervals of 30 metres (100 feet) commencing 30 metres (100 feet) from the runway threshold and extending for a distance of 720 metres (2400 feet), with a bar of green lights located at the runway threshold.

An approach lighting system consisting of a series of bars of white lights accompanied by single white lights along the extended runway centreline, with a bar of green lights located at the runway threshold.
An approach lighting system consisting of a single bar of white lights accompanied by single white lights along the extended runway centreline.

definicion: The aerodrome identifier of the collocated aerodrome, according to the appropriate authority.

datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying an aerodrome co-location identifier.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: Characters 1 and 2 indicate the ICAO region as stated in ICAO Doc7910, characters 3 and 4 are in the ranges A-Z and/or 0-9.

definicion: The type of a permanently marked geodetic survey point having a precise position (horizontal and vertical) that has been established in the vicinity of, and usually on, an aerodrome.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aerodrome control station type.

dominio.definicion: An aerodrome control station whose position is tied to the National Spatial Reference System (NSRS).
dominio.observaciones: The existence of a Primary Aerodrome Control Station (PACS) must be declared by the applicable National Geodetic Survey.

dominio.definicion: An aerodrome control station whose position is tied to the Primary Airport Control Station (PACS).
dominio.observaciones: The existence of a Secondary Aerodrome Control Station (SACS) must be declared by the applicable National Geodetic Survey.

definicion: The vertical distance above Mean Sea Level (MSL) of the highest point of the landing area.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

nombre: Aerodrome Emergency Medical Service Personnel Count
definicion: The number of personnel trained in performing emergency medical services that are stationed at an aerodrome.

datatype.definicion: A count domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a cardinal number or an ordinal number. For example, 4 (as in the number of legs of a cow).
datatype.nota: The realization of this count datatype is implementation-dependent.

nombre: Aerodrome Emergency Response Service Vehicle Count
definicion: The number of vehicles that are stationed at an aerodrome and designated for use in aircraft accidents, snow removal, and/or emergency medical incidents.

datatype.definicion: A count domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a cardinal number or an ordinal number. For example, 4 (as in the number of legs of a cow).
datatype.nota: The realization of this count datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: A standard categorisation of the rescue and fire-fighting capabilities of an aerodrome on the basis of the over-all length and fuselage width of the largest aircraft that may be rescued.
descripcion: The over-all length of a helicopter includes its tailboom and rotor.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aerodrome fire fighting category.

dominio.definicion: 0 up to, but not including, 9 metres over-all length and 2 metres maximum fuselage width.
9 metres up to, but not including, 12 metres over-all length and 2 metres maximum fuselage width.
12 metres up to, but not including, 18 metres over-all length and 3 metres maximum fuselage width.
18 metres up to, but not including, 24 metres over-all length and 4 metres maximum fuselage width.
24 metres up to, but not including, 28 metres over-all length and 4 metres maximum fuselage width.
28 metres up to, but not including, 39 metres over-all length and 5 metres maximum fuselage width.
39 metres up to, but not including, 49 metres over-all length and 5 metres maximum fuselage width.
49 metres up to, but not including, 61 metres over-all length and 7 metres maximum fuselage width.
61 metres up to, but not including, 76 metres over-all length and 7 metres maximum fuselage width.
76 metres up to, but not including, 90 metres over-all length and 8 metres maximum fuselage width.
Up to, but not including, 15 metres in length.
From 15 metres up to, but not including, 24 metres in length.
From 24 metres up to, but not including, 35 metres in length.

definicion: A location on an aerodrome movement area with a history or potential risk of either collision or runway incursion, and where heightened attention by pilots/drivers is necessary.
descripcion: An aerodrome hot spot is a runway safety-related problem area or intersection on an aerodrome.

datatype.nombre: Aerodrome Hot Spot Designator Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying an aerodrome hot spot designator
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: A five-character alphanumeric identifier that is often, but not necessarily, in the form of the 2-character prefix 'HS' followed by a three-digit number.

definicion: An indication that land-water boundaries (for example: shorelines or hydrography) are present around the aerodrome.
descripcion: Hydrography includes features for which water is a relatively permanent constituent part, for example: perennial lakes, reservoirs and pools, perennial streams, aqueducts, flumes, conduits, canals and ditches. Hydrographic impact typically occurs when the feature is located within 20 nautical miles of the aerodrome.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The unique identifier of an aerodrome, heliport or seaplane base.
descripcion: It may used to relate information about components (for example: runways, helipads, taxiways, and aprons) of the aerodrome, heliport or seaplane base to each other and to the overall facility.

datatype.definicion: A key domain value specifying an aerodrome identifier.
datatype.nota: The realization of this key datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: A seven character code consisting of a two character country code as specified in the Digital Aeronautical Flight Information File (DAFIF) Appendix C, followed by a five digit number that is uniquely assigned within that country by the U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) as part of the process of preparing DAFIF data.

definicion: A free text description of the aerodrome site direction and distance from the city it serves or from another point easily distinguishable from the air.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The mean lowest temperature of the coldest month of the year at an aerodrome.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of internal energy that a substance contains.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of thermodynamic temperature, based absolute zero and the freezing (triple point) point of water (those points being 273.16 degrees Celsius in separation), that is related to Kelvin by absolute zero being -273.15 degrees Celsius; the triple point of water is 0.01 degrees Celsius whereas the boiling point of water at 1 atmosphere pressure is 99.9839 degrees Celsius.

nombre: Aerodrome Movement Area Light System Type
definicion: The lighting system provided for a component of the aerodrome movement area.

datatype.nombre: Aerodrome Movement Area Light System Type Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aerodrome movement area light system type.

dominio.definicion: Rapid exit taxiway indicator lights (RETILs) provide pilots with distance-to-go information to the nearest rapid exit taxiway on the runway, to enhance situational awareness in low visibility conditions and enable pilots to apply braking action for more efficient roll-out and runway exit speeds.
dominio.observaciones: Rapid exit taxiway indicator lights shall be fixed unidirectional yellow lights, aligned so as to be visible to the pilot of a landing aircraft in the direction of approach to the runway.

dominio.definicion: Stopway edge lights are used to outline the edges of the stopway during periods of darkness or restricted visibility conditions.
dominio.observaciones: Stopway lights shall be placed along the full length of the stopway and shall be in two parallel rows that are equidistant from the centre line and coincident with the rows of the runway edge lights. Stopway lights shall also be provided across the end of a stopway on a line at right angles to the stopway axis as near to the end of the stopway as possible and, in any case, not more than 3 metres outside the end.

dominio.definicion: Apron floodlights provide adequate illumination on all apron service areas.
Taxiway centerline lights define the centerline of the taxiway and are used to facilitate ground traffic under low visibility conditions.
dominio.observaciones: They are located along the taxiway centerline in a straight line on straight portions, on the centerline of curved portions, and along designated taxiing paths in portions of runways, ramp, and apron areas. Taxiway centerline lights are steady burning and emit green light.

dominio.definicion: Taxiway edge lights are used to outline the edges of taxiways during periods of darkness or restricted visibility conditions.
dominio.observaciones: These fixtures emit blue light.

dominio.definicion: Runway turn pad lights provide continuous guidance on a runway turn pad intended for use in runway visual range conditions less than a value of 350 m, to enable an aeroplane to complete a 180-degree turn and align with the runway centre line.
dominio.observaciones: Runway turn pad lights shall be unidirectional fixed lights showing green with beam dimensions such that the light is visible only from aircraft on or approaching the runway turn pad.

dominio.definicion: Stop bar lights are used to confirm the ATC clearance to enter or cross the active runway in low visibility conditions.
dominio.observaciones: A stop bar consists of a row of red, unidirectional, steady−burning in-pavement lights installed across the entire taxiway at the runway holding position, and elevated steady−burning red lights on each side.

dominio.definicion: A light designating a position intended for traffic control at which taxiing aircraft and vehicles shall stop and hold until further cleared to proceed, when so instructed by the aerodrome control tower.
dominio.observaciones: Intermediate holding position lights shall consist of three fixed unidirectional lights showing yellow in the direction of approach to the intermediate holding position with a light distribution similar to taxiway centre line lights if provided. The lights shall be disposed symmetrically about and at right angle to the taxiway centre line, with individual lights spaced 1.5 metres apart.

dominio.definicion: De-icing/anti-icing area exit lights should be provided at the exit boundary of a remote de-icing/anti-icing area adjoining a taxiway.
dominio.observaciones: De-icing/anti-icing facility exit lights shall consist of in-pavement fixed unidirectional lights spaced at intervals of 6 metres showing yellow in the direction of the approach to the exit boundary with a light distribution similar to taxiway centre line lights.

dominio.definicion: Runway guard lights provide warning to pilots and drivers of vehicles when they are operating on taxiways, that they are about to enter an active runway.
dominio.observaciones: There are two standard configurations of runway guard lights. Configuration A is a pair of unidirectional flashing yellow lights located at each side of the taxiway at a distance from the runway centre line. Configuration B are unidirectional flashing yellow lights spaced at intervals of 3 metres located across the taxiway at a distance from the runway centre line.

dominio.definicion: A visual docking guidance system indicates, by a visual aid, the precise positioning of an aircraft on an aircraft stand when other alternative means, such as marshallers, are not practicable.

Aircraft stand manoeuvring guidance lights facilitate the positioning of an aircraft on an aircraft stand, on a paved apron, or on a de-icing/anti-icing facility intended for use in poor visibility conditions.
A road holding position light designates a position at which vehicles may be required to hold.
dominio.observaciones: The road-holding position light shall comprise of either a controllable red (stop)/green (go) traffic light or a flashing-red light.

dominio.definicion: Runway centerline lights define the centerline of a runway, and are installed on some precision approach runways to facilitate landing and Take-off under adverse visibility conditions.
dominio.observaciones: Runway centre line lights shall be fixed lights showing variable white from the threshold to the point 900 metres from the runway end; alternate red and variable white from 900 metres to 300 metres from the runway end; and red from 300 metres to the runway end, except that for runways less than 1 800 metres in length, the alternate red and variable white lights shall extend from the mid-point of the runway usable for landing to 300 metres from the runway end.

dominio.definicion: Runway edge lights are used to outline the edges of runways during periods of darkness or restricted visibility conditions.
dominio.observaciones: These light systems are classified according to the intensity or brightness they are capable of producing: they are the High Intensity Runway Lights (HIRL), Medium Intensity Runway Lights (MIRL), and the Low Intensity Runway Lights (LIRL). The HIRL and MIRL systems have variable intensity controls, whereas the LIRLs normally have one intensity setting.

dominio.definicion: REILs are installed at many airfields to provide rapid and positive identification of the approach end of a particular runway.
dominio.observaciones: The system consists of a pair of synchronized flashing lights located laterally on each side of the runway threshold. REILs may be either omnidirectional or unidirectional facing the approach area. They are effective for Identification of a runway surrounded by a preponderance of other lighting; Identification of a runway which lacks contrast with surrounding terrain; Identification of a runway during reduced visibility. REILs are flashing white lights with a flash frequency between 60 and 120 per minute.

dominio.definicion: Touchdown Zone lights define the touchdown zone of a runway, and are installed on some precision approach runways to facilitate landing and Take-off under adverse visibility conditions.
dominio.observaciones: Touchdown zone lights shall extend from the threshold for a longitudinal distance of 900 metres, except that on runways less than 1800 metres in length, the system shall be shortened so that it does not extend beyond the midpoint of the runway. The pattern shall be formed by pairs of barrettes symmetrically located about the runway centre line. The lateral spacing between the innermost lights of a pair of barrettes shall be equal to the lateral spacing selected for the touchdown zone marking. The longitudinal spacing between pairs of barrettes shall be either 30 metres or 60 metres.

dominio.definicion: A group of lights identifying the beginning of the landing surface of the runway.
dominio.observaciones: Runway threshold lights are variable intensity red and green units in the form of wing bars along each side of the runway centerline, except that for Category II and higher runways, the red and green lights extend along the full width of the runway. Green shows in the approach direction and red shows in the opposite. When a threshold is at the extremity of a runway, the threshold lights shall be placed in a row at right angles to the runway axis as near to the extremity of the runway as possible and, in any case, not more than 3 metres outside the extremity. When a threshold is displaced from the extremity of a runway, threshold lights shall be placed in a row at right angles to the runway axis at the displaced threshold.

dominio.definicion: Runway end lights are used to outline the landing end of the runway during periods of darkness or restricted visibility conditions.
dominio.observaciones: Runway end lights shall be fixed unidirectional lights showing red in the direction of the runway. The intensity and beam spread of the lights shall be adequate for the conditions of visibility and ambient light in which use of the runway is intended.

dominio.definicion: Land and hold short lights are used to indicate the hold short point on certain runways which are approved for Land and Hold Short Operations (LAHSO).
dominio.observaciones: Land and hold short lights consist of a row of pulsing white lights installed across the runway at the hold short point. Where installed, the lights will be on anytime LAHSO is in effect. These lights will be off when LAHSO is not in effect.

dominio.definicion: Taxiway exit centerline lights identify a track on a runway where an aircraft may make a smooth transition from the runway environment to an adjacent taxiway.
dominio.observaciones: The lights are spaced at longitudinal intervals of not more than 15 metres, except that, where runway centre line lights are not provided, a greater interval not exceeding 30 metres may be used. The lights alternate green and white.

dominio.definicion: Lights placed to identify the designated Touchdown and Lift-Off area.
dominio.observaciones: Touchdown and lift-off area perimeter lights shall be placed along the edge of the area designated for use as the touchdown and lift-off area or within a distance of 1.5 metres from the edge. Where the touchdown and lift-off area is a circle the lights shall be: a) located on straight lines in a pattern which will provide information to pilots on drift displacement; and b) where a) is not practicable, evenly spaced around the perimeter of the touchdown and lift-off area at the appropriate interval except that over a sector of 45 degrees the lights shall be spaced at half spacing.

dominio.definicion: Lights placed along the edge identifying the final approach and take-off area.
dominio.observaciones: Final approach and take-off area lights shall be fixed omnidirectional lights showing white. Where the intensity of the lights is to be varied the lights shall show variable white.

definicion: The surface condition of the aerodrome movement area, as a category.
descripcion: The surface condition does not include contaminations such as snow, ice, water, and/or fluid accumulation.

datatype.nombre: Aerodrome Movement Area Pavement Condition Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aerodrome movement area pavement condition.

dominio.definicion: The movement area shows minimal to no signs of deterioration and/or damage and is fully functional.
The movement area shows visible signs of deterioration and/or damage and is fully functional.
Construction or maintenance work is in progress and constitutes a danger to aircraft and/or aircraft navigation on the movement area.
The movement surface has significant rough, broken, or rutted areas due to neglect over a period of time, but may remain operational.
dominio.observaciones: A deteriorated surface may have characteristic such as vegetation growing through cracks.

dominio.definicion: The movement area has deteriorated to the point of becoming a permanent hazard to aircraft operations.
The movement area has been damaged in part causing non-specific degradation in function.
The movement area has been destroyed, resulting in total loss of function.

definicion: The level of preparation of the aerodrome movement area surface, as a category.
descripcion: Common category types may range from natural to completely paved.

datatype.nombre: Aerodrome Movement Area Surface Category Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aerodrome movement area surface category.

dominio.definicion: The subgrade has been prepared for load-bearing and the surface has been paved using durable materials.
dominio.observaciones: Intended to be a permanent surface that is highly resistant to the effects of weathering and traffic.

dominio.definicion: The surface is paved for at least 50 percent of its length.
The naturally occurring surface is used without any preparation.
dominio.observaciones: For example: no grading or rolling.

dominio.definicion: The surface is paved, but for less than 50 percent of its length.
The surface has been prepared (for example: by grading or rolling) but has not been paved.
dominio.observaciones: Generally considered to be only temporary in nature as unless regularly maintained the surface relatively rapidly degrades as a result of weathering and traffic. Non-local materials (for example: gravel or landing mats) may be used to improve the load-bearing and wear characteristics of the surface.

definicion: The type of the predominant material of which a surface of the movement area is composed.
descripcion: Example surfaces include: asphalt, concrete, or grass.

datatype.nombre: Aerodrome Movement Area Surface Composition Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aerodrome movement area surface composition.

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of various mixtures of sand, gravel, crushed rock, and/or recycled paving bound together by asphalt, a black or brownish-black, solid or viscous, bituminous pitch that may be of natural origin but is most commonly produced from petroleum.
dominio.observaciones: Depending on the formulation, known variously as 'asphaltic concrete', 'tar macadam', 'bitumen-bound macadam' or simply 'asphalt'. In some situations the pavement perimeter (edges and/or ends) may consist of solely of concrete (for example: around a runway).

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of the original surface material mixed in place with a bituminous binder (for example: tar or asphalt).
dominio.observaciones: Often referred to as 'earth cement'. Prepared by digging up the surface, mixing the material with bitumen or oil binder, and surfacing with the resulting mixture. Bitumen is the family name for either tar (derived from coal) or asphalt (derived from petroleum).

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of masonry units packed closely together on a firm subgrade, with or without mortar.
A surface composed of clay, packed over a firm subgrade, that has hardened over a period of time.
A surface composed of a mixture of broken stone or gravel, sand, cement, and water, that forms a stonelike mass on hardening.
dominio.observaciones: May include an internal steel mesh to improve resistance to cracking and minimize subsequent separation of the pieces. The joints between adjacent pavement slabs may incorporate steel pins to prevent vertical misalignment of the adjacent slabs over time.

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of crushed coral that has been graded and rolled to produce a firm regular surface.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes mixed with sand and/or clay.

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of the existing earth material(s).
dominio.observaciones: May be grass-covered or bare.

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of small water-worn or crushed stones compacted to produce a firm regular surface.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes mixed with sand and/or clay.

dominio.definicion: A cleared area of a frozen watercourse.
dominio.observaciones: Usually marked and intended to support regular traffic.

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of prefabricated, portable mats so designed that any number of planks (sections) may be fastened together to form a stable landing surface.
dominio.observaciones: Usually made of aluminum (for example: US Air Force AM-2 aluminum matting) with a non-skid coating applied. May also be used for beach landings, heliports, bridge decking, heavy duty roads, and other similar applications such as flooring for relocatable shelters, tents, and hangers.

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of a clayey (usually red) soil that hardens on exposure to the air, packed over a firm subgrade.
dominio.observaciones: Laterite is characterized by a high proportion of sesquioxides, especially of aluminum and iron, and a low proportion of bases and silica. It is formed by chemical weathering in tropical and subtropical regions. Also loosely any of various other reddish or iron-rich surface materials in the tropics and sub-tropics.

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of broken rock or ironstone slag of varying size and shape that is packed through repeated rolling and water-bound.
dominio.observaciones: The range of sizes and shapes results in a relatively firm interlocking of the materials.

dominio.definicion: A surface covered by spread rolls of protective laminate, providing waterproofing and dustproofing on soils that have adequate strength for airfield traffic areas.
dominio.observaciones: Usually rubber-based, but may be plastic (for example: nylon) or other coated fibre material.

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of the original surface material mixed in place with a non-bituminous binder (for example: portland cement).
A surface composed of pierced steel sheets, nominally 15 inches by 10 feet in size, that have been clipped together edgewise to form a continuous mat.
dominio.observaciones: Used to best effect on stabilized subgrade, resulting in a semi-permanent runway.

dominio.definicion: A surface composed of sand that has been graded, rolled, and/or oiled.
A surface composed of packed snow, usually resulting from multiple snowfalls, that may have additionally been rolled to ensure the absence of voids or cavities.
A surface composed of rock or similar mineral substances (other than metal) of generally regular form and size, usually artificially shaped.
A body of water that is kept clear for use as a seaplane run.
A surface composed of wood logs, beams, or planks.
A surface composed of asphalt applied over a concrete underlayment.

nombre: Aerodrome Movement Area Surface Preparation Method
definicion: The preparation technique(s) applied to a surface composition.

datatype.nombre: Aerodrome Movement Area Surface Preparation Method Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aerodrome movement area surface preparation method.

dominio.definicion: The paved surface is seal coated to bring aggregate particles into contact with vehicle tires to improve skid resistance.
The movement area has been leveled to result in a smooth surface.
dominio.observaciones: May include a slight grade to promote drainage.

dominio.definicion: The surface is covered with grass.
The paved surface is grooved to promote drainage and traction.
dominio.observaciones: Accomplished by, for example, cutting or the emplacement of plastic strips that are later removed.

dominio.definicion: The surface is coated with a light layer of oil to reduce dust formation.
dominio.observaciones: Usually accomplished by spraying.

dominio.definicion: The paved surface is covered by a material designed to improve drainage and reduce slippage.
dominio.observaciones: For example, Porous European Mix (PEM), a porous asphaltic concrete formulated with 20-24 percent air voids used as an open graded friction course (OGFC).

dominio.definicion: The surface is prepared with heavy rollers to result in a firm, packed surface without local dips or swales.
The paved surface is seal coated using an asphalt-rubber binder.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes termed a 'stress-absorbing membrane' (SAM). May be based on the use of recycled scrap tire rubber.

definicion: The primary official name of an aerodrome as designated by an appropriate authority.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The functional status of the pavement of an aerodrome movement area.
descripcion: An aerodrome movement area is that part of an aerodrome to be used for aircraft movement operations, consisting of the manoeuvring area and the apron(s).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aerodrome pavement functional status.

dominio.definicion: The condition is adequate for limited aircraft operations.
dominio.observaciones: It is capable of supporting 30 days of limited operations by the heaviest (highest Load Classification Number (LCN) or Aircraft Classification Number (ACN)) aircraft that can use the facility.

dominio.definicion: It is estimated (in lieu of reported information) that the condition is adequate for limited aircraft operations.
dominio.observaciones: It is estimated to be capable of supporting 30 days of limited operations by the heaviest (highest Load Classification Number (LCN) or Aircraft Classification Number (ACN)) aircraft that can use the facility.

dominio.definicion: The condition is adequate for sustained aircraft operations.
dominio.observaciones: It will support 30 days of sustained operations by the heaviest (highest Load Classification Number (LCN) or Aircraft Classification Number (ACN)) aircraft that can use the facility.

dominio.definicion: It is estimated (in lieu of reported information) that the condition is adequate for sustained aircraft operations.
dominio.observaciones: It is estimated that it will support 30 days of sustained operations by the heaviest (highest Load Classification Number (LCN) or Aircraft Classification Number (ACN)) aircraft that can use the facility.

dominio.definicion: The condition is sufficient for only emergency aircraft operations.
dominio.observaciones: It will support only emergency or occasional operations by the heaviest (highest Load Classification Number (LCN) or Aircraft Classification Number (ACN)) aircraft that can use the facility.

dominio.definicion: It is estimated (in lieu of reported information) that the condition is sufficient for only emergency aircraft operations.
dominio.observaciones: It is estimated that it will support only emergency or occasional operations by the heaviest (highest Load Classification Number (LCN) or Aircraft Classification Number (ACN)) aircraft that can use the facility.

dominio.definicion: The surface is under construction and is therefore not capable of supporting aircraft operations.
The surface is in such a state of deterioration or disrepair that it is completely unusable and cannot be safely used for any type of aircraft operations.
The surface is capable of supporting extended aircraft operations with minimal maintenance.
dominio.observaciones: The surface is newly constructed, less than 5 years old, and is capable of supporting extended aircraft operations by the heaviest (highest Load Classification Number (LCN) or Aircraft Classification Number (ACN)) aircraft that is rated to use the facility, with minimal need for maintenance.

definicion: The monthly mean of the daily maximum temperatures for the hottest month of the year at an aerodrome.
descripcion: The hottest month is that which has the highest monthly mean temperature; this temperature should be averaged over a period of years.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of internal energy that a substance contains.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of thermodynamic temperature, based absolute zero and the freezing (triple point) point of water (those points being 273.16 degrees Celsius in separation), that is related to Kelvin by absolute zero being -273.15 degrees Celsius; the triple point of water is 0.01 degrees Celsius whereas the boiling point of water at 1 atmosphere pressure is 99.9839 degrees Celsius.

definicion: A description of the general snow plan considerations at the aerodrome.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that contains only non-lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The operational status of an aerodrome movement area, as a category.
descripcion: For example: serviceable, unserviceable, closed, or work-in-progress.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aerodrome surface status.

dominio.definicion: Access is officially prohibited.
Access is officially permitted.
The surface is under construction and is therefore not capable of supporting aircraft operations.
Aircraft may be parked on the movement surface limiting operations.

definicion: An indication that the instrument approach path of the aerodrome is impacted by terrain features.
descripcion: Either the terrain rises at least 600 metres (2000 feet) above the aerodrome elevation within a 5 nautical mile radius of the aerodrome reference point, or the terrain rises at least 1200 metres (4000 feet) within the instrument approach path to the aerodrome.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

nombre: Aeronautical Advisory and Information Service Type
definicion: The type(s) of advice and information service(s) provided by a facility to assist in the safe conduct of flight and aircraft movement.

datatype.nombre: Aeronautical Advisory and Information Service Type Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an aeronautical advisory and information service type.

dominio.definicion: A unit providing pilots of aircraft with details of other known traffic taking off, landing and flying in the vicinity of the aerodrome where, despite not being busy enough for full Air Traffic Control, the traffic is such that some form of service is necessary.
The continuous broadcast of recorded non-control information at airports in Alaska where a FSS provides local airport advisory service.
dominio.observaciones: The AFI broadcast automates the repetitive transmission of essential but routine information such as weather, wind, altimeter, favored runway, breaking action, airport NOTAMs, and other applicable information. The information is continuously broadcast over a discrete VHF radio frequency (usually the ASOS frequency).

dominio.definicion: A service established within the defined area of coverage responsible for the provision of aeronautical information/data necessary for the safety, regularity and efficiency of air navigation.
A service providing altimeter setting information.
An automated weather sensor platforms that collect weather data at airports and disseminate the weather information via radio and/or landline.
dominio.observaciones: Information provided includes, altimeter, wind, temperature/dew point, visibility, clouds/ceiling, as well as precipitation and density altitude.

dominio.definicion: The automatic provision of current, routine information to arriving and departing aircraft throughout 24 hours or a specified portion thereof.
An automated weather sensor platforms that collect weather data at airports and disseminate the weather information via radio and/or landline.
dominio.observaciones: The Automated Weather Sensor System (AWSS) is a follow on program providing identical information as the Automated Surface Observation System (ASOS).

dominio.definicion: An automated weather sensor platforms that collect weather data at airports and disseminate the weather information via radio and/or landline.
dominio.observaciones: Information provided includes: altimeter, wind, temperature/dew point, visibility, clouds/ceiling, as well as density altitude. AWOS does not provide precipitation information.

dominio.definicion: Pre-flight and post-flight briefing service.
A service specifically designed to provide, upon pilot request, timely weather information pertinent to his/her type of flight, intended route of flight, and altitude.
A service provided for the purpose of giving advice and information useful for the safe and efficient conduct of flights.
A continuous recorded hazardous in-flight weather forecasts broadcasted to airborne aircraft.
Limited ad-hoc information provision, about a specific activity at a particular location.

Facilities and services that provide aviation with meteorological forecasts, briefs, and observations as well as SIGMET information, VOLMET broadcasting material and any other meteorological data provided by states for aeronautical use.

The provision of notices distributed by means of telecommunication containing information concerning the establishment, condition or change in any aeronautical facility, service, procedure or hazard, the timely knowledge of which is essential to personnel concerned with flight operations.
The service provided for the broadcast on the high frequency (HF) band, of meteorological information and operational information concerning navigation aids and aerodromes in an integrated form.

dominio.definicion: An office, located at an aerodrome, designated to provide meteorological service for international air navigation.
A unit established to provide air traffic control service to controlled flights in control areas under its jurisdiction.
A unit providing ADS support to equipped aircraft.
A unit providing a service within advisory airspace to ensure separation, in so far as practical, between aircraft which are operating on IFR flight plans.
Any facility intended to serve as an intermediary between a person reporting an emergency and a rescue coordination centre or rescue subcentre.
An office responsible for the provision of aeronautical information services within a defined area of coverage normally comprising a State or group of States.
A unit established to provide air traffic control service to controlled flights arriving at, or departing from, one or more aerodromes.
A facility providing Air Traffic Control service for arriving IFR and, under certain conditions, VFR aircraft.
A facility providing Air Traffic Control service for departing IFR and, under certain conditions, VFR aircraft.

A unit providing direction finding services over a very high frequency band radio, whose headings will lead the aircraft to a predetermined point such as the DF station or an airport.

A unit providing air traffic service within a temporary reserved airspace to participating and non-participating aircraft when the airspace is active.
A unit established at an aerodrome to provide aeronautical information/data for preflight planning.
