unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of plane angle equal to pi/180, approximately 0.01745532925199433 radians.

definicion: The type of a facility or building that is used to incarcerate prisoners serving terms of punishment detention, awaiting trial or other judiciary proceedings or awaiting further processing by authorities (for example: illegal immigrants awaiting deportation).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a corrections facility type.

dominio.definicion: A location where long (usually more than one year) sentences for criminal misconduct may be served.
dominio.observaciones: Typically larger than a jail and serving a larger administrative region.

dominio.definicion: A location where the criminally accused are initially taken to be processed and await trial and where short (usually less than one year) sentences for criminal misconduct may be served.
dominio.observaciones: Typically smaller than a prison and serving a local administrative region.

dominio.definicion: A building used for the discipline, reformation, and training of young and/or first offenders.
A building within which persons convicted or accused of crimes are confined.
A large facility created for detaining political opponents, enemy aliens, specific ethnic or religious groups, civilians of a critical war-zone, or other groups of people, usually during a war.
dominio.observaciones: The term is used for facilities whose inmates are selected according to some specific criteria, rather than individuals who are incarcerated after due process of law fairly applied by a judiciary.

dominio.definicion: A facility, building, or structure used to confine those accused of offences (for example: military, political, or immigration) against the State.

definicion: Instructions for reversing course on an Instrument Approach Procedure (IAP).

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that contains only non-lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: A descriptor of the aircraft course to be flown.
descripcion: For example: true track, magnetic track, heading, VOR radial, true bearing, or magnetic bearing.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a course type.

dominio.definicion: The horizontal direction of the aircraft as indicated by the aircraft's heading indicator.
The horizontal direction of an object or point measured clockwise from Magnetic North up to, but not including, 360 arc degrees.
The projection on the earth's surface of the path of an aircraft, the direction of which path at any point is usually expressed in degrees from Magnetic North.
The horizontal direction of an object or point measured clockwise from True North through 360 arc degrees.
The projection on the earth's surface of the path of an aircraft, the direction of which path at any point is usually expressed in degrees from True North.
A magnetic bearing extending from a VOR navigation facility.

definicion: The extent and/or nature of the cover (for example: a roof) of a structure.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a cover closure type.

dominio.definicion: No cover exists over the structure.
dominio.observaciones: It is completely open to the sun and weather.

dominio.definicion: A portion of the structure is covered, but a significant portion remains uncovered.
The structure is covered by a moveable surface that may be opened and closed.
dominio.observaciones: Typically used on stadiums where weather control is desired.

dominio.definicion: The structure is completely covered.

definicion: An indication that a watercourse section is completely covered over and connects to uncovered watercourses at each end.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The length of a watercourse section that is completely covered over and connects to uncovered watercourses at each end.

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The maximum horizontal distance from the center point of the rotation of the crane to either the end of the boom or the end of the jib.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The maximum reach of a crane.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The type of mobility of a crane.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a crane mobility type.

dominio.definicion: Non-mobile, power-operated, with lifting tackle and a pivoted boom that allows movement of loads horizontally as well as vertically.
Capable of moving along a fixed path (for example: parallel to the face of a wharf).
dominio.observaciones: May travel along rails, tracks, or reinforced channels.

dominio.definicion: Having a barge or scow for an undercarriage.
dominio.observaciones: Used, for example, for waterworks and waterfront work.

dominio.definicion: Capable of moving throughout an area (for example: adjacent to the face of a wharf).
dominio.observaciones: May be mounted on either solid rubber wheels or tracks (continuous articulated bands passing around two or more wheels).

definicion: The longest distance between the supports for a gantry or bridge crane.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The type of a crane based on its design and/or method of operation.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a crane type.

dominio.definicion: Permanently installed crane that is mounted between two overhead tracks with the main structure member forming a bridge between them.
Having a boom mounted on a fixed or movable structure that moves in a complete circle to handle heavy materials.
A crane in which a boom, swinging jib, or other structural member is mounted on a vertical mast or tower.
A mechanical device consisting of three poles bolted together at their upper ends and extended below, carrying tackle for raising heavy weights or machinery.
High-speed, shore-based, and used in the lift-on/lift-off operation of specially constructed containers.

definicion: The type of a crater based on its origin and/or shape.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a crater type.

dominio.definicion: Created by a volcanic explosion or the collapse of a volcanic cone.
Created by the explosive force originating from the impact of a meteorite or similar body with the surface of the Earth.
Created by the explosive force originating from both the impact and the subsequent explosion of a bomb, missile or similar man-made object.
A crater originating from the collapse of either a man-made (mine) or natural (cavern) subterranean void.
A usually funnel-shaped crater originating from eruptive volcanic activity, whereby lava or ashes have been thrown out.

definicion: The date and, optionally, time when a digital representation (for example: of a feature or a geographic name) was created.
descripcion: Midnight is understood to be 00:00:00 (the beginning of a day); when the time is not specified then midnight in the local time zone is typically implied.

datatype.nombre: Creation Date and Time Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a creation date and time.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.4.1, Combinations of date and time of day - Complete representation - Extended format, a calendar date and time representation, as a single data element comprising up to twenty characters, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, [hh] the ordinal number of an hour within the calendar day, [mm] the ordinal number of a minute within the hour, [ss] the ordinal number of a second within the minute, and an optional 'Z' when the time is according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12' for 12 April 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412T114520Z').

definicion: An indication that the process by which the digital representation of the feature(s) or data set(s) within an area is created, is complete in accordance with the specification that was used as the basis for defining the digital representation of the feature(s) or data set(s).

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The physical consequences to the crew of a vessel resulting from an aggressive act.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a crew injuries.

dominio.definicion: Piercing(s) from pointed weapons (for example: knives or swords).
Piercing(s) by projectiles from firearms (for example: a pistol, a gun, or an automatic weapon).
Injuries resulting from hand-to-hand combat (for example: contusions, abrasions, or minor lacerations).
Did not sustain any injuries.

definicion: The predominant species of a crop land.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a crop species.

dominio.definicion: The tree Prunus dulcis, allied to the plum and cherry, bearing stone-fruit consisting of kernels, oval with pointed ends.
dominio.observaciones: There are two almond varieties, the sweet and the bitter.

dominio.definicion: A tree of the rose family, Malus domestica, bearing a round firm fruit.
dominio.observaciones: It is cultivated in innumerable varieties in the temperate zones.

dominio.definicion: A hardy awned cereal of the genus Hordeum.
dominio.observaciones: The grain is used as food and in making malt liquors and spirits.

dominio.definicion: Any of several plants raised as crops and bearing small globular or ovate juicy fruits not having a stone.
dominio.observaciones: For example, strawberries, raspberries, and blackcurrants.

dominio.definicion: An evergreen leguminous tree, Ceratonia siliqua, native to the Mediterranean region bearing edible horn-shaped fleshy seed-pods.
A tree of the genus Castanea, of the beech family.
dominio.observaciones: Especially that of Castanea sativa (also Spanish chestnut, sweet chestnut). Also (with specifying word), any of various similar trees.

dominio.definicion: A fruit-bearing tree of the genus Citrus.
dominio.observaciones: Includes, for example, the lemon, citron, lime, orange, and grapefruit.

dominio.definicion: An evergreen oak, Quercus suber, which is native to the Mediterranean and has the distinctive property of producing more cork after some is removed.
The tree Theobroma cacao, from whose seed cocoa and chocolate are made.
dominio.observaciones: It is native to tropical America.

dominio.definicion: Any of certain members of the paleotropical genus Coffea (especially Coffea arabica), of the madder family, which bear white flowers succeeded by red berries each containing two seeds.
dominio.observaciones: The drink, coffee, is made by infusion from the seeds roasted and ground or (in the East) pounded.

dominio.definicion: A cereal grass of Central American origin, Zea mays, having a terminal male inflorescence and axillary female ears, the grains being embedded in a wooden core (the cob).
A member of the heath family, any of several Eurasian or American dwarf hardy shrubs of the genus Vaccinium, bearing acid bright red fruit.
dominio.observaciones: Especially Vaccinium oxycoccos, and the larger American Vaccinium macrocarpon.

dominio.definicion: A crop that is grown in moist or dry conditions and is are generally free of other vegetation (except near fences or hedgerows).
dominio.observaciones: For example, grains, tubers, legumes, and vegetables.

dominio.definicion: A crop grown for its fibre content.
dominio.observaciones: For example, cotton and sisal.

dominio.definicion: A tree, shrub, or other plant, producing edible fruits consisting of a seed and its envelope, especially when sweet, juicy, and pulpy.
dominio.observaciones: For example, apples, pears, and peaches.

dominio.definicion: A climbing plant of the genus Vitis (family Vitaceae), on which small oval berries, usually green, purple, or black, grow in clusters.
dominio.observaciones: The berries are eaten fresh or dried as fruit or used for making wine.

dominio.definicion: Any of various deciduous shrubs and low trees constituting the genus Corylus, of the birch family, bearing edible nuts enclosed in leafy involucres.
dominio.observaciones: Especially the European hazel, Corylus avellana, and its North American counterpart, Corylus americana.

dominio.definicion: A twining dioecious plant, Humulus lupulus, of the hemp family, with rough lobed leaves and small green flowers, the female becoming enlarged and conelike in seed.
dominio.observaciones: Found in damp bushy places and much cultivated as a source of hops, the ripened conelike spikes of the female plant, used to give a bitter flavour to malt liquors, and as a tonic and soporific.

dominio.definicion: A Eurasian tree, Acer campestre (family Aceraceae), with fruit in the form of two winged samaras joined together and palmately lobed leaves (more fully common maple, hedge maple).
dominio.observaciones: Also (with specifying word), any of numerous similar trees of this or other genera.

dominio.definicion: A cereal grass, Panicum miliaceum, widely grown in warm countries, with small spikelets arranged in a loose panicle.
dominio.observaciones: Also (with specifying word), any of various other drought-resistant usually small-seeded cereal grasses grown especially in warm countries of the world.

dominio.definicion: A hardy cereal plant of the genus Avena, usually Avena sativa.
dominio.observaciones: Used as food for people (for example: in porridge) and animals, especially horses.

dominio.definicion: A crop grown for its oil content.
dominio.observaciones: For example, oil palms, rape, and sunflower.

dominio.definicion: An evergreen tree, Olea europaea (family Oleaceae), with narrow leaves hoary on the underside and small whitish flowers.
dominio.observaciones: Long cultivated in the Mediterranean region for its fruit and the oil obtained from this. May also be used to describe any of various wild trees or shrubs of the genus Olea; (with specifying word) any of various trees and shrubs allied to the common olive, or resembling it in appearance or in providing oil.

dominio.definicion: A tree bearing a sweet juicy stone-fruit usually having a downy yellow and red-tinged skin.
A South American leguminous plant, Arachis hypogaea, widely grown in the tropics, bearing underground pods which contain nutlike seeds valuable as a food and a source of oil (also called groundnut).
dominio.observaciones: Also, any of several legumes with similar seeds, especially (more fully hog peanut) Amphicarpaea bracteata of North America.

dominio.definicion: A plant of the nightshade family of South American origin, Solanum tuberosum, widely cultivated for its starchy tubers.
Leguminous plants yielding edible seeds.
dominio.observaciones: For example, peas, beans, and lentils.

dominio.definicion: The grain of the grass Oryza sativa, a major world cereal.
dominio.observaciones: Grown in shallow irrigated or flooded fields known as rice paddies, rice-fields, or paddy-fields.

dominio.definicion: Any of various plants, especially Hevea brasiliensis, whose coagulated latex which in its natural state is thermoplastic and tacky and after vulcanization tough and elastic.
An awned cereal grass, Secale cereale, resembling barley, grown especially in colder parts of Eurasia.
dominio.observaciones: The grain of this cereal is used to make coarse bread, beer, and/or spirits.

dominio.definicion: Any of several Mexican agaves, especially Agave sisalana, raised for the extraction of fibre from its leaves.
dominio.observaciones: The fibre is used, for example, for cordage and matting.

dominio.definicion: A cereal grass, Sorghum bicolor, similar to maize and extensively grown in Africa, southern India, and elsewhere (different strains being known as durra, Guinea corn, Indian millet, Kaffir corn, and milo).
dominio.observaciones: A variety of this grass, Sorghum bicolor variety saccharatum, with a sweet juicy pith, is grown as fodder or for syrup manufacture.

dominio.definicion: A crop grown for its sugar content.
dominio.observaciones: For example, sugar cane (a grass, Saccharum officinarum, resembling bamboo, extensively cultivated in the tropics for the sugar extracted from its stems) and sugar beet (a cultivar of the beet, Beta vulgaris, grown for the high sugar content of its root).

dominio.definicion: Camellia sinensis (family Theaceae), a shrub or tree with white flowers and oval evergreen leaves, long cultivated in China and now also in Japan, India, Kenya, and elsewhere.
dominio.observaciones: A drink, tea, is made by infusing its dried leaves in hot (boiling) water.

dominio.definicion: Either of the plants (of tropical American origin) Nicotiana tabacum, of the nightshade family, and the allied Nicotiana rustica (more fully green tobacco, wild tobacco).
dominio.observaciones: A preparation of the dried leaves of these plants is smoked (for example: in pipes, cigarettes, and cigars) for its pleasantly relaxing effects, taken as snuff, or chewed. Also (with specifying word), any of various plants whose dried leaves are smoked in a similar way.

dominio.definicion: A much thickened underground part of a stem or rhizome (for example: in the potato), which serves as a food reserve and bears buds from which new plants arise.
Any cultivated (usually herbaceous) plant of which any part, especially the leaves or root, is eaten in savoury dishes, frequently with meat or fish.
Any tree of the genus Juglans (family Juglandaceae), members of which have drooping catkins and aromatic pinnate leaves.
dominio.observaciones: Especially the Eurasian Juglans regia and (more fully black walnut) the North American Juglans nigra. The green fleshy fruit contains an edible kernel in separate halves.

dominio.definicion: Any of various cereal grasses of the genus Triticum, with spikelets in dense distichous spikes.
dominio.observaciones: For example, Triticum aestivum (also known as bread wheat), widely grown in temperate climates, the source of the best bread flours, and Triticum durum (also known as durum wheat), the flour from which is used to make pasta.

dominio.definicion: The fruit of the date-palm, an oblong one-seeded drupe with sweet pulp, growing in clusters.
dominio.observaciones: The date-palm is a tree of the genus Phoenix; especially Phoenix dactylifera, source of most commercially-grown dates, native to northern Africa and western Asia.

dominio.definicion: A treelike herbaceous plant that has a stem of overlapping leaf sheaths and bears clusters of edible finger-shaped pulpy fruits that are yellow-skinned when ripe.
A West African palm tree, Elaeis guineensis, that bears fruit whose pericarp and seed-kernels are a valuable source of oil.
A tropical palm tree, Cocos nucifera, that bears a large ovate brown hard-shelled seed having an edible white lining enclosing a white liquid.
A grass, Saccharum officinarum, resembling bamboo, extensively cultivated in the tropics for the sugar extracted from its stems.
A plant of the genus Gossypium, of the mallow family, that is cultivated for cotton, a soft white fibrous substance that used for making thread and cloth.
Any of numerous, mainly tropical, giant grasses belonging to the genus Bambusa and various related genera.
dominio.observaciones: The mature canes are used for construction and furniture.

dominio.definicion: Any of various usually small and sometimes stemless fan palms, for example, the dwarf fan palm of the Mediterranean (Chamaerops humilis), the Sabal palmetto, and Serenoa repens of the south-eastern United States.
dominio.observaciones: Palmetto wood is used for pilings, leaf strips are used in weaving, and the leaves may be used for thatch. In some species (for example: the Sabal palmetto) the fan-shaped leaves are edible when young.

dominio.definicion: Trees suitable for conversion into industrial and/or commercial forest products (for example: timbers and/or lumber for construction, cabinetry, or paper production).
A leguminous plant, Medicago sativa, cultivated for fodder, which bears blue to violet flowers and trifoliate leaves.
A plant of the genus Aloe of the lily family, which includes succulent herbs, shrubs, and trees, bearing erect spikes of flowers and yielding bitter sap.
The tree Prunus armeniaca, of the rose family, cultivated for its juicy stone-fruit.
dominio.observaciones: It grows in the warmer temperate regions and is originally native to China.

dominio.definicion: A plant of the composite family, Cynara scolymus, resembling a thistle and whose flower-head is edible.
dominio.observaciones: It is native to the Mediterranean region.

dominio.definicion: A plant of the genus Asparagus, of the lily family, specifically Asparagus officinalis.
dominio.observaciones: The young shoots of this plant are eaten as a delicacy.

dominio.definicion: The tree Persea americana, of the laurel family, bearing a rough-skinned pear-shaped edible fruit.
dominio.observaciones: It is native to Central America and the West Indies.

dominio.definicion: A tropical American tree, Ochroma pyramidale having a strong and very light wood.
dominio.observaciones: Its wood is used, for example, in rafts and floats.

dominio.definicion: Any of numerous plants bearing a smooth kidney-shaped edible seed that is borne in long pods.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the Vicia faba and the Phaseolus vulgaris.

dominio.definicion: A variety of the tropical genus Capsicum, of the nightshade family, bearing large bell-shaped fruits.
A tropical Asian palm of the genus Areca, especially Areca catechu, that yields astringent seeds.
dominio.observaciones: Parings of the seeds are often chewed with leaves of a climbing evergreen shrub, Piper betle, of the pepper family, and a little lime.

dominio.definicion: Any of various tropical fruits with edible breadlike pulp.
dominio.observaciones: For example, that of the tree Artocarpus altilis of the Pacific islands.

dominio.definicion: A hardy variety of cauliflower producing many small heads.
A variety of cabbage producing many small cabbage-like buds.
dominio.observaciones: Individual buds are eaten as a vegetable.

dominio.definicion: A cultivated variety of the cruciferous plant Brassica oleracea whose leaves form a compact round head or heart.
dominio.observaciones: It is used as a green culinary vegetable.

dominio.definicion: Any of several varieties of oil-seed rape developed in Canada.
dominio.observaciones: Cultivated for the vegetable oil, canola oil, thereby obtained.

dominio.definicion: A small round ribbed variety of melon, with orange flesh.
Any of several Indo-Malayan plants, especially Elettaria cardamomum, whose seed capsules are used as a spice.
An umbelliferous plant, Daucus carota, having a large tapering root which in cultivated forms is orange-coloured and edible.
dominio.observaciones: Its roots are eaten as a vegetable.

dominio.definicion: A large tree, Anacardium occidentale, native to tropical America and cultivated for its edible kidney-shaped nuts.
A plant of the spurge family, Manihot esculenta (also called manioc), much grown in the tropics for its edible tuberous roots.
dominio.observaciones: It has two groups of cultivars, those containing high amounts of cyanide in their untreated roots (termed: bitter cassava) and those with low amounts of cyanide (termed: sweet cassava).

dominio.definicion: A cultivated variety of cabbage with a large, dense, white flower-head.
dominio.observaciones: The flower-heads are eaten as a vegetable.

dominio.definicion: An umbelliferous plant, Apium graveolens, grown for its crisp blanched leaf-stalks.
dominio.observaciones: The leaf-stalks are eaten raw in salads or cooked as a vegetable.

dominio.definicion: Any of the plants of the grass family Graminae that are cultivated for their edible seeds.
An evergreen tree or shrub of the South American genus Cinchona, of the madder family, with fragrant flowers.
dominio.observaciones: Its dried bark is a source of quinine and other medicinal alkaloids.

dominio.definicion: A southern Indian tree, Cinnamomum zeylanicum, whose powdered aromatic inner bark is used as a spice.
The tropical myrtle, Syzygium aromaticum, whose dried flower-buds are used as a pungent aromatic spice.
Any of various leguminous plants constituting the genus Trifolium, with flowers in crowded heads and trifoliate leaves.
dominio.observaciones: Grown as fodder.

dominio.definicion: The South American shrub, Erythroxylum coca, whose dried leaves are chewed as a stimulant.
Dried kernals of the tropical palm tree, Cocos nucifera, from which oil is obtained.
A leguminous plant, Vigna unguiculata, grown both as fodder and for its seed, eaten as pulse.
A trailing vine of the gourd family, Cucumis sativus native to southern Asia, with a long fleshy edible fruit.
The eggplant, Solanum melongena, whose fleshy elongated egg-shaped fruit is typically dark purple.
dominio.observaciones: The fruit is eaten as a vegetable.

dominio.definicion: A blue-flowered plant of the composite family, Cichorium endivia, grown as a salad (chiefly in a form with curled much-dissected leaves) or as a vegetable (in a form with wavy undivided leaves).
A blue-flowered plant, Linum usitatissimum (family Linaceae) cultivated for its seed (linseed), and for textile fibre made from its stalks.
Blossoms (and usually their stalks) often separated from the growing plant and used in groups for decoration or as a mark of honour or respect.
Any of various crops grown for animal feed (for example: alfalfa, clover, and hay).
A bulbous plant of the lily family, Allium sativum, grown as a herb.
dominio.observaciones: The strong-smelling pungent-tasting bulb of this plant (divisible into cloves or smaller bulbs) is much used as a flavouring.

dominio.definicion: The monocotyledonous plant, Zingiber officinale (family Zingiberaceae), that yields a hot spicy edible rhizome.
dominio.observaciones: It is native to Southeast Asia and used in cookery and medicine as well as candied as a sweet or preserved in syrup.

dominio.definicion: The tree, Citrus paradisi, that bears a large round yellow-skinned citrus fruit having juicy acid pulp.
dominio.observaciones: The tree is a hybrid or mutation of the shaddock, Citrus maxima, of West Indian origin.

dominio.definicion: Any of certain varieties of the plant Capsicum annuum, bearing a bell-shaped, smooth-skinned, mildly pungent fruit eaten in salads or as a vegetable.
dominio.observaciones: While green when unripe, when ripe they are usually yellow, orange, or red.

dominio.definicion: Any cultivated (usually herbaceous) plant of which any part, especially the leaves or root, is prepared for the table.
Any of several acacias, especially Acacia senegal, that exudes a water-soluble gum.
Any of numerous non-coniferous tree species (for example: oak) whose wood is noted for its hardness.
A cultivated variety of the melon, Cucumis melo, with smooth ivory or pale yellow skin and sweet green flesh.
A fibre obtained from the phloem of the plants Corchorus capsularis and Corchorus olitorius, of the linden family.
dominio.observaciones: It is grown chirfly ins Bangladesh and West Bengal, and is used in the manufacture of coarse sacking, canvas, twine, and rope.

dominio.definicion: Any of various pinnate-leaved palms of the former genus Kentia, especially Howeia forsterana and Howeia belmoreana.
dominio.observaciones: They are native to Australia and some Pacific islands and frequently grown as house-plants.

dominio.definicion: A shrub, Catha edulis, of the spindle tree family, cultivated in Arabia for its leaves.
dominio.observaciones: The leaves are chewed or infused as a stimulant and a narcotic drug may be prepared from them.

dominio.definicion: The eastern Asian climbing plant, Actinidia chinensis (family Actinidiaceae), that bear an oval fruit with brown skin, green flesh, and black seeds.
dominio.observaciones: It is cultivated in New Zealand and elsewhere.

dominio.definicion: The tree, Citrus limon, bearing an ovate pale yellow acid fruit.
dominio.observaciones: The fruit is much used for making drinks and as a flavouring.

dominio.definicion: A leguminous plant, Lens culinaris, bearing small rounded seeds.
dominio.observaciones: It is cultivated for food in Mediterranean countries and used in, for example, soups and stews.

dominio.definicion: Any plant of the genus Lactuca of the composite family, especially the cultivated species Lactuca sativa, whose leaves are much used as a salad.
The small spiny tree, Citrus aurantiifolia (family Rutaceae), of tropical regions that bears a globular citrus fruit that is smaller and greener than the lemon and has a more acid taste.
Any of various Australian evergreen trees of the genus Macadamia (family Proteaceae), especially Macadamia integrifolia and Macadamia tetraphylla, that yield edible nuts.
A spice consisting of the dried fleshy aril surrounding the seed (nutmeg) of the fruit of the nutmeg tree.
An Indian and Myanmar (Burmese) tree, Mangifera indica (family Anacardiaceae), bearing a sweet orange-fleshed fruit.
dominio.observaciones: The fruit is eaten as dessert or used in its unripe state to make chutney or jam.

dominio.definicion: The plant, Cucumis melo, bearing a gourd-like fruit with sweet green or yellowish-pink flesh.
Any of various aromatic often moisture-loving labiate plants of the genus Mentha, that bear lilac flowers.
dominio.observaciones: For example, spearmint (Mentha spicata) and peppermint.

dominio.definicion: Any of various trees of the genus Morus (family Moraceae), especially Morus nigra, grown for its purple, succulent berry-like multiple fruit, and Morus alba, which has white insipid fruit and whose leaves are used to feed silkworms.
Any of the cruciferous plants (for example: Sinapis alba (white mustard), Brassica nigra (black mustard), and Brassica juncea (brown mustard), whose crushed seeds are used as a pungent condiment.
A variety of the peach tree bearing a fruit resembling a peach but having a thinner downless skin and a firmer pulp.
Any of various species bearing edible or oil-yielding, usually woody or hard-shelled, fruit or seed kernals.
The Myristica fragrans (family Myristicaceae), an evergreen tree of the Moluccas, bearing a fruit whose kernal contains a hard spherical aromatic seed.
dominio.observaciones: The kernel is grated or ground and used as a spice in cooking.

dominio.definicion: Any of various seeds (for example: sesame, cottonseed, and castor bean) that are cultivated as a source of oil.
A plant, Allium cepa, of the lily family, cultivated for its edible bulb.
dominio.observaciones: The bulb has a strong pungent flavour and smell and consists of fleshy concentric leaf-bases. It is eaten raw, cooked, or pickled.

dominio.definicion: The plant, Papaver somniferum, a glaucous poppy with chiefly white or lilac flowers.
dominio.observaciones: It yelds opium, a reddish-brown strong-scented addictive drug prepared from the thickened dried juice of the unripe capsules.

dominio.definicion: The tree, Citrus sinensis, bearing any of several large round citrus fruits with segmented juicy pulp enclosed in a tough reddish-yellow rind.
dominio.observaciones: A common dessert fruit.

dominio.definicion: Any of numerous (frequently epiphytic) monocotyledonous plants of the family Orchidaceae, characterized by having one perianth segment (the labellum) differentiated from the rest and by commonly having only one anther, united with the style in a central body (the column), and often having brilliantly coloured or bizarrely shaped flowers.
The endosperm of the fruit of the oil palm, Elaeis guineensis, whose mesocarp may be used as food or for the extraction of oil.
dominio.observaciones: Palm-kernel oil (palm oil) is used in the manufacture of margarine and soap.

dominio.definicion: A tropical American tree, Carica papaya (family Caricaceae), with palmate leaves on an unbranched stem and bearing a melon-shaped fruit having pinkish or orange flesh enclosing a mass of dark grey seeds.

Any of several species of passion-flower, especially that of the Brazilian Passiflora edulis, bearing an edible egg-shaped berry with purple wrinkled skin and sweet yellow pulp surrounding small black seeds.
The hardy annual leguminous climbing plant, Pisum sativum, which bears papilionaceous flowers with round seeds in elongated pods.
dominio.observaciones: Eaten as a vegetable when green or as a pulse when dried.

dominio.definicion: The tree of the rose family, Pyrus communis, bearing a large usually yellowish or brownish-green fruit, broadest at the base and tapering towards the stalk.
The tree Carya illinoinensis, a very tall hickory of the southern United States, bearing pinkish-brown smooth nut having a rich-flavoured oily kernel resembling a walnut.
Piper nigrum (family Piperaceae), a climbing shrub having alternate stalked entire leaves, flowers in pendulous spikes, and small berries which turn red when ripe.
dominio.observaciones: Indigenous to southern India and Sri Lanka and the chief plant yielding pepper.

dominio.definicion: The tropical American bromeliad, Ananas comosus, bearing a large juicy edible collective fruit developed from a conical spike of flowers and having yellow flesh surrounded by a tough segmented skin and topped with a tuft of stiff leaves.
The tree Pistacia vera (family Anacardiaceae) bearing a nutlike drupe with an edible greenish kernel.
dominio.observaciones: It is a native of western Asia much cultivated in southern Europe.

dominio.definicion: A plant, especially Musa paradisiaca, producing a banana-like fruit with a high starch content.
dominio.observaciones: The fruit is picked when not yet ripe and cooked as a vegetable in tropical countries.

dominio.definicion: The tree Prunus domestica, of the rose family and allied to the blackthorn, bearing an edible roundish fleshy fruit, usually purple, red, or yellow when ripe, with a sweet pulp and a flattish pointed stone.
dominio.observaciones: The fruit when dried is referred to as a prune.

dominio.definicion: A yellow-flowered plant, Brassica napus, allied to the turnip.
dominio.observaciones: A variety of this plant, Brassica napus subspecies rapifera, is grown as a vegetable, while another variety, Brassica napus subspecies oleifera, is grown as green feed for livestock and for its seed which yields an edible oil.

dominio.definicion: A plant of the composite family, Carthamus tinctorius, with orange-yellow thistle-like flower-heads.
dominio.observaciones: It is cultivated in Egypt and Asia for the dye obtained from its florets and for the oil from its seeds, used especially in cooking.

dominio.definicion: An African plant, Sesamum orientale (family Pedaliaceae), widely grown in the tropics, producing seeds used as food and yielding an edible oil.
A nut-bearing tree of tropical Africa, Vitellaria paradoxa (family Sapotaceae).
A leguminous plant, Glycine max, grown as a vegetable or for its protein-rich seeds which yield an edible oil and when ground a flour.
Any of various plants yielding strongly flavoured or aromatic vegetable substances.
dominio.observaciones: They are used especially to flavour or scent food, or as medicines.

dominio.definicion: A plant of the goosefoot family, Spinacia oleracea, cultivated for its edible dark green succulent leaves.
dominio.observaciones: The leaves are used as a vegetable.

dominio.definicion: Young tender shoots or side-growth of various plants (for example: a brassica, a bean, or alfalfa), eaten as a vegetable.
The fruit of any of several kinds of gourd, cooked and eaten as a vegetable.
dominio.observaciones: For example, Cucurbita pepo variety melopepo, eaten before the seeds and rinds have hardened (summer squash), and both Cucurbita maxima and Cucurbita moschata, stored and eaten when mature (winter squash).

dominio.definicion: Any of the plants constituting the genus Fragaria, of the rose family, which are characterized by having trifoliate leaves in a basal rosette, five-petalled white flowers, long trailing runners, and an edible fruit consisting of enlarged pulpy usually scarlet receptacle studded with small yellow achenes.
A cultivar of the beet, Beta vulgaris, grown for the high sugar content of its root.

Any of several plants constituting the genus Helianthus, of the composite family, having conspicuous yellow-rayed flower-heads and commonly cultivated (for example: Helianthus annus) for its oily seeds.
A plant of the bindweed family, Ipomoea batatas, cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions for its sweetish edible tubers.
dominio.observaciones: The root is usually eaten boiled and mashed.

dominio.definicion: The tree Citrus reticulata, bearing a mandarin orange, especially one with a deep reddish-orange peel.
A food-plant, Colocasia esculenta, of the arum family, cultivated in many varieties in the tropics for its starchy tubers or its succulent leaves.
A plant of the nightshade family, Lycopersicon esculentum, bearing a glossy, usually bright red and spherical, pulpy fruit.
dominio.observaciones: It is a native of the Andes and its fruit is often cooked as a vegetable or eaten in salads.

dominio.definicion: The yellow-flowered cruciferous plant, Brassica rapa, having a globular root (the swollen hypocotyl) that is usually white.
dominio.observaciones: Long cultivated as a vegetable and as cattle-feed.

dominio.definicion: Any of various tropical climbing epiphytic orchids constituting the genus Vanilla, especially Vanilla fragrans which native to Central America.
dominio.observaciones: The dried pods yield a fragrant substance used to flavour chocolate, ice-cream, and other foods as well as in perfumery.

dominio.definicion: The gourd Citrullus lanatus, whose fruit has a green rind and sweet, very juicy flesh.
dominio.observaciones: The plant is native to Africa and widely grown in warmer parts of the world.

dominio.definicion: Any of various chiefly tropical vines constituting the genus Dioscorea (family Dioscoreaceae), that are grown for their edible starchy tubers.
dominio.observaciones: For example, (in Southeast Asia) Dioscorea alata and (in West Africa) Dioscorea x cayenensis (yellow yam).

dominio.definicion: A tall erect herb, Cannabis sativa or common hemp, of the family Moraceae having long dentate leaves on long petioles and cultivated for its fibre, intoxicating properties, and/or the oil obtained from its seeds.
dominio.observaciones: It is common in central Asia and other warm regions with different regional varieties (for example: Cannabis indica or Indian hemp).

dominio.definicion: Any plant that is used to produce narcotics.
dominio.observaciones: Narcotics are a drugs that produce numbness or stupor; often taken for pleasure or to reduce pain; extensive use can lead to addiction. For example: opium or cocaine.

dominio.definicion: Any plant of the genus Rosa (family Rosaceae), which comprises pinnate-leaved, usually prickly, frequently climbing shrubs bearing large usually pink, white, yellow, or crimson flowers and includes many species, varieties, and hybrids grown for ornament.

Any of various small labiate shrubs constituting the genus Lavandula, with spikes of purple flowers and narrow oblong or lanceolate leaves, native to the Mediterranean region; specifically any of those grown in gardens or cultivated for perfume, especially Lavandula angustifolia, Lavandula latifolia, and their hybrid.
A species of crocus in the family Iridaceae whose flower has three stigmas, which are the distal ends of the plant's carpels.
dominio.observaciones: Together with its style, the stalk connecting the stigmas to the rest of the plant, these components are often dried and used in cooking as a seasoning and coloring agent. Saffron is a spice derived from the dried stigma of the flower.

dominio.definicion: Any tree or shrub of the large, chiefly tropical, monocotyledonous family Palmae, typically having an unbranched stem with a crown of very large leaves either palmate or pinnate in shape.
dominio.observaciones: Also (with specifying word), any of various palmlike plants of other families, such as cycads.

dominio.definicion: A crop grown purely for its aesthetic attractions (for example: beautification, screening, accent, or color), rather than for food or any other economic use.
dominio.observaciones: For example, flowering trees or shrubs to be transplanted for landscaping around buildings.

definicion: The ratio of the area covered by cropland within an area, relative to the entire area.

datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A scaled dimensionless measure denoting one part in every hundred.

definicion: An indication of the degree to which terrain of a given area will permit cross country movement.
descripcion: Reference NATO STANAG 2259.

datatype.definicion: An integer domain value that is restricted to fall in the range from zero to 100, inclusive.
datatype.nota: The realization of this integer datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A dimensionless physical quantity, one which has no unit of measure.

definicion: The cross-sectional profile of an opening (for example: a tunnel or the space under a bridge span).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a cross-sectional profile.

dominio.definicion: Shaped like an arch, consisting of a curved top on two vertical sidewalls.
Shaped like a box, consisting of a flat top on two vertical sidewalls.
Shaped like a portion of a circle, consisting of a curved top extending smoothly to the base (for example: a floor or the ground).
Shaped like a circle.

definicion: The cross-sectional shape of a feature in the horizontal plane.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a cross-sectional shape.

dominio.definicion: Not of regular or symmetrical shape.
Shaped like an ellipse, a symmetrical closed curve traced by a point moving in a plane so that the sum of its distances from two other points is constant.
Shaped like a rectangle, a plane figure having four straight sides and four right angles.
Shaped like a circle, a perfectly round plane figure whose circumference is everywhere equidistant from its centre.
Shaped like a square, a plane figure with four right angles and four equal straight sides.
Shaped like a triangle, a plane figure with three straight sides.
Shaped like a hexagon, a polygon with six edges and six vertices.
Shaped like a pentagon, a polygon with five sides and five vertices.
Shaped like a octagon, a polygon with eight sides and eight vertices.
Shaped like a half-circle, a plane figure consisting of half of the circumference of a circle plus a line connecting the two ends of that circumference.
dominio.observaciones: A circle is a perfectly round plane figure whose circumference is everywhere equidistant from its centre. A line passing through the centre from circumference to circumference is termed its 'diameter'.

definicion: The average diameter of tree crowns within a defined area.
descripcion: The tree crown displays the leaves to allow capture of radiant energy for photosynthesis. Its diameter is usually measured by projecting the edges of the crown to the ground and measuring the length along one axis from edge to edge through the crown centre. Unless the crown has a regular shape, the width measured will depend on the axis selected for measurement. Two orthogonal axes are normally selected and averaged (for example: the maximum axis and the axis at 90 degrees to it); the two measurements are then averaged using an arithmetic mean (most common) or a geometric mean (for highly elliptical boles).

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The type of a cultural factor shared by a group of people and establishing a common context for their behaviour.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a cultural context type.

dominio.definicion: An ethical and philosophical doctrine in which all humans are divided into groups termed 'nations' in which members are distinguished by a common identity, the status of belonging to a particular nation by birth or naturalization, and almost always by a common origin, in the sense of ancestry, parentage or descent.

A human population whose members identify with each other, usually on the basis of having a common cultural heritage (for example: as distinguished by customs, language, religious practices, or common history) or a presumed common genealogy or ancestry.
dominio.observaciones: Kinship-based ethnic groups are sometimes referred to as 'tribes' whereas those more closely associated with the evolution of the State are referred to as 'nations'.

dominio.definicion: A human population united by a common language, spoken and/or written.
dominio.observaciones: Languages may be divided into dialects, language varieties used by people in a particular geographic locality.

dominio.definicion: A human population united by a common group of beliefs or disbelief in a divine or superhuman power or powers to be obeyed and worshiped as the creator(s) and ruler(s) of the universe, and the moral codes, practices, values, institutions and rituals associated with such beliefs.
A human population whose members identify with each other by the methods used in securing the necessaries of life.
A human population united by a common tie to a territory.
A human population united by common political interests.

definicion: The portion of an area that is covered by buildings and other cultural features (for example: roads).

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value that is restricted to be completely contained in the range from 0 to 100, inclusive.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A scaled dimensionless measure denoting one part in every hundred.

definicion: The method(s) of satisfying a people's material needs within an area.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a cultural economic system.

dominio.definicion: Commercial livestock breeding, raising, and use in a fixed location.
The cultivation of plants for subsistence and/or sale.
The capture of fish for subsistence and/or sale.
Small-scale manufacturing of goods and corresponding services.
Collective term for securing the necessaries of life from nature.
Large-scale production of goods by the utilization of technical equipment.
Commercial livestock breeding, raising, and use in multiple locations.
dominio.observaciones: Normally subject to season-driven migrations to maintain sufficient availability of forage and water. Can be differentiated as: full nomadism, semi-nomadism, transhumance and partial nomadism.

dominio.definicion: Collective term for the totality of non-industrial business (for example: trade, traffic, telecommunication, and medicine).
The seasonal transfer of grazing animals to different pastures, often over long distances.
dominio.observaciones: Special form of spatial mobility of stock breeding groups in mountainous (sub) alpine regions. Annual migration of households and herds between winter pastures and summer pastures at higher elevations, partially with fixed abodes at both places.

definicion: The type of a facility or building that is used for cultural activities.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a cultural facility type.

dominio.definicion: A large fortified building with thick walls, usually dominating the surrounding region.
A building devoted to the acquisition, conservation, study, exhibition, and educational interpretation of objects having scientific, historical, or artistic value.
A large building for public meetings and/or performances.
A building that houses a theatre designed chiefly for the performance of operas.
An site consisting of buildings, associated facilities, roads, and supporting terrain that is used for performing and observing sporting events.
A building used for recreational exercise and minor sports competitions, which typically serves a small town, community, or local region.
A building, a room or outdoor structure used for the presentation of plays, films, or other dramatic performances.

A building, or part of building, in which literary and artistic materials (for example: books, periodicals, newspapers, pamphlets, prints, records, and/or tapes) are kept for reading, reference, and/or lending.
A hall in which public lectures, concerts, and similar programs are presented.
A place for artistic entertainment purposes that is established outdoors.
A distinctive type of museum exhibiting its collections out-of-doors.
dominio.aliases: Skansen, Living Farm Museum, Living Museum, Folk Museum

dominio.definicion: An enclosure or structure adapted or prepared for keeping animals under conditions approximating to the natural conditions, for observation or study; especially an aquarium or a terrarium.
An indoor sport facility.
A swimming pool inside a buidling with attached facilities (for example: changing rooms).

definicion: Additional or secondary names applied to a specific cultural group.
descripcion: May include its name(s) in other languages.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: A description of particular rites, customs, and/or traditions of a cultural group within an area.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The fraction of the total population consisting of members of a specific cultural group, within an area.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A scaled dimensionless measure denoting one part in every hundred.

definicion: A general name that may be applied to several cultural groups within an area, where they may be meaningfully combined on the basis of common cultural elements.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The name of the head of the cultural group within an area.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The name ascribed to a cultural or ethnic group with an established common behavioural context within an area.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The form of rule imposed on a people by the person or group wielding power or authority over that people.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a culture rule structure.

dominio.definicion: Non-hierarchical or akephali societies are organised in an egalitarian way; authority is not wielded by specific persons or institutions, and possession is limited in time and shared out between families, hordes, lineage groups, and other forms of cooperation.
dominio.observaciones: In concrete situations, individuals may take on leadership functions that are not tied to sanctioning forms (for example: monopoly on the use of force, duties and taxes).

dominio.definicion: The social status depends on prestige and power positions; wealth is not a decisive factor.
Social stratification related to the hierarchical ranking of different social groups within a society or nation.
dominio.observaciones: The underlying reasons for social inequity are not based on age, sex, family, and lineage, but on the different opportunities to get access to the socially relevant goods and objectives, for example: prestige, status, power, possessions, wealth, and education. Castes and classes are examples of stratified societies.

dominio.definicion: The existence of a central authority with the monopoly on the legitimate use of force within an existing territory.
dominio.observaciones: Modern states define themselves through desacralisation, depersonalisation, and increasing bureaucratisation of authority and power. A typical feature is the formal strengthening of the rights and obligations of the individual, irrespective of his/her integration into local, religious, family-related and other loyalties and networks that were often of importance under the law in the pre-modern state.

definicion: A description of the ruling structure in an area.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that has no restrictions on lexicality or length.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a character string. For example: Golden Gate Bridge.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of a culvert based on its shape and fill.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a culvert type.

dominio.definicion: Arch-shaped in which a significant dead load of soil overlies the culvert and dominates the total loading.
dominio.observaciones: The actual cross-section may be circular, arch, or elliptical.

dominio.definicion: Box-shaped in which a significant dead load of soil overlies the culvert and generally dominates the total loading.
Box-shaped in which the live traffic load is essentially directly applied to the culvert, there being no soil back-fill.
dominio.observaciones: May be either precast or cast-in-place. There may be a thin overlying soil burden.

definicion: The total cumulative length of track contained within the confines of the feature, exclusive of the branch or main trunk lines running into and/or out of the feature.

definicion: The type of horizontal movement of a body of water based on the mechanism(s) causing the flow.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a current type category.

dominio.definicion: The horizontal movement of water associated with falling tide.
dominio.observaciones: Ebb streams generally set seaward, or in the opposite direction to the tide progression.

dominio.definicion: The horizontal movement of water associated with the rising tide.
dominio.observaciones: Flood streams generally set towards the shore, or in the direction of the tide progression.

dominio.definicion: The flow of water from a river or its estuary to the sea.
dominio.observaciones: In general, water movement in the general direction of drainage in the non-tidal portion of rivers.

dominio.definicion: A movement of ocean water characterized by regularity, either of a cyclic nature or as a continuous stream flowing along a definable path.
dominio.observaciones: Generally, the combination of tidal stream and current, the whole water movement in an oceanic context.

dominio.definicion: The return flow of water piled up on the shore by incoming waves and wind.
dominio.observaciones: Longshore currents feed into rip currents.

dominio.definicion: A current paralleling the shore largely within the surf zone.
dominio.observaciones: It is caused by the excess water brought to the zone by the small net mass transport of wind waves. Longshore currents feed into rip currents.

dominio.definicion: The flow of water along a river bed on the ocean floor.
The horizontal movement of water associated with the tide.

definicion: The angle between the angle of orientation of the entry point and the angle of orientation of the exit point.

datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of an angle in two dimensions (the angle between two half-lines terminating at the same point).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of plane angle equal to pi/180, approximately 0.01745532925199433 radians.

definicion: The radius of curvature of a segment of a feature (or the feature as a whole, if applicable).
descripcion: Typically the smallest radius of a curved feature with more than one radius will be collected.

dominio.definicion: A dam on a watercourse that is not bypassed by locks.
dominio.observaciones: Portage is required for boats to bypass the dam. It may serve, for example, as a source of water for a canal or mill.

dominio.definicion: A large dam that ensures that a waterway is navigable by ensuring sufficient upriver channel depth and that is bypassed by one or more locks.
dominio.observaciones: Typically more than 15 metres tall, navigation dams normally permit water flow by means of spillways or gates with roller and tainter gates being the most commonly installed. Most navigation pools in the United States are maintained at a constant minimum water depth of 3 metres (9 feet). The installation of navigation dams permit river vessels to use a series of locks to 'step' up or down a river from one water level to another.

dominio.definicion: A dam whose reservoir is regulated to accomplish flood control.
dominio.observaciones: It may also provide a source of water for irrigation and/or hydroelectric power. For example, the Grand Coulee Dam.

dominio.definicion: A dam which is intended to produce electrical power from the potential energy of dammed water driving a water turbine and generator.
dominio.observaciones: To boost the power generation capabilities of a dam, the water may be run through a large pipe called a penstock before the turbine. A variant on this simple model uses pumped storage hydroelectricity to produce electricity to match periods of high and low water.

dominio.definicion: A small overflow-type dam commonly used to raise the upstream water level of a river or stream.
dominio.observaciones: Typically less than 15 metres tall, water flows over the top of a weir although some weirs have sluice gates which release water at a level below the top of the weir. The crest of an overflow spillway on a large dam is often called a weir. Weirs have traditionally been used to create mill ponds or to provide adequate water supply to maintain levels in an adjacent canal. Weirs may be associated with locks to permit the passage of boats around the weir.

definicion: The direction of traffic flow.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a direction of traffic flow.

dominio.definicion: Traffic is allowed in both directions.
Traffic is only allowed in the direction of the feature.
Traffic is only allowed in the opposite direction of the feature.
Traffic is not allowed in any direction.

definicion: The side(s) of a feature that produce the greatest visual significance and/or reflectivity potential.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a directivity.

dominio.definicion: Visually significant or reflective from one side only.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a cliff.

dominio.definicion: Visually significant or reflective from two sides.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a metal fence.

dominio.definicion: Visually significant or reflective from any direction.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a metal tower.

dominio.definicion: Visually significant or reflective from the right side only.
dominio.observaciones: The right side is determined by following the linear component from the westmost node (southmost if the feature follows a meridian of longitude).

dominio.definicion: Visually significant or reflective from the left side only.
dominio.observaciones: The left side is determined by following the linear component from the westmost node (southmost if the feature follows a meridian of longitude).

definicion: A characterization of the degree of localization of a disease within an area, as a category.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a disease localization.

dominio.definicion: Remaining in the close surroundings of the place of outbreak.
Extending far from the surroundings of the place of outbreak.
Widely epidemic, affecting an entire country or the entire world.

definicion: The type of organism (usually an animal or human) that serves as the permanent host of a parasitic organism, virus and/or bacterium, and in which it lives and multiplies.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a disease reservoir type.

dominio.definicion: Any of a number of burrowing edentate mammals native to South and Central America, which have bodies encased in bony plates and are able to roll themselves into a ball when threatened.
A member of the order Chiroptera of mainly nocturnal flying mammals which have forelimbs modified to support membranous wings extending to the tail.
A feathered, warm-blooded, amniote animal of the vertebrate class Aves, characterized by modification of the forelimbs as wings for flight, oviparous reproduction, and care for the young.
Domesticated animal, especially oxen and cows.
A domesticated quadruped of numerous breeds classed together as Canis familiaris, derived from crossing of various species, bred as a pet or for special ranges of use.
A hairy, horned and bearded domesticated ruminant belonging to the genus Capra.
Any of various spiny nocturnal insectivorous mammals of the family Erinaceidae (especially the western European Erinaceus europaeus), noted for the ability to roll up into a ball when alarmed.
An animal, especially a mammal, that feeds naturally on plants and is kept or dealt in for use or profit.
A solid-hoofed quadruped with mane and tail of long coarse hair, domesticated for the sake of pack or draught animal as well as for sports.
Of, pertaining to, or characteristic of humankind or people; belonging to humankind; of or belonging to the species.

Any of numerous primates of a group including the families Cebidae (including capuchins and howler monkeys), Callitricidae (including marmosets and tamarins), and Cercopithecidae (including baboons, macaques, and colobuses), especially any of the long-tailed kinds.

Any of various small or medium-sized marsupial mammals, mostly arboreal, of the mainly neotropical family Didelphidae, which have an opposable thumb on the hind foot and a usually prehensile and hairless tail; especially (more fully Virginian opossum) the common North American species, Didelphis virginiana, which is the size of a cat.
A swine, domesticated for the sake of its flesh and skin.
Domestic fowl, including barn-door fowls, geese, ducks, and turkeys, that are used for their flesh, eggs and/or feathers.
Any of various gregarious burrowing plant-eating mammals of the family Leporidae (order Lagomorpha), with long ears (but not as long as a hare's) and a short stumpy tail.
Order of mammals also known as rodents, characterised by two continuously growing incisors in the upper and lower jaws which must be kept short by gnawing.
A gregarious ruminant animal, especially the domesticated Ovis aries, reared for the sake of its flesh and wool.
The material comprising the thin top layer of much of the Earth's land surface, composed of fragmented rock particles with humus, water, and air.
Any of various slender agile seed-eating arboreal rodents having a long bushy tail and furry coat, chiefly of the genus Sciurus and related genera, noted for hoarding nuts for food in winter.

definicion: The type of transmission or vector that is used to infect humans with a disease.
descripcion: A vector is an organism (often an insect or tick) that carries a parasite/virus/bacterium from one host to another.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a disease transmission type.

dominio.definicion: Many flying insects in the families Culicidae, Tabanidae, Glossinidae, Psychodidae.
dominio.observaciones: Examples of diseases transmitted: Malaria, St. Louis empcephalitis, Dengue fever, Yellow Fever and West Nile virus, Sleeping Sickness, Leishmaniasis, Rift Valley Fever.

dominio.definicion: Many crawling insects and ticks of the families Reduviidae, Pulicidae and Ixodidae.
dominio.observaciones: Examples of diseases transmitted: Plague, Chagas Disease, Tick-borne Encephalitis, Lyme Disease, Relapsing Fever, Crim-Congo-Haemorrhagic Fever.

dominio.definicion: General for minute solid particles with diameters less than 20 thou (500 micrometers).
dominio.observaciones: Examples of diseases transmitted: Tuberculosis, Q-Fever.

dominio.definicion: Order of mammals also known as rodents, characterised by two continuously growing incisors in the upper and lower jaws which must be kept short by gnawing.
dominio.observaciones: Examples of diseases transmitted: Hanta Virus, Leptospirosis, Lassa Fever.

dominio.definicion: A class of vertebrate animals whose name is derived from their distinctive feature, mammary glands, with which they feed their young; they are also characterized by the possession of sweat glands, hair, three middle ear bones used in hearing, and a neocortex region in the brain.
dominio.observaciones: Examples of diseases transmitted: Rabies, Q-Fever.

dominio.definicion: All kinds of eatables or drinks.
dominio.observaciones: Examples of diseases transmitted: Vast numbers of pathogens including Brucellosis, Hepatitis A, Cholera, some Helminths, Norovirus, Amoebiasis, Lambliasis and many more.

dominio.definicion: All kinds of fluids that occure naturally in the body of humans.
dominio.observaciones: Examples of diseases transmitted: Hepatitis B and C, Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), Marburg Virus, Ebola.

dominio.definicion: A suspension of fine solid particles exhalated or coughed by humans.
dominio.observaciones: Examples of diseases transmitted: Measles, Influenza, Pneumonic plague, Mumps, Rubella, Tuberculosis, Meningococcal disease.

definicion: The distance from the runway end to that point of the runway that is usable for landing.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: An indication that the terrain surface is divided into relatively small areas of varying elevation resulting in high local relief.
descripcion: Typically formed by the dissection of a once flat plateau or plain by erosion but may also be caused by artificial means (for example: construction).

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The distance from the DME antenna to the position where the zero range indication occurs in the DME receiver.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The particular spectrum characteristics or accuracy of Ultra High Frequency (UHF) Distance Measuring Equipment (DME), as a category.
descripcion: For example: DME/N, DME/W, or DME/P.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a distance measuring equipment type.

dominio.definicion: A DME with narrow spectrum characteristics.
A DME with improved accuracy compared to the DME/N.
A DME with wide spectrum characteristics.

dominio.definicion: Serves to distribute irrigation water.

definicion: An indication that the lanes or tracks in a land transportation route (for example: a road or a railway), are horizontally separated (for example: by a median strip) and not adjoining.
descripcion: May be used to indicate the separation of opposing flows of traffic in order to improve safety or to meet route engineering restrictions by some means. For example, the two travelled ways of a divided highway may pass at different elevations along the side of a mountain or may diverge when passing around significant engineering obstacles (for example: rocky outcrops).

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

dominio.definicion: A dredge located on a floating structure.
dominio.observaciones: Includes, for example, the dipper and hopper types.

dominio.definicion: A mechanical dredge consisting of a scoop that swings on a chain from a movable jib; the scoop is cast into the material to be excavated and dragged back to the jib where it is lifted and dumped; the material excavated is placed in scows or hopper barges that are towed to the disposal area.
dominio.observaciones: The crane may mounted on a flat-bottomed barge, on fixed-shore installations, or on a crawler mount. Different types of buckets (for example: the clamshell, orangepeel, and dragline types) can fulfill various types of dredging requirements and can be quickly changed to suit the operational requirements. The vessel can be positioned and moved within a limited area using only anchors; however, in most cases anchors and spuds are used to position and move bucket dredges. Bucket dredges range in capacity from 1 to 12 cubic yard. Twenty to thirty cycles per hour is typical, but large variations exist in production rates because of the variability in depths and materials being excavated. The effective working depth is limited to about 100 feet.

dominio.definicion: A mechanical dredging-boat with a single bucket at the end of an arm; the material excavated is placed in scows or hopper barges that are towed to the disposal area.
dominio.observaciones: The dipper dredge is basically a barge-mounted power shovel. It is equipped with a power-driven ladder structure and operated from a barge-type hull. A bucket is firmly attached to the ladder structure and is forcibly thrust into the material to be removed. To increase digging power, the dredge barge is moored on powered spuds that transfer the weight of the forward section of the dredge to the bottom. Dipper dredges normally have a bucket capacity of 8 to 12 cubic yard and a working depth of up to 50 feet. There is a great variability in production rates, but 30 to 60 cycles per hour is routinely achieved.

dominio.definicion: A hydraulic dredge that is self-propelled, stores dredged material onboard, transports it to the disposal area, and then dumps it.
dominio.observaciones: Hopper dredges are limited to work in deep waters, and they cannot dredge continuously. Direct pumpout is a common method of removing dredged material from hopper dredges. The dredge moors to a structure, buoy, or multiple buoy berth. Hoses connected to a pipeline extending to shore are attached to the hopper dredge discharge manifold. The dredge mixes the dredged material with water to form a slurry and pumps the slurry from its discharge manifold through the hoses and pipeline to a designated discharge location.

dominio.definicion: A hydraulic dredge that is is equipped with a cutter with teeth that continuously churns up the material while sediment and water is suctioned up a long tube and pumped directly to a disposal site.
dominio.observaciones: Advantages of cutterhead pipeline dredges include their ability to excavate most materials, to pump directly to a disposal site, to dredge almost continuously, and to dredge some types of rock without blasting.

definicion: The magnitude of the earthquake.
descripcion: Magnitude, a logarithmic measure of the 'size' of an earthquake, is related to the energy released as seismic waves at the focus of an earthquake. Although the magnitude scale has neither maximum nor minimum values, the highest magnitude known is about 9.5 and the lowest about -3.0. On this logarithmic scale, a magnitude 6.0 shallow-focus earthquake represents elastic-wave energy about 30 times larger than that generated by a magnitude 5.0 earthquake, and 900 times (30x30) larger than that of a magnitude 4.0 shock.
