definicion: The type(s) of medical services provided by the facility.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a medical services.

dominio.definicion: A medical facility specialising in acute care of patients who present without prior appointment, either by their own means or by ambulance.
dominio.observaciones: This facility is usually found in a hospital or other primary care centre, and would usually be found in a deployed Medical Treatment Facility (ref. AJP-4.10(A)).

dominio.definicion: A specialisation concerning life support and pain relief normally associated with surgical capability.
dominio.observaciones: Anaesthetics is normally found at all hospitals and Medical Treatment Facilities (ref. AJP-4.10(A)) with a surgical capability.

dominio.definicion: A medical specialisation dealing with the treatment and care of patients with a condition relating to the heart.
dominio.observaciones: Usually found in general hospitals, but unlikely to be found on deployed military operations in most circumstances.

dominio.definicion: A medical specialisation concerned with the diagnosis and management of life threatening conditions requiring sophisticated organ support and persistent monitoring.
dominio.observaciones: Critical care is normally found in general hospitals or in a Role 2 Light Manoeuvre and above (ref. AJP-4.10(A)) Medical Treatment Facility.

dominio.definicion: The technique and process used to create images of the human body, or parts of the body, and their function in order to reveal, diagnose or examine disease, or to study anatomy and physiology.
dominio.observaciones: For example this may include radiography and other forms of medical imaging such as MRI and CAT scanners. Diagnostic imaging is usually found at all hospitals with a surgical capability and would be found to some degree in all deployed Medical Treatment Facilities (ref. AJP-4.10(A)).

dominio.definicion: The medical practice and surgery that specialises in the diagnosis and treatment of ear, nose, throat, head and neck disorders.
dominio.observaciones: Also known as ENT or otolaryngology. Normally found in all hospitals and Medical Treatment Facilities (ref. AJP-4.10(A)) with a surgical capability.

dominio.definicion: General surgery is practiced by a surgeon widely experienced in all forms of surgery, and may normally be found at all hospitals, with widespread use by the military.
A specialised department, normally found at all hospitals, dealing with the health of the female reproductive system (uterus, vagina and ovaries).
A specialised department normally found in general hositals or specialist maternity hospitals dealing with pre- and postnatal care.

A medical speciality dealing with disorders of the nervous system, including diagnosis and treatment of all categories of disease involving the central, peripheral and autonomic nervous systems, including their coverings, blood vessels and all effector tissue, such as muscle.
dominio.observaciones: It may be found in many general hospitals and is also being increasingly recognised as an important element in the medical order of battle for deployed operations.

dominio.definicion: The branch of medicine that deals with tumours (cancer).
dominio.observaciones: This includes diagnosis, therapy, follow-up of cancer patients after treatment, palliative care and screening. Normally found in larger hospitals.

dominio.definicion: The branch of medicine dealing with the anatomy, physiology and diseases of the eye and eye-related conditions.
dominio.observaciones: Normally found in general hospitals.

dominio.definicion: The branch of surgery concerned with conditions involving the musculoskeletal system.
dominio.observaciones: Orthopaedic surgeons use both surgical and nonsurgical means to treat musculoskeletal trauma, tumours and congenital disorders. Normally found in all hospitals with surgical capability. Orthopaedics is of significant interest to military medical forces given their responsibility for force health protection.

dominio.definicion: Pharmacy includes the funtions of compounding and dispensing medications, as well as clinical services, reviewing medication for safety and efficacy and providing drug information.
dominio.observaciones: Normally widely available to the population and not limited to medical facilities. In a military context pharmacy is also normally responsible for many apsects of medical logistics.

dominio.definicion: A medical specialisation concerned with the care and treatment of all disease and conditions relating to the genitourinary system.
dominio.observaciones: Normally found in general hospitals and at specialised clinics.

dominio.definicion: That element relating to the prevention of, identification, care and treatment of disease and conditions relating to sexual activity.
dominio.observaciones: Normally found in general hospitals and at specialised clinics.

dominio.definicion: The branch of internal medicine, physiology, pathology, clinical laboratory work and pediatrics concerned with the study of blood, the blood-forming organs and blood diseases.
dominio.observaciones: It includes the study of etiology, diagnosis, treatment, prognosis and prevention of blood diseases. Normally found in general hospitals.

dominio.definicion: Physiotherapy is concerned with identifying and maximising quality of life and movement potential through promotion, prevention, diagnosis, treatment, intervention and/or rehabilitation.
dominio.observaciones: Normally widespread in both primary and secondary care. Physiotherapy is of significant military interest for maintaining fighting fitness in a force.

dominio.definicion: The interpretation and communication of the science of nutrition to enable people to make informed and practical choices about food and lifestyle, in both health and disease.
dominio.observaciones: Dietetics departments are normally found in general hosptials or provided by visiting professionals to the general population.

dominio.definicion: A specialisation concerned with preventing diseases and conditions that may arise as a result of environmental threats to health caused by such elements as temperature, humidity, animal and insect threats.
dominio.observaciones: Widely deployed on military operations and throughout the health care system of developed nations. It is of critical importance to force health protection and reduction of Disease and Non-Battle Injuries (DNBI).

dominio.definicion: A cache or bank of blood or blood components, gathered as a result of blood donation, stored and preserved for later use in blood transfusion.
dominio.observaciones: It is typically a division of a hospital laboratory where the storage of blood products occurs and where proper testing is performed to reduce the risk of transfusion related events. A blood bank is an essential element of support to military operations.

dominio.definicion: The branch of medicine dealing with all forms of conditions, diseases and treatment effecting young children.
dominio.observaciones: Normally found in general hospitals. Paediatrics is a specialisation not normally found within NATO medical forces.

dominio.definicion: A medical specialisation concerned with the diagnosis, care and treatment resulting from disorders effecting mental stability.
dominio.observaciones: Normally found in general hospitals, and included within the medical order of battle for operations. Psychiatric screening is an increasingly important element of aftercare provided to troops returning from operations.

dominio.definicion: A specialised department normally found in larger regional hospitals for the care of burns victims, usually capable of providing lengthy and specialised care.
dominio.observaciones: In a military context victims would be most likely to receive stabilising care and be quickly sent back to their home nation by strategic aeromedical evacuation (STRATEVAC).

dominio.definicion: The medical practice of treating acute and chronic illness and providing preventive care and health education for all ages and sexes.
dominio.observaciones: This includes the particular skill of treating patients with multiple health issues and comorbidities. General practice is normally found at various kinds of medical facilities and would be widely available to the populace. It is also widely deployed on military operations.

dominio.definicion: Those services which support the medical and surgical care of patients within any medical facility.
dominio.observaciones: For example this may include medical stores, or a medical laboratory. Clinical services are normally found at all hospitals and Medical Treatment Facilities (ref. AJP-4.10(A)) with a surgical capability.

definicion: A narrative or other textual description that records observation(s) and/or event(s) associated with a particular subject (for example: a data instance, a data set or a data processing activity).
descripcion: No restriction is placed on its length.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of a memorandum based on the nature of the information recorded and/or its intended use.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a memorandum type.

dominio.definicion: The memorandum records information that is generally applicable.
The memorandum records information specifically related to aeronautical Safety of Navigation (SON).
dominio.observaciones: For example, provides additional information concerning routes, aerodrome approach procedures, or NAVAIDS.

dominio.definicion: The memorandum records information specifically related to maritime Safety of Navigation (SON).
dominio.observaciones: For example, provides additional information concerning obstructions, hazards, or NAVAIDS.

dominio.definicion: The memorandum records information specifically related to land Safety of Navigation (SON).
dominio.observaciones: For example, provides additional information concerning favorable routes, road construction, or signage.

dominio.definicion: The memorandum records information specifically related to geographic naming.
dominio.observaciones: For example, provides additional information concerning the scope of application and/or use of one or more geographic name(s).

definicion: A narrative description that records information pertinent to a message (for example: what, where, or why).
descripcion: No restriction is placed on its length.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The authority that determined that an active message could be cancelled (for example: due to the determination that a threat no longer existed).

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that contains only non-lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The date that a message was originally transmitted or subsequently updated with additional information.

datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a message date active.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.2.1.1, Basic format, as a single numeric data element comprising eight digits, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, and [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, as 'YYYYMMDD' (for example: '19850412' for 12 April 1985).

definicion: The sequence number of a message within the Gregorian calendar year in which the message was sent.

datatype.definicion: An integer domain value that is restricted to be non-negative.
datatype.nota: The realization of this integer datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A dimensionless physical quantity, one which has no unit of measure.

definicion: The type of an ore mineral from which metal may be profitably extracted.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a metallic ore type.

dominio.definicion: Material from which antimony of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Antimony minerals of economic value: the most important source of antimony is stibnite (antimony sulfide).

dominio.definicion: Material from which bismuth of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Bismuth minerals of economic value: The most important ores of bismuth are bismuthinite (bismuth sulfide) and bismite (bismuth oxide).

dominio.definicion: Material from which caesium of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Caesium minerals of economic value: lepidolite, pollucite (hydrated silicate of aluminium and caesium).

dominio.definicion: Material from which chrome of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Chrome minerals of economic value: chromite (iron magnesium chromium oxide).

dominio.definicion: Material from which cobalt of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Cobalt minerals of economic value: The main ores of cobalt are cobaltite (cobalt, iron, arsenic sulfide), erythrite (hydrated cobalt arsenate), glaucodot (cobalt iron arsenic sulfide), and skutterudite (cobalt arsenide).

dominio.definicion: Material from which copper of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Copper minerals of economic value: the most common source of copper ore is the mineral chalcopyrite (copper iron sulfide).

dominio.definicion: Material from which iron of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Iron minerals of economic value: iron oxides hematite and magnetite.

dominio.definicion: Material from which lead of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Lead minerals of economic value: The main lead mineral is galena (lead sulfide).

dominio.definicion: Material from which lithium of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Lithium minerals of economic value: Some lithium is recovered from the mineral spodumene (lithium aluminium inosilicate) and as secondary product from lepidolite (hydrated silicate of aluminium and caesium). Most lithium is recovered from brine, or water.

dominio.definicion: Material from which manganese of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Manganese minerals of economic value: the principal ore mineral is pyrolusite (manganese dioxide). Manganese is also obtained from manganese nodules, that are rock concretions on the sea bottom formed of concentric layers of iron and manganese hydroxides.

dominio.definicion: Material from which mercury of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Mercury minerals of economic value: cinnabar (mercury sulfide) is the most common ore.

dominio.definicion: Material from which molybdenum of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Molybdenum minerals of economic value: the main commercial source of molybdenum is molybdenite (molybdenum disulfide).

dominio.definicion: Material from which nickel of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Nickel minerals of economic value: limonite (hydrated iron oxide-hydroxide), garnierite (hydrous nickel silicate) and pentlandite (iron-nickel sulfide).

dominio.definicion: Material from which niobium of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Niobium minerals of economic value: The main primary source of niobium is niobit (iron manganese niobium tantalum oxide). Coltan is the colloquial African name for columbite-tantalite, a metallic ore used to produce the elements niobium and tantalum.

dominio.definicion: Material from which tantalum of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Tantalum minerals of economic value: The main primary source of tantalum is tantalite (iron manganese tantalum niobium oxide). Coltan is the colloquial African name for columbite-tantalite, a metallic ore used to produce the elements niobium and tantalum.

dominio.definicion: Material from which tin of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Tin minerals of economic value: The only mineral of commercial importance as a source of tin is cassiterite (tin dioxide).

dominio.definicion: Material from which titanium of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Titanium minerals of economic value: rutile (titanium dioxide) and ilmenite (iron titanium oxide).

dominio.definicion: Material from which tungsten of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Tungsten minerals of economic value: wolframite (iron-manganese tungstate) and scheelite (calcium tungstate).

dominio.definicion: Material from which uranium of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: The major primary ore mineral is uraninite (uranium oxide), though a range of other uranium minerals is found in particular deposits.

dominio.definicion: Material from which vanadium of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Vanadium minerals of economic value: There is no single mineral ore from which vanadium is recovered. Vanadium is found as a trace element in a number of different rock materials and is a by-product of other mining operations.

dominio.definicion: Material from which zinc of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Zinc minerals of economic value: sphalerite (zinc sulfide), smithsonite (zinc carbonate), hemimorphite (zinc silicate), and franklinite (a zinc spinel).

dominio.definicion: Material from which beryllium of economic value can be extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Beryllium minerals of economic value: Bertrandite (beryllium aluminium silicate), Beryl (beryllium aluminium silicate).

dominio.definicion: A dull black metallic ore from which the elements niobium (formerly "columbium") and tantalum are extracted.
dominio.observaciones: Coltan is the industrial name for columbite-tantalite.

descripcion: The MLS angle and data functions shall operate on any one of the 200 channels assigned in the frequencies from 5031.0 to 5090.7 megahertz (MHz) as shown in ICAO Annex 10, Chapter 3, Table A.

nombre: Microwave Landing System (MLS) Elevation Angle Accuracy
definicion: The accuracy of the scanning beam being transmitted by the Microwave Landing System (MLS) elevation ground substation, as compared to the published elevation angle.
descripcion: Angle accuracy may be affected by multiple factors, including the local physical environment, beam point errors, antenna alignment, and antenna field patterns in the scanning plane. All of these can yield false guidance unless appropriately compensated for in the design, construction, and/or implementation of the MLS.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value that is restricted to be non-negative.
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of an angle in two dimensions (the angle between two half-lines terminating at the same point).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of plane angle equal to pi/180, approximately 0.01745532925199433 radians.

definicion: The reason(s) for the movement of groups of people from their homeland.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a migration reason.

dominio.definicion: A lack of available work or available welfare which permits the securing the material needs.
dominio.observaciones: For example. search for work.

dominio.definicion: A misfortune endangering human life.
dominio.observaciones: For example: famine or epidemic disease.

dominio.definicion: A ruinous impact on the environment.
dominio.observaciones: For example: volcanic eruption or earthquake.

dominio.definicion: A lack of perceived peace and freedom.
dominio.observaciones: For example: war, armed conflict, or riots.

dominio.definicion: A lack of the right to the free practice of one's religion.
All reasons related to the persecution of a cultural group.
dominio.observaciones: For example: racism or discrimination.

definicion: The type(s) of transport used during a migration movement.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a migration transport type.

dominio.definicion: Collective term for all types of flying machines.
Any animal upon which people may ride.
dominio.observaciones: For example: a horse, a camel, or an ass.

dominio.definicion: Any type of carriage drawn by animals.
A motor vehicle providing a means of transport for more than six persons on average.
A motor vehicle used for heavy loads.
On foot due to no other means of transport available.
A motor vehicle providing a means of transport for less than or equal to six persons on average.
A series of railway carriages drawn by an engine.
Collective term for all types of boats.
A two-wheeled velocipede, with the wheels one behind the other, and usually with a seat for the rider.

definicion: The density of mine-like sonar echoes (MILEC) per square mile.
descripcion: Reference NATO Publication ATP 24(c) Vol 1.

21-40 MILEC per square nautical mile.
41-70 MILEC per square nautical mile.
71 MILEC per square nautical mile, or more.

definicion: The main operational function of a military aerodrome.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a military aerodrome function.

dominio.definicion: A deployed operating base (DOB) is a secured forward military position, used for an extended period of time to support temporarily deployed forces, supported by a main operating base (MOB).
A main operating base (MOB) is a permanently manned, well protected base, used to support permanently deployed forces.
dominio.observaciones: It has usually robust sea and/or air access.

definicion: Information describing a bridge, typically one that is subject to preplanned military interdiction.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is 255 characters in maximum length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The category(ies) of environmental hazards present in a region that affect military operations.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a military environmental hazard category.

dominio.definicion: Disease-causing organisms (pathogens), toxins, or other agents of biological origin (ABO) intended to: incapacitate, injure, or kill humans and animals; to destroy crops; to weaken resistance to attack; and to reduce the will to fight.
dominio.observaciones: A biological agent is a microorganism that causes disease in personnel, plants, or animals, or cause the deterioration of material.

dominio.definicion: The deposit, absorption, or adsorption of chemical agents on or by structures, areas, personnel, or objects.
dominio.observaciones: A chemical agent is a substance that is intended to kill, seriously injure, or incapacitate through its physiological effects.

dominio.definicion: The emission of radiation, either directly from unstable atomic nuclei or as a consequence of a nuclear reaction.
dominio.observaciones: Radioactive contamination is typically the result of a loss of control of radioactive materials during the production or use of radioisotopes. This includes nuclear fallout (the distribution of radioactive contamination by a nuclear explosion). Radiological weapons ('dirty bombs') use conventional explosives to scatter powdered radioactive material over the area around the bomb's explosion.

dominio.definicion: The process of contamination by a rapid change in temperature.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the dumping of hot water into a normally cooler body of water (or vice versa) or the effect of steam pipes on the temperature of the surrounding environment (for example: frozen soil that thaws).

definicion: The type of a facility or building that is used for military purposes.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a military facility type.

dominio.definicion: A building or a facility devoted to the act or process of managing military forces or overseeing the conduct of military operations.
A site designated for the purpose of discharging firearms or detonating munitions.
A building or a facility used to house civilians that is typically large, unadorned, and intended for relatively temporary occupancy.
Used to house the families of military personnel.
Serves as an emplacement for one or more pieces of field artillery.
A building or a facility for storing arms and military equipment, especially one serving as headquarters for reserve personnel.
A building or place fortified for defensive or protective purposes.
dominio.observaciones: It is usually surrounded with a ditch, rampart, and parapet, and garrisoned with soldiers.

dominio.definicion: A detached fortified defensive building with loopholes.
dominio.observaciones: Usually constructed of timber or concrete.

dominio.definicion: A small circular fort with very thick walls, especially any of those erected in Britain as a coastal defence during the Napoleonic Wars.
dominio.observaciones: Usually includes a gun platform, ammunition magazine, and accommodations for a garrison.

dominio.definicion: An elevated enclosed building including one or more guardrooms.
A usually square or polygonal outwork or fieldwork, with little or no flanking defences.
A building or a facility used to house military personnel, which is typically large, unadorned, and intended for relatively temporary occupancy.
A relatively small building that is separate from but is located near a main building and whose military use has not been determined.
A building or a facility where long (usually more than one year) sentences for military misconduct may be served.
A large fortified building with thick walls that has been maintained in sufficient repair to serve a military function.
dominio.observaciones: Historically, usually dominates the surrounding region.

definicion: A location specified using the Military Grid Reference System (MGRS) in terms of a world-wide grid zone and square designation plus a metre-based coordinate pair within a given grid square.
descripcion: It is based on the use of the Universal Transverse Mercator map projection between 84 arc degrees north and 80 arc degrees south and the Universal Polar Stereographic map projection in the polar regions.

datatype.nombre: Military Grid Reference System Location Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a military grid reference system location.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: The world is generally divided into 6 arc degree by 8 arc degree geographic areas, each of which is given a unique identification, termed the 'Grid Zone Designation', encoded by a 3 character alphanumeric value (for example: '13H'). These areas are covered by a pattern of 100,000-metre squares, with each square identified by a 2-character alphabetic value (for example: 'AA') that is unique within the grid zone. Within a square the location is designated by a 5-digit metre-based offset eastwards followed by a 5-digit metre-based offset northwards, from the southwest corner of the square (for example: '0015502350'). The location within the square may be truncated to lesser precision, resulting in either a 10-digit offset (full 1 metre precision) or an 8-digit, 6-digit, 4-digit, or 2-digit (10 kilometre precision) offset. See DMA Technical Manual 8358.1 'Datums, Ellipsoids, Grids, and Grid Reference Systems' for the method of calculation.

definicion: The minimum decision height or decision altitude for use by the military for certain instrument landing procedures.

definicion: The type of a military restriction zone based on its intended use.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a military restriction zone type.

dominio.definicion: A large military used area for training and exercise purposes which avoids settlement areas.
An area for testing of weapons, ammunition and equipment for military purposes.
An area for training and exercises involving the firing of various weapons.
Any other area restricted for military use only.
A small area located adjacent to or within a garrison which is used for military training and exercise purposes.
An area located adjacent to or within a garrison that consists of buildings and/or other facilities which are used for training and exercise in the firing of weapons.
An area used for the storage of military equipment.

definicion: The military classification of a route based on the responsible level of command.
descripcion: For example, ISAF is classifying a route as theatre controlled, provincial controlled or regional controlled.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of activity associated with a military air route.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a military route use.

dominio.definicion: An air route established for the conduct of military night low altitude training.
An air route established for the strategic movement of military forces.
An air route established for the conduct of military training, within which IFR or VFR flights may operate and that may be established in controlled and/or uncontrolled airspace.

definicion: The branch of the armed forces of a nation.
descripcion: May also be applied to similar organizations following military discipline (for example: a coastguard).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a military service branch.

dominio.definicion: The branch of a country's armed forces which conducts operations primarily by means of aircraft.
The branch of a country's armed forces which conducts operations on land.
A naval force employed to guard the coast, and often responsible for the safety, order, and operation of marine traffic in neighbouring waters.
A body of soldiers trained to serve at sea, or on shore under specified circumstances.
The branch of a country's armed forces which conducts operations at sea and/or using sea-based capabilities, including both ships and ship-based aircraft.
dominio.observaciones: Navy operations are supported by land-based capabilities including ports and maintenance systems typically also belonging to the Navy.

dominio.definicion: An organization in which elements of two or more military departments (for example: a navy and an air force) participate.
A military reserve force which conducts operations primarily by means of aircraft.
dominio.observaciones: A military reserve force is a military organization composed of residents of a country who combine a military role or career with a civilian career. They are not normally kept under arms and their main role is to be available to fight when a nation mobilizes for total war or to defend against invasion. Military reserve forces may be employed in non-military settings (for example: disaster relief).

dominio.definicion: A military reserve force equipped to fight on land.
dominio.observaciones: A military reserve force is a military organization composed of residents of a country who combine a military role or career with a civilian career. They are not normally kept under arms and their main role is be available to fight when a nation mobilizes for total war or to defend against invasion. Military reserve forces may be employed in non-military settings (for example: disaster relief).

definicion: The type of a military training facility.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a military training facility type.

dominio.definicion: A tower to train climbing.
An area where new drivers are trained to drive a particular type of vehicle.
A tower for parachute training of individuals by ascending and simulating a parachute landing by jumping from it.
A sport ground consisting of a series of challenging physical obstacles that an individual or team must navigate through while usually being timed.
dominio.observaciones: Obstacle courses can include running, climbing, jumping, crawling and balancing elements with the aim of testing endurance; sometimes a course involves mental tests.

definicion: The frequency band(s) in which an explosive mine is sensitive.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine acoustic sensitivity.

dominio.definicion: Responds to low frequency signals.
dominio.observaciones: Generally below 15 hertz.

dominio.definicion: Responds to audio frequency signals.
dominio.observaciones: Generally between 15 hertz to 20,000 hertz.

dominio.definicion: Responds to high frequency signals.
dominio.observaciones: Generally above 20,000 hertz.

dominio.definicion: Responds to signals within multiple frequency ranges.

The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity by which events are compared in position and duration.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of time that is 60 minutes in duration, being 3600 seconds.

definicion: The allegiance of the force responsible for the creation and/or maintenance of an explosive mine.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine allegiance.

dominio.definicion: A military force positively identified as friendly.
A military force positively identified as hostile.
A military force that is not hostile or in any way supportive of only one belligerent force.

definicion: The type(s) of anti-hunting capability of a naval mine.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine anti-hunting capability.

dominio.definicion: Avoids acoustic detection by employing an anechoic coating.
Avoids detection through automatic case burial.
Avoids detection by possessing an irregularly-shaped case.
Avoids acoustic detection through manipulation of acoustic impedance.
Avoids acoustic detection by appearing acoustically transparent.
Avoids magnetic detection by possessing a non-metallic case.
Avoids detection by possessing and employing sonar decoys.

definicion: The type(s) of anti-recovery capability of a naval mine.
descripcion: Anti-recovery devices may be fitted to mines to prevent discovery of details of the mechanisms of new types of mine.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine anti-recovery capability.

dominio.definicion: A hydrostatic switch included in a mine that is set to fire the mine or to keep it live when it is lifted above its preset depth.
dominio.observaciones: Usually used in conjunction with a soluble plug to prevent actuation for a certain period after laying and/or until the mine has reached a certain depth.

dominio.definicion: A switch that may be fitted to cut out the mooring lever safety switch, which normally renders a moored mine safe on breaking adrift or being swept.
dominio.observaciones: Its purpose is to leave the mine fully armed whilst drifting and hence liable to detonation during recovery or on being washed ashore. The Hague Convention forbids the use of the drifting mine as a weapon, except for very short-term use.

dominio.definicion: A booby trap included in a mine to fire the main or an auxiliary charge when an attempt is made to open the mechanism chambers.
A device included in a mine to render it inoperative on expiration of a predetermined period after laying.
dominio.observaciones: The steriliser may be a device to short-out the mine's batteries, to fire the mine, or to flood the mine case.

dominio.definicion: A steriliser included in buoyant mines that floods the mine case after a preset time, rendering it inoperative.
A device fitted to a moored mine that causes the mine to sink should it for any reason rise and break the surface (watch).
dominio.observaciones: Activation of the anti-watching device prevents the position of the mine (or minefield) being disclosed.

definicion: The type(s) of anti-sweep wire capability of a naval mine.
descripcion: Moorings of mines (for example: chains, piano wire, rubber-covered manila line, and canvas fire hose) may be designed to not be cut cleanly or not cut at all by mechanical sweeps. These may cause the mine to hang up in the sweep wire, endangering the ship during recovery operations.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine anti-sweep wire capability.

dominio.definicion: Resists being swept by possessing a chain mooring.
Allows a sweep wire to pass through the mooring without parting the mine from its sinker.
Grapples the sweep wire when the mooring is cut.
Resists being swept by possessing a sweep-wire cutter.
Designed to actuate the mine on pressure from the sweep wire.
dominio.observaciones: Normally fitted to the upper end of the mine mooring.

definicion: The degree to which an explosive mine may be externally controlled or self-activated.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine autonomy type.

dominio.definicion: Controlled so that it may be disarmed for safe passage of friendly vessels.
dominio.observaciones: For example, connected by electric cable to a shore station. Attribute: 'Mine Control Method' may be used to characterize the control method.

dominio.definicion: Directly actuated by the presence of any vessel, whether friendly or enemy.
dominio.observaciones: Attribute: 'Mine Self-Actuation Method' may be used to characterize the self-actuation method.

definicion: The method of cableless control of an explosive mine.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine cableless control method.

definicion: The mass of an explosive mine charge.

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of the property of a body that causes it to have weight in a gravitational field.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "mass", defined as equal to the mass of the international prototype of the kilogram.

definicion: The method of control of an explosive mine.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine control method.

dominio.definicion: Controlled by signals sent along a cable (for example: electric), usually from a shore station.
Controlled by signals not requiring a cable for transmission.
dominio.observaciones: Attribute: 'Mine Cableless Control Method' may be used to characterize the cableless control method.

definicion: The magnetic sensitivity of an explosive mine.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine magnetic sensitivity.

dominio.definicion: Requires a relatively small magnitude of influence (as from a vessel, with weak magnetic signature) to actuate.
dominio.observaciones: Relatively easy for Mine Hunters to safely actuate with sweeping gear designed to influence mines.

dominio.definicion: Requires a relatively moderate magnitude of influence (as from a vessel, with medium strength magnetic signature) to actuate.
dominio.observaciones: Moderately difficult for Mine Hunters to safely actuate with sweeping gear designed to influence mines.

dominio.definicion: Requires a relatively large magnitude of influence (as from a vessel, with strong magnetic signature) to actuate.
dominio.observaciones: Difficult for Mine Hunters to safely actuate with sweeping gear designed to influence mines.

dominio.definicion: Requires a relatively very small magnitude of influence (as from a degaussed vessel) to actuate.
dominio.observaciones: Relatively very easy for Mine Hunters to safely actuate with sweeping gear designed to influence mines. Generally requires a relatively small magnitude of influence (as from a slow, small, quiet and degaussed vessel) to actuate.

dominio.definicion: Responds to the horizontal component of the magnetic field of a ship, submarine, or sweep.
Responds to the vertical component of the magnetic field of a ship, submarine, or sweep.
Responds to the total magnetic field of a ship, submarine, or sweep.

definicion: Specifies the method and/or pattern of placement of explosive mines.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine placement method.

dominio.definicion: Emplaced using a hand-held delivery system.
dominio.observaciones: The pattern may be regular or pseudo-random.

dominio.definicion: Remotely delivered by field artillery.
dominio.observaciones: The explosive mines are scattered randomly within a generally elliptical region determined by artillery bearing.

dominio.definicion: Remotely delivered by aircraft.
dominio.observaciones: The explosive mines are scattered randomly within a region determined by aircraft movement.

dominio.definicion: Laid mechanically by vehicle-mounted scattering systems.
dominio.observaciones: The explosive mines are generally laid in lines determined by vehicle movement.

dominio.definicion: Emplaced using a method and/or pattern not commonly used.
dominio.observaciones: The laydown is, for example, responsive to local terrain constraints and opportunities.

dominio.definicion: Emplaced by a specialized minelayer ship.
Emplaced by a helicopter.
Emplaced by a mine launcher.

definicion: The method of self-actuation of an explosive mine.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine self-actuation method.

dominio.definicion: Actuated through physical contact.
dominio.observaciones: Attribute: 'Contact Mine Actuation Method' may be used to characterize the contact method.

dominio.definicion: Actuated through proximity sensing based on pressure, magnetic, and/or acoustic sensing.
dominio.observaciones: Attribute: 'Influence Mine Actuation Method' may be used to characterize the influence method.

dominio.definicion: Actuated through remote sensing (for example: electric fields, cosmic rays, and/or lasers).
dominio.observaciones: Attribute: 'Remote Sensing Mine Actuation Method' may be used to characterize the remote sensing method.

definicion: The special capabilities of an explosive mine.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine special capability.

dominio.definicion: A device fitted in an explosive mine to prevent it being actuated for a preset time after laying.
A device in a naval mine that prevents detonation until a preset number of actuations has taken place.
A device included in an explosive mine so that it will be armed only at set times.
A sinker that holds a moored naval mine on the bottom for a pre-determined time after laying.
A naval mine-like device laid with the sole object of obstructing or damaging mechanical minesweeping vessels or equipment.
A device in an explosive mine that renders it permanently inoperative on expiration of a pre-determined time after laying.
A device fitted to a buoyant naval mine which, on operation after a preset time, floods its case and causes it to sink to the bottom.
A device fitted in a moored naval mine which causes it to sink should it 'watch' (become visible from the surface), so as to prevent the position of the mine or minefield being disclosed.
Any device incorporated in either the mooring of a naval mine or obstructer, or in the mine circuits to make the sweeping of the mine more difficult.
dominio.observaciones: Attribute: 'Mine Anti-Sweep Wire Capability' may be used to characterize the anti-sweep wire method.

dominio.definicion: Any device in an explosive mine designed to prevent an enemy discovering details of the working of the mine mechanism.
dominio.observaciones: Attribute: 'Mine Anti-Recovery Capability' may be used to characterize the antirecovery method.

dominio.definicion: Any device in a naval mine designed to prevent discovery (for example: using sonar arrays and/or magnetometers).
dominio.observaciones: Attribute: 'Mine Anti-Hunting Capability' may be used to characterize the antihunting method.

dominio.definicion: A device fitted in an influence explosive mine designed to prevent its actuation by shock (for example: local explosions caused by 'countermining').
Arranged to detonate the explosive mine to which it is attached, or to detonate another mine nearby, if the mine is disturbed.
A sinker that holds a moored or rising naval mine at the bottom and releases it when actuated by a suitable influence from a vessel.

definicion: An indication that a region has been swept for explosive mines.

definicion: The method used to specify the geometry of a minefield.

dominio.definicion: The perimeter of the minefield is specified.
The two endpoints of the minefield along the enemy side are specified.
dominio.observaciones: Typically used together with Attribute: 'Width'.

dominio.definicion: The two endpoints of the minefield along the friendly side are specified.
dominio.observaciones: Typically used together with Attribute: 'Width'.

dominio.definicion: An circle enclosing the minefield is specified by a center point and the radius.
dominio.observaciones: Typically used together with Attribute: 'Width' (twice the radius).

definicion: The classification of the profile of the sea bed from the perspective of minehunting.
descripcion: Reference NATO Publication ATP 24(c) Vol 1.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mine-hunting sea bed classification.

dominio.definicion: Very few craters, gullies, ridges or seaweed patches (5 percent of the area or less), sand ripples 15 centimetres high or less.
Large numbers of craters, gullies, ridges or seaweed patches (5 to 15 percent of the area), sand ripples 15 to 30 centimetres high.
Extensive areas (over 15 percent of the whole) of craters, gullies, ridges, or large sand ripples or closely spaced sandwaves.
Very extensive areas (over 50 percent of the whole) of craters, gullies, ridges or seaweed patches.

definicion: The status of determination of the nature of an object on or in the seabed or floating in the water volume.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a minehunting status.

dominio.definicion: The action of operating minehunting sensors (acoustic, optical or magnetic) to find objects on or in the seabed which distinguish themselves from the general structure of the bottom, or to find objects floating in the water volume.

The action of operating minehunting equipment to investigate detected contacts with the intention of discerning those which have properties (for example: size, shape, shadow, and/or structure) leading to the assumption that they may be mines.
The result of the operation of divers, underwater vehicles or other systems which permit a positive (specifically by sight or touch) identification of objects as explosive mines (or not).
dominio.observaciones: The identification thus results in a decision about the contact being a CERTMINE or a NONMINE.

definicion: The classification of an exploitable natural accumulation of mineral and/or rock based on their extractability.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mineral deposit classification.

dominio.definicion: That part of a mineral resource for which tonnage, densities, shape, physical characteristics, grade and mineral content can be estimated with a reasonable level of confidence.
dominio.observaciones: It is based on exploration, sampling and testing information gathered through appropriate techniques from locations such as outcrops, trenches, pits, workings and drill holes. The locations are too widely or inappropriately spaced to confirm geological and/or grade continuity.

dominio.definicion: That part of a mineral resource for which tonnage, grade and mineral content can be estimated with a low level of confidence.
dominio.observaciones: It is inferred from geological evidence and assumed but not verified geological and/or grade continuity. The Inferred category is intended to cover situations where a mineral concentration or occurrence has been identified and limited measurements and sampling completed, but where the data are insufficient to allow the geological and/or grade continuity to be verified.

dominio.definicion: That part of a mineral resource for which tonnage, densities, shape, physical characteristics, grade and mineral content can be estimated with a high level of confidence.
dominio.observaciones: It is based on detailed and reliable exploration, sampling and testing information gathered through appropriate techniques from locations such as outcrops, trenches, pits, workings and drill holes.

dominio.definicion: A concentration or occurrence of material (solid, liquid, or gaseous) of economic interest in or on the Earth's crust in such form and quantity and of such grade or quality that it has reasonable prospects for economic extraction.
dominio.observaciones: The location, quantity, grade, continuity and other geological characteristics of a Mineral Resource are known (Identified Resource), estimated or interpreted from specific geological evidence, sampling and knowledge.

dominio.definicion: The economically mineable part of a Measured Mineral Resource.
dominio.observaciones: These assessments demonstrate at the time of reporting that extraction is justified. A Proven Mineral Reserve represents the highest confidence category of reserve estimate.

dominio.definicion: A mineral occurrence that is uneconomic but still an anomalous concentration of material that are considered common ore/industrial minerals elsewhere.
dominio.observaciones: Materials that are too low grade or for other reasons are not considered potentially economic, in the same sense as the defined resource, may be recognized and their magnitude estimated, but they are not classified as resources.

dominio.definicion: The economically mineable part of an Indicated, and in some circumstances, a Measured Mineral Resource.
dominio.observaciones: These assessments demonstrate at the time of reporting that extraction could reasonably be justified. A Probable Mineral Reserve has a lower level of confidence than a Proved Mineral Reserve but is of sufficient quality to serve as the basis for a decision on the development of the deposit.

dominio.definicion: The economically mineable part of a Measured and/or Indicated Mineral Resource.
dominio.observaciones: Appropriate assessments and studies have been carried out, and include consideration of and modification by realistically assumed mining, metallurgical, economic, marketing, legal, environmental, social and governmental factors.

dominio.definicion: Unspecified body of economic material surmised to exist on the basis of broad (regional) geologic knowledge and theory.
dominio.observaciones: The existence of the resource is only postulated, comprising deposits that are separate from identified resources (mineral resources). To reflect varying degrees of geologic certainty, undiscovered resources may be divided into Hypothetical and Speculative.

dominio.definicion: Undiscovered resources that may occur either in known types of deposits in favorable geologic settings where mineral dicoveries have not been made, or in types of deposits as yet unrecognized for their economic potential.
dominio.observaciones: If exploration confirms their existence and reveals enough information about their quantity, grade, and quality, they will be reclassified as identified resources (Identified Resources).

dominio.definicion: Undiscovered resources that are similar to known mineral bodies and that may be reasonably expected to exist in the same producing district or region under analogous geologic conditions.
dominio.observaciones: If exploration confirms their existence and reveals enough information about their quality, grade, and quantity, they will be reclassified as identified resources (Identified Resources).

dominio.definicion: That part of any resource or reserve category that is restricted from extraction by laws or regulations.
dominio.observaciones: For example, restricted reserves meet all the requirements of reserves except that they are restricted from extraction by laws or regulations.

dominio.definicion: Used for medicinal treatment, often through bathing or other external remedies.

dominio.definicion: Used for the production of mineral water, bottled at the source for distributed consumption.

dominio.definicion: A fire control unit is a number of components working together which is designed to assisst a weapon system in hitting its target.
An area, located near the operational missile launching location and designed for the final assembly and checkout of the missile system.
An area or building specifically used to test missiles or rockets

definicion: The type of a missile site based on the class of missiles it houses.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a missile site type.

dominio.definicion: A defensive missile designed to destroy an incoming enemy missile, typically an intercontinental ballistic missile.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the Nike and A-35 missiles.

dominio.definicion: A ballistic missile able to be sent from one continent to another, generally with a range capability in excess of 5,500 kilometres.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the Atlas, Titian, Minuteman, Peacekeeper, SS-6, SS-7, SS-8, SS-9, SS-11, SS18, and SS-20 missiles.

dominio.definicion: A ballistic missile with a range of 2,750 to 5,500 kilometres.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the Thor, Redstone, Jupiter, Shavit, Taepo Dong 2, Pluton and Hades missiles.

dominio.definicion: A Soviet anti-aircraft surface-to-air missile (SAM) system, the first operational SAM deployed by the Soviet Union.
dominio.observaciones: It was used only to defend Moscow. The missile uses a single liquid-fueled rocket motor. Its maximum speed is approximately Mach 2.5. Typical range for the missile is about 30 kilometres with a maximum altitude around 60,000 feet.

dominio.definicion: A Soviet high-altitude surface-to-air guided missile (SAM) system, the most widely deployed and used air defence missile in history.
dominio.observaciones: It is a two-stage missile, consisting of a solid-fuel booster and a storable liquid-fuel upper stage burning red fuming nitric acid as the oxidizer, and kerosene as the fuel. Each battalion consists of six semi-fixed trainable single-rail launchers for their missiles about 60 to100 metres apart, deployed in a hexagonal 'flower' pattern around the central radars and guidance systems. Typically another six missiles are stored on tractor-trailers near the center of the site. Typical range for the missile is about 45 kilometres, with a maximum altitude around 60,000 feet.

dominio.definicion: A Soviet short-range surface-to-air missile (SAM) system designed to complement the S-25 Berkut (SA-1 'Guild') and V-75 (SA-2 'Guideline').
dominio.observaciones: The missiles are typically deployed on originally fixed, but later trailer-mounted, turrets containing two or four but can be carried ready-to-fire on Zil trucks in pairs or on tracked chassis carrying three missiles. It has a shorter effective range and lower engagement altitude than either of its predecessors and also flies slower, but due to its two-stage design it is more effective against more maneuverable targets. It is also able to engage lower flying targets than the previous systems, and being more modern it is much more resistant to ECM than the SA-2. The 5V24 (V-600) missiles reach around Mach 3 to 3.5 in flight, both stages powered by solid fuel rocket motors, and has an effective range of 25 kilometres. The SA-3, like the SA-2, uses radio command guidance.

dominio.definicion: A Soviet long range, medium-to-high altitude surface-to-air missile (SAM) system.
dominio.observaciones: The Transporter-Erector-Launcher (TEL) vehicles are tracked (modified AT-Ts) and carry two missiles each on an elevating turntable for up to 360 degree rotation and 70 degree elevation. The missiles are launched with the aid of four solid fuel rocket motors inside boosters attached to the outside of the massive missile. Once they have burned and the missile is aloft, it fires a liquid-fuelled ramjet sustainer engine. It reaches speeds of up to Mach 4 and has an effective range of 50 to 55 kilometres depending upon the version. It carries a 135 kilogram warhead.

dominio.definicion: A Soviet very long range medium-to-high altitude surface-to-air missile (SAM) system designed to defend large areas from bomber attack or other strategic aircraft (such as the SR-71 'Blackbird').
dominio.observaciones: Each battalion has six single-rail missile launchers for the 10.72 metre long missiles as well as a number of radar systems. The missile range is 200 to 400 kilometres depending on the model.

dominio.definicion: A Soviet mobile surface-to-air missile (SAM) system used in low level air defence system designed to protect ground forces from air attack.
dominio.observaciones: Each battery consists of a number of similar tracked vehicles, one of which carries the 1S91 (NATO designation 'Straight Flush') 25 kilowatt G/H-band continuous-wave radar (range 75 kilometres) in addition to an optical sight and is usually accompanied by four triple-missile TELs and four trucks carrying three spare missiles and a crane. The missile range is 3 to 24 kilometres.

dominio.definicion: A Soviet man-portable, shoulder-fired, low-altitude surface-to-air missile (SAM) system similar to the US Army REDEYE, with a high explosive warhead and passive infrared homing guidance.
dominio.observaciones: The missile range is about thirteen kilometres. The SA-7 is a tail-chase missile system and its effectiveness depends on its ability to lock onto the heat source of low-flying fixed and rotary-wing aircraft.

dominio.definicion: A Soviet short-range, anti-aircraft amphibious-vehicle-mounted mobile surface-to-air missile (SAM) system based on the SA-N-4 and an all-in-one TELAR vehicle which can detect, track and engage aircraft independently or with the aid of regimental surveillance radars.
dominio.observaciones: The Gecko carries four SA-8 missiles, and another 8 inside for reload purposes. The missile range is about 13 kilometres with a launch weight of 190 kilograms. The SA-8 missile uses infrared tracking to find its targets.

dominio.definicion: A Soviet short-range, anti-aircraft amphibious-vehicle-mounted mobile surface-to-air missile (SAM) system consisting of the SA-9 launcher atop the BRDM-2A.
dominio.observaciones: The Gaskin can carry two missiles boxes on the launch pad and four more inside for reload purposes. Missiles can be launched one at a time, two at a time, or four at a time. The Gaskin does not have radar. The missile range is 5 to 8 kilometres with a launch weight of 30 kilograms.

dominio.definicion: A ballistic missile with a range of 130 to 2,750 kilometres.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the Soviet SS-1 (R-1, or Scud), SS-2 (R-2), SS-3, SS-4, and SS-5 missiles.

dominio.definicion: A surface-to-surface guided projectile launched from a hand-held, vehicle mounted, trailer mounted or fixed installation or from a ship.
dominio.observaciones: Surface-to-surface missiles are usually guided (an unguided surface-to-surface missile is usually referred to as a rocket). They are often powered by a rocket motor or sometimes fired by an explosive charge, since the launching platform is typically stationary or moving slowly. They usually have fins and/or wings for lift and stability, although hyper-velocity or short-ranged missiles may utilise body lift or fly a ballistic trajectory.

dominio.definicion: A missile designed to be launched from the ground to destroy aircraft.
dominio.observaciones: It is a type of anti-aircraft system. For example, the US MIM-series and RIM-series, and the Soviet SA-series missiles.

dominio.definicion: A Russian surface-to-air missile (SAM) system similar to the US Patriot.
dominio.observaciones: It was developed as a PVO long-range system to defend strategic targets against both conventional aircraft and cruise missiles, while the contemporary S-300V (NATO designation SA-12A Gladiator/SA-12B Giant) series was developed as a more mobile system to protect the ground forces from aircraft and short-range ballistic missiles. The S-300 missiles are sealed rounds and require no maintenance over their lifetime. The missile range is 50 to 200 kilometres depending on the model.

dominio.definicion: A Russian medium-range, medium-altitude surface-to-air missile (SAM) system, the successor to the SA-6 'Gainful'.
dominio.observaciones: It features improvements in number of missiles carried per TEL, range and altitude performance, missile speed, guidance accuracy and warhead potency. It is designed to engage maneuverable aircraft such as jets, helicopters and cruise missiles. The missile range is 3 to 50 kilometres depending on the model.

dominio.definicion: A Russian long-range, high-altitude surface-to-air missile system designed primarily to intercept incoming ballistic missiles (counterpart to the SA-10 'Grumble').
dominio.observaciones: The system is very similar to the SA-10 in terms of configuration, but unlike the SA-10 there are two different sizes of missiles. The smaller 9M82 missiles, called SA-12B 'Gladiator' by NATO, are similar in size and range to those of the SA-10 system. However the 9M83 (SA-12A 'Giant') missiles are much larger and only two can be carried on each TELAR, rather than four. These vehicles, in combination with the command vehicle and 'Grill Pan' tracking radar, 'Bill Board A' surveillance radar and 'High Screen' ballistic missile detection radar, scan a specific area of the sky and engage aerial theats including ballistic missiles which are detected transiting it. The 'Gladiator' missiles have a maximum engagement range of around 75 kilometres while the 'Giant' missiles can engage targets out to 100 kilometres and up to altitudes of around 100,000 feet. In both cases the warhead is around 150 kilograms.

dominio.definicion: A Russian highly mobile, visually aimed, optical/infra-red guided, low-altitude, short-range surface-to-air missile (SAM) system (successor of the SA-9 'Gaskin').
dominio.observaciones: Rather than being mounted on an amphibious but lightly armoured BRDM chassis like the SA-9, the SA-13 is mounted on a slightly better protected and more mobile tracked, modified MT-LB. Four missiles are mounted on the turret in boxes, ready to launch, and eight more are carried inside the vehicle as reloads. Top missile speed is around Mach 2, engagement range is 500 to 5000 metres and engagement altitude is up to 11,500 feet. It can also use the SA-9 'Gaskin', SA-7 'Grail', and SA-14 'Gremlin' missiles.

dominio.definicion: A Russian man-portable air defence missile system (MANPADS) was developed in the Soviet Union as a response to the poor performance of the earlier SA-7 'Grail' system.
dominio.observaciones: The missile includes an all-new infra-red homing seeker head. The missile range is about 4,500 metres.

dominio.definicion: A Russian low and medium-altitude, short-range surface-to-air missile (SAM) system designed for engaging aircraft, helicopters, cruise-missiles, precision munitions and remotely-piloted vehicles.
dominio.observaciones: It is designed to protect targets from attack at all times and in any weather not only by shooting down attacking aircraft but also destroying any munitions before they reach the target. It is air-portable and equipped with NBC (nuclear, biological and chemical) protection. Each 9K331 vehicle is a completely autonomous TELAR although it can be linked into a greater air-defence system. The radar is a modern, phased-array type and eight missiles are stored vertically, ready to fire. The 9M330 missile is 3.5 metres long with a peak speed speed of around Mach 2.8. Guidance is via radio command and detonation via a radar proximity fuze.

dominio.definicion: A Russian man-portable air defence missile system (MANPADS), the successor to the SA-14 'Gremlin' system.
dominio.observaciones: Uses infra-red homing.

dominio.definicion: A Russian medium-range, medium-altitude surface-to-air missile (SAM) system, the successor to the SA-11 'Gadfly'.
dominio.observaciones: Possibly the biggest change from the SA-11 'Gadfly' system is the fact that the 9S18M1 'Snow Drift' surveillance radar is mounted on the TELAR, making each launcher more independent and allowing more targets to be tracked in different locations at the same time. Range, altitude and target engagement have improved as well. Range is reported as being up to 50 kilometres, maximum altitude around 82,000 feet and maximum target speed around Mach 4.

dominio.definicion: A Russian man-portable air defence missile system (MANPADS), the successor to the SA-16 'Gimlet' system.
dominio.observaciones: Uses infra-red homing.

dominio.definicion: A Soviet Integrated Air Defense System carrying six (2S6) or eight (2S6M/2S6M1) 9K111 missiles in two banks of two pairs, each pair being able to be elevated independently.
dominio.observaciones: Effective engagement ranges are 2.4 to 8 kilometres and altitudes are up to 11,500 feet. Each missile is 3.2 metres long, weighs 65 kilograms with a warhead of 16 kilograms, flies at around Mach 3.5 and can engage targets flying at up to Mach 1.5.

definicion: An indication that a bridge span moves in some manner to allow passage underneath.

datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.4.1, Combinations of date and time of day - Complete representation - Extended format, a calendar date and time representation, as a single data element comprising up to twenty characters, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, [hh] the ordinal number of an hour within the calendar day, [mm] the ordinal number of a minute within the hour, [ss] the ordinal number of a second within the minute, and an optional 'Z' when the time is according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12' for 12 April 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412T114520Z').

definicion: The intensity of the earthquake as measured on the Modified Mercalli (MM) Scale.
descripcion: The Modified Mercalli (MM) Scale quantifies the effects of an earthquake on the Earth's surface, humans, objects of nature, and man-made structures on a scale of I through XII, with I ('Instrumental') indicating that it was not felt by many people unless in favourable conditions, and XII ('Catastrophic') one that causes almost complete destruction. It has been updated since its original definition in 1931, most recently in 1995, to account for changes in building practices.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an earthquake Modified Mercalli (MM) intensity.

dominio.definicion: Not felt by many people unless in favourable conditions.
Felt only by a few people at best, especially on the upper floors of buildings; delicately suspended objects may swing.

Felt quite noticeably by people indoors, especially on the upper floors of buildings, but many do not recognize it as an earthquake; standing motor cars may rock slightly; vibration similar to the passing of a truck; event duration estimated.
Felt by many to all; trees and bushes shaken slightly; buildings shaken moderately to strongly; walls creak loudly; observer described the shaking as 'strong'.
dominio.observaciones: Formerly described as follows: felt indoors by many people, outdoors by few people during the day, at night some awakened; dishes, windows, doors disturbed; dishes and windows rattle alarmingly; walls make cracking sound; sensation like heavy truck striking building; standing motor cars rock noticeably.

dominio.definicion: A few small objects overturned and fallen; a few items thrown from store shelves; hairline cracks in interior walls; a few windows cracked; hanging pictures tilted, out of place, or fallen; trees and bushes shaken moderately to strongly; observer reported difficulty standing or walking; felt moderately by people in moving vehicles.
dominio.observaciones: Formerly described as follows: felt outside by most, may not be felt by some outside in non-favourable conditions; dishes and windows may break and large bells will ring; vibrations like large train passing close to house.

dominio.definicion: Some windows broken out; a few instances of fallen plaster or damaged unreinforced masonry (URM) chimneys; large cracks in interior walls; many small objects overturned and fallen; many items thrown from store shelves; many glassware items or dishes broken; light furniture overturned and moderately heavy furniture displaced.
dominio.observaciones: Formerly described as follows: felt by all; many frightened and run outdoors, walk unsteadily; windows, dishes, glassware broken; books fall off shelves; some heavy furniture moved or overturned; a few instances of fallen plaster; damage slight.

dominio.definicion: Significant damage to unreinforced masonry (URM) buildings, including cracks in bearing walls and out-of-plane movement or fall of upper walls and parapets; many URM chimneys fallen or broken at the roofline; some masonry fences fallen or destroyed; heavy furniture overturned.
dominio.observaciones: Formerly described as follows: difficult to stand; furniture broken; damage negligible in building of good design and construction; damage slight to moderate in well-built ordinary structures; considerable damage in poorly built or badly designed structures; some chimneys broken; noticed by people driving motor cars.

dominio.definicion: Considerable damage to unreinforced masonry buildings, with partial collapse; old wood-frame houses shifted off foundations; damage to wood-frame apartment buildings having open first-stories, with some cases of apartments being destroyed; significant damage to reinforced, lined, masonry chimneys on single-family homes; structural damage to some reinforced-concrete structures that would have been built when a seismic code was in effect; very heavy furniture moved conspicuously or overturned.
dominio.observaciones: Formerly described as follows: damage slight in specially designed structures; damage considerable in ordinary substantial buildings with partial collapse; damage great in poorly built structures; fall of chimneys, factory stacks, columns, monuments, walls; heavy furniture moved.

dominio.definicion: Multiple cases of structural damage to reinforced-concrete buildings and parking structures that would have been built when a seismic code was in effect, with some cases of partial or complete collapse; widespread destruction of wood-frame apartment buildings having large open areas in their first stories; collapse of elevated freeway sections.
dominio.observaciones: Formerly described as follows: general panic; damage considerable in specially designed structures; well designed frame structures thrown out of plumb; damage great in substantial buildings, with partial collapse; buildings shifted off foundations.

dominio.definicion: Some well built wooden structures destroyed; most masonry and frame structures destroyed with foundation; railway track rails bent.
Few, if any masonry structures remain standing; bridges destroyed; railway track rails bent greatly.
Total damage; almost everything is destroyed; lines of sight and level distorted; objects thrown into the air; ground moves in waves or ripples; large amounts of rock may move position.

definicion: The numeric identifier of a Mobile Offshore Drilling Unit (MODU).
descripcion: The scope of uniqueness is global; uniqueness is guaranteed by drilling industry procedures.

The feature is superintended by permanently stationed personnel.

definicion: The intended purpose of a monument based on its origin and/or function.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a monument purpose.

dominio.definicion: An artistic, formed object that was created with the intention to publically commemorate an event, a custom and/or a person.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a statue, war memorial, or tomb.

dominio.definicion: Objects, buildings or their ruins as sources and testimonies of human history and development.
dominio.observaciones: For example, historical, religious, industrial, and/or archaeological reasons.

dominio.definicion: Isolated landscape features under nature protection.
dominio.observaciones: For example, caves, rock formations, and historical trees.

definicion: The type of a mooring and/or warping facility based on its structural and intended use characteristics.

datatype.nombre: Mooring and/or Warping Facility Type Code

dominio.definicion: A post or group of posts, which may support a deck, used for mooring or warping a vessel.
A post or group of posts, which a vessel may swing around for compass adjustment.
A small shaped post, mounted on a wharf or dolphin used to secure ship's lines.
A section of wall designated for tying-up vessels awaiting transit.
dominio.observaciones: Bollards and mooring devices are available for both large and small ships.

dominio.definicion: A long heavy pile (for example: a timber or section of steel, wood, or concrete), forced into the seabed to serve as a mooring facility.
A connection between two independent objects, in particular between a buoy and pile or between two buoys used as a mooring facility.
A buoy secured to the bottom by permanent moorings with means for mooring a vessel by use of its anchor chain or mooring lines.
A buoy so located that lines to it can be used for the movement of vessels.

definicion: The type of system that is used to moor vessels, based on the nature and/or number of mooring points.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a mooring type.

dominio.definicion: A single point mooring attached to a floating buoy to which a vessel may be attached.
A set of anchors to which boats are attached by both bow and stem lines.
A floating structure secured by an anchor to which one or more boats may be moored.
An anchor to which a vessel is attached to allow alignment with wave, wind or current.
A system for the fore and aft mooring of several boats in rows.

definicion: The type of a moraine based on its relationship to the glacier that produced it.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a moraine type.

dominio.definicion: A ridgelike accumulation that is being produced at the margin of an active glacier.
dominio.observaciones: It is deposited at the lower or outer end of a glacier.

dominio.definicion: A low ridgelike moraine carried on, or deposited at or near, the side margin of a mountain glacier.
An accumulation of till after it has been deposited or released from glacier ice during ablation, to form an extensive area of low relief devoid of transverse linear elements.
dominio.observaciones: It appears as an irregularly undulating surface of till, glacial drift, and/or boulder clay.

dominio.definicion: The moraine results from the merging of lateral moraines when two glaciers converge.

definicion: The maximum entry width of a movement area considering the taxiway width plus clearance from hazards (for example: trees, revetments, and buildings).

definicion: An indication that a building is divided into two or more distinct sets of rooms or other interior spaces that are internally fully-connected while being separated from each other and common areas by controlled access point(s) (for example: lockable doors) that enable physical privacy and security for its occupants.
descripcion: For example, an apartment building consisting of multiple self-contained residences individually including spaces for personal activities, cooking, eating, sleeping, and (usually) a private bathroom, or an office building housing multiple commercial establishments individually including spaces for reception, meetings, single or open-plan work areas, as well as individual or common-use bathrooms or cafeterias.

datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: The numbers are separated by a slash (/) if only two visibilities exist, or by a dash ('-') separating the greatest and least visibilities if three or more exist.

definicion: An indication that a feature has more than one official, native script, geographic name.
descripcion: Multiple official names may exist when a feature passes through more than one country and those multiple countries have different official names for that feature. Some countries have more than one official language and therefore may have an official name for a feature in each official language.

datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.4.1, Combinations of date and time of day - Complete representation - Extended format, a calendar date and time representation, as a single data element comprising up to twenty characters, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, [hh] the ordinal number of an hour within the calendar day, [mm] the ordinal number of a minute within the hour, [ss] the ordinal number of a second within the minute, and an optional 'Z' when the time is according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985). descripcion: Typically used together with Attribute: 'Name Identifier' to provide a unique index into the NGA Geographic Names Data Base (GNDB) from which NGA draws all of its feature name information.
