definicion: The type of a location that normally does not appear as a specific, characterized object but that has a name that is required to be displayed in association with that location.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a named location type.

dominio.definicion: A tract of land without homogeneous character or boundaries.
A minor area or place of unspecified or mixed character and indefinite boundaries.
An area distinguished by one or more observable physical or cultural characteristics.
A tract of land in the Arctic.
A minor area or place of unspecified or mixed character and indefinite boundaries that includes a small group of dwellings or other buildings.

definicion: The type of an intrastate conflict within an area.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a national conflict type.

dominio.definicion: A war between citizens of the same State or an armed conflict on the territory of a single State between several native groups.
A momentous juncture in, for example, politics, commerce, or domestic affairs.
The state of imminent evolution of a non-violent (non-warlike) confrontation into violent confrontation (war).

definicion: The total amount of offically acknowledged debt of a State to creditors.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The monetary unit establishing a currency.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The unit of monetary exchange serving as legal tender in the United States, the dollar.

definicion: The degree to which a feature (for example: monument or icon) is of such national significance that its damage or destruction would have a great impact on the morale and public confidence of the nation as a whole, as a category.
descripcion: National monuments or icons are internationally recognized symbols of national power, culture, and tradition. They include sites and structures such as prominent historical attractions, monuments, cultural icons, and centers of government and commerce. Icons can be considered to include any structure, system, or resource that has cultural, historic, psychological, or political significance at the local, regional or national level if compromised or destroyed. National monuments or icons are usually located within the territory of the nation; the most common exceptions are cultural sites of religious significance which may be located within the territory of another nation.

datatype.nombre: National Monument or Icon Category Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a national monument or icon category.

dominio.definicion: Features of unique quality, widely recognized both nationally and internationally to be symbolic of the nation.
Features generally recognized nationally to be significant symbols of the nation.
Features of unique quality, widely recognized as having significance on a regional level within the nation.
Features generally recognized as significant on a local level within the nation.

definicion: The State with which a legal relationship has been established by an entity (for example: a person, a corporation, or a ship).
descripcion: In the case of a person this relationship is usually termed 'citizenship' whereas in the case of a corporation or ship it is usually termed 'registration'.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a native settlement type.

dominio.definicion: Dwellings are concentrated around one or more points.
Dwellings are relatively homogeneously distributed.
Temporarily existing, moveable dwellings of nomads, usually tents.

definicion: The type of a natural disaster.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a natural disaster type.

dominio.definicion: A large mass of snow, ice, soil, or rock, or mixtures of these materials, falling, sliding, or flowing very rapidly under the force of gravity.
A severe storm condition characterized by low temperatures, strong winds, and heavy blowing snow.
A storm or atmospheric disturbance involving circular motion of winds.
The rupture of a dam leading to the sudden release of a typically large volume of water.
An extended period of months or years when a region notes a deficiency in its water supply.
Surface tremors and following occurrence of fractions and mass movements.
Combustion of flammable materials (for example: structures, trees, or brush).
A storm that produces hailstones that fall to the ground.
A prolonged period of excessively hot weather, which may be accompanied by high humidity.
A collision of a large meteorite, asteroid, comet, or other celestial object with the Earth.
A mudflow composed chiefly of volcanoclasitc materials on the flank of a volcano.
Any of a wide variety of mass-movement landforms and processes involving the downslope transport of soil and rock material as a whole.
A rare type of natural disaster in which carbon dioxide suddenly erupts from deep lake water, suffocating wildlife, livestock and humans.
Mass movement of predominantly fine-grained material possesing a high degree of fluidity during movement.
Fast-moving currents of hot gas and rock (collectively known as tephra), which travel away from the volcano at speeds generally as great as 700 km/h.
A flowing over the banks of a stream or a river.
A mass of fallen rocks.

A violent disturbance of the atmosphere, taking the form of high winds, often with heavy falls of rain, hail, or snow, thunder and lightning, rough conditions with high foaming waves at sea, and clouds of sand or dust in arid regions.
An offshore rise of water associated with a low pressure weather system, typically a tropical cyclone.
A violent, dangerous, rotating column of air which is in contact with both the surface of the earth and a cumulonimbus cloud or, in rare cases, the base of a cumulus cloud.
Gravitational seawave produced by a submarine earthquake.

Ash is created when solid rock shatters and magma separates into minute particles during explosive volcanic activity. The usually violent nature of an eruption involving steam (phreatic eruption or phreatomagmatic eruption) results in the magma and solid
A spell of activity in which a volcano ejects lava, ash, etc.

definicion: The reason for a limit of natural characteristics.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a natural environmental limit reason.

dominio.definicion: The limit is defined by its rate of precipitation.
The limit is defined by its nearness to the pole.
The limit is defined by its height above mean sea level.

definicion: The type of a natural-spatial limit.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a natural environmental limit type.

dominio.definicion: A boundary or limitation beyond which any cultivation of crops is impossible.
Boundary of an area in which no trees exist, beyond the forest line.
Boundary of the area in which the soil permanently shows temperatures below freezing point.
Boundary of a trough of low pressure in the equator-area where the northeastery trade winds of the northern hemisphere.
Boundary between climate regions, for example, southern alpine versus mediterranean.
Climatic boundary of the Antarctic (northern boundary of the southern polar sea).
Boundary of the area in which ocean water is frozen and consists of ice floes put in layers on each other.
A boundary or limitation beyond which any settlement is either impossible or not useful for climatic or topographic reasons.
Boundary of an area up to which single ice bergs from the continental ice sheet and ice floes find their movement limit towards the equator.
The boundary of a habitat where trees do not form closed stocks.
Boundary between areas of different weather.
The limit is defined by its rate of precipitation and evapotranspiration.
The limit is defined by its maximal nearness to the pole.

definicion: The type of a natural pool, generally based on its origin.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a natural pool type.

dominio.definicion: A hot spring that intermittently spouts steam and water.
dominio.observaciones: Usually located in a volcanic area.

dominio.definicion: A spring of naturally hot water.
dominio.observaciones: Usually located in a volcanic area.

dominio.definicion: A vent in or near a volcano, from which hot vapour is emitted.
A flow of water rising or welling naturally from the earth.
A small natural terrain depression in which water collects, especially a pool where animals come to drink.
A spring whose outflow has been collected by an enclosure.

dominio.definicion: The location at which a watercourse re-emerges from the terrain at the end of an underground part of its course.
A spring whose water contains sulphur or sulphurous gases.

definicion: The type(s) of an area where firing and/or munition exercises are conducted by Naval forces (for example: vessels or aircraft) based on the purpose(s) of the firing, practice, or exercise and/or the nature of the equipment employed.

datatype.nombre: Naval Firing and/or Practice Type Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a naval firing and/or practice type.

dominio.definicion: An area formerly used to carry out mine warfare drills and/or standard operating procedures (for example: to check sonar) but now abandoned.
A Naval military exercise area designated specifically for bombardment and/or strafing of targets.
An area in which military bombing and missile exercises are, or may be, carried out and constitute a firing danger.
An acoustically enabled weapons range where ships, aircraft (planes and/or helicopters) and/or submarines can target, track, and engage remotely operated targets with torpedoes.
An area in which military exercises for the laying of naval mines are, or may be, carried out.
A military exercise area designated specifically for the testing, firing and practice of AWW missile engagements.
dominio.observaciones: Missile firings could include surface to air, surface to surface and air to air engagements.

dominio.definicion: An area allocated for bombardment during the live firing of weapons.
A Naval training area where re-usable mines designated for exercise and training are deployed and recovered.

dominio.definicion: An area where military exercises involving torpedoes are, or may be, carried out.
An area where Naval forces conduct weapons tests and/or exercises.

dominio.observaciones: For example: moored mines fitted with grapnel devices, medium-actuation-level magnetic mines which a normally energized sweep will detonate within the mine sweepers' damage area, and course acoustic mines actuated when the sweeper is towing an acoustic sweep beam.

dominio.definicion: Laid for the purpose of, or whose mechanism is specifically designed or adjusted with the object of, sinking or damaging minehunter vessels.

dominio.definicion: An object constructed to have mine-like characteristics (for example: oil drums welded together) and filled with inert material to give enhanced mine-like characteristics for mine hunting training.
dominio.observaciones: A re-usable mine designed for exercise and training.

dominio.definicion: An object constructed to have mine-like characteristics (for example: oil drums welded together) for mine hunting training purposes.
dominio.observaciones: A re-usable mine designed for exercise and training. They may be either ground mines or buoyant mines. For example, the VErsatile Mine firing System (VEMS) is an exercise ground mine that senses and records ship traffic, sending a radio signal or releasing a buoy if it calculates that it has sunk a 'target'.

dominio.definicion: An inert replica mine for mine hunting training purposes.
Laid for the purpose of, or whose mechanism is specifically designed or adjusted with the object of, sinking or damaging Mine Counter-Mine Vessels (MCMV).
dominio.observaciones: These mines do not target specific features of the MCMV (for example: Anti-Sweeper Mine or Anti-Hunter Mine); they are anti-surface ship mines laid or adjusted to counter MCMVs. For example: shallow moored mines, snagline mines, highly sensitive magnetic mines, and medium actuation level acoustic mines.

dominio.definicion: Laid for the purpose of, or whose mechanism is specifically designed or adjusted with the object of, sinking surface effect vehicles in water depth of 3 - 60 metres.
An object (for example: a decoy or dummy) designed to have the sonar signature attributes of a mine, with the intention of wasting an enemies time and resources.
dominio.observaciones: These are either small objects with a large sonar signal, or inert minelike objects.

definicion: The capability by which an explosive naval mine maintains or changes position.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a naval mine positioning.

dominio.definicion: A negatively buoyant mine that rests on, or can become buried in, the sea bed and is held there by its own mass.
dominio.observaciones: Its firing mechanism is usually of the influence type (some anti-invasion naval mines used in the Very Shallow Water (VSL) are contact actuated).

dominio.definicion: A mine of positive buoyancy held down below the surface by a mooring attached to a sinker on the bottom.
dominio.observaciones: Its firing mechanism can be of either contact or influence type. Some 'Deep Moored Mines' use very strong moorings (usually small gauge wire) to permit use in water depth down to 1000 metres.

dominio.definicion: A moored mine of positive buoyancy whose position is hydrostatically controlled, maintaining a pre-set depth below the water surface independently of the rise and fall of the tide.
A moored mine with a very short scope mooring that keeps the mine case close to the sinker.
dominio.observaciones: There are three typical types of short-tethered moored mines: anti-invasion moored contact mines, anti-submarine deep moored mines, and rising mines.

dominio.definicion: A moored contact mine for use in the Very Shallow Water (VSL).
dominio.observaciones: Employed against landing craft.

dominio.definicion: A deep moored mine designed to sink submarines, usually influence actuated.
dominio.observaciones: Moored contact mines laid at great depth which remain moored near the sinker may also pose a threat to submarines.

dominio.definicion: A mine that rises from its deployed position, either using its own positive buoyancy or by means of a propulsion system.
dominio.observaciones: Most rising mines are short-tethered and can be straight rising, vectored by attached pre-set fins, or homing.

dominio.definicion: A mine having positive buoyancy which is released from a sinker by target influence.
A rising mine that is launched from its deployed position by a propelling charge and continues in motion within a cavitation bubble by virtue of its kinetic energy.
A rising mine with a very short scope mooring that keeps the mine case close to the sinker.
A moored mine with a number of buoyant mine cases attached to the same sinker such that when the mooring of one mine case is severed, another mine case rises from the sinker to its preset case depth.
dominio.observaciones: Bouquet mines are used to counter mechanical mine sweeping operations.

dominio.definicion: A buoyant naval mine held below the water surface by a weight, usually in the form of a chain, which is free to creep along the bottom under the influence of currents.
A mine visible on the surface of the water.
dominio.observaciones: It can be either 'watching', 'drifting', or 'free'.

dominio.definicion: A moored mine, still connected to its sinker, whose case breaks frequently or permanently the surface of the water.
dominio.observaciones: This normally occurs when the scope of the mooring is too long for the prevailing water depth.

dominio.definicion: A buoyant or neutrally buoyant naval mine, free to drift under the influence of waves, wind, currents, or the tide.
A mine that moves on its own when it is deployed.
dominio.observaciones: For example, submarines deploy free (mobile) mines and they have the form of a torpedo; thus the mine can be deployed deep inside an enemy harbour.

definicion: Specifies the general purpose or intent of a minefield.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a naval minefield purpose.

dominio.definicion: Laid in friendly territorial waters to protect ports, harbours, anchorages, coasts, and coastal routes.
Laid in response to a perceived or real enemy threat.
A relatively small number of mines laid randomly over a large area designed to disrupt shipping.
Laid in a busy shipping lane or in an area where maximum destruction will occur.

definicion: The type(s) of an area in which operations are conducted by Naval forces (for example: vessels or aircraft) based on the size, purpose, forces deployed and/or operation(s) conducted.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a naval operations type.

dominio.definicion: An area where Naval forces conduct Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) operations.
dominio.observaciones: May include both surface and submerged vessels working in conjunction with aircraft.

dominio.definicion: A Joint Exercise Notification and Operating Area (JENOA) management grid used by the Joint Maritime Operational Training Staff (JMOTS) for the positioning of forces.
dominio.observaciones: It provides a framework for operating forces in widely dispersed groups.

dominio.definicion: A large area where Naval forces conduct operations.
dominio.observaciones: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct firing and/or munition exercises.

dominio.definicion: A region that has been swept for explosive mines.
A small area where Naval forces conduct operations.
dominio.observaciones: Distinguished from areas where Naval forces conduct firing and/or munition exercises.

dominio.definicion: An area laid and maintained with explosive mines for defence or practice purposes.
An area within which notification is required between respective military authorities of future military exercises/activities.
An area that has been surveyed and reported as safe for submarines to rest on the sea bed.
A designated area for the testing of Naval shipboard machinery and systems.
dominio.observaciones: Often referred to as 'conducting sea trials'.
dominio.aliases: Sea Trial Area, Sea Test Range

dominio.definicion: An area where military submarine exercises are, or may be, carried out.
An area where military submarines conduct operations.
A designated circular water column with a specified radius that is used by submarines for vertical navigation between allocated `Depth Separation' layers within a submarine operating area/zone.
A designated transit lane below the surface used by submarines to effect safe passage.
A designated transit lane on the surface used by submarines to effect safe passage.
An area defined within a naval operations area that restricts surface ship movements within submarine transit lanes.
A safe transit corridor for surface vessels through an exercise area.
An area designated for testing UQC (now superseded) and/or WQC underwater acoustic telephone systems.
dominio.observaciones: The UQC/WQC operational range is limited due signal degradation caused by reverberation in the form of (frequently severe) multipath intersymbol interference.

dominio.definicion: A position where Fast Patrol Boats can moor to an islet or land.
A specified location that is identified and used as a rendezvous point.
An area in which practical instruction in diving techniques is given and practiced.
The limit of a NATO Fleet Operational Readiness Accuracy Check Site (FORACS) Naval Forces Sensor and Weapons Accuracy Check Site established under Programme V.
An area where Landing Craft Air Cushion (LCAC) vehicles are used in the conduct of operations.

definicion: Information about the navigability of a body of water by ocean-going and/or large vessels.
descripcion: Navigability is not intended to include jet skis, motorboats or other recreational craft.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a navigability information.

dominio.definicion: Affords passage to vessels and is operating in accordance with stated schedule and/or stated depth and clearance.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a channel is maintained at stated depth or a lock is manned on a regular schedule.

dominio.definicion: Affords passage to vessels but operational support has been abandoned.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a channel remains navigable but may no longer be maintained at stated depth.

dominio.definicion: Affording passage to vessels; capable of being navigated.
Affords passage to vessels but periodic restrictions apply.
dominio.observaciones: For example, seasonally restricted due to ice or only manned at regular intervals.

dominio.definicion: Does not afford passage to vessels; incapable of being navigated.

definicion: A published bearing to or radial from a radio navigation aid, referenced to a significant point or radio navigation aid checkpoint.

datatype.nombre: Navigation Aid Point Angular Indication Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a navigation aid point angular indication.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: The first three characters are either 'RDL' (Radial) or 'BRG' (Bearing), followed by a space, followed by a 3 digit angular value measured from True North in the range '000'-'359', followed by a space, followed by a three character navigation aid identifier. For example: 'RDL 237 FFM' or 'BRG 040 SIB'.

definicion: A published distance between a radio navigation aid and a significant point or radio navigation aid checkpoint.

datatype.nombre: Navigation Aid Point Distance Indication Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a navigation aid point distance indication.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: An up to three digit numeric value with no leading zeros, followed by a space, followed by a designation of the unit of measure as one of: 'NM' (Nautical Mile), 'KM' (Kilometre), or 'SM' (Statute Mile), followed by a space, followed by the three character navigation aid identifier. For example: '37 NM FFM'.

definicion: An indication that a feature may serve as a navigation landmark, allowing for rapid and positive orientation of a navigator.
descripcion: Its size, shape, location, and/or isolation make it prominent in relation to its surroundings, and it is therefore easily recognized from the surface and/or from the air.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The sequence, grouping, and/or distinctive character (rythym and colour or colours) of a navigation light.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a navigation light characteristic.

dominio.definicion: A signal light that shows, in any given direction, two or more colours in a regularly repeated sequence with a regular periodicity.
A light showing 160 or more, usually 240 to 300, flashes per minute.
A signal light that shows continuously, in any given direction, with constant luminous intensity and colour.
A rhythmic light in which a fixed light is combined with a flashing light of higher luminous intensity.
A rhythmic light in which the total duration of light in a period is clearly shorter than the total duration of darkness and all the appearances of light are of equal duration.
A quick light in which the sequence of flashes is interrupted by regularly repeated eclipses of constant and long duration.
A light in which the ultra quick flashes (160 or more per minute) are interrupted at regular intervals by eclipses of long duration.

A light in which the very rapid alterations of light (repetition rate: 80 to 159 flashes, usually either 100 or 120, flashes per minute) and darkness are interrupted at regular intervals by eclipses of long duration.
A light with all durations of light and darkness equal.
A flashing light in which a single flash of not less than two seconds duration is regularly repeated.
A rhythmic light in which appearances of light of two clearly different durations are grouped to represent a character or characters in the Morse code.
A rhythmic light in which the total duration of light in a period is clearly longer than the total duration of darkness and all the eclipses are of equal duration.
A light in which flashes are combined in groups including the same number of quick flashes (repetition rate: 50-79 per minute) and in which groups are repeated at regular intervals.
A light in which very quick flashes are combined in groups including the same number of flashes (repetition rate: 80-159 per minute) and in which groups are repeated at regular intervals.
A light exhibiting without interruption very rapid regular alternations of light and darkness (repetition rate: 50-79 per minute).
dominio.observaciones: The repetition rate is not less than 50 flashes per minute but less than 80 flashes per minute.

dominio.definicion: A light showing 80 to 159, usually either 100 or 120, flashes per minute.
A flashing light in which a regular appearance of a long flash (greater than two seconds duration) is regularly repeated.
An occulting light on which is superimposed a flashing light.
A fixed long-flashing light, in which a single flash of higher luminous intensity of not less than two seconds duration is regularly repeated.
An occulting light that is alternating in two or more colours.
A long-flashing light that is alternating in two or more colours.
A flashing light that is alternating in two or more colours.
A quick-flashing light in which a regular appearance of a long flash (greater than two seconds duration) is regularly repeated.
dominio.observaciones: The light shows 50 to 79 flashes per minute.

dominio.definicion: A very quick-flashing light in which a regular appearance of a long flash (greater than two seconds duration) is regularly repeated.
dominio.observaciones: The light shows 80 to 159, usually either 100 or 120, flashes per minute.

dominio.definicion: An ultra quick-flashing light in which a regular appearance of a long flash (greater than two seconds duration) is regularly repeated.
dominio.observaciones: The light shows 160 or more, usually 240 to 300, flashes per minute.

dominio.definicion: A fixed flashing light that is alternating in two or more colours.

definicion: The colour(s) of a International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) navigation mark.
descripcion: When the navigation mark is patterned, the Attribute: 'Colour Pattern' may be used to identify the pattern and a corresponding list of colours specified.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a navigation mark colour.

dominio.definicion: White, an IALA colour.
Black, an IALA colour.
Red, an IALA colour.
dominio.observaciones: Used in IALA (when unpatterned) to indicate a lateral mark; the direction depends on the IALA Region.

dominio.definicion: Green, an IALA colour.
dominio.observaciones: Used in IALA (when unpatterned) to indicate a lateral mark; the direction depends on the IALA Region.

dominio.definicion: Blue, an IALA colour.
Yellow, an IALA colour.
Grey, an IALA colour.
Brown, an IALA colour.
Amber, an IALA colour.
Violet, an IALA colour.
Orange, an IALA colour.
dominio.observaciones: Commonly used as a border for information marks.

dominio.definicion: Magenta, an IALA colour.
Pink, an IALA colour.

definicion: The type of navigation system for which the checkpoint has been established.
descripcion: For example: Inertial Navigation System (INS), VHF Omnidirectional Range (VOR), or Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) systems.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a navigation service checkpoint type.

dominio.definicion: Ultra High Frequency (UHF) ground equipment that is used in conjunction with airborne equipment to determine distance between the airborne and ground equipment.
dominio.observaciones: DME Distance is defined as the line of sight distance (slant range) from the source of a DME signal to the receiving antenna. DME operates on the interrogation-answer principle where the time required for the round trip of the signal exchange is measured in the airborne DME unit and translated into DME Distance.

dominio.definicion: A wide area service based on a satellite constellation providing radio frequency signals which can be used by airborne equipment to determine the aircraft's two-dimensional position, or depending upon the capabilities of the system, a three-dimensional position.
dominio.observaciones: For example: GLONASS, GPS, WAAS, or EGNOS.

dominio.definicion: An identified location on an aerodrome surface where initialization of an Inertial Navigation System (INS) may take place.
A low or medium radio navigation service transmitting signals whereby the pilot of a suitably equipped aircraft can determine bearings, 'home in' on, and/or track to or from the station.
dominio.observaciones: The radio frequencies assigned to an NDB shall be selected from those available in that portion of the spectrum between 190 and 1750 kilohertz (kHz).

dominio.definicion: A military Ultra High Frequency (UHF) radio navigation service able to provide continuous bearing and Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) distance to a selected station.
dominio.observaciones: A navigation system developed by military and naval forces providing, as far as the navigating pilot is concerned and for suitably equipped aircraft, the same indication as a VOR/DME system. DME Distance is defined as the line of sight distance (slant range) from the source of a DME signal to the receiving antenna.

dominio.definicion: A Very High Frequency (VHF) radio navigation service which uses phase comparisons of a ground transmitted signal to determine bearing.
dominio.observaciones: This term is derived from the expression 'very high frequency omnidirectional radio range'.

definicion: The name of the navigation system used to measure the sounding depths.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is 80 characters in maximum length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type(s) of equipment or system used in electronic navigation.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a navigation system type.

dominio.definicion: A type of long-range position fixing radio beacon.
A high accuracy, short- to medium-range radio NAVAID intended for coastal and landfall navigation.
A radio receiver equipped with a directional sensing aerial used to take bearings on a radio transmitter.
A low frequency electronic position fixing system using pulsed transmissions at 100 kilohertz.
A long-range radio navigational aid, which operates within the VLF band.
dominio.observaciones: The system comprises eight land-based stations.

dominio.definicion: A type of radar transponder commonly used to mark maritime navigational hazards.
dominio.observaciones: When a RACON receives a radar pulse, it responds with a signal on the same frequency that leaves an image on the plan position indicator (PPI) radar display that radiates from the centre of the display to its edge. This takes the form of a short line of dots and dashes forming a Morse character radiating away from the location of the beacon.

dominio.definicion: A system for detecting the presence of objects at a distance and determining their position or motion by transmitting short radio waves and detecting or measuring the return of these after being reflected by the objects.
Transmitting and/or receiving radio-frequency electromagnetic waves as a means of communication.
A radio apparatus resembling a telephone but operating by means of radio waves transmitted between the instruments.
A system for reproducing on a screen visual images transmitted (usually with sound) by radio signals.

An L/MF or UHF radio beacon transmitting non-directional (omnidirectional) signals whereby the pilot of an aircraft equipped with direction finding equipment can determine his bearing to or from the radio beacon and 'home' on, or track to or from, the station.

dominio.etiqueta: Non-Directional Radio Beacon (NDB) with Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) (NDB/DME)
dominio.definicion: A non-directional radio beacon combined with distance measuring equipment.
A radio navigation service which uses phase comparisons of a ground transmitted signal to determine bearing.
dominio.observaciones: This term is derived from the words 'very high frequency omnidirectional radio range'.

dominio.etiqueta: VHF Omnidirectional Radio Beacon (VOR) with Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) (VOR/DME)
dominio.definicion: The colocation of a VHF Omnidirectional Radio beacon (VOR) with Distance Measuring Equipment (DME).

dominio.etiqueta: VHF Omnidirectional Radio Beacon (VOR) with Tactical Air Navigation Aid (TACAN) (VORTAC)
dominio.definicion: A facility consisting of two components, a VHF Omnidirectional Radio beacon (VOR) and a Tactical Air Navigation Aid (TACAN), that provides three individual services: VOR azimuth, TACAN azimuth and TACAN distance (Distance Measuring Equipemnt: DME) at one site.
dominio.observaciones: Although consisting of more than one component, incorporating more than one operating frequency, and using more than one antenna system, a VORTAC is considered to be a unified navigational aid.

dominio.definicion: A military Ultra High Frequency (UHF) radio navigation service able to provide continuous bearing and Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) distance to a selected station.
dominio.observaciones: A navigation system developed by military and naval forces providing, as far as the navigating pilot is concerned and for suitably equipped aircraft, the same indication as a VOR/DME system. The DME distance is defined as the line of sight distance (slant range) from the source of a DME signal to the receiving antenna.

dominio.definicion: A combination of radio navigation services intended to facilitate aircraft in landing by providing lateral and vertical guidance including indications of distance from the optimum point of landing.
dominio.observaciones: A precision instrument approach system which normally consists of the following electronic components and visual aids: localizer, glide slope, outer marker, middle marker, and approach lights.

dominio.etiqueta: Instrument Landing System (ILS) with Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) (ILS/DME)
dominio.definicion: A combination of radio navigation services intended to facilitate aircraft in landing by providing lateral and vertical guidance including indications of distance from the optimum point of landing that is collocated with Distance Measuring Equipment (DME).

A component of an Instrument Landing System (ILS) consisting of a Very High Frequency (VHF) transmitter, radiating signals in the direction served by the ILS, and providing a straight line azimuth path in the horizontal plane containing the centre line of the runway.
The colocation of Instrument Landing System Localizer (LOC) equipment with Distance Measuring Equipment (DME).
A directional aid facility providing only lateral guidance (front or back course) for approach from a final approach fix.
dominio.observaciones: The Simplified Directional Facility (SDF) antenna may be offset from the runway centerline. Because of this, the angle of convergence between the final approach course and the runway bearing should be determined by reference to the instrument approach procedure chart. This angle is generally not more than 3 degrees. However, it should be noted that inasmuch as the approach course originates at the antenna site, an approach which is continued beyond the runway threshold will lead the aircraft to the SDF offset position rather than along the runway centerline.

dominio.definicion: A precision approach and landing guidance system operating in the microwave spectrum, which provides position information and various ground-to-air data; the position information is provided in a wide coverage sector and is determined by an azimuth angle measurement, an elevation angle measurement and a range (distance) measurement.
dominio.observaciones: A precision instrument approach system operating in the microwave spectrum that normally consists of three components: an azimuth station, an elevation station, and precision Distance Measuring Equipment (DME).

dominio.definicion: An electronic navigation system transmitting a 75 megahertz bone-shaped radiation pattern.
An instrument for sending radio-telegrams.
The antenna of a radio detection device that provides information on range, azimuth, and/or elevation of objects.
Radar equipment used to detect and display azimuth, elevation, and range of aircraft on the final approach course to a runway.

dominio.etiqueta: Visual Flight Rules (VFR) Test Signal Maker

dominio.definicion: A radio transmitter which emits a distinctive, or characteristic, signal that may be used for the determination of bearings, courses, or location, where the nature and/or purpose of the signal is unknown.
A wide-band beacon that transmits either continuously or periodically on the radar bands and is used to mark maritime navigational hazards.
dominio.observaciones: The transmission forms a line of Morse characters on a plan position indicator (PPI) radar display that radiates from the centre of the display to its edge. Periodic transmissions every few seconds are often used so that important radar targets behind the RAMARK beacon are not masked by the Morse characters.

dominio.definicion: Ultra High Frequency (UHF) ground equipment used in conjunction with airborne equipment, operating on the interrogation-answer principle where the time required for the round trip of the signal exchange is measured in the airborne Distance Measuring Equipment (DME) unit and translated into DME distance.
dominio.observaciones: The DME distance is defined as the line of sight distance (slant range) from the source of a DME signal to the receiving antenna.

dominio.definicion: A component of a Microwave Landing System (MLS) consisting of a Super High Frequency (SHF) transmitter radiating signals to provide a lateral position indication to an aircraft approaching the runway.

A component of a Microwave Landing System (MLS) consisting of a Super High Frequency (SHF) transmitter radiating signals to provide a vertical position indication as an angular value to an aircraft approaching the runway.

Airport Surveillance Radar (ASR) is designed to provide relatively short-range coverage in the general vicinity of an aerodrome and to serve as an expeditious means of handling terminal area traffic through observation of precise aircraft locations on a radarscope.
A device normally placed near the threshold of a runway that is used for reflecting radar signals when conducting a Precision Approach Radar (PAR) approach.

A component of an Instrument Landing System (ILS) consisting of an Ultra High Frequency (UHF) transmitter radiating signals and providing a straight line descent path in the vertical plane containing the centreline of the runway served by the ILS, and thereby furnishing descent information down to the lowest authorized decision height or to the surface of a runway, depending on the Facility Performance Category of the ILS.
dominio.observaciones: The descent information is that locus of points in the vertical plane containing the runway centreline at which the receiver indicator deflection is zero.

dominio.definicion: A marker beacon used in conjunction with the backcourse of a localizer.
dominio.observaciones: Identification signals of marker beacons used in conjunction with the back course of a localizer shall be clearly distinguishable from the inner, middle and outer marker beacon identifications.

dominio.definicion: A radio navigation service identifying a particular location in space by means of a 75 MHz transmitter which transmits a directional signal to be received by aircraft flying overhead.
A type of marker radiobeacon, the emissions of which radiate in a vertical fan-shaped pattern for general use.
A marker beacon that defines a point along the glide slope of an Instrument Landing System (ILS) normally located at or near the decision height of an ILS Category I approach.
dominio.observaciones: The signal is keyed to transmit alternate dots and dashes at the rate of 95 dot/dash combinations per minute on a 1300 Hz modulation frequency. The signal can be received aurally and visually by compatible airborne equipment. The middle marker should be located so as to indicate, in low visibility conditions, the missed approach point, and the point that visual contact with the runway is imminent.

dominio.definicion: A marker beacon that defines a point along the glide slope of an Instrument Landing System (ILS) normally located at or near the decision height of an ILS Category I approach.
dominio.observaciones: The signal is keyed to transmit two dashes per second on a 400 Hz modulation frequency. The signal can be received aurally and visually by compatible airborne equipment. The outer marker is normally located four to seven miles from the runway threshold on the extended centerline of the runway.

dominio.definicion: A Non-Directional Radio Beacon (NDB) used as an Instrument Landing System (ILS) Outer Marker.
A Non-Directional Radio Beacon (NDB) used as an Instrument Landing System (ILS) Middle Marker.
Global System for Mobiles; used as a method of location positioning in conjunction with GPS.

dominio.etiqueta: Instrument Landing System (ILS) Glide Slope with Distance Measuring Equipment (DME)
dominio.definicion: The colocation of Instrument Landing System (ILS) glide slope equipment with Distance Measuring Equipment (DME).
A marker beacon used with an Instrument Landing System (ILS) CAT II precision approach located between the middle marker and the end of the ILS runway.
dominio.observaciones: The signal is keyed at six dots per second on a 3000 Hz modulation frequency. The signal can be received both aurally and visually by compatible airborne equipment that it is at the designated decision height (DH), normally 100 feet above the touchdown zone elevation, on the ILS CAT II approach. It also marks progress during a CAT III approach.

definicion: The name of the nearest settlement to the feature.
descripcion: A settlement is understood as to be important enough to be a centre of potential resources.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The cloudiness or haziness of a volume of solution as determined by its degree of light scattering.
descripcion: Turbidity is caused by suspended solids that are generally invisible to the naked eye, for example: suspended clay, silt, organic and inorganic matter, and plankton and other microorganisms. The units of turbidity from a calibrated nephelometer (based on the scattering of a focused beam of light) are called Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU).

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A dimensionless physical quantity, one which has no unit of measure.

definicion: The season(s) in which a nomadic people are camped at a given location.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a nomadic seasonal location.

dominio.definicion: The fourth and coldest season of the year, coming between autumn and spring; reckoned astronomically from the winter solstice to the vernal equinox.
dominio.observaciones: For example, in the northern hemisphere, nominally from December 21 to March 21.

dominio.definicion: The second and warmest season of the year, coming between spring and autumn; reckoned astronomically from the summer solstice to the autumnal equinox.
dominio.observaciones: For example, in the northern hemisphere, nominally from June 21 to September 21.

dominio.definicion: The first season of the year, coming between winter and summer, reckoned astronomically from the vernal equinox to the summer solstice.
dominio.observaciones: For example, in the northern hemisphere, nominally from March 21 to June 21.

dominio.definicion: The third season of the year, coming between summer and winter, reckoned astronomically from the autumnal equinox to the winter solstice.
dominio.observaciones: For example, in the northern hemisphere, nominally from September 21 to December 21.

definicion: The density of non-mine-like bottom objects (NOMBO) per square mile.
descripcion: Reference NATO Publication ATP 24(c) Vol 1.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a NOMBO density measure.

dominio.definicion: 1-4 NOMBO per square nautical mile.
5-8 NOMBO per square nautical mile.
9-14 NOMBO per square nautical mile.
15 NOMBO per square nautical mile, or more.

definicion: The maximum distance at which a light can be seen (or signal detected) in a homogeneous atmosphere in which the meteorological visibility is 10 nautical miles (clear weather as defined by the International Visibility Code).
descripcion: The actual luminous range will be lesser (or occasionally greater) than the nominal range depending on prevailing weather conditions. The lesser of the geographic range and the luminous range is the range at which a light will first be sighted.

datatype.definicion: An integer domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is an integer. For example, 6 (as in the length of a fathom in feet).
datatype.nota: The realization of this integer datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of primary structure of an offshore construction upon which various pieces of operation-specific equipment are affixed.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an offshore construction primary structure.

dominio.definicion: A working surface that is raised well above the waves.
dominio.observaciones: The 'surface' may consist of multiple levels, shapes, and configurations, often resulting in a complex configuration tailored to the specific operations supported.

dominio.definicion: A large buoy that serves as both a single point mooring and supports equipment used for the transfer of fluids (for example: liquefied petroleum gas) between a vessel and pipelines leading to facilities ashore or to wells below.
dominio.observaciones: It may be as large as 10 metres across, is moored by multiple cables, and supports one or more submarine hose strings (individually termed 'riser') connecting to pipelines on the waterbody bottom. When in use floating hoses connect to the vessel which is free to 'weather-vane' around the buoy in response to environmental conditions.

dominio.definicion: A specialized buoy that is shaped as a short, wide cylinder on top of which is a rotating turntable to which equipment is affixed (for example: a hose connection) and serves a single point mooring.
dominio.observaciones: The mooring system consists of a number of anchor chains (typically six or eight) laid radial from the buoy. An attached vessel is free to 'weather-vane' around the buoy in response to environmental conditions.

dominio.definicion: A large buoy-like device that is pulled into and temporarily secured in a mating cone on the underside of a vessel.
dominio.observaciones: Internal to the buoy is a turret with connections to the mooring and riser systems. The outer buoy hull can rotate freely with the vessel around the turret by means of internal turret bearings. The internal swivel (a rotating connector) transfers well streams, water, gas, signals and power from the geo-stationary risers to the piping system (for example: to an onboard process plant) of the freely weather-vaning vessel.

dominio.definicion: A vessel-based facility that is self-propelled.
dominio.observaciones: Usually capable of producing petroleum and/or natural gas from underwater wells and storing and offloading it into shuttle tankers.

dominio.definicion: A barge-based facility that is not self-propelled.
dominio.observaciones: May be used to support a rig in relatively placid waters after towing to a site.

definicion: The means by which a offshore construction is supported above the water level.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an offshore construction support structure.

dominio.definicion: A site that has been reclaimed as land.
dominio.observaciones: Usually accomplished by the dumping of earth and other material (for example: dredged fill).

dominio.definicion: A structure consisting of a single column extending downwards into the water.
dominio.observaciones: The column is usually affixed to the waterbody floor.

dominio.definicion: A structure consisting of multiple (commonly three or four) columns extending downwards into the water.
dominio.observaciones: The columns may be affixed to the waterbody floor (termed a 'submersible rig') or may terminate in underwater flotation tanks (termed a 'semi-submersible rig') to provide dynamic stability and be moored in place.

dominio.definicion: A structure based on a series of trusses (diagonal frameworks) assembled in various configurations.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a jackup rig. There may be a single wide tower or an array of narrower towers.

definicion: The type of an offshore platform based on its structure and/or use(s).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an offshore platform type.

dominio.definicion: A temporary mobile structure, either fixed or floating, used in the exploration stages of oil and gas fields.
A permanent offshore structure equipped to control the flow of oil or gas or exploit natural resources.
A platform from which surroundings or events can be observed, noted or recorded such as for scientific study.
A metal lattice tower, buoyant at one end and attached at the other by a universal joint to a concrete-filled base on the sea bed.
dominio.observaciones: The platform may be fitted with a helicopter platform, emergency accommodation and hawser and/or hose retrieval.

dominio.definicion: A rigid frame or tube with a buoyancy device at its upper end, secured at its lower end to a universal joint on a large steel or concrete base resting on the sea bed, and at its upper end to a mooring buoy by a chain or wire.
A platform secured to the sea bed and surmounted by a turntable to which ships moor.
A man-made structure usually built for the exploration or exploitation of marine resources (for example: marine scientific research or tidal observations).

dominio.etiqueta: Floating Production, Storage and Off-loading (FPSO) Vessel
dominio.definicion: An offshore oil and/or gas facility consisting of a moored tanker/barge by which the product is extracted, stored and exported.
A platform used primarily for eating, sleeping and recreation purposes.
Supports a navigation aid (for example: a towered light).
dominio.observaciones: May be of significant size (for example: large enough for a helicopter to land). For example, Chesapeake Light.

dominio.definicion: Platform for defence purposes (for example: anti-aircraft defence).
A mooring structure used by tankers to load and unload in port approaches or in offshore oil and/or gas fields.
dominio.observaciones: The size of the structure may vary between that of a large mooring buoy and that of a manned structure that may be either floating or fixed to the sea bed.

definicion: The method by which the position of an offshore construction is maintained.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting an offshore positioning method.

dominio.definicion: Located in a firm, fixed position through rigid attachment to the waterbody floor.

dominio.definicion: Floating on the water surface and attached to the waterbody floor with moorings (for example: cables fastened to anchors).
dominio.observaciones: The accuracy of position maintenance will depend on wave height and tidal effects.

dominio.definicion: Floating on the water surface and maintained in position dynamically using on-board propulsion.
dominio.observaciones: Usually there is a system of waterbody floor beacons that are used to measure horizontal motion and thus signal required changes in thrust in order for the vessel to maintain position with the desired degree of accuracy.

definicion: An indication that a standard omnidirectional departure is authorised.
descripcion: The omnidirectional departure is a standard means of departing an aerodrome under instrument flight rule conditions. It is designed to assure that the aircraft has appropriate obstacle clearance at all times from the departure end of the runway to the first point along the predetermined flight plan. The basic procedure for this departure is that the aircraft is to fly the runway heading after takeoff until reaching an altitude of 120 metres (394 feet), and only after reaching this altitude can the aircraft initiate a turn towards the predetermined fligth plan.

datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.4.1, Combinations of date and time of day - Complete representation - Extended format, a calendar date and time representation, as a single data element comprising up to twenty characters, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, [hh] the ordinal number of an hour within the calendar day, [mm] the ordinal number of a minute within the hour, [ss] the ordinal number of a second within the minute, and an optional 'Z' when the time is according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12' for 12 April 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412T114520Z').

datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.5.4.1, Representation of time-intervals identified by start and end - Extended format, as a single data element comprising up to forty-one characters, using an expression in accordance with 5.5.2 combining any two date and time of the day representations as defined in 5.4.1, as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ/YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z/1985-07-01T08:23:50Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985 through 8 hours, 23 minutes and 50 seconds UTC on 1 July 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12/1985-07-01' for 12 April 1985 through 1 July 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412/19850701'). Either of the dates may be left unspecified by the use of '--------' (for example: '19850412/--------' for 12 April 1985 through an unspecified ending date).

datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.2.1, Calendar date - month, as a single data element comprising four digits, where the first [MM] represents the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, and the second [MM] the ordinal number of a subsequent calendar month within the same or subsequent calendar year, as 'MMMM' (for example: '0309' for March through September). Either of the months may be left unspecified by the use of '--' (for example: '11--' for November through an unspecified ending month).

definicion: The month interval in which seasonal restrictions (for example: due to climate) are present.
descripcion: For example, a port may be closed during the months of October through April due to ice blockage.

descripcion: The pH (potential of Hydrogen) scale provides an indication of the acidity or alkalinity of a water sample. The scale ranges from 0 to 14, where 7 is neutral, greater than 7 is more alkaline and less than 7 is more acidic. The measure is termed the 'pH unit'.

definicion: The physical condition of a man-made structure, as a whole, including the inside and/or outside of the structure and any contained and/or associated equipment.
descripcion: The physical condition applies to any phase of the life cycle of a man-made structure from construction to destruction. Examples of man-made structures include roads, canals, buildings, towers, aerodromes and facilities.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a physical condition.

dominio.definicion: The man-made structure is being built or undergoing renovation or repair.
dominio.observaciones: Incorporates site preparations, building of new construction and the renovation or repair of existing structures.

dominio.definicion: The man-made structure is complete and intact.
dominio.observaciones: The man-made structure may or may not be in operation or use.

dominio.definicion: The man-made structure is left in place to deteriorate.
dominio.observaciones: The man-made structure has been abandoned and no maintenance or repairs are being carried out. While the structure is physically intact, no signs of operation are visible.

dominio.definicion: The man-made structure is damaged.
dominio.observaciones: Damage may be a consequence of accident, military action, or natural disaster. The damaged man-made structure can be repaired.

dominio.definicion: The man-made structure has undergone a systematic selective removal of components.
dominio.observaciones: Low value components and/or equipment may remain. The man-made structure cannot be repaired without a great deal of time and effort.

dominio.definicion: The man-made structure has undergone complete destruction and is in a state of total disrepair.
dominio.observaciones: Destruction may be a consequence of military action, natural disaster, planned demolition or a long period of no maintenance. A destroyed man-made structure can only be restored by complete reconstruction.

definicion: The physical state of a feature.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a physical state category.

dominio.definicion: Composed of a substance of fixed shape and volume.
Composed of a substance that flows and takes a shape determined by its container while occupying the same volume (rather than dispersing like a gaseous substance).
dominio.observaciones: A gas may be in such a state by reason of low temperature or high pressure.

dominio.definicion: Composed of an airlike fluid that can change its volume indefinitely.
dominio.observaciones: Especially used to describe substances that do not become liquid or solid at ordinary temperatures.

definicion: Specifies a resource site where a pictorial representation of a feature is available.

dominio.observaciones: A linear piling is sometimes termed 'row of piles' which is either a linear arrangement of individual piles, or 'sheet piling' consisting of a series of connecting tall metal sheets interlocked so as to form a barrier.

dominio.observaciones: For example, transport of natural gas, oil, or coal slurry.

dominio.definicion: A pipe (generally a sewer or drainage pipe) discharging in to the sea or a river.
A pipe taking water from a river or other body of water.
dominio.observaciones: For example, to supply an aqueduct or a water treatment facility.

dominio.definicion: A pipe in a sewage system for carrying water or sewage to a disposal area.

dominio.observaciones: May be used for flood control and/or as a source of water for irrigation, industrial processes, and/or human consumption.

dominio.definicion: A small reservoir where solid matter is precipitated from a liquid by evaporating or settling.
A pond for the treatment of water that consists of a bed of material (for example: sand) where water is filtered.

Consisting of from 21 to 99 habitation places.
Consisting of from 100 to 400 habitation places.

dominio.definicion: A central place of upper level (with highest centrality for its sphere of influence).
dominio.observaciones: For example, a capital of country.

dominio.definicion: A central place of medium level (with medium centrality for its minor sphere of influence).
dominio.observaciones: For example, a district town.

dominio.definicion: A central place of lower level (with low centrality for its small sphere of influence).
dominio.observaciones: For example, a small town or market town in rural area.

definicion: The arrangement (pattern) of a populated place based on the distribution of buildings.

dominio.definicion: Regular arrangement with rectangular placement of parcels and streets.
An irregularly structured arrangement with areas of concentration.
Parcels and streets are predominantly aligned to a central square.
dominio.observaciones: For example: a circular village, a green village, a village with a rectilinear square.

Isolated houses or sparsely arranged groups of houses.

dominio.observaciones: Usually located on the outskirts of the built-up area. The shacks are generally crude, improvised, and made from salvaged materials.

dominio.definicion: The temporary quarters of nomads, travellers, and/or troops, consisting of portable tent shelters.
A self-contained group of houses and associated buildings, usually in a country area.
An inhabited place larger and more regularly built and with more complete and independent local government than a village but not created a city.
A major town inhabited by a large permanent community with all essential services.
An area predominantly occupied by man-made structures used for residential, recreational, commercial, and/or industrial purposes.
A complex for holiday-makers with cottages, shops, and entertainment, on site.

dominio.definicion: A site containing one or more historical and/or culturally significant buildings and/or other structures.
A facility devoted to religion; exhibiting the spiritual or practical effects of religion, following the requirements of a religion.
A city that is the seat of an administrative authority.
dominio.observaciones: Administrative authorities may be governmental or non-governmental.

dominio.definicion: A city that is the official seat of the government of a nation State.

For example, Netherlands - Seat of Government: Den Haag, Capital: Amsterdam; Bolivia - Seat of Government: La Paz, Capital: Sucre; Chile - Seat of Government: Valparaiso, Capital: Santiago de Chile; Malaysia - Seat of Government: Putrajaya, Capital: Kuala Lumpur.

A populated place with predominantly harbour-facilities, apart from its residential function.

A populated place with predominantly facilities according to traffic affairs.
A populated place located at a border to a adjacent state with border-crossing traffic importance.
A populated place with predominantly rude dwellings used by the aborigines of a region.
A populated place predominantly consisting of transportable homes, subject to a seasonal change of location.

Zone of tropical coastal woodlands on tidal flats.
Zone above 1000 metres; characterized by coniferous forests.
Zone with high density and variety of vegetation, characterized by heavy and regular precipitation as well as high temperatures.

datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.5, Time-intervals, as a single data element comprising up to seventeen characters, where the first [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, and [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month of the start of the time interval, followed by a solidus '/', followed by the second [YYYY] representing a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, and [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month of the end of the time interval as 'YYYYMMDD/YYYYMMDD' (for example: '19850412/19871007' for 12 April 1985 through 7 October 1987). Either of the dates may be left unspecified by the use of '--------' (for example: '19861201/--------' for 1 December 1986 through an unspecified ending date). Other truncated date representations in accordance with ISO 8601:2000 may be used.

dominio.definicion: Composed of or containing calcium or calcium carbonate.

dominio.definicion: Being of greater than average size.
dominio.observaciones: For example, large boulders.

dominio.definicion: Abounding in rocks.
dominio.observaciones: The rocks may be lying free on a swept surface or partially embedded in sediments.

dominio.definicion: Being below the average in size.
dominio.observaciones: For example, small rocks.

dominio.definicion: Flecked with small spots of contrasting colour.

definicion: The maximum allowed altitude for the flight procedure segment.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of length equal to 0.3048 metres.

definicion: The date and time, or range of date and time, on or over which a process step occurred.
descripcion: A process step is an event or transformation in the life of a dataset that is used to define, review and/or update the digital representation of a feature and/or attribute.

datatype.nombre: Process Step Date and Time Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a process step date and time.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: For a single date and time, formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.4.1, Combinations of date and time of day - Complete representation - Extended format, a calendar date and time representation, as a single data element comprising up to twenty characters, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, [hh] the ordinal number of an hour within the calendar day, [mm] the ordinal number of a minute within the hour, [ss] the ordinal number of a second within the minute, and an optional 'Z' when the time is according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12' for 12 April 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412T114520Z'). For a range of date and time, formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.5.4.1, Representation of time-intervals identified by start and end - Extended format, as a single data element comprising up to forty-one characters, using an expression in accordance with 5.5.2 combining any two date and time of the day representations as defined in 5.4.1, as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ/YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z/1985-07-01T08:23:50Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985 through 8 hours, 23 minutes and 50 seconds UTC on 1 July 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12/1985-07-01' for 12 April 1985 through 1 July 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412/19850701'). Either of the dates may be left unspecified by the use of '--------' (for example: '19850412/--------' for 12 April 1985 through an unspecified ending date).

definicion: A narrative or other textual description of a process step, including related processing parameters and/or tolerances.
descripcion: A process step is an event or transformation in the life of a dataset that is used to define, review and/or update the digital representation of a feature and/or attribute. No restriction is placed on the length of the description.

datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a process step description.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: A value representing a process step description, as specified by ISO 19115:2003, LI_ProcessStep.description.

definicion: The identity of, and means of communication with, person(s) and/or organisation(s) associated with a process step.
descripcion: A process step is an event or transformation in the life of a dataset that is used to define, review and/or update the digital representation of a feature and/or attribute.

datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a process step processor.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: A value representing a processor, as specified by ISO 19115:2003, B.3.2.1 Line 374, CI_Responsible Party.

definicion: A narrative or other textual description of the requirement or purpose for a process step.
descripcion: A process step is an event or transformation in the life of a dataset that is used to define, review and/or update the digital representation of a feature and/or attribute. No restriction is placed on the length of the rationale.

datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a process step rationale.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: A value representing a process step rationale, as specified by ISO 19115:2003, LI_ProcessStep.rationale.

definicion: The principal product(s) resulting from a production, mining, or agricultural activity.
descripcion: If multiple products are specified then they are usually listed in descending order of importance.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a product.

dominio.definicion: A machine that can be flown in the air.
dominio.observaciones: For example, an aeroplane or a helicopter.

dominio.definicion: A light silvery ductile and malleable metal, not readily tarnished by air, which is a chemical element, atomic number 13. (Symbol Al.)
Military stores or supplies consisting of projectiles (for example: bullets, shells, and/or grenades) and propellants.
Black or brownish-black, solid or viscous, bituminous pitch, of natural occurrence or produced from petroleum.
A road vehicle.
dominio.observaciones: Usually powered by an internal-combustion engine, but occasionally by electricity.

dominio.definicion: The hollow stem of numerous, mainly tropical, giant grasses belonging to the genus Bambusa and various related genera.
dominio.observaciones: Used as a stick or as a material in manufacture.

dominio.definicion: The edible finger-shaped pulpy fruit of any of various tropical and subtropical plants of the genus Musa (family Musaceae), borne in clusters and yellow-skinned when ripe.
Basalt in the form of blocks, slabs, and other shapes for use in construction (for example: building or paving).
dominio.observaciones: A dark, fine-grained, igneous rock, often displaying columnar structure and usually composed largely of plagioclase with pyroxene and olivine.

dominio.definicion: An earthy rock consisting of hydrated alumina with variable proportions of iron oxides and other impurities.
dominio.observaciones: The major commercial source of aluminium.

dominio.definicion: A member of the class Bivalvia, having a shell of two parts hinged together by a ligament.
dominio.observaciones: For example, clams, scallops, oysters, and mussels.

dominio.definicion: Clay kneaded, moulded, and baked or sun-dried, used as a building material.
Containing calcium carbonate and/or other, usually insoluble, calcium salt.
A powdered substance, usually consisting of a strong mortar of calcined lime and clay, mixed with water and applied as a paste which hardens into a stony consistency.
dominio.observaciones: Used for binding together stones and/or bricks and for forming structures (for example: floors and/or walls).

dominio.definicion: A distinct substance obtained by or used in a chemical process.
A stiff tenacious fine-grained earth consisting mainly of hydrated aluminosilicates, which become more plastic when water is added and can be moulded and dried.
dominio.observaciones: Used to make bricks and/or pottery.

dominio.definicion: A hard opaque black or blackish mineral, mainly carbonized plant matter, found in seams or strata at or below the Earth's surface.
dominio.observaciones: Used as fuel and in manufacture (for example: to produce gas and/or tar).

dominio.definicion: Water-worn rounded stones, especially of the size used for paving.

The seeds obtained from any of certain members of the paleotropical genus Coffea (especially Coffea arabica), of the madder family, that bear white flowers succeeded by red berries each containing two seeds.
dominio.observaciones: May be either raw or roasted (and ground).

dominio.definicion: Coal deprived by dry distillation of its volatile constituents.
A heavy-duty building material made from a mixture of broken stone or gravel, sand, cement, and water, that forms a stonelike mass on hardening.
A coarse-grained sedimentary rock composed of rounded fragments embedded in a matrix of a cementing material such as silica.
Goods that are used or bought for use primarily for personal, family, and/or household purposes.
dominio.observaciones: These goods include, for example, food, clothing, automobiles, television sets, and appliances.

dominio.definicion: A malleable and ductile reddish metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 29. (Symbol Cu.)
dominio.observaciones: Used especially for electrical conductors and as the base of alloys.

dominio.definicion: A usually hard calcareous substance secreted by many marine polyps as an external skeleton for support and habitation.
dominio.observaciones: Occurs in both single specimens and extensive accumulations. A similar substance may be produced by other lime-secreting marine organisms.

dominio.definicion: The soft white fibrous substance which surrounds the seeds of various plants of the tropical and subtropical genus Gossypium.
dominio.observaciones: Used for making thread and cloth.

dominio.definicion: Any member of the large class Crustacea of mainly aquatic, hard-shelled arthropods.
dominio.observaciones: For example, crab, lobster, and shrimp.

dominio.definicion: Any farmed aquatic invertebrate animal whose outer covering is a shell, usually a mollusc (for example: an oyster) or a crustacean (for example: a crab, a prawn, or a shrimp).
Pearl formed by an oyster after the insertion of a suitable foreign body.
Water from which the salt has been removed (especially seawater).
A usually colourless or lightly tinted precious stone of great brilliance, hardness, and value, occurring chiefly in alluvial deposits.
dominio.observaciones: The hardest naturally occurring substance, commonly used for cutting and abrading.

dominio.definicion: A soft, friable, porous material consisting of fossilized microscopic unicellular alga that have rigid siliceous cell walls.
dominio.observaciones: Used for filters and insulation.

dominio.definicion: Dolomite in the form of blocks, slabs, and other shapes for use in construction (for example: building or paving).
dominio.observaciones: A sedimentary rock composed chiefly of a hexagonal carbonate of calcium, magnesium, and usually iron that occurs as translucent crystals of various colours, alone or with calcite.

dominio.definicion: Power in the form of an electric current.
dominio.observaciones: Also, the product of electromotive force (voltage) and electric current.

dominio.definicion: Any chemical compound, mixture, and/or device the primary or common purpose of which is to function by explosion, that is with substantially instantaneous release of gas and/or heat.
Any of a large and varied group of cold-blooded aquatic vertebrates possessing gills and fins.
Substance(s) (to be) taken into the body to maintain life and growth.
Water solidified by exposure to cold.
dominio.observaciones: For example, snow or ice.

dominio.definicion: The edible product of a tree, shrub, or other plant, consisting of the seed and its envelope.
dominio.observaciones: May be either pulpy or covered by a woody, hard shell (termed a nut).

dominio.definicion: A gaseous hydrocarbon or hydrocarbon mixture that is suitable for burning in order to provide heat, light, or power.
Refined petroleum as used as a fuel in motor vehicles.
A substance made by fusing soda and/or potash with other ingredients.
dominio.observaciones: Usually transparent, lustrous, hard, and brittle.

dominio.definicion: A precious metal which is characterized by its yellowish colour, resistance to tarnishing and corrosion, and great malleability and ductility, and is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 79 (symbol Au).
Collectively, the fruit or seeds of cereal grasses.
dominio.observaciones: For example, corn and wheat.

dominio.definicion: Granite in the form of blocks, slabs, and other shapes for use in construction (for example: building or paving).
dominio.observaciones: Any of a broad class of granular crystalline plutonic rocks, consisting essentially of quartz, orthoclase, feldspar, and mica or hornblende.

dominio.definicion: Plant material (for example: straw and/or tall coarse grass), possibly also containing the slices of soil to which the plant material is attached.
Small water-worn or pounded stones.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes with an intermixture of sand and/or clay. Used for laying paths and roads.

dominio.definicion: Greenstone in the form of blocks, slabs, and other shapes for use in construction (for example: building or paving).
dominio.observaciones: Any igneous rock of dark-green appearance, especially containing chlorite, epidote, and/or hornblende. Includes nephrites and, in particular, jade.

dominio.definicion: Ground calcareous remains of macroscopic marine animals.
A form of energy arising from the random motion of molecules and capable of transmission by conduction, convection, or radiation.
Frozen water, a brittle transparent crystalline solid.
A malleable, magnetic, readily oxidizable metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 26. (Symbol Fe.)
dominio.observaciones: Occurs abundantly in certain ores and in meteorites, and is widely used, chiefly in alloys such as steel.

dominio.definicion: A soft, heavy, malleable, bluish-grey metal that is a chemical element, atomic number 82, occurring in galena and other minerals. (Symbol Pb.)
