dominio.definicion: Loose fragmented solid material ejected from a volcano.
The transparent, colourless, tasteless, odourless, liquid compound of hydrogen and oxygen (formula H2O).
dominio.observaciones: Forms the main constituent of seas, lakes, rivers, and rain, and is put to many domestic and industrial uses.

dominio.definicion: The hard, compact, fibrous substance of which the roots, trunks, and branches of trees and shrubs consist.
dominio.observaciones: Consists largely of secondary xylem, which forms the strengthening and water-transporting tissue of the plant.

dominio.definicion: Pieces of wood separated by a cutting instrument, usually in large volume.
dominio.observaciones: For example, chips for use in manufacturing pressed board.

dominio.definicion: A hard lustrous bluish-white metallic chemical element, atomic number 30, which is obtained from sphalerite and other ores. (Symbol Zn.)
dominio.observaciones: Used for roofing, galvanizing iron, and making alloys with copper.

dominio.definicion: Water from which all contaminants have been removed through a process of distillation.
Stony and/or silaceous coral.
White soft earthy limestone consisting almost wholly of calcite and derived chiefly from microscopic salt water fossil shells and fragments.
Fine yellowish-grey loam composed of material transported by the wind.

A rhizopod of the chiefly marine order Foraminiferida, typically having a calcareous shell with perforations (foramina) through which pseudopodia extend, the fossils forming a major constituent of chalk and many marine oozes.
White to gray accumulation on lake bottoms caused by precipitation of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) mixed with microscopic fresh water fossil shells and fragments.
Mosslike colonies of sessile, polypoid aquatic animals that reproduce by budding.
Marine protozoa with amoeba-like bodies and radiating filamentous pseudopods.
A sedimentary rock consisting of angular, coarse-grained fragments cemented together by a fine-grained matrix (for example: by lime).
An igneous rock chemically the same as basalt and gabbro but medium-grained with a usually ophitic texture.
dominio.observaciones: Usually dark coloured and fine or medium textured. Occurs in minor intrusions such as sills and dykes.

dominio.definicion: A foliated, usually coarse-grained, metamorphic rock in which bands of granular minerals alternate with bands of flaky or prismatic ones.
dominio.observaciones: Formed by the metamorphism of granite and other igneous rocks, and typically consisting of feldspar, quartz, and mica. Usually of a streaked, wavy or banded appearance.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock composed chiefly of calcium carbonate.
dominio.observaciones: Yields lime when calcined and is used as a building material and in the making of cement.

dominio.definicion: The milk of ruminants (for example: cows, goats, and sheep) used as food for humans.
dominio.observaciones: Generally, an opaque white or bluish-white fluid secreted by the mammary glands of female mammals for nourishing their young.

dominio.definicion: A extremely compact, hard, granular rock consisting essentially of quartz.
dominio.observaciones: It is a metamorphosed sandstone in which the siliceous element is often so blended with the quartz grains so as to give the rock a nearly homogenous texture.

dominio.definicion: A dense, fine-grained, metamorphic rock that develops a characteristic cleavage which may be at any angle with the original bedding plane.
dominio.observaciones: Typically dark grey, blue, or green in colour. Splits readily into smooth parallel-sided flat plates, and used for making tiles for roofing and flooring.

dominio.definicion: The stems or stalks of certain cereals, chiefly wheat, barley, oats, and rye, especially when dry and separated by threshing.
dominio.observaciones: Used as thatch, as litter and fodder for cattle, filling for bedding, and plaited or woven as material for hats and/or baskets.

dominio.definicion: Alcoholic liquor produced from fermented grape juice.
dominio.observaciones: Also, alcoholic liquor resembling wine made from the fermented juice of other fruits, or from grain, flowers, and the sap of various trees.

dominio.definicion: A mixture of crude oil (petroleum) and/or natural gas that is extracted from underground reservoirs and separated and/or cleaned as necessary before transport and use.
dominio.observaciones: After processing (for example: refining) it may be used as a primary energy source (for example: as fuel oil or natural gas) or as the raw material for chemical manufacturing (for example: the production of plastics, solvents, pesticides, or fertilizers).

dominio.definicion: A fuel made from vegetable oils (for example: soybean or canola), animal fats, and/or recycled grease, and intended for use in diesel engines.
dominio.observaciones: For U.S. Energy Information Administration reporting, it is a fuel composed of mono-alkyl esters of long chain fatty acids derived from vegetable oils or animal fats, designated B100, and meeting the requirements of American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D 6751. It can serve as a substitute for petroleum-derived diesel or distillate fuel.

dominio.definicion: Vegetable matter partly decomposed in wet acid conditions in bogs and fens to form a firm brown deposit resembling soil.

definicion: The general classification of a raw material based on its origin, composition, and/or utilization.
descripcion: For example, a metallic ore.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a raw material class.

dominio.definicion: Mineral raw material such as coal, hydrocarbons (crude oil, gas) and radioactive (uranium) raw materials for energy production purposes.
Any metallic and non-metallic element found uncombained state in the nature.
dominio.observaciones: For example: gold, copper, sulphur.

dominio.definicion: Mineral or rock that has an intrinsic value and posseses the necessary rarity, color, hardness, beauty, durability, shine, size and beauty for use in jewelry.
Non-metallic mineral for technical purposes due to their chemical and physical properties, excluding mineral fuels, salt rock and gemstones.
dominio.observaciones: For example: fluorite, quarz, felspar, graphite.

datatype.estructura: The leading character of the designator references the system providing service (for example: 'W' for WAAS, 'E' for EGNOS, and 'M' for MSAS); this is followed by the two-digit runway number. The last character, assigned starting with the letter 'A' designates the first procedure for the runway; successive letters, excluding the three letters 'C', 'L', and 'R', designate each additional procedure to the runway. For example, an aerodrome has 3 parallel runways where the left and right runways have both a straight-in procedure and an offset procedure, while the centre runway has a straight-in procedure only. The following (extreme) examples would be applicable: 'W09A' and 'W09B' would designate the two unique final approach segment data blocks to Rwy '09L'; 'W09D' would designate the final approach segment data block for Rwy '09C'; and 'W09E' and 'W09F' would designate the final approach segment data blocks for Rwy '09R'.

dominio.definicion: A Catholic denomination, originally part of the Church of the East (also called the East Syriac Church), that established peace and communion with the Church of Rome in the 16th Century.
dominio.observaciones: It retains its own distinctive theological, liturgical and canonical traditions with a single patriarch located in Baghdad and four archdioceses.

dominio.definicion: A mix of two or more religious designations, or a mix of one or more religious designations and no religious designation.
Regional and local faiths and rituals, which cannot be considered as a unit.
dominio.observaciones: Often with syncretic character.

definicion: The type of a facility, building, structure or site that is designed and designated to be used for religious activities, based on its structure and/or the principal activity for which it was designed.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a religious facility type.

dominio.definicion: A Christian church, specifically of a denomination with an episcopal hierarchy (for example: Anglican, Catholic or Lutheran), that serves as the central church of a diocese, and thus as a bishop's seat.
dominio.observaciones: As cathedrals are often particularly impressive edifices, the term is sometimes also used loosely as a designation for any large important church.

dominio.definicion: A private Christian church or similar place of worship (for example: a dedicated chamber or sanctuary within a building).
dominio.observaciones: When a free-standing building it may be smaller than a (public) church and is located on the grounds of an institution (for example: a college, a hospital, a palace, an estate, or a prison) where it may be attached to a larger building.

dominio.definicion: A Christian temple, reserved for religious or spiritual activities.
A shrine, often a whitewashed dome, marking the burial place of an Islamic holy man (who is also known as a 'marabout').
dominio.observaciones: A marabout is a personal spiritual leader in the Islam faith as practiced in West Africa, and still to a limited extent in the Maghreb. The marabout is often a scholar of the Qur'an, and many make amulets for good luck, preside at various ceremonies, and in some cases actively guide the life of the follower.

dominio.definicion: A tower providing a vantage point from which a muezzin (a servant at a mosque) can call at hours of prayer.
dominio.observaciones: Usually a tall, graceful spire, with an onion-shaped crown, connected with a mosque. May be either free standing or much taller than any surrounding support structure.

dominio.definicion: A religious centre established for missionary, evangelical, or humanitarian work.
dominio.observaciones: May be characterized by one or more dwellings, a school, a church, a hospital and/or other facilities operated by a religious group.

dominio.definicion: An Islamic temple, reserved for religious or spiritual activities.
A Hindu or Buddhist temple or sacred building, usually in the form of a many-tiered tower with stories of diminishing size, each with an ornamented projecting roof.
dominio.observaciones: It is evolved from the stupa but it can be entered and may serve a secular purpose. They are found mainly in east Asia whereas the stupa is found in India and south-east Asia.

dominio.definicion: A facility housing a community under religious vows.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a monastery or a convent.

dominio.definicion: A facility housing a specialized university-like institution for the purpose of instructing students (termed 'seminarians') in theology, often in order to prepare them for religious service (for example: congregation leadership).
dominio.observaciones: These usually, though not always, teach Christian (for example: priests or ministers) or Jewish (for example: rabbis) doctrine. Monks, nuns and/or lay people may also be instructed.
dominio.aliases: Divinity School, School of Theology, Theological College

dominio.definicion: A place of worship or devotion to a saint or deity, usually housing a relic (for example: a bone or other body part) or man-made object (for example: an icon) that is venerated for the deity, spirit or daemon that it embodies.
dominio.observaciones: May be constructed on a site which is thought to be particularly holy, as opposed to being placed for the convenience of worshippers, and consequently may be associated with the practice of pilgrimage.

dominio.definicion: A round, usually dome-shaped, Buddhist shrine topped with a cupola.
dominio.observaciones: It is intended to house relics of the Buddha, and includes such features as the torana (gateway), the vedica (fence-like enclosure), the harmika (a square platform with railings on top of the stupa), the chattrayashti (a parasol or canopy) and a circumambulatory around the stupa.

dominio.definicion: A place for Jewish worship and religious instruction.
dominio.observaciones: May also be termed a 'temple' by some Reform and conservative congregations, although Orthodox Judaism reserves that term for the Temple in Jerusalem.

dominio.definicion: A church that has been specially designated (for example: by religious authority).
dominio.observaciones: May take on a variety of shapes and sizes (for example: as a shrine, a chapel, or a temple). The term is most closely associated with The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (for example: the Salt Lake Tabernacle) but may be applied to other named churches associated with revivalism (for example: the Metropolitan Tabernacle or the Maxwell Memorial Tabernacle).

dominio.definicion: An edifice reserved for religious or spiritual activities (for example: prayer or sacrifice), or analogous rites (as in masonry).
dominio.observaciones: In some religions it is regarded as the dwelling-place of a god or gods. Many religions have specialized versions of this term (for example: a Christian church, a Mormon temple, or an Islamic mosque).

dominio.definicion: A facility housing a community of priests, religious brothers and/or religious sisters, that is meant to be the presence in the world of a group dedicated to charitable or preaching service.
dominio.observaciones: The religious orders served are mainly those in the Roman Catholic Church and, to a lesser degree, in the Anglican Communion. May be used to refer specifically to a community comprised only of religious sisters. Both religious brothers and religious sisters take vows, usually of poverty, chastity and obedience.

dominio.definicion: A facility housing a community of monks living in seclusion, adopting a strict religious and ascetic lifestyle and retreating from the world for contemplative prayer.
dominio.observaciones: The community usually follows a single rule, is governed by an abbott, and all members live together, pray together, and share all possessions.

dominio.definicion: A facility housing a community of prospective members of a religious order (termed 'novices') who have not yet been admitted to vows and have to undergo training in order to be found eligible or qualified for admission.
A secluded residence, allowing life in relative seclusion and/or isolation from society.
dominio.observaciones: The resident (termed a 'hermit') renounces wordly concerns and pleasures in order to come closer to the deity or deities they worship or revere, a form of asceticism.

dominio.definicion: A place established for temporary seclusion and a time of solitude, religious prayer and/or meditation.
dominio.observaciones: Retreats are considered essential in Buddhism and they are common in many Christian churches. They are typically conducted in a remote location (for example: at a private facility or at a monastery).

dominio.definicion: A structure within which a corpse is entombed or an area of ground in which the dead are buried.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a cemetery, a grave, and a crypt.

dominio.definicion: Located at a cemetery and associated with the burial of the dead.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a crypt.

descripcion: For example: RNP 4 represents a navigation accuracy of plus or minus 7.4 kilometres (4 nautical miles) on a 95 percent containment basis. RNP is a statement of the navigation performance necessary for operation within a defined airspace.

dominio.definicion: A structure used for the scientific study of matter in space, especially the locations, dimensions, distribution, motion, composition, energy, and evolution of celestial phenomena.
A building designed and equipped for making observations of astronomical, meteorological, or other natural phenomena.
A building supporting scientific experimentation or research, including scholarly investigation or inquiry, intended to ultimately result in commercial products.
An observation station where meteorological data are gathered, recorded, and released.
An establishment supporting nuclear (atomic) experimentation or research.
dominio.observaciones: May support scholarly investigation or inquiry, but generally intended to ultimately result in commercial and/or military products.

dominio.definicion: An apparatus for imparting high velocities to charged particles.

definicion: An indication that a vessel is in reserve status and potentially could be made seaworthy through a reactivation process.
descripcion: For example, a reserve fleet is a collection of naval vessels that are fully equipped for fighting but are not currently needed. They may be modified, for instance by having rustprone areas sealed off or wrapped in plastic. Ships of the reserve fleet are usually moored in backwater areas near naval bases or shipyards, to speed the reactivation process.

datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: An indication that horizontal clearance for vehicles on a land transportation route is restricted.
descripcion: Horizontal clearance affects the maximum width of loads that extend laterally beyond the wheels of a vehicle.

datatype.nombre: Review Source Date and Time Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a review source date and time.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.4.1, Combinations of date and time of day - Complete representation - Extended format, a calendar date and time representation, as a single data element comprising up to twenty characters, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, [hh] the ordinal number of an hour within the calendar day, [mm] the ordinal number of a minute within the hour, [ss] the ordinal number of a second within the minute, and an optional 'Z' when the time is according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12' for 12 April 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412T114520Z').

descripcion: A rig is a superstructure fitted for drilling or lifting operations for extraction and/or exploitation of natural resources.

dominio.definicion: Covered by one of several genera of tropical trees (for example: mangrove or nipa) or shrubs that produce many prop roots and grow along low-lying banks into shallow water.
Made up of spongy land saturated with water.
dominio.observaciones: It may have a shallow covering of water, usually with a considerable amount of vegetation appearing above the surface.

dominio.definicion: Made up of rock and rock fragments ranging in size from pebbles and gravel to boulders or large rock masses.
Made up of the debris (for example: waste fragments of masonry) of decayed or demolished buildings and/or other structures.
Made up of material weathered or eroded from a rocky coast, usually collected at the base of a cliff.
dominio.observaciones: Associated with landslides and coastal erosion. There will be an irregular jagged line produced by the rubble and coastal water interface.

dominio.definicion: Made up of sand, loose material consisting of small but easily distinguishable, separate grains, between 0.0625 and 2.000 millimetres in diameter.
Made up of rounded, often flat waterworn rock fragments larger than approximately 16 millimetres in diameter.

definicion: The amount of upward inclination between the horizontal surface of the mean water level of a watercourse where it touches the right bank and the top of the first usable break in slope, measured at the same point on the upper right bank as the military gap width.
descripcion: The right bank is determined by facing downstream (in the direction of flow). The (percent) slope is determined as the change in height divided by the horizontal distance over which the change takes place, multiplied by one hundred: ((h2-h1)/d)*100.

descripcion: The right bank is determined by facing downstream (in the direction of flow). The (percent) slope is determined as the change in depth divided by the horizontal distance over which the change takes place, multiplied by one hundred: ((h2-h1)/d)*100.

datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of linear density equal to one thousandth of a metre per square metre.

definicion: An indication that a road serves as a section of a road interchange, providing traffic access from one through road to another, but does not itself carry through traffic.
descripcion: Through roads normally are located on separate vertical levels, thus affording uninterrupted traffic flow, with at least one road being supported by a bridge and the other proceeding through an underpass. In the case of a rotary interchange on a single level there is no uninterrupted through route, therefore all traffic flows pass along road interchange ramps.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of physical arrangement of a road interchange.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a road interchange type.

dominio.definicion: Consists of two roads crossing at separate vertical levels and a set of eight radially symmetric ramps for traffic to flow without stopping from either direction on either road to either direction on the other road, with the four inner ramps arranged in the shape of a cloverleaf.

Consists of two roads crossing at separate vertical levels and a set of four radially symmetric ramps for traffic to flow from either direction on one road to a stopping location from which a turn in either direction on the other road may be made, with the four ramps arranged in the shape of a diamond.

Consists of a road where a second road originates and diverges and an overpass and ramps allow traffic to flow without stopping between the originating road and the diverging road, with traffic flow not allowed between the diverging roads.

Consists of two roads crossing at separate vertical levels and a set of four radially symmetric ramps joined to a circular ramp at a lower vertical level for traffic to flow without stopping from either direction on either road to either direction on the other road.

Consists of two roads crossing at separate vertical levels and a set of four radially symmetric paired ramps for traffic to flow in either direction on one road to stopping locations from which a turn in either direction on the other road may be made.
Consists of a set of ramps, and possibly overpass, allowing traffic to flow with limited or no restrictions between two crossing or meeting roads.

Consists of two roads crossing at separate vertical levels and a set of four paired ramps for traffic to flow from either direction on one road to stopping locations from which a turn in either direction on the other road may be made.
Consists of a road where a second road originates and four ramps and an overpass allow traffic to flow without stopping from either direction on either road to either direction on the other road.

Consists of two roads crossing at an angle at separate vertical levels and a set of four radially symmetric ramps and two overpass for traffic to flow without stopping from either direction on the upper road to either direction on the lower road and with ramps from the lower road only provided for traffic to flow from either direction to only two of the four directions on the upper road.

Consists of three roads meeting at the same vertical level and a set of six ramps and associated (typically three) overpass for traffic to flow without stopping from either direction on either road to either direction on another road.
A thoroughfare junction at which traffic moves in one direction round a central island.

definicion: The type of weather conditions under which a road is usable.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a road weather restriction.

dominio.definicion: Suitable for use regardless of the weather.
dominio.observaciones: It usually has the following characteristics: (1) With reasonable maintenance, passable throughout the year to a volume of traffic never appreciably less than its maximum capacity. (2) Normally having a waterproof surface and only slightly affected by rain, frost, thaw, or heat. (3) Never closed because of weather effects other than snow or flood blockage. For example, NATO class 'X'.

dominio.definicion: Under fair conditions only.
dominio.observaciones: It usually has the following characteristics: (1) Passable only in fair and dry weather. (2) So seriously affected by adverse conditions that the road may remain closed for long periods. (3) Improvement of such a road can only be achieved by construction or realignment. For example, NATO class 'Z'.

dominio.definicion: Under winter season conditions only.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the road may cross a waterbody and therefore is nonoperational until a sufficiently thick layer of ice has formed.

dominio.definicion: All-weather, however may have limited traffic due to weather.
dominio.observaciones: It usually has the following characteristics: (1) With reasonable maintenance, passable throughout the year but at times the volume of traffic is considerably less than maximum capacity. (2) Normally not having a waterproof surface and considerably affected by rain, frost, thaw, or heat. (3) Closed for short periods of up to one day at a time by adverse weather conditions during which heavy use of the road would probably lead to collapse. For example, NATO class 'Y'.

dominio.definicion: Suitable for use other than during the winter season, when it is closed.
dominio.observaciones: For example, regular plowing, salting, and/or sanding may not take place during the winter season.

definicion: The structure of a signficiant outcropping of exposed rock.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a rock formation structure.

dominio.definicion: In tabular bodies of igneous rock, a pattern of jointing produced because of contraction during cooling and characterized by the division of rocks into long, parallel prisms or pillars.
A pointed, elevated, detached needle-like mass of rock formed by erosion.
A high, tapering, or pointed tower, pinnacle or spire-shaped pillar of rock.
dominio.observaciones: May be either isolated, as on steep slopes or cliffs formed in karst or other massive rocks, or located at the summit of a hill or mountain.

dominio.definicion: A forest that has been buried and fossilized by geologic processes and is now re-exposed at the Earth's surface.

definicion: The depth to the upper surface of the rock layer.

definicion: The ratio of the aggregate volume of pore space in a rock or sediment to its total volume.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A scaled dimensionless measure denoting one part in every hundred.

definicion: The general type of a rock based on its geologic origin and/or observed characteristics.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a rock type.

dominio.definicion: A chemical sedimentary rock consisting of carbonate minerals.
dominio.observaciones: For example: limestone, dolomite.

dominio.definicion: A sediment or sedimentary rock composed of fragments of pre-existing rocks (clasts).
dominio.observaciones: Consolidated clastic rocks include conglomerates, sandstones and shales.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock with a significant content of carbon, derived from altered organic material.
dominio.observaciones: For example, anthracite and bituminous coal.

dominio.definicion: A carbonate sedimentary rock of which more than 50 percent by weight or by areal percentages under the microscope consists of the mineral dolomite (calcium magnesium carbonate).
A sedimentary rock composed primarily of minerals produced from a saline solution as a result of extensive or total evaporation of the solvent.
dominio.observaciones: For example: gypsum, anhydrite, or halite.

dominio.definicion: A general petrological term applied to coarse-grained, banded metamorphic rock.
A rock formed by the crystallization of magma and includes both the plutonic and volcanic rocks.
An igneous rock that is transitional between basic and acid (or between mafic and felsic), generally having silica content between 52 to 65 percent by weight.
dominio.observaciones: For example, andesites.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock, composed mainly of calcite or dolomite, which is often of organic, chemical or detritial origin.
Igneous rock composed chiefly of one or more ferromagnesian (iron and magnesium rich), dark-colored (mafic) minerals.
dominio.observaciones: For example, basalt. They have relatively low silica content.

dominio.definicion: A metamorphic rock consisting predominantly of fine- to coarse-grained recrystallized limestone.
A rock formed by the recrystallization of pre-existing rocks in response to the effects of pressure, temperature, or volatile content.
A fine grained massive sedimentary rock consisting of mostly fine-grained silt and clay size fragments (over 75 percent by volume of clay and/or silt).
A sedimentary rock rich in phosphate.
A relatively coarse-grained rock formed at considerable depth by crystallization of magma.
A clastic sedimentary rock composed chiefly of grains of volcanic origin, derived from contemporaneous volcanic activity.
dominio.observaciones: For example: tuff, lahar.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock composed of cemented sand-sized particles (0.063 to 2 millimetres in diameter), consisting mostly of quartz, feldspar and rock fragments.
A strongly foliated metamorphic rock, that can be split into flakes or slabs.
A sedimentary rock, which represents a variety of quartz made up solely of microscopic crystals.
dominio.observaciones: For example: opal, chalcedony.

dominio.definicion: A very fine grained consolidated clastic rock composed predominantly of particles of silt grade (0.05 to 0.002 millimetres in diameter), and less than 12 percent clay.
A rock resulting from the consolidation and/or cementation of loose sediment (organic and anorganic) and/or precipitation of dissolved material.
A relatively fine-grained rock formed at the Earth's surface by crystallization of magma.
An igneous rock having silica content over 65 percent by weight.
dominio.observaciones: For example, granite.

dominio.definicion: A dark coloured metamorphic rock, consisting mainly of amphibole and plagioclase.
A fine-grained, intermediate volcanic rock, consisting of plagioclase.
A sandstone, main grain size (0.063 - 2 millimetres in diameter), containing less than 15 percent by volume fine-grained matrix (silt and/or clay).
A sandstone that contains quartz and more than 25 percent by volume of feldspar.
A dark-coloured, fine-grained, basic volcanic rock, consisting of plagioclase, pyroxene and magnetite.
An igneous rock having silica content between 45 to 52 percent by weight.
dominio.observaciones: For example, basalt.

dominio.definicion: A rock composed of a mixture of various hydrous aluminum oxides and hydroxides and formed in tropical and subtropical environment by weathering of aluminium-bearing rocks.
A sedimentary rock characterized by, or resulting directly or indirectly from, the chemical processes and activities of living organisms.
dominio.observaciones: For example: limestone, phosphorite.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock composed primarily of material formed direct by precipitation from solution or evaporation or by deposition of insoluble precipitates.
dominio.observaciones: For example: rock salt, chert.

dominio.definicion: A coarse-grained sedimentary rock with rounded clasts that are greater than 2 millimetres in diameter.
A light-coloured, fine-grained felsic plutonic rock, consisting of plagioclase, alkali feldspar, quartz, biotite and hornblende.
A coarse-grained intermediate plutonic rock, consisting of plagioclase, pyroxene or hornblende and quartz.
A dark grey, medium grained, mafic intrusive rock, mainly composed of plagioclase, pyroxene and opaque minerals.
A plutonic rock with feldspathoid mineral content.
dominio.observaciones: Feldspathoid minerals are any of a group of alkali aluminosilicate minerals similar to the feldspars in chemical composition but either having a lower silica-alkali ratio or containing chloride, sulfide, sulphate, or carbonate.

dominio.definicion: A igneous rock having abundant light-colored (felsic) minerals, mainly quarz and feldspars.
dominio.observaciones: For example: granites, rhyolites. They have high silica content.

dominio.definicion: A coarse-grained basic plutonic rock, consisting of plagioclase (approximately 60 percent by volume) and pyroxene.
A light-coloured, felsic plutonic rock, consisting of essentially quartz, alkali feldspar, plagioclase and mica.
A plutonic rock consisting essentially of quartz, sodic plagioclase, less amount of alkali feldspar, hornblende and biotite.
A coarse-grained, equigranular high pressure metamorphic rock.
A low-grade, green metamorphic rock produced by the metamorphism of basic igneous rocks.
dominio.observaciones: For example, basalt.

dominio.definicion: A dark-grey sandstone that contain more than 15 percent by volume of clay minerals.
A rock that has been altered by the action of hot water (hydrothermal fluid) associated with igneous activity.
An iron-rich variety of chert (more than 15 percent by weight of iron).
A rock composed mainly of hydrated iron and aluminum oxides and hydroxides, formed in tropical and subtropical environment by weathering of iron- and aluminium-bearing rocks.
A volcanic rock containing essentialy crystals of alkali feldspar and plagioclase in a glassy matrix.
A soft brownish-black coal that is intermediate in coalification between peat and bituminous coal.
A dark-coloured, ultrabasic volcanic rock.
A coarse-grained, intermediate plutonic rock, consisting of plagioclase, alkali feldspar, pyroxene and biotite.
A well laminated and often hard and splintery metamorphic rock produced in zones of tectonic dislocation.
dominio.observaciones: For example, fault and shear zones.

dominio.definicion: An unconsolidated deposit of semicarbonized plant remains in a water-satured environment.
A very coarse-grained plutonic rock, usually of granitic composition, in which the individual crystals are at least 2.5 centimetres, and often more than 1 metre, long.
A coarse-grained, ultrabasic plutonic rock, consisting of olivine.
A fine grained sedimentary rock composed of clay- or mud-size particles (less than 0.063 millimetres in diameter).
A fine-grained volcanic rock, consisting of essential alkali feldspar and no quartz (undersaturated).
A fine grained, low-grade metamorphic rock, with a well developed schistosity (planar alignment of minerals), that has often a silky sheen.
A fine-grained, felsic volcanic rock, consisting of quarz and alkali feldspar.
A chemical sedimentary rock, composed mainly of coarsely to fine crystalline gypsum, as a result of evaporation of saline waters or dehydration of gypsum.
A chemical sedimentary rock, composed mainly of anhydrite, as a result of evaporation of saline waters.
A chemical sedimentary rock, composed mainly of coarsely crystalline halite, as a result of evaporation of saline waters.
A metamorphic rock derived from the alteration of a ultrabasic rock.
dominio.observaciones: For example, peridotite.

dominio.definicion: A fine-grained (clay, silt), fissile sedimentary rock.
A compact, fine-grained and fissile low-grade metamorphic rock, that has a dull luster.
A coarse-grained, intermediate plutonic rock, consisting of alkali feldspar and ferromagnesian minerals.
dominio.observaciones: For example, for ferromagnesian minerals biotite, hornblende.

dominio.definicion: Fine-grained volcanic rock, consisting of calcium plagioclase and no quartz (undersatured).
A coarse-grained acid plutonic rock, consisting of plagioclase, quarz, hornblende and/or biotite.
Fine-grained, intermediate volcanic rock of the rocks, having alkali feldspar.
An igneous rock having silica content below 45 percent by mass.
dominio.observaciones: For example, basanite.

dominio.definicion: A dark igneous rock composed of olivine and pyroxenes (mafic minerals).
dominio.observaciones: For example, peridotite.

dominio.definicion: A sandstone that contain perceptible fine-grained matrix (15-75 percent by volume of silt and/or clay).

definicion: The portion of an area that contains structures having roofs or tops (for example: buildings and storage tanks).

definicion: The configuration(s) and/or appearance(s) of a roof.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a roof shape.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a cone, tapering upwards from a more or less circular base to a point.
In the shape of a polyhedron of which the base is a polygon of any number of sides, and the other faces are triangles with a common vertex.
dominio.observaciones: Usually four-sided.

dominio.definicion: In the general shape of a half-cylinder, often as a rounded vault forming all or part of the roof of a building.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a Quonset hut. May be less than a full half-cylinder or only approximately hemi-cylindrical in cross-section.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a hemispherical (or occasionally peaked) surface, often as a rounded vault forming all or part of the roof of a building.
dominio.observaciones: Typically the structure supporting the dome has an elliptical (including circular) or polygonal base.

dominio.definicion: Generally flat and level, but usually with a small local pitch to ensure proper drainage.
Generally flat but with a steep pitch, usually consisting of a pair of surfaces sharing a ridge.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a gabled roof.

dominio.definicion: Having a serrated profile incorporating windows in the steeper (usually sunward-facing) sides.
Having an accessory raised section containing a series of windows and/or ventilators along its sides.
dominio.observaciones: Often located along a roof ridge.

dominio.definicion: A flat roof including one or more raised sections that contain windows and/or ventilators along their sides.
A pitched roof whose ridge or sides consists of one or more raised sections that contain windows and/or ventilators along their sides.
dominio.observaciones: For example, may be used in large churches to admit light to the central parts of the building.

definicion: An indication that a feature is covered by a roof.
descripcion: The roof may be supported by spaced pillars with intervening openings or the sides may be completely closed (for example: by walls or windows) and thus afford substantial protection from the weather.

datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The diameter of a rotor.
descripcion: For example, the rotor of a wind turbine.

datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of a route based on the function or responsible authority.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a route classification.

dominio.definicion: A route in a forest mainly used for the transportation of wood after logging.
A major route in the country side mainly used for agricultural purposes and mostly hard paved.
A paved area in populated places, which could be used by automotives but in which the automotive traffic is forbidden.
dominio.observaciones: Pedestrian zones have a great variety of attitudes or rules towards human powered vehicles such as bicycles, inline skates, skateboards and kick scooters. Some have a total ban on anything with wheels, others ban certain categories, others segregate the human-powered wheels from foot traffic, and others still have no rules at all. Many of the Middle Eastern examples have no wheeled traffic, but use donkeys for freight transport.

dominio.definicion: A mountain route which is equipped with fixed cables, stemples, ladders, and bridges.
A minor route in the country side mainly used for agricultural purposes that may be paved.
A designated and marked path through tidal flats that may be usable by vehicles or pedestrians.
dominio.observaciones: A tidal flat is a large flat area of mud or sand attached to the shore and alternately covered and uncovered by the tide.

dominio.definicion: A path through a mine field that has been cleared of mines by mine sweeping operations.
A specially prepared track in the snow for cross-country skiing.
A path worn by the passage of people or animals.
A route used by guards on their patrol.
A paved or improved pedestrian path, typically located adjacent and parallel to a street or road.

definicion: The official designation assigned to a route.
descripcion: For example, 'I-95', 'A-1', 'E-6', or 'M-5'. The route designation may continue along ferry crossing or ice routes in order to provide continuity with the transportation network.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is 24 characters in maximum length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of designation(s) of a road network according to the nature of service that it is intended to provide, as designated by international, national and/or other administrative authorities.
descripcion: The type(s) of route designation may continue along ferry crossing or ice routes in order to provide continuity with the transportation network.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a route designation type.

dominio.definicion: A designated set of major highways which interconnect countries and major cities.
dominio.observaciones: Are usually identified by a letter code in their designations, for example, an 'E' in Europe or 'A' in Asia.

dominio.definicion: A designated set of limited access motorways which interconnect major cities and provide for the vast majority of long-distance road travel within a country.
dominio.observaciones: May be identified in their designations, for example, with an 'I' for Interstate in the US, a 'M' for Motorway in the UK, or an 'A' (for example: for Autoroute, Autobahn, Autostrade or Autopista) for Autoroute in some European countries. In many areas there is no preceding letter designation.

dominio.definicion: A designated set of highways which may have limited access or semi-controlled access and interconnect secondary routes with national motorways.
dominio.observaciones: May be identified in their designations, for example, with a 'US' in the US, or an 'N' for National in other countries. In many areas there is no preceding letter designation.

dominio.definicion: A designated set of collector or regional highways that feed national routes or motorways.
dominio.observaciones: May be identified in their designations, for example, with an 'R' in France or state highways in the US. In most areas there is no preceding letter designation.

dominio.definicion: A designated set of roads which form the link between secondary highways and residential and rural roads.
dominio.observaciones: Traditionally comprised of farm-to-market routes, country lanes, and larger urban streets. In most areas there is no preceding letter designation.

definicion: The intended use of a maritime route.
descripcion: Unless stated otherwise, routeing systems are recommended for use by all ships and may be made mandatory for all ships, certain categories of ships or ships carrying certain cargoes, or types and quantities of bunker fuel. Routeing systems are intended for use by day and by night in all weathers, in ice-free waters or under light ice conditions where no extraordinary manoeuvres or icebreaker assistance are required.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a route intended use.

dominio.definicion: Recommended tracks include all channels recommended for hydrographic reasons to lead safely between shoal depths.
dominio.observaciones: The use of such a track is generally left to the discretion of the mariner and will depend on the vessel's draught, the state of the tide, adequacy of navigational aids and/or other considerations.

dominio.etiqueta: Recommended Track for Other Than Deep Draft Vessels
dominio.definicion: A route which is primarily selected for use by ships which are not restricted by their draft to deep draft routes and which are able to navigate safely outside such routes.

dominio.etiqueta: Recommended Track for Deep Draft Vessels
dominio.definicion: A route which is primarily selected for use by ships which, because of their deep draft, may not be able to navigate safely outside such route.
A route within defined limits that has been surveyed for clearance of sea bottom and submerged obstacles as indicated on a chart.
dominio.observaciones: It is primarily intended for use by ships which, because of their draught in relation to the available depth of water in the area concerned, require the use of such a route. Through traffic to which the draught consideration does not apply should, as far as practicable, avoid using deep-water routes.

dominio.definicion: A marked route established to permit vessels to pass through or transit a canal, port, harbour or other body of water.
A route within defined limits inside which two-way traffic is established.
dominio.observaciones: The aim is to provide safe passage of ships through waters where navigation is difficult or dangerous. In two-way routes, including two-way deep-water routes, ships should as far as practicable keep to the starboard side.

dominio.definicion: A traffic flow pattern indicating the directional movement of traffic as established within a traffic separation scheme, or a traffic flow pattern indicating a recommended directional movement of traffic where it is impractical or unnecessary to adopt an established direction of traffic flow.

A pre-planned dormant channel and or maritime route between two or more positions, surveyed for explosive mine-like contacts during peacetime, that can be 'activated' to provide shipping with safe navigable routes.
A route of undefined width, for the convenience of ships in transit, that is often marked by centerline buoys.
A navigation channel, in a situation where there exist multiple channels, that is the one recommended by local authorities for use by general maritime traffic.
The centerline of a recommended route.
The centerline of a deep water route.

definicion: The official designation assigned to a road interchange with respect to a route that passes through that interchange.
descripcion: For example, '5' or '32A'.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The degree to which at a junction (meeting and/or crossing) of multiple routes, all routes can be accessed from all other routes.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a route junction connectivity.

dominio.definicion: Vehicles may access all routes.
dominio.observaciones: For example, at an overpass there are access ramps allowing all possible vehicle flows from one route to another.

dominio.definicion: Vehicles are able to access only some routes.
dominio.observaciones: For example, at an overpass the available access ramps may limit the vehicle flow from one route to another.

definicion: The type of shape formed by the junction (meeting and/or crossing) of multiple routes.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a route junction type.

dominio.definicion: One route ends at the junction, forming a 'T' shape.
Two routes cross, forming a four-way intersection.
Multiple routes meet and/or cross, forming a star-shaped branching.

definicion: The width of a divider that separates adjacent route lanes or tracks in a land transportation route.
descripcion: The adjacent route lanes may carry traffic in opposing directions (for example: a divided highway or a dual track railway) or in the same direction (for example: a high-speed 'thru' lane and a local collector/distributor lane).

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The military load classification (MLC) of a route is a number which represents the safe load carrying capacity of a route and indicates the maximum MLC of vehicle that can be accepted under normal conditions.
descripcion: The MLC of the route is determined by first calculating the highest value of MLC (whether tracked or wheeled) for each structure along the route, and then selecting the lowest value from that list of structure-specific MLC values. See STANAGs 2021 and 2253 for the method of MLC calculation; see also AMovP-1(A), page 4-3.

datatype.definicion: An integer domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is an integer. For example, 6 (as in the length of a fathom in feet).
datatype.nota: The realization of this integer datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A quantity that is not related to any other quantity by a factor or formula.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A dynamic live load weight-bearing capacity of a span of a horizontal construction that is calculated in accordance with STANAGs 2021 and 2253.
unidadRecomendada.descripcion: The calculation is  based on the size, cross-sectional shape, and material of the longitudinal weight-bearing members of the span. It is similar to, but not the same as, the short ton.

definicion: The minimum width of the travelled way of a route.
descripcion: Excludes pavements and shoulders.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The significance of a route based on its importance within a national traffic network.
descripcion: Routes refer to the road traffic network and include roads, ferries, and vehicle shuttles.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a route significance type.

dominio.definicion: The most significant route network of a country; routes connecting the most important cities of a country.
The network of important routes connecting cities and important infrastructures (for example: airports and ports).
The network of routes connecting cities and towns and main routes within populated areas.
The network of routes connecting neighbourhoods within populated areas.
The network of routes connecting small, outlying infrastructure.
dominio.observaciones: For example: agricultural activities.

definicion: The composition(s) of a durable surface (for example: a pavement) intended to sustain ground traffic (for example: vehicular traffic or foot traffic).
descripcion: Depending on the traffic situation (for example: on a floor, in a courtyard, or on a road) different compositions may be used, however in general such surfaces are composed of pieces of a hard material fitted closely together (for example: cobble-stone or brick) or of an undivided hard layer (for example: concrete) so as to give a compact, uniform, and smooth surface.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a route surface composition.

dominio.definicion: An unprepared route whose surface is generally a flat track following the natural terrain.
dominio.observaciones: It often appears as a rough track with two wheel paths, and close vegetation.

dominio.definicion: A minimally prepared route constructed from a layer of local materials (for example: consolidated soils) that have been graded, rolled and possibly treated to improve their resistance to moisture and/or load-bearing capacity (sometimes termed 'stabilized').
A pavement in which the load is carried mainly through unbound materials (for example: crushed aggregates).
dominio.observaciones: A topping or seal coat may be applied to improve weather or flooding resistance, control surface dust production or raveling (pulling apart), and/or improve traction characteristics.

dominio.definicion: A pavement constructed from well-graded aggregates, usually consisting of a base course of larger aggregate covered by a 'open' wearing course.
dominio.observaciones: A variety of compacted aggregates may be used depending on local availability. These include, for example, crushed rock, gravel, cinders, and occasionally coral or shells. Where locally available aggregates are of poor quality, or the pavement may traverse an area often innundated by water, they may be 'stabilized' by a variety of chemical means (for example: by mixing a cementitious, lime or bituminous binder with the base material) to improve its resistance to moisture and/or load-bearing capacity.

dominio.definicion: A type of aggregate-based pavement consisting of three layers of stones laid and compacted on a sloped subgrade with side ditches for drainage.
dominio.observaciones: This type of road construction was pioneered by the Scotsman John Loudon McAdam in the early 1800s. The lower layers consisted of angular hand-broken aggregate, maximum size 75 millimetres (3 inches), to a total depth of about 200 millimetres (8 inches). The top layer was about 50 millimetres (2 inches) thick with a maximum aggregate size of 25 mm (1 inch). The layers were compacted with a heavy roller, causing the angular stones to lock together with their neighbours. This basic method of construction is sometimes known as 'water-bound macadam'. Although this method required a great deal of manual labor, it resulted in a strong and free-draining pavement. Roads constructed in this manner were described as 'macadamized'. With the advent of motor vehicles, dust became a serious problem on macadam roads. The vacuum created under fast-moving vehicles sucked dust from the road surface, creating unpleasant dust clouds and a gradual raveling (pulling apart) of the road material. This problem was later rectified by spraying tar on the surface to create 'tar-bound macadam' (tarmac). Macadam roads are only infrequently used, having been replaced by other forms of Aggregate and Bound Surface pavements.

dominio.definicion: A pavement constructed from an unbound base covered by a bound surface layer (for example: a seal coat or a thin layer of asphalt).
dominio.observaciones: The base may be 'stabilized' by a variety of chemical means (for example: by mixing a cementitious, lime or bituminous binder with the base material) to improve its load-carrying properties.

dominio.definicion: A pavement in which the load is carried by tightly bound materials (for example: concretes).
dominio.observaciones: The most common forms are concrete and asphalt (also referred to as 'semi-rigid'), however in specialized situations other materials may be used, for example steel.

dominio.definicion: A rigid pavement structure formed from cast-in-place slabs of a composite stone-like material also known as Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) that consists of a binding medium (Portland cement and water) within which are embedded particles or fragments of aggregate, usually a combination of fine aggregate and course aggregate.

A semi-rigid pavement that is formed-in-place through a process of continuous layering and rolling of a material known as 'Asphalt Concrete' or 'Bituminous Concrete', formed from a hot mixture of AC (asphalt/cement binder) and high quality aggregate.
dominio.observaciones: Includes, for example: Hot Mix Asphalt (HMA), Recycled HMA, Stone Matrix Asphalt (SMA), Dense-Graded Mix, and Open-Graded Friction Course (OGFC). SMA is a premium gap-graded HMA requiring high quality materials. Cubical low abrasion crushed stone and manufactured sands are recommended. Manufactured sands, mineral fillers and additives (fibers and/or polymers) make a stiff matrix that is important to the rutting resistance of these mixes. Dense-Graded Mix is a well-graded HMA intended for general use. When properly designed and constructed, a dense-graded mix is relatively impermeable. Dense-graded mixes are generally referred to by their nominal maximum aggregate size. They can further be classified as either fine-graded or coarse-graded. Fine-graded mixes have more fine and sand sized particles than coarse-graded mixes. OGFC is a pavement surface course that consists of a high-void, asphalt plant mix that permits rapid drainage of rainwater through the course and out the shoulder. The mixture is characterized by a large percentage of one-sized coarse aggregate. This course reduces hydroplaning and provides a skid-resistant pavement surface with significant noise reduction.

dominio.definicion: A layered pavement in which a concrete base is surfaced with a layer of asphalt.
dominio.observaciones: The asphalt protects the base from salt exposure by forming a sacrificial layer that may be relatively easily repaired and/or replaced. May also result when an original concrete pavement has become significantly degraded and then been resurfaced with asphalt as a form of repair.

dominio.definicion: Cobbles packed closely together on a firm subgrade, with or without mortar.
dominio.observaciones: Traditionally, cobbles are smooth stones taken from riverbeds and cobbled (roughly assembled) together with mortar. In more recent pavements the cobbles consist of manufactured rectangular paving stones that may not have curved tops.

dominio.definicion: Bricks packed closely together on a firm subgrade, with or without mortar.
Surfaced by metal (for example: grating or diamond plate sheet).
dominio.observaciones: Typically used in special constructions, for example: moveable bridge surfaces.

dominio.definicion: Surfaced by wood (for example: logs, beams, or planks).
Surfaced by rough-hewn logs loosely laid together transversely exposing irregular amounts of the underlying material(s).
dominio.observaciones: Often used in relatively low or swampy areas to provide a rough relatively durable surface that is elevated above the surrounding terrain.

dominio.definicion: Surfaced by wooden planks laid tightly together transversely and secured along stringers.
dominio.observaciones: For example, as on a pier or boardwalk or (historically) a plank road.

dominio.definicion: A cleared route over a frozen watercourse.
dominio.observaciones: Usually marked and intended to support substantial vehicle traffic.

dominio.definicion: A minimally prepared route passing over packed snow.
dominio.observaciones: The snow, usually accumulated from multiple snowfalls, may have been rolled to ensure the absence of voids or cavities.

dominio.definicion: A beam or piece of wood forming or capable of forming part of any structure.

definicion: The total usable width of the travelled way of a route.
descripcion: Includes pavements and shoulders.

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The type of a route width constriction based on the nature of the surrounding area.
descripcion: For example, reduction in road width to less than 4 metres is considered to be a constriction. Width restrictions cause vehicles and people to travel through narrow passages creating choke points.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a route constriction type.

dominio.definicion: The route is constrained to pass through a dropgate.
dominio.observaciones: A dropgate is a massive assemblage of material, usually in the form of concrete logs or blocks, positioned alongside or over a transportation route (for example: a road or a railway) as a potential barrier to an advancing enemy ground force. It is generally tied into large fortified embankments on both sides of the route to form part of a continuous defensive line when activated.

dominio.definicion: The route is constrained to pass through a narrow channel hemmed in by steep slopes, rocks, and/or other impediments to off-route vehicle movement.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a mountain pass.

dominio.definicion: The route is constrained to pass through a narrow channel hemmed in by buildings on both sides and, occasionally, above.
The route is constrained to pass through a narrow channel hemmed in by bridge abutments on both sides and a deck above.
A covered pedestrian route composed of arches and pillars, usually open along one or both sides.
A pillar or abutment that supports a bridge span.
A superstructure of a bridge, above the lowest deck.
A tower and/or pylon from which the deck of a bridge is suspended.
A solid raised way across a terrain obstacle (for example: a wetland or a body of shallow water) that is intended to support a transportation route (for example: a road or a railway).
dominio.observaciones: The causeway structure is often constructed from local fill supplemented by other materials (for example: rocks, boulders or gravel) and consists of a solid linear structure in the configuration of an embankment. Causeway structures are built just high enough to insure that the transportation route will remain passable during periods of flooding, tides and seasonal rainfall. Culverts may occur along the length of the causeway structure and individual sections of the causeway structure may be interrupted by bridges.

dominio.definicion: An interconnected series of subterranean chambers.
dominio.observaciones: Typically located in limestone, and often open to the Earth's surface either vertically or horizontally.

dominio.definicion: An enclosed channel for carrying a watercourse (for example: a stream, a sewer, or a drain) under a route (for example: a road, a railway, or an embankment).
dominio.observaciones: Usually the construction of the route is unaffected.

dominio.definicion: A border of concrete, asphalt or stone forming part of a gutter along the edge of a street or road.
An excavation in the terrain to provide passage for a land or water transportation route (for example: a road, a railway, and/or a canal).
A barrier constructed to hold back water and raise its level to form a reservoir or to prevent flooding.
A man-made raised long mound of earth or other material.
A location of entrance and/or exit.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a cave mouth or a doorway.

dominio.definicion: A man-made barrier of relatively light structure used as an enclosure or boundary.
An apparatus for drawing water directly from a main, especially alongside a street or road, consisting of a pipe with one or more nozzles or spouts, to which a hose of a fire-engine may be attached.
A shallow place in a body of water used as a crossing.
A sunken or cut passageway along a transportation route in mountainous regions constructed to protect vehicles from the elements.
dominio.observaciones: A series of openings on one side may be present for light or ventilation.

dominio.definicion: A permanent raised structure used to support equipment (for example: cranes, signal lights, or signs) while spanning over or around an object (for example: over a road or railroad, or around a ship hull or rocket).
dominio.observaciones: A gantry may be moveable (for example: a rocket gantry may be repositioned away from the launch pad when pre-launch preparations are complete). A 'scaffold' is a structure that may be similar in appearance but is assembled only for temporary use (for example: during external repair of a building).

dominio.definicion: A barrier on a transportation route (for example: a road, a railway, a tunnel, or a bridge) that controls passage (may be opened and closed).
A continuous growth of shrubs planted as a fence, a boundary, and/or a windbreak.
A marker erected and/or maintained as a memorial to a person and/or event.
Overhung and/or enclosed (covers and extends to both sides) by a non-building structure.
A designated, multi-level, structure used for parking and/or storing vehicles.
dominio.observaciones: May be present as part of a building or as a separate structure.

dominio.definicion: A connected set of pipes for conveying liquids, slurries, or gases.
dominio.observaciones: Usually for long distances and often located underground.

dominio.definicion: A traversable site extending across a pipeline that acts as a passageway for cross-country movement of vehicles or troops.

A location on a watercourse that has ramps, structural piles, and/or piers constructed on one or both shores to allow for suitable future crossing operations using floating bridges or rafting equipment.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a prepared float bridge site or a prepared raft site.

dominio.definicion: A signal used to control traffic on a railway.
A device integrated with a railway track with which the rails may be switched to permit access to another railway track.
An inclined plane, usually man-made, for moving between two levels.
Reduction in the number of independent, parallel paths (for example: a railway track and/or a road lane) in either direction within a route.

A small structure that stands alone, and is designated for the purpose of supplying a product (for example: souvenirs, magazines, snacks or refreshments) or service (for example: a shoe shine) to passers-by.
dominio.observaciones: It may be roofed (for example: a newspaper stand along the side of a city street or the attendant's booth in a parking lot or at a taxi cab stand), covered by an awning (for example: a cellular phone booth in the center of the promenade of a shopping mall.

dominio.definicion: A connection designed to provide traffic access from one road to another.
A significant outcropping of exposed bedrock.
Restricted by closely placed objects (for example: route-related signs, lamps, designated vehicle stops (for example: a bus stop), benches, and/or their support structures) along a route.
A series of fixed steps leading from one level to another, especially such a series leading from one floor level to another inside a structure.
dominio.observaciones: The steps may also be on the outside of the structure, for example, on a gasometer.

dominio.definicion: A steep, vertical, or overhanging face of rock and/or soil.
dominio.observaciones: For example, an escarpment, a bluff, or a cliff.

dominio.definicion: A substantial semi-permanent assemblage of material, usually in the form of concrete blocks and/or cylinders, positioned alongside or above a land transportation route, ready to be activated as a potential barrier.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a rolling block is positioned alongside the route and a drop gate is positioned above the route.

dominio.definicion: A structure built over and/or along a transportation route designed to prevent damage to, or blockage of, the route from rock slides, snow slides and/or weather phenomena.
An underground passage that is open at both ends and usually contains a land transportation route (for example: a road and/or a railway).
dominio.observaciones: Commonly used to pass through a hill or mountain, or under a river or road. May also provide underground passage in a mine.

dominio.definicion: A raised way, path, or road across a low or wet place or stretch of water that is constructed from wooden planks.

definicion: The type of a route width expansion based on the nature of the expansion and/or surrounding area.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a route expansion type.

dominio.definicion: A siding enabling the passing and/or parking of vehicles.
dominio.observaciones: Typically located along narrow roads, especially in mountainous regions.

dominio.definicion: Increase in the number of independent, parallel paths (for example: a railway track and/or a road lane) in either direction within a route.
A stretch of railway track connected to a main railway and used for temporary storage, passing, loading, and/or unloading.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a passing track.

dominio.definicion: A roadside place usually having facilities for people and/or vehicles.
A strip adjacent to the edge of a pavement so prepared as to provide a transition between the pavement and the adjacent surface.
dominio.observaciones: Not normally used by vehicles but provided as an allowable margin in case of emergency situations.

definicion: The runway weight bearing capacity expressed in terms of the gross weight which is allowed for continuing operations.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value that is restricted to be non-negative.
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of the property of a body that causes it to have weight in a gravitational field.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "mass", defined as equal to the mass of the international prototype of the kilogram.

definicion: The role of a location that is established along a runway direction centre-line based on its relationship to an intended use of the runway or runway-related equipment.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a runway centre-line location role.

dominio.definicion: Established on the runway centre-line at the location perpendicular to the Elevation Antenna.
Established on the runway centre-line at the location perpendicular to the Glideslope Antenna.
Established on the runway centre-line at the location perpendicular to the Precision Approach Radar (PAR) Antenna.
Established on the runway centre-line at the location perpendicular to the Runway End Reflector (RER).
Established on the runway centre-line at the location perpendicular to the Touchdown Reflector (TDR).
Established on the runway centre-line at the location that is the highest point of the usable runways of an aerodrome.
Established on the runway centre-line at the midpoint of the runway.
Established on the runway centre-line at the start of the take-off run.
Established on the runway centre-line at the start of the runway threshold.
dominio.observaciones: It is intended that landing aircraft first contact the runway in the touchdown zone.

definicion: The number of runways at a facility or site.

datatype.definicion: A count domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a cardinal number or an ordinal number. For example, 4 (as in the number of legs of a cow).
datatype.nota: The realization of this count datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The designator of the runway that is used to uniquely identify it at an aerodrome.
descripcion: This may be used to identify either both directions of the runway (for example: '09/27' or '02R/20L') or one direction independently (for example: '27', '35L', '01R').

datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a runway designator.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: The structure is composed of the two digit runway identifier with suffix of 'L' (left), 'R' (right), 'C' (center) and if denoting both directions separated by a back slash ('\').

definicion: An indication that a runway element is bounded at one end by a displaced runway threshold and at the other by a runway end.
descripcion: A runway threshold may be displaced from the end of the runway for a variety of purposes, such as for a safety area from jet blast in the case of a runway blast area, or for an obstacle free approach area in the case of a displaced threshold area.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: Indicates high or low end of runway.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a runway end type.

definicion: The distance in which the runway may be increased in length should an operational requirement exist.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value that is restricted to be non-negative.
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The higher degree identification of the runway.

datatype.nombre: Runway Identifier - High End Structured Text

definicion: A value specifying the longitudinal offset of the strip, when it is not symmetrically extended beyond the two runway ends.
descripcion: The longitudinal offset defines the distance along the centreline from the middle of the runway centreline towards the middle of the strip centreline. An offset in the direction defined from the threshold with the lower runway direction designation number towards the opposite runway threshold is indicated by a positive value. An offset in the opposite sense is indicated by a negative value. For Example: a runway oriented 09/27 has a strip that is extending 120 metres before the threshold of the runway direction 09 and only 100 metres before the threshold of the runway direction 27. The value of the longitudinal offset will be -10 metres.

definicion: A value specifying the lateral offset of the strip, when it is not symmetrically extended beyond the two runway edges.
descripcion: The lateral offset defines the distance from the runway centreline to the strip centreline in direction perpendicular to the runway centreline. An offset to the right, based on the direction defined from the threshold with the lower runway direction designation number towards the opposite runway threshold, is indicated by a positive value. An offset to the left is indicated by a negative value. For Example: a runway oriented 09/27 has a strip that is extending 150 metres to the right of the runway direction 09 and 300 metres to the left of the same runway direction. The value of the lateral offset will be -75 metres.

descripcion: The dune(s) are usually vegetated and in consequence they are relatively unaffected by the scouring action of local winds.
