definicion: The type of a sand dune based on its shape and/or structure.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a sand dune type.

dominio.definicion: Crescent-shaped mounds generally wider than long whose slipface is on the dune's concave side.
Oval or circular mounds that generally lack a slipface.
dominio.observaciones: They are rare and generally occur at the far upwind margins of sand seas.

dominio.definicion: Long, relatively straight dunes, oriented perpendicular to the direction of the wind and consisting of accumulations of loose, well-sorted, very fine to medium sand in ridges that have a gentle stoss (upwind) slope and a steep slip face on the lee slope.
dominio.observaciones: Although appearing similar to linear dunes, they differ from linear dunes in that the two flanks of a transverse dune have different, rather than similar, angles of slope; the gentler upwind slope is composed of firmly packed sand and the steeper lee (avalanche) slope is soft and loose sand. Transverse dunes also migrate laterally, toward the next dune ridge, instead of longitudinally down the long axis of the ridge.

dominio.definicion: Straight or slightly sinuous sand ridges typically much longer than they are wide and whose long axis extends in the direction of sand movement.
dominio.observaciones: Linear dunes may occur as isolated ridges, but they generally form sets of parallel ridges separated by miles of sand, gravel, and/or rocky interdune corridors.

dominio.definicion: U-shaped mounds of sand with convex noses trailed by elongated arms whose slipface is on the dune's convex side.
dominio.observaciones: Generally located in coastal deserts, their arms have been fixed by vegetation while the bulk of the sand in the dune migrates forward.

dominio.definicion: A series of small, linear, parallel sand accumulations (incipient dunes) that occur in very fine sand.
Pyramidal sand mounds with slipfaces on three or more arms that radiate from the high centre of the mound, growing upward rather than laterally.
dominio.observaciones: They tend to accumulate in areas with multidirectional wind regimes.

dominio.definicion: A mix of transverse dunes and, less frequently (usually around the peripheral edges), oval or circular mounds that generally lack a slipface.

definicion: A network of ground stations and satellites designed to receive navigation signals, improving the accuracy and ensuring the integrity of information for navigation and landing.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a satellite based augmentation system.

dominio.definicion: EGNOS is intended to supplement the GPS, GLONASS and Galileo systems by reporting on the reliability and accuracy of the signals.

MSAS is a Japanese Satellite Based Augmentation System which supports Differential GPS (DGPS) designed to supplement the GPS system by reporting (then improving) on the reliability and accuracy of those signals.
An air navigation aid developed by the US Federal Aviation Administration to augment the Global Positioning System (GPS), with the goal of improving its accuracy, integrity, and availability.
dominio.observaciones: WAAS uses a network of ground-based reference stations, in North America and Hawaii, to measure small variations in the GPS satellites' signals in the western hemisphere. Measurements from the reference stations are routed to master stations, which queue the received DCs and send the correction messages to geostationary WAAS satellites in a timely manner (at least every 5 seconds or better). Those satellites broadcast the correction messages back to Earth, where WAAS-enabled GPS receiver uses the corrections while computing its position to improve accuracy.

dominio.definicion: An all-weather aircraft landing system based on real-time differential correction of the GPS signal.
dominio.observaciones: Local reference receivers send data to a central location at the airport. This data is used to formulate a correction message, which is then transmitted to users via a VHF data link. A receiver on an aircraft uses this information to correct GPS signals, which then provides a standard ILS-style display to use while flying a precision approach.

nombre: Satellite Based Augmentation System (SBAS) Service Provider

Cast or wrought iron broken up and set aside for reprocessing.

dominio.definicion: Paper intended for repulping or reuse.
Plastic intended for recycling.
Glass intended for recycling.

descripcion: Its trunk and branches may form an obstruction in the river much like a strainer.

definicion: The type of ice in the sea based on origin, morphology and/or age.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a sea ice type.

dominio.definicion: Sea ice which remains fast, generally in the position where originally formed, and which may attain a considerable thickness.
Any form of ice which has originated from sea water.
dominio.observaciones: Generally any ice in the sea.

dominio.definicion: A low-lying mass of flow ice which is not easily seen by approaching vessels owing to its dark indigo colour.
dominio.observaciones: It is usually caused by the capsizing and disintegration of an iceberg and is a menace to shipping.

dominio.definicion: Pieces of new ice, usually approximately circular, about 30 centimetres to 3 metres across, and with raised rims, due to the pieces striking against each other as the result of wind and swell.
A mass of snow and ice continuously moving from higher to lower ground or, if afloat, continuously spreading.
A rocky peak projecting above a surrounding ice field that may be perpetually covered with ice.
Term used in a wide sense to include any area of sea ice other than fast ice.
dominio.observaciones: Pack ice commonly consists of connected floating plates of ice and has a mosaic look. Fast Ice is defined as sea ice which remains fast, generally in the position where originally formed, and which may attain a considerable thickness. Fast ice is found along coasts, where it is attached to the shore, or over shoals, where it may be held in position by islands, grounded icebergs, or grounded polar ice.

dominio.definicion: Sea ice that is more than one year old (in contrast to winter ice).
dominio.observaciones: The WMO code defines polar ice as any sea ice more than one year old and more than 3 metres thick.

definicion: The month of the seasonal limit of the presence of ice that poses a hazard to maritime traffic.
descripcion: Used to specify the month for which an ice limit line is determined; hazardous ice may be present up to the polar side of the ice limit line.

datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a seasonal ice limit.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.

descripcion: Used for additional, alternate, and/or backup transmissions.

definicion: The full name that designates a subdivision of a principal administrative division of a geopolitical entity (for example: a State).
descripcion: For example, in the United States a principal administrative division is a 'state' and a subdivision of a state is a 'county'; in the 'state' of 'Maryland' lies the 'county' of 'Montgomery County'.

descripcion: The description may include power available and switch-over time.

datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

descripcion: For example, 'Eisenhower Highway' or 'Hudson River Expressway'.

datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

descripcion: The basis for 'secondary' may be, for example, compositional dominance or structural organization.

dominio.definicion: The powdery residue, composed chiefly of earthy or mineral particles, left after the combustion of any substance.
Large water- or weather-worn stones.
White soft earthy limestone consisting almost wholly of calcite and derived chiefly from microscopic salt water fossil shells and fragments.
Residual pieces of combustible matter (for example: coal or wood) that has ceased to flame but has still combustible matter in them.
A member of the subclass Cirripedia, a marine crustacean that is generally sessile as an adult and has limbs modified for filter-feeding.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a barnacle.

dominio.definicion: A stiff tenacious fine-grained earth consisting mainly of hydrated aluminosilicates, which become more plastic when water is added and can be moulded and dried.
dominio.observaciones: Used to make bricks and/or pottery.

dominio.definicion: Water-worn rounded stones, especially of the size used for paving.
A usually hard calcareous substance secreted by many marine polyps as an external skeleton for support and habitation.
dominio.observaciones: Occurs in both single specimens and extensive accumulations. A similar substance may be produced by other lime-secreting marine organisms.

dominio.definicion: A significant, dense, coral outcrop consisting of corals grown, usually, from a single embryo.
A soft, friable, porous material consisting of fossilized microscopic unicellular alga that have rigid siliceous cell walls.
dominio.observaciones: Used for filters and insulation.

dominio.definicion: A rhizopod of the chiefly marine order Foraminiferida, typically having a calcareous shell with perforations (foramina) through which pseudopodia extend, the fossils forming a major constituent of chalk and many marine oozes.
A member of the genus Fucus, a seaweed with leathery fronds.
dominio.observaciones: For example, bladderwrack.

dominio.definicion: Plant material (for example: straw and/or tall coarse grass), possibly also containing the slices of soil to which the plant material is attached.
dominio.observaciones: For example, used in thatching or sodding a roof.

dominio.definicion: Small water-worn or pounded stones.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes with an intermixture of sand and/or clay. Used for laying paths and roads.

dominio.definicion: The fluid or semifluid magma or molten rock which flows from a volcano or other fissure in the Earth.
Fine yellowish-grey loam composed of material transported by the wind.
Stony and/or silaceous coral.
A hard grey brittle chemical element, atomic number 25, which is one of the transition metals. (Symbol Mn.)
dominio.observaciones: Used in steels and magnetic alloys.

dominio.definicion: White to gray accumulation on lake bottoms caused by precipitation of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) mixed with microscopic fresh water fossil shells and fragments.
Soft wet soil, sand, dust, and/or other earthy matter.
dominio.observaciones: Also, the hard ground produced by the drying of an area of mud.

dominio.definicion: Any of various bivalve molluscs belonging chiefly to the marine superfamily Mytilacea or to the freshwater superfamily Unionacea.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the common edible marine bivalve, Mytilus edulis, which has a dark grey, slightly elongated shell and adheres by a byssus, frequently in large aggregations.

dominio.definicion: A deposit or layer of white or grey calcareous matter largely composed of foraminiferan remains, covering large areas of the ocean floor.
Any of various bivalve molluscs of the family Ostreidae, several of which are eaten (especially raw) as a delicacy and may be farmed for food or pearls.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the common European Ostrea edulis, and members of the widespread genus Crassostrea.

dominio.definicion: Small, smooth, rounded stones, that have been worn by the action of water, ice, and/or sand.
Mosslike colonies of sessile, polypoid aquatic animals that reproduce by budding.
A light spongy form of volcanic glass, usually of pyroclastic origin and with a high silica content.
dominio.observaciones: Used, for example, as an abrasive (for example: in cleaning, polishing, removing stains and/or dead skin) or as an absorbent for moisture.

dominio.definicion: A trigonal rock-forming mineral consisting of silica, massive or crystallizing in colourless or white hexagonal prisms.
dominio.observaciones: Found widely in igneous and metamorphic rocks. Often coloured by impurities (as amethyst, citrine, cairngorm).

dominio.definicion: Marine protozoa with amoeba-like bodies and radiating filamentous pseudopods.
Stones of any size.
Granular material consisting of small eroded fragments of (mainly siliceous) rocks, finer than gravel and larger than a coarse silt grain.
dominio.observaciones: Generally ranging between 0.074 millimetres (No. 200 sieve) and 4.76 millimetres (No. 4 sieve) in size. Often a major constituent of a beach, desert, or the bed of a river or sea. Used for various purposes, as in smoothing stone, founding, or as an ingredient in mortar.

dominio.definicion: A coarse-grained pelitic metamorphic rock that has a structure marked by parallel layers of various minerals and can be split into thin irregular plates.
Rough masses resembling clinker, formed by the cooling of volcanic ejecta, and of a light aerated texture.
Calcareous remains of macroscopic marine animals, whole or in fragments.
Small, loose, rounded waterworn pebbles, especially as accumulated on a seashore.
Material consisting of particles whose sizes fall within a specified range (typically 0.002-0.06 millimetres) between those of sand and clay.
The material comprising the thin top layer of much of the Earth's land surface, composed of fragmented rock particles with humus, water, and air.
Accumulated remains of sponges consisting of the small pointed structures of calcite or silica that compose their skeletons.
Any of various primitive sessile aquatic (chiefly marine) animals of the phylum Porifera, which have porous baglike bodies with a skeleton of hard spicules or elastic fibres.
Pieces of rock or mineral substance (other than metal) of definite form and size, usually artificially shaped, and used for some special purpose.
dominio.observaciones: Used, for example, for building, for paving, or in the form of a block, slab, or pillar set up as a memorial and/or a boundary-mark.

dominio.definicion: A soft porous calcium carbonate rock formed by deposition around mineral springs.
dominio.observaciones: Also any friable porous stone formed of consolidated, often stratified material.

dominio.definicion: A mineral that may be used for the extraction of uranium.
dominio.observaciones: For example, pitchblende, uraninite, carnotite, torbernite, tyuyamunite, autunite, uranophane, and brannerite.

dominio.definicion: Plants collectively, especially those dominating a particular area or habitat.
Loose fragmented solid material ejected from a volcano.
The transparent, colourless, tasteless, odourless, liquid compound of hydrogen and oxygen (formula H2O).
dominio.observaciones: Forms the main constituent of seas, lakes, rivers, and rain, and is put to many domestic and industrial uses.

dominio.definicion: The hard, compact, fibrous substance of which the roots, trunks, and branches of trees and shrubs consist.
dominio.observaciones: Consists largely of secondary xylem, which forms the strengthening and water-transporting tissue of the plant.

dominio.definicion: A hard lustrous bluish-white metallic chemical element, atomic number 30, which is obtained from sphalerite and other ores. (Symbol Zn.)
dominio.observaciones: Used for roofing, galvanizing iron, and making alloys with copper.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary salt deposit left after the evaporation of a body of water.
A plastic composition in which glass reinforcements are imbedded with strength properties greatly superior to those of the base resin.
dominio.observaciones: The reinforcements are usually fibres, rovings, fabrics or mats.

dominio.definicion: A light silvery ductile and malleable metal, not readily tarnished by air, which is a chemical element, atomic number 13. (Symbol Al.)
A dark, fine-grained igneous rock, often displaying columnar structure and usually composed largely of plagioclase with pyroxene and olivine.
Native consolidated solid rock that has been unaffected by the processes of weathering and underlies the surface of the Earth.
dominio.observaciones: Often overlain by the results of weathering processes, including soil, clay, sand, gravel and related loose materials.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock consisting of angular, coarse-grained fragments cemented together by a fine-grained matrix (for example: by lime).
Clay kneaded, moulded, and baked or sun-dried, used as a building material.
A nonmetallic material made from clay and hardened by firing at high temperature.
dominio.observaciones: It contains minute silicate crystals suspended in a glassy cement.

dominio.definicion: A substance or preparation formed by the combination or mixture of various ingredients, especially a compound artificial substance serving the purpose of a natural one.
A heavy-duty building material made from a mixture of broken stone or gravel, sand, cement, and water, that forms a stonelike mass on hardening.
A malleable and ductile reddish metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 29. (Symbol Cu.)
dominio.observaciones: Used especially for electrical conductors and as the base of alloys.

dominio.definicion: An igneous rock chemically the same as basalt and gabbro but medium-grained with a usually ophitic texture.
dominio.observaciones: Usually dark coloured and fine or medium textured. Occurs in minor intrusions such as sills and dykes.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock composed chiefly of a hexagonal carbonate of calcium, magnesium, and usually iron that occurs as translucent crystals of various colours, alone or with calcite.
A thinly-bedded sedimentary deposit consisting of shales and marls alternating with coarser strata such as sandstones and conglomerates.
A foliated, usually coarse-grained, metamorphic rock in which bands of granular minerals alternate with bands of flaky or prismatic ones.
dominio.observaciones: Formed by the metamorphism of granite and other igneous rocks, and typically consisting of feldspar, quartz, and mica. Usually of a streaked, wavy or banded appearance.

dominio.definicion: A precious metal which is characterized by its yellowish colour, resistance to tarnishing and corrosion, and great malleability and ductility, and is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 79 (symbol Au).
Any of a broad class of granular crystalline plutonic rocks, consisting essentially of quartz, orthoclase, feldspar, and mica or hornblende.
dominio.observaciones: Often used for building.

dominio.definicion: Any igneous rock of dark-green appearance, especially containing chlorite, epidote, and/or hornblende.
dominio.observaciones: Includes nephrites and, in particular, jade.

dominio.definicion: A malleable, magnetic, readily oxidizable metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 26. (Symbol Fe.)
dominio.observaciones: Occurs abundantly in certain ores and in meteorites, and is widely used, chiefly in alloys such as steel.

dominio.definicion: A clayey (usually red) soil or soil horizon characterized by a high proportion of sesquioxides, especially of aluminum and iron, and a low proportion of bases and silica.
dominio.observaciones: Formed by chemical weathering in tropical and subtropical regions, especially one which hardens or has hardened on exposure to air. Also loosely any of various other reddish or iron-rich surface materials in the tropics and sub-tropics.

dominio.definicion: A soft, heavy, malleable, bluish-grey metal that is a chemical element, atomic number 82, occurring in galena and other minerals. (Symbol Pb.)
A sedimentary rock composed chiefly of calcium carbonate.
dominio.observaciones: Yields lime when calcined and is used as a building material and in the making of cement.

dominio.definicion: Timber sawn into rough planks or otherwise partly prepared.
Limestone that has been recrystallized by metamorphism and is capable of taking a polish, especially one that is pure white or has a mottled surface.

Building materials (for example: stone, brick, concrete, hollow-tile, concrete block, gypsum block, or other similar building units or materials and/or a combination of the same) bonded together with mortar to form a structure (for example: a wall, a pier, or a buttress).
Any of the class of substances that are characteristically lustrous, ductile, fusible, malleable solids and are good conductors of heat and electricity.
dominio.observaciones: For example, gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, tin, and certain alloys (as brass and bronze).

dominio.definicion: Composed in part, but not completely, by metal.
Any of a large class of substances which are polymers based on synthetic resins or modified natural polymers.
dominio.observaciones: May be moulded, extruded, or cast while soft or liquid, and then set into a rigid or slightly elastic form, usually by heating or cooling.

dominio.definicion: An unstratified or igneous rock having a homogeneous groundmass containing larger crystals of one or more minerals (frequently feldspar).
dominio.observaciones: For example, a hard rock quarried in ancient Egypt, having crystals of white or red plagioclase feldspar in a fine red groundmass of hornblende or apatite. Loosely, any attractive red or purple stone taking a high polish.

dominio.definicion: Reinforced concrete in which internal stresses have been introduced to reduce potential tensile stress in the concrete resulting from loads.
A extremely compact, hard, granular rock consisting essentially of quartz.
dominio.observaciones: It is a metamorphosed sandstone in which the siliceous element is often so blended with the quartz grains so as to give the rock a nearly homogenous texture.

dominio.definicion: Any material or combination of materials which spontaneously emits ionizing radiation (for example: nuclear particles and/or gamma rays).
Poured concrete containing steel bars or metal netting to increase its tensile strength.
Any of various sedimentary rocks composed of sand grains, especially of quartz, cemented together.
dominio.observaciones: Typically red, yellow, brown, grey, or white in colour.

dominio.definicion: Soft finely stratified rock that splits easily into fragile laminae, consisting of consolidated mud or clay.
A precious metal which is characterized by its lustrous white colour and great malleability and ductility, and is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 47. (Symbol Ag.)
A dense, fine-grained, metamorphic rock that develops a characteristic cleavage which may be at any angle with the original bedding plane.
dominio.observaciones: Typically dark grey, blue, or green in colour. Splits readily into smooth parallel-sided flat plates, and used for making tiles for roofing and flooring.

dominio.definicion: Any of numerous artificially produced alloys of iron containing up to 3 percent of other elements (including less than about 2.2 percent carbon) and having great strength and malleability.
dominio.observaciones: Able to be tempered to many different degrees of hardness. Used for making tools, weapons, and/or machinery.

dominio.definicion: A beam or piece of wood forming or capable of forming part of any structure.
A white or light-coloured concretionary limestone, usually hard and semi-crystalline, precipitated from water holding calcium carbonate in solution (for example: in hot springs).
dominio.observaciones: May be used for building.

dominio.definicion: A timber that has been impregnated with chemicals (for example: cresote oil) to reduce damage from wood rot and/or insects.
dominio.observaciones: Often used for the portions of a structure that are likely to be in ongoing contact with soil and/or water.

definicion: The general colour of a waterbody sediment based on the Geological Society of America (GSA) rock colour chart and the Munsell colour system.
descripcion: The Munsell system is based on a colour solid, or approximately a colour sphere, which has a neutral gray central axis grading from white at the top to black at the bottom. This property of lightness is called value. Around the circumference or equator of the solid are the ten major hues, each of which is divided into ten numbered divisions, so that 5 marks the middle of the hue, and 10 marks the boundary between one hue and the next. Thus, any particular hue can be designated by a number and a letter such as 5R or 10YR. Any single vertical section through the neutral gray axis and a particular hue constitutes a colour chart on which the colors grade in value from light at the top to dark at the bottom, and in chroma (degree of saturation) from gray at one edge to the most vivid colors out at the margin. Both value and chroma are numbered so any particular colour can be given a numerical designation representing hue, value, and chroma such as 5R 6/4 and 10YR 8/2. Colour names are based on the Inter-Society Color Council-National Bureau of Standards system of names.

definicion: The pattern of settlement of an urban area based on the most frequently occurring geometric configuration (pattern) of streets and/or canals.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a settlement pattern.

dominio.definicion: The streets form an intersecting grid pattern of approximately regularly spaced lines at right angles to each other.
The streets form a discontinuous intersecting grid pattern of approximately regularly spaced lines at right angles to each other.
dominio.observaciones: Street discontinuities are often created to form small urban parks, or to discourage through-traffic in a residential neighborhood; the consequence is blocky irregularities in the overall pattern.

dominio.definicion: The streets follow a planned pattern of curves and irregularities designed to discourage through traffic and ensure increased privacy.
dominio.observaciones: Usually only found in residential neighborhoods.

dominio.definicion: The streets tend to radiate out from a central point in a somewhat evenly spaced pattern in all directions similar to the spokes of a wheel; side streets connecting to the radials tend to be unevenly spaced and to connect only a few of the radials instead of going completely around.

The streets tend to radiate out from a central point in an unevenly spaced pattern in all directions similar to the spokes of a wheel; side streets connecting to the radials tend to be unevenly spaced and to connect only a few of the radials instead of going completely around.
The streets follow a mix of rectangular and curvilinear patterns.
The streets follow a mix of rectangular and radial patterns.
The streets follow a mix of radial and curvilinear patterns.
There is a single main street perhaps with a short paralleling side street, or it stretches out in both directions along two main intersecting roads (in outline configured as a cross).
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes referred to a strip development and common on the edge of expanding urban areas or in rural areas where the main thoroughfare or intersecting roads are the only ones paved or otherwise improved.

dominio.definicion: The main street pattern is a series of somewhat evenly spaced, increasingly large circles around a central point; side streets connecting to the circles tend to be unevenly spaced and to connect only a few of the circles instead of radiating out continuously from the center.
The main thoroughfare areas are a series of regularly spaced canals, similar to the regular street pattern.
The main thoroughfare areas are a series of irregularly organized unevenly spaced canals.
The majority of the somewhat evenly spaced streets follow the contour of the land, staying near the same elevation throughout.
dominio.observaciones: Usually found in urban areas on steep slopes where a few steep and sharply twisting side streets connect the paralleling contour streets.

dominio.definicion: The majority of the streets follow the contour of the land, staying near the same elevation throughout, however they are unevenly or widely spaced from each other.
dominio.observaciones: Usually found in urban areas on steep slopes where a few steep and sharply twisting side streets connect the paralleling contour streets.

dominio.definicion: The streets extend in an irregular pattern from the center reflecting the historic pattern of development, often centred by a church or fortress.
dominio.observaciones: Usually found in the center of older urban areas.

descripcion: The description may include, for example, the construction materials and colour.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of a shoreline construction (for example: a pier, a wharf, or a quay).
descripcion: May be used as a means of subtyping Feature: 'Shoreline Construction'.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a shoreline construction type.

dominio.definicion: A long, narrow structure extending into the water to afford a berthing place for vessels.
dominio.observaciones: May also serve as a promenade.

dominio.definicion: A structure serving as a berthing place for vessels.
A wharf approximately parallel to the shoreline and accommodating ships on one side only, the other side being attached to the shore.
dominio.observaciones: It is usually of solid construction, as contrasted with the open pile construction usually used for piers.

dominio.definicion: A structure that protects a waterbody region (for example: a shore, a harbour, and/or an anchorage) from water waves by preventing them from reaching the protected region or reducing their magnitude.
A low artificial wall-like structure of durable material extending from the land to seaward for a particular purpose, such as to prevent coast erosion.
A form of breakwater alongside which vessels may lie on the sheltered side only.
dominio.observaciones: In some cases it may lie entirely within an artificial harbour, permitting vessels to lie along both sides.

dominio.definicion: A structure extending into the water used as a platform for recreational purposes and not intended as a berthing place for vessels.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a fishing pier or a promenade pier.

dominio.definicion: A wall, bank or jetty often submerged, built to direct or confine the flow of a river or tidal current or to promote scour actions.
A layer of broken rock, cobbles, boulders, or fragments of sufficient size to resist the erosive forces of flowing water and wave action.
dominio.observaciones: The materials are typically poured into place, with little if any internal structure, resulting in a loose irregular surface that may need to be refreshed over time.

dominio.definicion: A facing of stone or other material placed along the edge of a waterbody (for example: a river, a canal, or a shoreline) to stabilize the bank and to protect it from the erosive action of the water.
dominio.observaciones: The facing presents a relatively smooth face to the water flow and is typically a substantial, permanent, engineering construction.

dominio.definicion: An embankment or wall for protection against waves or tidal action along a shore or water front.
Steps at the shoreline as the connection between land and water on different levels.

A sloping structure that can either be used, as a landing place, at variable water levels, for small vessels (for example: landing ships and ferry boats), or for hauling a cradle carrying a small vessel.
dominio.observaciones: The cradle may travel on rails.

dominio.definicion: The prepared and usually reinforced inclined surface on which keel- and bilge-blocks are laid for supporting a vessel under construction.
dominio.observaciones: Rails associated with a slipway are usually represented separately, for example as a marine railway.

dominio.definicion: A wharf consisting of a solid wall of concrete, masonry, and/or wood such that the water cannot circulate freely under the wharf.
dominio.observaciones: The type of construction affects ship-handling; for example, a solid face wharf may give shelter from tidal streams, but under certain circumstances a cushion of water may build up between such a wharf and a ship attempting to berth at it, causing difficulties in ship handling.

dominio.definicion: A wharf supported on piles or other structures that allow free circulation of water under the wharf.
An inclined plane used to dump logs into the water for transport, or to haul logs out of the water for processing.
A paved public walk along a sea-front.
dominio.observaciones: May include piers and/or boardwalks, and usually located at a resort.

definicion: An indication that the delineation of a shoreline is definite.
descripcion: The delineation of the shoreline along a beach is typically definite whereas along a mangrove swamp it is typically indefinite.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of a shoreline ramp based on its design and intended use.
descripcion: May be used as a means of subtyping Feature: 'Shoreline Ramp'.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a shoreline ramp type.

dominio.definicion: An inclined plane used to dump logs into the water for transport, or to haul logs out of the water for processing.

A sloping structure that can either be used, as a landing place, at variable water levels, for small vessels (for example: landing ships and ferry boats), or for hauling a cradle carrying a small vessel.
dominio.observaciones: The cradle may travel on rails.

dominio.definicion: The prepared and usually reinforced inclined surface on which keel- and bilge-blocks are laid for supporting a vessel under construction.
dominio.observaciones: Rails associated with a slipway are usually represented separately, for example as a marine railway.

definicion: The physical characteristics of a shoreline.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a shoreline type.

dominio.definicion: Covered by one of several genera of tropical trees (for example: mangrove or nipa) or shrubs that produce many prop roots and grow along low-lying banks into shallow water.
Made up of spongy land saturated with water.
dominio.observaciones: It may have a shallow covering of water, usually with a considerable amount of vegetation appearing above the surface.

dominio.definicion: Made up of rock and rock fragments ranging in size from pebbles and gravel to boulders or large rock masses.
Made up of the debris (for example: waste fragments of masonry) of decayed or demolished buildings and/or other structures.
Made up of material weathered or eroded from a rocky coast, usually collected at the base of a cliff.
dominio.observaciones: Associated with landslides and coastal erosion. There will be an irregular jagged line produced by the rubble and coastal water interface.

dominio.definicion: Made up of sand, loose material consisting of small but easily distinguishable, separate grains, between 0.0625 and 2.000 millimetres in diameter.
Made up of rounded, often flat waterworn rock fragments larger than approximately 16 millimetres in diameter.
Faced by a reef, often of large extent, composed chiefly of coral and its derivatives.
Faced by a vertical cliff forming the seaward edge of an ice shelf, ranging in height from 2 metres to 50 metres or more above sea level.
Made up of soft wet soil, sand, dust, and/or other earthy matter.

definicion: A shortened form of a full name that could substitute for the full name and consists of the specific part of the full name.
descripcion: It usually includes the specific term(s) in the full name for the following types of features: geopolitical entities and their administrative divisions; specific geomorphologic forms (for example: islands, mountains, mountain passes, and rivers); specific places (for example: railway stations); and in general those full names that are in English (excepting those that are considered to be variants) or have been transliterated.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is 128 characters in maximum length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: A shortened form of a full name that could substitute for the full name and consists of the specific part of the full name, except that any diacritics and special characters have been replaced with their corresponding Roman characters.
descripcion: It usually includes the specific term(s) in the full name for the following types of features: geopolitical entities and their administrative divisions; specific geomorphologic forms (for example: islands, mountains, mountain passes, and rivers); specific places (for example: railway stations); and in general those full names that are in English (excepting those that are considered to be variants) or have been transliterated.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that contains only non-lexical characters and is 128 characters in maximum length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of a reserved lane by the verge of a road.
descripcion: Road shoulders are generally kept clear of traffic for breakdown, emergency purposes and use by maintenance vehicles.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a shoulder type.

dominio.definicion: A road shoulder consisting of a different material from the road it adjoins that makes a softer or looser surface.
dominio.observaciones: For example, gravel.

dominio.definicion: A road shoulder consisting of the same hard material as the road itself.
dominio.observaciones: Usually a hard surface material such as asphalt or concrete.

definicion: The type of a sign based on its function and/or structure.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a sign type.

dominio.definicion: A large outdoor board for advertisements.
dominio.observaciones: May be attached to another structure or self-supporting. Usually elevated so as to be seen for a significant distance.

dominio.definicion: A large outdoor board for publicly displaying the score in an athletic event.
dominio.observaciones: Usually associated with an athletic stadium or major playing field.

dominio.definicion: A roadside sign conveying information (for example: navigation directions or hazard warnings) to drivers of motor vehicles.
A signboard used to indicate speed restrictions, cable landings, and other items of interest to maritime navigation.
A large outdoor screen for showing motion pictures.

definicion: The number of signals, the combination of signals or the Morse character(s) within one period of full sequence of a repeating signal.

datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a signal group pattern.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: The signal group of a light is encoded using curved brackets to separate the individual groups. A group of signals may be a single number, a chain of numbers separated by '+', a sequence of up to 4 letters or a letter and a number. Where no specific signal group is given for one of the light characteristics, this should be shown by an empty pair of brackets. A fixed light has no signal group. For example, for a Very Quick (6) and Long Flashing light the encoding is '(6)(1)' whereas as for a Fixed and Flashing light the encoding is '()(1)'.

definicion: The distance from a radio navigational aid at which the radio signal becomes usable or reliable after a range of unusable signal.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value that is restricted to be non-negative.
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of length equal to 1,852.0 metres.

definicion: The minimum distance from a radio navigational aid at which the radio signal becomes unusable or unreliable.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value that is restricted to be non-negative.
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of length equal to 1,852.0 metres.

definicion: The strength of the returning signal from the target.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of the logarithmic ratio (base 10) between two power levels.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of power level difference (power quantity ratio) equal to 0.1 bel, approximately 0.1151293 neper.

nombre: Significant Point Association Use in Airspace
definicion: The manner in which a significant point is used in association to an airspace.
descripcion: For example: entry point or exit point.

datatype.nombre: Significant Point Association Use in Airspace Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a significant point association use in airspace.

dominio.definicion: The first reporting point, determined by reference to a significant point, over which an aircraft passes or is expected to pass upon entering an airspace.
The last reporting point, determined by reference to a significant point, over which an aircraft passes or is expected to pass before leaving an airspace.
The first or the last reporting point, determined by reference to a significant point, over which an aircraft passes or is expected to pass upon entering or before leaving an airspace.

nombre: Significant Point Relative Location to Airspace
definicion: The location of a significant point in relation to an airspace, as a category.
descripcion: For example: In, Out, or On Border.

datatype.nombre: Significant Point Relative Location to Airspace Code
datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a significant point relative location to airspace.

dominio.definicion: Situated on the border of the airspace.
Situated in the airspace.
Situated outside the airspace.

definicion: The maximum calculated load on each tire of a landing gear assembly that a movement area surface can support.
descripcion: The single isolated wheel load is computed by dividing the assembly load by the number of tires on the assembly. There may be a different value for each landing gear assembly on the aircraft.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of the property of a body that causes it to have weight in a gravitational field.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "mass", defined as equal to the mass of the international prototype of the kilogram.

nombre: Single Isolated Wheel Load (SIWL) Tire Inflation Pressure
definicion: The maximum aircraft tire pressure that a movement area surface can support.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of force applied to a unit area of surface.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of pressure equal to 6,894.76 pascal.

definicion: The estimated maximum load bearing capacity of a thoroughfare (for example: a road) for a single vehicle wheel.
descripcion: Exceeding the estimated load bearing capacity results in excessive surface degradation and premature failure.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of the property of a body that causes it to have weight in a gravitational field.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of mass equal to 453.59237 kilograms.

definicion: The method, if known, by which a wrecked vessel was sunk.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a sinking method.

dominio.definicion: The wrecked vessel was sunk by the hostile action of an aircraft.
The wrecked vessel was sunk by encountering an explosive mine.
The wrecked vessel was sunk by accidental means.
The wrecked vessel was sunk during the course of ordnance testing or firing practice.
The wrecked vessel was deliberately sunk by actions of its own crew.
The wrecked vessel was sunk by gunfire directed from hostile land based artillery.
The wrecked vessel was sunk by the hostile action of submarine(s).
The wrecked vessel was sunk by the hostile action of surface vessel(s).
The wrecked vessel was sunk by enemy action(s) not specified or unknown.

definicion: A fixed value of magnetic declination applied within an aid to navigation to the true direction in order to obtain the reported magnetic directions for radials, courses and headings.
descripcion: The value is fixed for a period of time and therefore may differ from the true declination due to subsequent drift of the Earth's magnetic field.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value that is restricted to fall in the range from -180 to 180, inclusive.
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of an angle in two dimensions (the angle between two half-lines terminating at the same point).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of plane angle equal to pi/180, approximately 0.01745532925199433 radians.

definicion: The date and, optionally, time in which the slaved variation was programmed into the radio navigation aid installation.
descripcion: Midnight is understood to be 00:00:00 (the beginning of a day); when the time is not specified then midnight in the local time zone is typically implied.

datatype.nombre: Slaved Variation Date and Time Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a slaved variation date and time.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.4.1, Combinations of date and time of day - Complete representation - Extended format, a calendar date and time representation, as a single data element comprising up to twenty characters, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, [hh] the ordinal number of an hour within the calendar day, [mm] the ordinal number of a minute within the hour, [ss] the ordinal number of a second within the minute, and an optional 'Z' when the time is according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12' for 12 April 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412T114520Z').

definicion: The maximum number of beds or equivalent sleeping spaces normally available at a facility where guests or occupants can sleep for the night.
descripcion: This quantity indicates the maximum number of people that can sleep at the facility at any given time.

datatype.definicion: A count domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a cardinal number or an ordinal number. For example, 4 (as in the number of legs of a cow).
datatype.nota: The realization of this count datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The direction of maximum uphill surface slope of a feature.
descripcion: The direction is measured as an angle in a clockwise direction from true north (0 arc degrees). May be reported in whole arc degrees.

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value that is restricted to be completely contained in the range from 0 to 360, inclusive.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of an angle in two dimensions (the angle between two half-lines terminating at the same point).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of plane angle equal to pi/180, approximately 0.01745532925199433 radians.

definicion: The small-scale shape and/or configuration of the land surface in a localized area.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a small-scale geomorphologic type.

dominio.definicion: A natural or man-made structure in the form of an arch.
A ring-shaped coral reef which has closely spaced islands on it encircling a lagoon.
A hole in coastal rock through which sea water is forced by a rising tide or waves and spurted through an outlet into the air.
A small depression in sandy terrain that is caused by wind erosion.
A long, narrow bedrock platform bounded by steeper slopes above and below, usually overlooking a waterbody.
A small, isolated, usually flat-topped hill with steep sides.
A land area, more prominent than a point, projecting into the sea and marking a notable change in coastal direction.
A deep narrow slot, notch, or groove in a coastal cliff.
A strip or area of land having significance as an access way.
A bowl-like hollow partially surrounded by cliffs or steep slopes at the head of a glaciated valley.
An asymmetric ridge formed on tilted strata.
A dome-shaped landform (for example: an incipient volcano).
A low place in a mountain ridge, not used for transportation.
A relatively undissected upland between adjacent stream valleys.
A narrow strip of land connecting two larger land masses and bordered by water.
A narrow strip of land between the two limbs of a meander loop at its narrowest point.
An area reclaimed from the sea by dyking and draining.
A bluff or prominent hill overlooking or projecting into a lowland.
A tapering piece of land projecting into a body of water, less prominent than a cape.
A broad, open pass crossing a ridge or between hills or mountains.
A small crater-shape depression in a karst area.
A land surface with a relatively uniform slope angle.
A narrow, straight or curved continuation of a beach into a waterbody.
A subordinate ridge projecting outward from a hill, mountain or other elevation.
A steep concave slope formed by an accumulation of loose rock fragments at the base of a cliff or steep slope.
A long wind-swept trough between parallel longitudinal sand dunes.
A long, narrow alluvial platform bounded by steeper slopes above and below, usually overlooking a waterbody.
A valley, the floor of which is notably higher than the valley or shore to which it leads.
dominio.observaciones: Most common in areas that have been glaciated.

dominio.definicion: A fan-shaped alluvial deposit formed especially where a watercourse begins to descend a gentler slope.
dominio.observaciones: The watercourse may be intermittent or currently dry.

dominio.definicion: A mangrove swamp surrounded by a waterbody thus forming an island.
It may occur singly or as one of a series of approximately parallel deposits representing successive positions of an advancing shoreline.
dominio.observaciones: A low, essentially continuous mound of beach and dune material heaped up by the action of waves and currents on the backshore of a beach beyond the present limit of storm waves or of ordinary tides.

dominio.definicion: A flat-topped, isolated elevation with steep slopes on all sides, less extensive than a plateau.

definicion: The depth of the soil or unconsolidated surface material.
descripcion: The soil layer ranges from the top of the organic horizon 'O' to the bottom of the substratum 'C'.

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The agent(s) that are responsible for soil deterioration.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a soil deterioration cause.

dominio.definicion: Heavy waves of destructive force.
Erosion of fine material by water on slopes and plains.
Battering movement of water on the coastline.
Extremely heavy continuous rainfalls.
Downhill movement of rock masses due to tectonic activity.
Downhill movement of rock masses due to their own weight.
Destruction of rocks by density variation in frost change climates.
Harmful substances.
Radiation resulting from the decay of radioactive materials.
Supply of fertilizers.
Uncultivated arable land.
Loss of minerals in soils due to excessive cultivation.
A conscious and complete deforestation of an area under acceptance of ecological changes.
Downhill movement of the water-saturated topsoils on a frozen layer.
Extraction of mineral resources.
Extensive devastation after a meteorite impact.
Pervasive and extensive devastation of the surface as a consequence of military actions.
Extensive destruction of the vegetation by fire.

dominio.etiqueta: Mud Flow and/or Flow of Debris
dominio.definicion: Water-enriched sediment-flow.
Sudden and desastrous floating of an area after a dam break.
Surface tremors and following occurrence of fractions and mass movements.
Cut down of the stock of trees and subsequent total burning down of the vegetation.
Occurence of extremly heavy waves with destructive force in coastal areas due to volcanic eruptions, seaquakes or mass movements.
Mass movements downhill with a coverage of the surface at the bottom.
Sudden and disastrous mass movements of rocks and their deposition at the bottom.
Sudden and rapid fall of snow and ice on a slide of snow or on the subsoil.
Soil coverage by buildings.
Filling of a body of water with (mostly) fine sediments and subsequent colonisation by plants.
Reduction of the total volume of the soil and variation of the soil structure.
Desertification and erosion due to excessive and concentrated livestock keeping.
Artifical supply of water.
Pollution and enrichment by foreign and harmful substances.

definicion: The type(s) of soil deterioration based on the effects to the soil.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a soil deterioration type.

dominio.definicion: Salt accumulations in the topsoil.
Anthropogenic influenced landscape change in arid areas.
Increase of the soil water and transformation of the soil structure.
Increase in concentration of free hydrogenions in the soil.
Coverage of the soil layers by transported materials.
Seepage water caused eluviation of readily soluble substances at the rock formation.
Constant water logging (underground water,upper water, precipitations ) of an area.
Runoff-prevention of seepage water by impermeable strata.
Deep transformation of the soil structure.
Gravity caused extensive erosion on slopes and faces.
Expansive coverage of the surface with water.
Erosion and transport by wind.
Erosion and transport at the coast line by water.
Coverage of the surface due to building over.
Spread out of harmful substances.
Expansive interference by radioactive imission.
Excessive spread out of fertilizers.
Erosion and transport at river banks and the inundation area.
Hardening of the surface and catch of the plant-growth after heavy and prolonged rain-falls with subsequent dry periods.
Erosion of rocks by glacier flowing.
Erosion and transport by the movement of solid substances.

definicion: Force which has caused erosion to occur.
descripcion: For example: gravity, water, air.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a soil erosion cause.

dominio.definicion: Wind erosion on an area of shifting sand or loose soil, or where protective vegetation is disturbed or destroyed.
Heavy rainfall (minimum of 5 millimetres in 5 minutes, 7.1 millimetres in 10 minutes, 10 millimetres in 20 minutes, or 17.1 millimetres in 60 minutes).
dominio.observaciones: Torrential rain or intense rain.

dominio.definicion: A mechanical weathering process caused by alternate or repeated cycles of freezing and thawing of water in pores, cracks, and other openings, usually at the surface, fracturing the rock by the expansionary pressure associated with the freezing of water.
The mechanical weathering process caused by the movement of glacier ice, together with the erosive action of subglacial meltwater streams.
Mass transfer by gravity and/or a agent (for example: water, ice, or air).
The wave activity in the surf zone (where the wave breaks).
An abnormal wave in a lake, produced by a massive gravity slide from flanks into the lake.
The action of wearing away supporting material, as the undermining of a cliff by stream erosion.
Transport (erosion) of earth materials by water.
Transport (erosion) of earth materials by wind.

definicion: The soil type as specified by the Unified Soil Classification System (USCS).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a soil type.

dominio.definicion: Well-graded gravels and/or gravel-sand mixtures, with little or no fines.
Poorly-graded gravels and/or gravel-sand mixtures, with little or no fines.
Silty gravels and/or gravel-sand-silt mixtures.
Clayey gravels and/or gravel-sand-clay mixtures.
Well-graded sand and/or gravelly sands, with little or no fines.
Poorly graded sands and/or gravelly sands, with little or no fines.
Silty sands and/or sand-silt mixtures.
Clayey sands and/or sand-clay mixtures.
Inorganic silts and very fine sands, rock floor, silty or clayey fine sands or clayey with slight plasticity.
Inorganic clays of low to medium plasticity, gravelly clays, sandy clays, silty clays.
Organic silts and organic silty clays.
Inorganic clays of high plasticity.
Micaceous or diatomaceous inorganic silts.
Organic clays of medium to high plasticity and/or organic silts.
Peat and other highly organic soils.

dominio.etiqueta: ML-CL: Silt, Fine Sand and Lean Clay
dominio.definicion: Having both ML (inorganic silts and very fine sands, rock floor, silty or clayey fine sands or clayey with slight plasticity) and CL (inorganic clays of low to medium plasticity, gravelly clays, sandy clays, silty clays) characteristics.
Sedimentary salt deposits left after the evaporation of a body of water.
The soil was not evaluated.

definicion: The class of the formative element for second-level soil units.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a soil unit qualifier.

dominio.definicion: Having an abrupt textural change within 100 centimetres of the soil surface.
dominio.observaciones: Code: 'ap'.

dominio.definicion: Having a pH (1:1 in water) between 3.5 and 5 and jarosite mottles in some layer within 100 centimetres of the soil surface (in Solonchaks only).
dominio.observaciones: Code: 'ae'.

definicion: General moisture content or condition of a soil.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a soil wetness condition.

dominio.definicion: The soil moisture content is normally less than the field capacity.
dominio.observaciones: The field capacity is the amount of water held in the soil after excess gravitational or free water has drained away or moved out of the upper horizons (usually two or three days after a soaking rain). Dry soils are well drained and exhibit good to moderate internal and external drainage characteristics without any influence from impervious pans, cemented layers, or other soil horizons restricting free water movement within the soil. Dry soils do not have physical indications of saturation by water, such as strongly mottled and gleyed soil horizons, nor do they have water tables within 1.2 metres of the surface. Dry soils usually occupy upland positions in the landscape (for example: on ridges and/or upper slopes) where the depth to the water table is more than 1.2 metres. However, dry soils can also exist in many other landscape positions such as terrace slopes, upland toe slopes, upland flats, terrace flats, and flood plains that have well drained soil moisture conditions.

dominio.definicion: The soil moisture content is normally greater than or equal to field capacity but less than the soil moisture content at the liquid limit.
dominio.observaciones: At the liquid limit the soil is fully saturated and all soil pores contain water; this usually occurs at about 150 percent of field capacity. Soils in a moist state commonly have mottled and grayish or bluish horizons that as indicative of poor drainage wherein the water table is usually within 0.3 to 1.2 metres from the surface. The more mottled and gray the subsoil, the poorer the soil drainage. The more intense the mottles and the closer they are to the soil surface, the longer the period of saturation or the higher the water table. Moist soils generally occupy low-lying and concave or depressed positions in the landscape where the water table is found at a depth of 0.3 meter to 1.2 metres from the surface. These topographic sites are not only more susceptible to accumulating soil moisture after a precipitation event, but they also subsequently retain this moisture longer than other topographic positions in the landscape that have received equal amounts of precipitation. These sites can occur at the base of slopes, in upland depressions, and on some floodplains, low terraces, or other low-lying land along watercourses. Moist conditions can also exist in upland flats and other level areas that have soils with poor internal or external drainage, or in soils with impervious pans or cemented layers that restrict percolation and cause perched water tables. In additions, soils influenced by seepage can also exhibit moist soil conditions.

dominio.definicion: The soil moisture content ranges from the soil's liquid limit to its maximum water holding capacity, which approaches complete saturation.
dominio.observaciones: At complete saturation all soil pores contain water and is equal to approximately 200 percent of field capacity. A soil in a wet condition commonly has free standing water at or near the soil surface. Areas exhibiting wet soil conditions are commonly waterlogged or flooded at least part of the year, and have water tables within 0.3 metres of the surface throughout most of the year. Soils in a wet condition are commonly found in swamps, marshes, bogs, and other low-lying, perennially wet areas. Wet soils can also exist seasonally in level to nearly level upland flats with poor internal drainage or shallow, restrictive pans or impervious layers, or in sloping areas with soils that have very poor internals drainage, are affected by seepage, or both. Wet soils will bind easily and may form a 'muddy' or 'wet' ball when squeezed in the hand.

dominio.definicion: The soil is normally frozen, often permanently (for example: Arctic tundra with permafrost).

dominio.definicion: The highest level reached at a location by the water surface in one tidal cycle.
dominio.observaciones: When used on inland waters it is generally defined as a level that the daily mean water level exceeds less than 5 percent of the time.

dominio.definicion: The highest of the high waters (or single high water) of any specified tidal day due to the declination A1 effects of the moon and sun.
A tidal surface datum approximating the level of the mean of the lower low water at spring tides.
dominio.observaciones: This tidal datum approximates the lowest water level observed at a location and is usually below that of the lower low water at spring tides.

dominio.definicion: An approximation of mean low water adopted as the reference level for a limited region, irrespective of better determinations later.
dominio.observaciones: Used mostly in harbour and river engineering. Used in inland waters. It is generally defined as a level which the daily mean water level would fall below less than 5 percent of the time and by no more than 0.2 metres during the navigation season. A single level surface is usually chosen as the low water datum for a whole lake. On a river, low water datum is a sloping surface, which approximates the surface of the river at a low state.

dominio.definicion: The lowest of the low waters (or single low water) of any specified tidal day due to the declination A1 effects of the moon and sun.

dominio.definicion: The average height of the low waters of spring tides.

The average height of the sea at a tide station measured from a fixed predetermined reference level.
dominio.observaciones: Usually determined from hourly height readings, for all stages of the tide, over a 19-year period.

dominio.definicion: The arithmetic mean of mean high water and mean low water.
A tide of decreased range (or tidal currents of decreased speed) occurring semi-monthly as the result of the moon being in quadrature.
dominio.observaciones: The neap range of the tide is the average range occurring at the time of neap tides and is most conveniently computed from the harmonic constants. It is smaller than the mean range where the type of tide is either semi-diurnal or mixed and is of no practical significance where the type of tide is predominantly diurnal.

dominio.definicion: A tide of increased range (or tidal water currents of increased speed) occurring semi-monthly as the result of the moon being new or full.
dominio.observaciones: The spring range of tide is the average range occurring at the time of spring tides and is most conveniently computed from the harmonic constants. It is larger than the mean range where the type of tide is either semi-diurnal or mixed, and is of no practical significance where the type of tide is predominantly diurnal.

dominio.definicion: An approximation of mean low water that has been adopted as a standard reference for a limited area and is retained for an indefinite period regardless of the fact that it may differ slightly from a better determination of mean low water from a subsequent series of observations.

datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.4.1, Combinations of date and time of day - Complete representation - Extended format, a calendar date and time representation, as a single data element comprising up to twenty characters, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, [hh] the ordinal number of an hour within the calendar day, [mm] the ordinal number of a minute within the hour, [ss] the ordinal number of a second within the minute, and an optional 'Z' when the time is according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12' for 12 April 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412T114520Z').

datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.4.1, Combinations of date and time of day - Complete representation - Extended format, a calendar date and time representation, as a single data element comprising up to twenty characters, where [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month, [hh] the ordinal number of an hour within the calendar day, [mm] the ordinal number of a minute within the hour, [ss] the ordinal number of a second within the minute, and an optional 'Z' when the time is according to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ' (for example: '1985-04-12T11:45:20Z' for 11 hours, 45 minutes and 20 seconds UTC on 12 April 1985). Representations with reduced precision may be used in accordance with 5.4.2 (for example: '1985-04-12' for 12 April 1985). Representations consistently using basic format (eliminating the hyphen '-' and the colon ':') may be used in accordance with 5.4.1 (for example: '19850412T114520Z').

datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The type(s) of storage facilities available at a location (for example: a storage depot) or in the near vicinity (for example: near a pier).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a storage facilities available.

dominio.definicion: A tract of firm material capable of supporting only light vehicles, light equipment and/or light packaged goods.
A tract of hard material capable of supporting vehicles, heavy equipment and/or heavy packaged goods (for example: containerized).
An overhead construction intended to provide protection from the weather, especially precipitation.
dominio.observaciones: May be internally supported by posts but is independent of walls, for example, a Dutch barn.

dominio.definicion: A building, or part of a building, that is used for the storage of goods.
A building, or part of a building, that is used for the specialized storage of goods.
dominio.observaciones: For example, temperature-controlled, humidity-controlled, or cold storage.

dominio.definicion: Facilities for storing bulk (unpackaged) cereal grains (for example: wheat) and derivatives.
dominio.observaciones: May also include pneumatic, mechanical and electrical equipment for handling, conveying, cleaning, and weighing free-flowing and non-free-flowing cereal grains and derivatives.

dominio.definicion: Facilities for storing bulk (unpackaged) ore (for example: bauxite and iron), usually in uncovered areas.
dominio.observaciones: May also include mechanical and electrical equipment for handling, conveying, and weighing free-flowing ores.

dominio.definicion: Facilities for storing bulk liquids (for example: chemicals, petrochemicals, petroleum products and vegetable oils), usually in large free-standing tanks.
dominio.observaciones: May also include hydraulic, mechanical and electrical equipment for pumping, metering, and filtering free-flowing liquids.

dominio.definicion: Facilities for storing bulk gases (for example: oxygen, chlorine, chemicals, liquid propane gas (LPG) and compressed natural gas (CNG)), usually in large free-standing tanks.
dominio.observaciones: May also include hydraulic, mechanical and electrical equipment for pumping, metering, filtering, and weighing gases.

dominio.definicion: Facilities for storing potable water, often in large free-standing tanks that may be elevated.
dominio.observaciones: May also include hydraulic, mechanical and electrical equipment for pumping, metering, and filtering.

dominio.definicion: No storage facilities are available.
Facilities for storing shipping containers, usually by stacking in rows.
dominio.observaciones: The most widely used type of container is the general purpose (dry cargo) container having a nominal length and height of 20' x 8.5', 40' x 8.5', and 40' x 9.5' (termed 'high cube').

dominio.definicion: Facilities for storing bulk (unpackaged) granular materials (for example: salt and sand).
dominio.observaciones: May also include mechanical and electrical equipment for handling, conveying, and weighing, as well as roofed areas serving as protection from precipitation.

dominio.definicion: A surface structure that may be covered and/or surrounded with earth and is resistant to accidental explosion.
dominio.observaciones: Usually located away from other facilities and used for storage of explosive materials and/or ammunition.

dominio.definicion: A facility for handling bulk fuel (for example: steam coal, coke, liquid propane gas (LPG) and compressed natural gas (CNG)).
dominio.observaciones: May also include hydraulic, mechanical and electrical equipment for handling, conveying, weighing, pumping, metering, and filtering free-flowing liquids.

definicion: An indication that from one end of a tunnel the opposite end is visible when sighting through its interior.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: An indication that an entity poses a hazard to water-borne movement by blocking the passage of larger objects whilst permitting the free flow of water to continue.
descripcion: These objects can be very dangerous, because the force of the water will pin an object or body against the strainer and then pile up, pushing it down under water. Strainers are formed by many different objects, for example: storm grates over tunnels, trees that have fallen into a river (a 'log jam'), bushes by the side of the river that are flooded during high water, and reinforcing bars from broken concrete.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The designation by a dimensionless integer series (1, 2, 3, …) of the relative position of stream segments in the network of a drainage basin (catchment area), with the fourth order being the lowest rating.
descripcion: In general, all unbranched streams are first order streams. When two first order streams meet, the resulting channel is a second order stream. Where two second order streams meet a third order stream results, and so on. Any tributary of a lower order than the main channel is ignored.
aliases: Channel Order, River Order, Drain Order

datatype.definicion: An integer domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is an integer. For example, 6 (as in the length of a fathom in feet).
datatype.nota: The realization of this integer datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A dimensionless physical quantity, one which has no unit of measure.

definicion: The type of a street sign based on the nature of the information that it displays.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a street sign type.

dominio.definicion: Displays information about one or more potential destinations and directions that may be followed to reach that destination.
dominio.observaciones: The display often includes distance information.

dominio.definicion: Displays a temporary message regarding conditions on the road ahead.
dominio.observaciones: Usually the message is controlled remotely. For example, a sign warning of traffic congestion, accidents, incidents, construction zones, alternative routes or temporary speed limit changes.

dominio.definicion: Displays general information intended to be useful to motorists.
dominio.observaciones: For example: displays the name of a business, service, or facility that may be located along or near the road.

dominio.definicion: Displays information indicating what traffic must do when traversing a specific segment or lane of the road.
dominio.observaciones: For example, allocating certain lanes of the road to specific vehicles (for example: bus or taxi lanes). It may also be used to indicate special instructions, such as, 'attach or remove snow chains', 'use this lane only at road construction sites', or 'mandatory route for vehicles carrying dangerous loads'.

dominio.definicion: Displays the place name of a landmark.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the name of a town, river, mountain or administrative boundary (for example: a 'state line').

dominio.definicion: Displays information indicating that certain types of vehicle movements or types of traffic are prohibited.
dominio.observaciones: These signs may indicate, for example: 'no entry', 'no parking', 'no passing', 'no turns', 'wrong way', or specify a speed limit.

dominio.definicion: Displays the name of the road.
dominio.observaciones: The road name usually forms part of the postal address of sites along the sides of the road.

dominio.definicion: Displays the designated name and/or identifying number of a road.
dominio.observaciones: The sign may also display an emblem used to designate the road type (for example: national, interstate, or local).

dominio.definicion: Displays an indication of the order in which vehicles should merge at road junctions or pass through intersections.
dominio.observaciones: For example: 'yield', 'stop', and similar traffic right-of-way signs.

dominio.definicion: Displays an indication of a potential hazard, obstacle or situation on the road ahead that requires caution as it is traversed.
