dominio.observaciones: These signs may indicate, for example, approach to: the beginning or end of a divided highway; a recognized animal, pedestrian or railway crossing; a road junction; a traffic signal; a bridge or tunnel; road construction; an unusual degree of road curvature; unusual conditions caused by oncoming traffic; or the nature of road conditions ahead (for example: potential rock slides).

definicion: The primary type(s) of material composing a feature, exclusive of the surface.
descripcion: The basis for 'primary' may be, for example, compositional dominance or structural organization.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a structural material type.

dominio.definicion: A light silvery ductile and malleable metal, not readily tarnished by air, which is a chemical element, atomic number 13. (Symbol Al.)
The powdery residue, composed chiefly of earthy or mineral particles, left after the combustion of any substance.
Black or brownish-black, solid or viscous, bituminous pitch, of natural occurrence or produced from petroleum.
A dark, fine-grained igneous rock, often displaying columnar structure and usually composed largely of plagioclase with pyroxene and olivine.
Native consolidated solid rock that has been unaffected by the processes of weathering and underlies the surface of the Earth.
dominio.observaciones: Often overlain by the results of weathering processes, including soil, clay, sand, gravel and related loose materials.

dominio.definicion: Large water- or weather-worn stones.
Clay kneaded, moulded, and baked or sun-dried, used as a building material.
Containing calcium carbonate and/or other, usually insoluble, calcium salt.
White soft earthy limestone consisting almost wholly of calcite and derived chiefly from microscopic salt water fossil shells and fragments.
Residual pieces of combustible matter (for example: coal or wood) that has ceased to flame but has still combustible matter in them.
A member of the subclass Cirripedia, a marine crustacean that is generally sessile as an adult and has limbs modified for filter-feeding.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a barnacle.

dominio.definicion: A stiff tenacious fine-grained earth consisting mainly of hydrated aluminosilicates, which become more plastic when water is added and can be moulded and dried.
dominio.observaciones: Used to make bricks and/or pottery.

dominio.definicion: A hard opaque black or blackish mineral, mainly carbonized plant matter, found in seams or strata at or below the Earth's surface.
dominio.observaciones: Used as fuel and in manufacture (for example: to produce gas and/or tar).

dominio.definicion: Water-worn rounded stones, especially of the size used for paving.
Coal deprived by dry distillation of its volatile constituents.
A substance or preparation formed by the combination or mixture of various ingredients, especially a compound artificial substance serving the purpose of a natural one.
A heavy-duty building material made from a mixture of broken stone or gravel, sand, cement, and water, that forms a stonelike mass on hardening.
A coarse-grained sedimentary rock composed of rounded fragments embedded in a matrix of a cementing material such as silica.
A malleable and ductile reddish metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 29. (Symbol Cu.)
dominio.observaciones: Used especially for electrical conductors and as the base of alloys.

dominio.definicion: A usually hard calcareous substance secreted by many marine polyps as an external skeleton for support and habitation.
dominio.observaciones: Occurs in both single specimens and extensive accumulations. A similar substance may be produced by other lime-secreting marine organisms.

dominio.definicion: A significant, dense, coral outcrop consisting of corals grown, usually, from a single embryo.
A soft, friable, porous material consisting of fossilized microscopic unicellular alga that have rigid siliceous cell walls.
dominio.observaciones: Used for filters and insulation.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock composed chiefly of a hexagonal carbonate of calcium, magnesium, and usually iron that occurs as translucent crystals of various colours, alone or with calcite.
A thinly-bedded sedimentary deposit consisting of shales and marls alternating with coarser strata such as sandstones and conglomerates.

A rhizopod of the chiefly marine order Foraminiferida, typically having a calcareous shell with perforations (foramina) through which pseudopodia extend, the fossils forming a major constituent of chalk and many marine oozes.
A member of the genus Fucus, a seaweed with leathery fronds.
dominio.observaciones: For example, bladderwrack.

dominio.definicion: A substance made by fusing soda and/or potash with other ingredients.
dominio.observaciones: Usually transparent, lustrous, hard, and brittle.

dominio.definicion: A precious metal which is characterized by its yellowish colour, resistance to tarnishing and corrosion, and great malleability and ductility, and is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 79 (symbol Au).
Any of a broad class of granular crystalline plutonic rocks, consisting essentially of quartz, orthoclase, feldspar, and mica or hornblende.
dominio.observaciones: Often used for building.

dominio.definicion: Plant material (for example: straw and/or tall coarse grass), possibly also containing the slices of soil to which the plant material is attached.
dominio.observaciones: For example, used in thatching or sodding a roof.

dominio.definicion: Small water-worn or pounded stones.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes with an intermixture of sand and/or clay. Used for laying paths and roads.

dominio.definicion: Any igneous rock of dark-green appearance, especially containing chlorite, epidote, and/or hornblende.
dominio.observaciones: Includes nephrites and, in particular, jade.

dominio.definicion: Ground calcareous remains of macroscopic marine animals.
A malleable, magnetic, readily oxidizable metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 26. (Symbol Fe.)
dominio.observaciones: Occurs abundantly in certain ores and in meteorites, and is widely used, chiefly in alloys such as steel.

dominio.definicion: The fluid or semifluid magma or molten rock which flows from a volcano or other fissure in the Earth.
A soft, heavy, malleable, bluish-grey metal that is a chemical element, atomic number 82, occurring in galena and other minerals. (Symbol Pb.)
Fine yellowish-grey loam composed of material transported by the wind.
Timber sawn into rough planks or otherwise partly prepared.
A material for surfacing roads, consisting of broken stone or ironstone slag bound with tar alone, or of tar mixed with pitch or creosote.
dominio.observaciones: Historically, water-bound rather than using tar or pitch.

dominio.definicion: Stony and/or silaceous coral.
A hard grey brittle chemical element, atomic number 25, which is one of the transition metals. (Symbol Mn.)
dominio.observaciones: Used in steels and magnetic alloys.

dominio.definicion: Limestone that has been recrystallized by metamorphism and is capable of taking a polish, especially one that is pure white or has a mottled surface.
White to gray accumulation on lake bottoms caused by precipitation of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) mixed with microscopic fresh water fossil shells and fragments.

Building materials (for example: stone, brick, concrete, hollow-tile, concrete block, gypsum block, or other similar building units or materials and/or a combination of the same) bonded together with mortar to form a structure (for example: a wall, a pier, or a buttress).
A mixture of impure metal sulphides produced during the smelting of sulphide ores (for example: of copper or nickel).
Any of the class of substances that are characteristically lustrous, ductile, fusible, malleable solids and are good conductors of heat and electricity.
dominio.observaciones: For example, gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, tin, and certain alloys (as brass and bronze).

dominio.definicion: Soft wet soil, sand, dust, and/or other earthy matter.
dominio.observaciones: Also, the hard ground produced by the drying of an area of mud.

dominio.definicion: Any of various bivalve molluscs belonging chiefly to the marine superfamily Mytilacea or to the freshwater superfamily Unionacea.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the common edible marine bivalve, Mytilus edulis, which has a dark grey, slightly elongated shell and adheres by a byssus, frequently in large aggregations.

dominio.definicion: Any of numerous liquids with a smooth sticky feel that are immiscible with water (but miscible with organic solvents), flammable, and chemically neutral.
dominio.observaciones: For example, crude oil (or a refined product of this), lubricating oil, or vegetable oil.

dominio.definicion: A deposit or layer of white or grey calcareous matter largely composed of foraminiferan remains, covering large areas of the ocean floor.
Any of various bivalve molluscs of the family Ostreidae, several of which are eaten (especially raw) as a delicacy and may be farmed for food or pearls.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the common European Ostrea edulis, and members of the widespread genus Crassostrea.

dominio.definicion: Material in the form of thin flexible (frequently white) sheets made from the pulp of wood or other fibrous matter which is dried, pressed, and often bleached.
dominio.observaciones: Used for writing, printing, or drawing on, or for wrapping and/or covering.

dominio.definicion: Composed in part, but not completely, by metal.
Small, smooth, rounded stones, that have been worn by the action of water, ice, and/or sand.
Any of a large class of substances which are polymers based on synthetic resins or modified natural polymers.
dominio.observaciones: May be moulded, extruded, or cast while soft or liquid, and then set into a rigid or slightly elastic form, usually by heating or cooling.

dominio.definicion: Mosslike colonies of sessile, polypoid aquatic animals that reproduce by budding.
An unstratified or igneous rock having a homogeneous groundmass containing larger crystals of one or more minerals (frequently feldspar).
dominio.observaciones: For example, a hard rock quarried in ancient Egypt, having crystals of white or red plagioclase feldspar in a fine red groundmass of hornblende or apatite. Loosely, any attractive red or purple stone taking a high polish.

dominio.definicion: Reinforced concrete in which internal stresses have been introduced to reduce potential tensile stress in the concrete resulting from loads.
A light spongy form of volcanic glass, usually of pyroclastic origin and with a high silica content.
dominio.observaciones: Used, for example, as an abrasive (for example: in cleaning, polishing, removing stains and/or dead skin) or as an absorbent for moisture.

dominio.definicion: A trigonal rock-forming mineral consisting of silica, massive or crystallizing in colourless or white hexagonal prisms.
dominio.observaciones: Found widely in igneous and metamorphic rocks. Often coloured by impurities (as amethyst, citrine, cairngorm).

dominio.definicion: Marine protozoa with amoeba-like bodies and radiating filamentous pseudopods.
Any material or combination of materials which spontaneously emits ionizing radiation (for example: nuclear particles and/or gamma rays).
Poured concrete containing steel bars or metal netting to increase its tensile strength.
Stones of any size.
Any of various artificial polymeric substances that are tough and elastic.
dominio.observaciones: Originally an organic substance made from the coagulated latex of various plants, especially Hevea brasiliensis, which in its natural state is thermoplastic.

dominio.definicion: The debris (for example: waste fragments of masonry) of decayed or demolished buildings and/or other structures.
A white or (when impure) reddish-brown mineral crystallizing in the cubic system (sodium chloride, NaCl).
dominio.observaciones: Obtained by mining or by evaporation of seawater and used especially for seasoning and preserving food.

dominio.definicion: Granular material consisting of small eroded fragments of (mainly siliceous) rocks, finer than gravel and larger than a coarse silt grain.
dominio.observaciones: Generally ranging between 0.074 millimetres (No. 200 sieve) and 4.76 millimetres (No. 4 sieve) in size. Often a major constituent of a beach, desert, or the bed of a river or sea. Used for various purposes, as in smoothing stone, founding, or as an ingredient in mortar.

dominio.definicion: Any of various sedimentary rocks composed of sand grains, especially of quartz, cemented together.
dominio.observaciones: Typically red, yellow, brown, grey, or white in colour.

dominio.definicion: A coarse-grained pelitic metamorphic rock that has a structure marked by parallel layers of various minerals and can be split into thin irregular plates.
Rocky or soil-like material resulting from excavating, mining, dredging, and/or processing activities.
Rough masses resembling clinker, formed by the cooling of volcanic ejecta, and of a light aerated texture.
Waste, especially excremental, matter conveyed in sewers.
Calcareous remains of macroscopic marine animals, whole or in fragments.
Small, loose, rounded waterworn pebbles, especially as accumulated on a seashore.
Material consisting of particles whose sizes fall within a specified range (typically 0.002-0.06 millimetres) between those of sand and clay.
A precious metal which is characterized by its lustrous white colour and great malleability and ductility, and is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 47. (Symbol Ag.)
Stony material composed of waste matter or dross separated from metals during smelting or refining.
dominio.observaciones: Also any similar waste product resulting from the fusion of other substances.

dominio.definicion: A muddy or slimy matter or deposit consisting of a thick suspension of fine particles or gel in a liquid, especially one formed as waste in any of various industrial and mechanical processes.
Water solidified by exposure to cold.
dominio.observaciones: For example, snow or ice.

dominio.definicion: The material comprising the thin top layer of much of the Earth's land surface, composed of fragmented rock particles with humus, water, and air.
Accumulated remains of sponges consisting of the small pointed structures of calcite or silica that compose their skeletons.
Any of various primitive sessile aquatic (chiefly marine) animals of the phylum Porifera, which have porous baglike bodies with a skeleton of hard spicules or elastic fibres.
Any of numerous artificially produced alloys of iron containing up to 3 percent of other elements (including less than about 2.2 percent carbon) and having great strength and malleability.
dominio.observaciones: Able to be tempered to many different degrees of hardness. Used for making tools, weapons, and/or machinery.

dominio.definicion: Pieces of rock or mineral substance (other than metal) of definite form and size, usually artificially shaped, and used for some special purpose.
dominio.observaciones: Used, for example, for building, for paving, or in the form of a block, slab, or pillar set up as a memorial and/or a boundary-mark.

dominio.definicion: A white or light-coloured concretionary limestone, usually hard and semi-crystalline, precipitated from water holding calcium carbonate in solution (for example: in hot springs).
dominio.observaciones: May be used for building.

dominio.definicion: A soft porous calcium carbonate rock formed by deposition around mineral springs.
dominio.observaciones: Also any friable porous stone formed of consolidated, often stratified material.

dominio.definicion: A mineral that may be used for the extraction of uranium.
dominio.observaciones: For example, pitchblende, uraninite, carnotite, torbernite, tyuyamunite, autunite, uranophane, and brannerite.

dominio.definicion: Plants collectively, especially those dominating a particular area or habitat.
Loose fragmented solid material ejected from a volcano.
The transparent, colourless, tasteless, odourless, liquid compound of hydrogen and oxygen (formula H2O).
dominio.observaciones: Forms the main constituent of seas, lakes, rivers, and rain, and is put to many domestic and industrial uses.

dominio.definicion: The hard, compact, fibrous substance of which the roots, trunks, and branches of trees and shrubs consist.
dominio.observaciones: Consists largely of secondary xylem, which forms the strengthening and water-transporting tissue of the plant.

dominio.definicion: A hard lustrous bluish-white metallic chemical element, atomic number 30, which is obtained from sphalerite and other ores. (Symbol Zn.)
dominio.observaciones: Used for roofing, galvanizing iron, and making alloys with copper.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary salt deposit left after the evaporation of a body of water.
A plastic composition in which glass reinforcements are imbedded with strength properties greatly superior to those of the base resin.
dominio.observaciones: The reinforcements are usually fibres, rovings, fabrics or mats.

dominio.definicion: Rock formed by alteration of existing rocks by heat, pressure, or other processes in the Earth's crust.
dominio.observaciones: May be foliated or nonfoliated. Common foliated metamorphic rocks include slate, metasandstone, metaconglomerate, phyllite, schist, gneiss, and the 'hybrid rock' (part igneous, part metamorphic) migmatite. Common nonfoliated metamorphic rocks include hornfels, quartzite, marble, and dolomitic marble.

dominio.definicion: Rock formed by solidification of molten lava or magma.
dominio.observaciones: When extrusive igneous rock solidifies near or on the surface of the Earth it is termed volcanic.

dominio.definicion: An igneous rock chemically the same as basalt and gabbro but medium-grained with a usually ophitic texture.
dominio.observaciones: Usually dark coloured and fine or medium textured. Occurs in minor intrusions such as sills and dykes.

dominio.definicion: A foliated, usually coarse-grained, metamorphic rock in which bands of granular minerals alternate with bands of flaky or prismatic ones.
dominio.observaciones: Formed by the metamorphism of granite and other igneous rocks, and typically consisting of feldspar, quartz, and mica. Usually of a streaked, wavy or banded appearance.

dominio.definicion: A extremely compact, hard, granular rock consisting essentially of quartz.
dominio.observaciones: It is a metamorphosed sandstone in which the siliceous element is often so blended with the quartz grains so as to give the rock a nearly homogenous texture.

dominio.definicion: A dense fine-grained metamorphic rock that develops a characteristic cleavage which may be at any angle with the original bedding plane.
dominio.observaciones: Typically dark grey, blue, or green in colour. Splits readily into smooth parallel-sided flat plates, and used for making tiles for roofing and flooring.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock consisting of angular, coarse-grained fragments cemented together by a fine-grained matrix (for example: by lime).
Soft finely stratified rock that splits easily into fragile laminae, consisting of consolidated mud or clay.
Types of rock formed of compacted and hardened silt and mud.
A sedimentary rock composed chiefly of calcium carbonate.
dominio.observaciones: Yields lime when calcined and is used as a building material and in the making of cement.

dominio.definicion: A nonmetallic material made from clay and hardened by firing at high temperature.
dominio.observaciones: It contains minute silicate crystals suspended in a glassy cement.

dominio.definicion: Frozen water, a brittle transparent crystalline solid.
A clayey (usually red) soil or soil horizon characterized by a high proportion of sesquioxides, especially of aluminum and iron, and a low proportion of bases and silica.
dominio.observaciones: Formed by chemical weathering in tropical and subtropical regions, especially one which hardens or has hardened on exposure to air. Also loosely any of various other reddish or iron-rich surface materials in the tropics and sub-tropics.

dominio.definicion: A thin rectangular tile used as a roofing material and/or for cladding walls.
dominio.observaciones: Often made of wood or bituminous materials.

dominio.definicion: A mass of snow flakes (minute hexagonal ice crystals).
dominio.observaciones: Usually as the result of snow falling on the ground.

dominio.definicion: A usually square or oblong piece or slice of earth together with the grass growing on it.
Material used in thatching (for example: straw, reeds, and/or palm leaves).
A beam or piece of wood forming or capable of forming part of any structure.
Rock formed by the deposition of sediment.
dominio.observaciones: For example, sandstone, shale, and limestone.

dominio.definicion: Material consisting of particles finer than 0.074 millimetres (No. 200 sieve) including fine-textured materials of both low plasticity (for example: silt) and high plasticity (for example: clay).
Granular material consisting of small eroded fragments of (mainly siliceous) rocks, including fine-textured materials of low plasticity.
dominio.observaciones: Generally finer than 4.76 millimetres in diametre (No. 4 sieve).

dominio.definicion: Granular material consisting of a mixture of small sandy eroded fragments of (mainly siliceous) rocks and small water-worn or pounded stones that are larger than a coarse silt grain.
dominio.observaciones: Generally ranging between 0.074 millimetres (No. 200 sieve) and 7.62 centimetres in size.

dominio.definicion: Small water-worn, rounded or pounded stones up to the sizes used for paving.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes with an intermixture of sand and/or clay but generally ranging from 4.76 millimetres (No.4 sieve) up to 15-20 centimetres in size.

dominio.definicion: Large water- or weather-worn stones.
dominio.observaciones: Generally ranging from 15-20 centimetres to several metres in size.

dominio.definicion: Made of pieces of a hard material (for example: cobbles or concrete blocks) fitted closely together or of an undivided hard coating so as to give a compact, uniform, and smooth surface.
Vegetable matter partly decomposed in wet acid conditions in bogs and fens to form a firm brown deposit resembling soil.
Swampy ground.
dominio.observaciones: Often located along in a low-lying coastal region.

dominio.definicion: Granular material consisting of small eroded fragments of (mainly siliceous) rocks, finer than gravel and larger than a coarse silt grain that are underlain with soft soil, silt, and/or clay.
Brick made of adobe clay and straw, dried in the sun rather than by oven firing (as are standard bricks).
dominio.observaciones: Larger than standard bricks, adobe bricks require a type of clay that contains between 25 and 45 percent aluminum salts.

dominio.definicion: A timber that has been impregnated with chemicals (for example: cresote oil) to reduce damage from wood rot and/or insects.
dominio.observaciones: Often used for the portions of a structure that are likely to be in ongoing contact with soil and/or water.

dominio.definicion: Constructed principally from mud applied to a structural scaffold of plant material (for example: wooden posts).
dominio.observaciones: Effective only in extremely dry climates and usually must be resurfaced on a regular basis (for example: yearly) otherwise the structure steadily disintegrates under the effect of weather.

dominio.definicion: Any material consisting of glass filaments woven into a textile or paper, or embedded in plastic, for use as a construction or insulation material.
Any thin, flexible sheet material consisting of cured animal hides and/or textiles.
dominio.observaciones: The textile may be based on a mixture of natural (for example: cotton) and/or man-made (for example: nylon) fibres.

dominio.definicion: A class of natural and not man-made materials that are continuous filaments, or are in discrete elongated pieces that can be spun into filaments, creating thread, string, or rope.
dominio.observaciones: May be used directly for load-bearing (for example: a rope) or woven into a textile (for example: for use in clothing manufacture). Naturally occurring vegetable fibres include, for example, cotton, linen, jute, flax, ramie, sisal and hemp.

dominio.definicion: A collection of one or more optical fibres, organized into a cable and protectively wrapped.
A cement-based material that is usually reinforced with steel and shaped to a variety of forms (for example: ship or barge hulls).
dominio.observaciones: Other materials (for example: metal mesh or artificial fibre textile) may be used to reinforce the cement while providing a degree of flexibility.

dominio.definicion: A layer of loose stone of relatively constant size and shape.
dominio.observaciones: For example, as used to form a foundation for a breakwater.

dominio.definicion: A surface layer of soil containing grsss plants with their matted roots.

definicion: An indication that at least 50 percent of the terrain within an area is covered by a large number of vertical structures that are separated by ground-level passageways (for example: walkways, alleys, roads).
descripcion: A high concentration of vertical structures provides good cover and concealment, limits fields of observation and fire, and slows, diverts, or stops the movement of personnel or vehicles. Vertical structures are man-made features or objects, for example, buildings or non-building structures, such as, water towers, storage tanks, tombs, grave markers or memorial monuments.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The density of structures in an area.
descripcion: The number of structures in the area are counted and divided by the total area. Major wings may be counted as separate buildings provided there are significant changes in roof directions from the main building.

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A dimensionless physical quantity, one which has no unit of measure.

definicion: The geometric form, appearance, and/or configuration of the feature as a whole.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a structure shape.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a horizontal cylinder whose ends are rounded.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes referred to as 'blimp shaped'.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of the upper half of an ellipsoid of revolution whose axes are of unequal length, one being especially long and the others relatively equal and short.
dominio.observaciones: A misshapen hemisphere.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a vertical cylinder whose ends are rounded.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes referred to as 'bullet shaped'.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a polyhedron of which the base is a polygon of any number of sides, and the other faces are triangles with a common vertex.
dominio.observaciones: Usually four-sided.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a sphere.
dominio.observaciones: If the sphere is half-buried then it may appear as a dome.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of an upright cylinder, usually with an external bracing structure.
dominio.observaciones: The height of the cylinder may vary over time. The top may be of various shapes, for example, flat, rounded, or conical. For example, a telescoping gasholder (gasometer).

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a vertical cylinder with a flat top.
In the shape of a vertical cylinder with a domed top.
In the shape of a vertical cylinder with a conical top.
In the shape of a polyhedron of which the base is a triangle, and the other faces are triangles with a common vertex.
In the shape of a cone, apex at the bottom, with a small hole or tube at the apex.
dominio.observaciones: Used, for example, for guiding liquid or powder through a narrow opening.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a curved structure spanning an opening.
dominio.observaciones: May be used, for example, as a support (for example: for a bridge, roof, wall, or floor), as a monument, or as an ornamental feature.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a series of arches.
dominio.observaciones: For example, as along an arcade.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a series of rectangular prisms joined so as to be in the overall shape of the capital letter 'I' when viewed from above.
In the shape of a hemispherical surface, often as a rounded vault forming all or part of the roof of a building.
dominio.observaciones: Typically the structure supporting the dome has an elliptical (including circular) or polygonal base.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a sphere raised up on a column.
dominio.observaciones: The column serves as the sole support structure. The sphere may be 'flattened' so that its vertical dimension is smaller than its horizontal dimension (an ellipsoidal shape).

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a vertical cylinder raised up on a support structure.
dominio.observaciones: The top may be of various shapes, for example, flat, rounded, and/or conical. The support structure may be in the form of multiple poles or trusses.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a vertical cylinder.
dominio.observaciones: The top may be of various shapes, for example, flat, rounded, and/or conical.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a rectangular prism with all faces of equal size.
In the shape of a rectangular prism with the short faces oriented vertically and the base shaped as a wide rectangle.
In the shape of a long vertical, often slightly tapering, cylinder.
dominio.observaciones: For example, surmounted by an entablature and forming part of an arcade or colonnade, or standing alone as a monument.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of an ornamental plate or tablet.
dominio.observaciones: For example, affixed to a monument or building and containing identifying or commemorative details.

dominio.definicion: A representation of a living being, sculptured, moulded, or cast in a variety of materials (for example: marble, metal, or plaster).
dominio.observaciones: Especially a life-size or larger figure of a deity, mythical being, or eminent person.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a tall upright post surmounted with an attached short transverse beam.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a Calvary cross.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a horizontal cylinder.
dominio.observaciones: The ends may be various shapes, for example, flat, rounded, and/or conical.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a rectangular prism with the long faces oriented vertically and the base shaped as a rectangle (not as a square).
In the shape of a rectangular prism with the long faces oriented vertically and the base shaped as a square.
In the shape of a series of rectangular prisms joined so as to be in the overall shape of the capital letter 'H' when viewed from above.
In the shape of a relatively tall, narrow structure.
dominio.observaciones: May be of various shapes, sizes, and either open-frame or solid.

dominio.definicion: In the shape of a tapering, four-sided pillar with a pyramidal apex.
In the shape of an ellipsoid of revolution whose axes are of unequal length, one being especially long and the others relatively equal and short.
dominio.observaciones: A misshapen sphere.

dominio.definicion: A representation of a living being, sculptured, moulded, or cast in a variety of materials (for example: marble, metal, or plaster) whose base is mounted on a column.
dominio.observaciones: Especially a life-size or larger figure of a deity, mythical being, or eminent person. Although the pedestal is typically only a few metres in height it can be quite significant; for example, the 17 foot high statue of Lord Nelson in Trafalgar Square, London, is mounted on a 185 foot tall column.

definicion: The type of an underwater acoustic signal based on method of generation, control, and/or intended use.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a submarine acoustic signal type.

dominio.definicion: A large, electrically-operated diaphragm horn which produces a sound for transmission through water.
A sound signal transmitted through water that is controlled from on shore.
A sound signal transmitted through water that is not controlled from on shore.

definicion: An indication that an object on the sea floor (for example: a wreck) could be mistakenly identified as an operable submarine when detected (for example: using acoustic or magnetic sensors).

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of an electricity distribution substation based on its function(s).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a substation type.

dominio.definicion: A substation at which electrical current is switched.
dominio.observaciones: Usually located between a electrical power generating station and an electrical power distribution network.

dominio.definicion: A substation at which electrical voltage is transformed, typically to a lower level.
dominio.observaciones: Usually located between a high-tension long-distance transmission network and a local low-tension distribution network.

dominio.definicion: A substation where alternating current (AC) is converted to direct current (DC), or vice versa.
dominio.observaciones: Conversion from alternating to direct current is typically associated with an electrified railway.

definicion: The process by which an object has or could become buried under the surface of the sea bed.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a subsurface burial process.

dominio.definicion: The object has become buried by the force of the object hitting the sediment.
The object has become buried by the action of current or flow of water around the object.
The object has become buried by the process whereby under certain conditions, a solid seafloor sediment behaves as a liquid.
The object has become buried by the movement of sandwaves.
The object has become buried by the movement of sediment.

definicion: The mass of sulfate ions per volume of solution.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of matter contained by a given volume.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of mass density equal to 0.001 kilograms per cubic metre.

definicion: The fraction of canopy cover within a defined area during the summer season.
descripcion: The canopy is formed by the upper branches of the trees in a forest forming a more or less continuous layer.

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value that is restricted to be completely contained in the range from 0 to 100, inclusive.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A scaled dimensionless measure denoting one part in every hundred.

definicion: An indication that a feature is physically supported by another feature.
descripcion: For example, a tower may be supported by a building, an aerial may be supported by a tower, or a pipeline may be supported by a trestle.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The object is at least partially supported by, or passes across, a bridge span.
descripcion: For example, an aqueduct carried across a valley by one or more bridge spans.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of an aerodrome surface detection station based on the nature of its sensing equipment.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a surface detection station type.

dominio.definicion: A ground station that can receive, interrogate, relay, and send a radio signal to and/or from an aircraft equipped with Automatic Dependant Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) avionics.

A ground station located in a strategic position on an aerodrome surface that receives and interrogates signals emitted from an aircraft transponder to aid in calculating the position of the aircraft relative to that ground station.
dominio.observaciones: The use of several multilateration sensors on an aerodrome surface, each receiving and interrogating the transponder emission from an aircraft, results in triangulating the exact position of the aircraft on the aerodrome. This information can then be relayed to the aerodrome ground control service, which can use this information to aid in aircraft separation and safety.

definicion: The surface material composition of a feature, excluding its internal (structural) composition.
descripcion: Usually determined by remotely sensed characteristics, for example radar return. Generally, the very thin layer that interacts with electro-optical wavelengths.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a surface material type.

dominio.definicion: A light silvery ductile and malleable metal, not readily tarnished by air, which is a chemical element, atomic number 13. (Symbol Al.)
The powdery residue, composed chiefly of earthy or mineral particles, left after the combustion of any substance.
Black or brownish-black, solid or viscous, bituminous pitch, of natural occurrence or produced from petroleum.
A dark, fine-grained igneous rock, often displaying columnar structure and usually composed largely of plagioclase with pyroxene and olivine.
Native consolidated solid rock that has been unaffected by the processes of weathering and underlies the surface of the Earth.
dominio.observaciones: Often overlain by the results of weathering processes, including soil, clay, sand, gravel and related loose materials.

dominio.definicion: Large water- or weather-worn stones.
Clay kneaded, moulded, and baked or sun-dried, used as a building material.
Containing calcium carbonate and/or other, usually insoluble, calcium salt.
White soft earthy limestone consisting almost wholly of calcite and derived chiefly from microscopic salt water fossil shells and fragments.
Residual pieces of combustible matter (for example: coal or wood) that has ceased to flame but has still combustible matter in them.
A member of the subclass Cirripedia, a marine crustacean that is generally sessile as an adult and has limbs modified for filter-feeding.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a barnacle.

dominio.definicion: A stiff tenacious fine-grained earth consisting mainly of hydrated aluminosilicates, which become more plastic when water is added and can be moulded and dried.
dominio.observaciones: Used to make bricks and/or pottery.

dominio.definicion: A hard opaque black or blackish mineral, mainly carbonized plant matter, found in seams or strata at or below the Earth's surface.
dominio.observaciones: Used as fuel and in manufacture (for example: to produce gas and/or tar).

dominio.definicion: Water-worn rounded stones, especially of the size used for paving.
Coal deprived by dry distillation of its volatile constituents.
A substance or preparation formed by the combination or mixture of various ingredients, especially a compound artificial substance serving the purpose of a natural one.
A heavy-duty building material made from a mixture of broken stone or gravel, sand, cement, and water, that forms a stonelike mass on hardening.
A coarse-grained sedimentary rock composed of rounded fragments embedded in a matrix of a cementing material such as silica.
A malleable and ductile reddish metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 29. (Symbol Cu.)
dominio.observaciones: Used especially for electrical conductors and as the base of alloys.

dominio.definicion: A usually hard calcareous substance secreted by many marine polyps as an external skeleton for support and habitation.
dominio.observaciones: Occurs in both single specimens and extensive accumulations. A similar substance may be produced by other lime-secreting marine organisms.

dominio.definicion: A significant, dense, coral outcrop consisting of corals grown, usually, from a single embryo.
A soft, friable, porous material consisting of fossilized microscopic unicellular alga that have rigid siliceous cell walls.
dominio.observaciones: Used for filters and insulation.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock composed chiefly of a hexagonal carbonate of calcium, magnesium, and usually iron that occurs as translucent crystals of various colours, alone or with calcite.
A thinly-bedded sedimentary deposit consisting of shales and marls alternating with coarser strata such as sandstones and conglomerates.

A rhizopod of the chiefly marine order Foraminiferida, typically having a calcareous shell with perforations (foramina) through which pseudopodia extend, the fossils forming a major constituent of chalk and many marine oozes.
A member of the genus Fucus, a seaweed with leathery fronds.
dominio.observaciones: For example, bladderwrack.

dominio.definicion: A substance made by fusing soda and/or potash with other ingredients.
dominio.observaciones: Usually transparent, lustrous, hard, and brittle.

dominio.definicion: A precious metal which is characterized by its yellowish colour, resistance to tarnishing and corrosion, and great malleability and ductility, and is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 79 (symbol Au).
Any of a broad class of granular crystalline plutonic rocks, consisting essentially of quartz, orthoclase, feldspar, and mica or hornblende.
dominio.observaciones: Often used for building.

dominio.definicion: Plant material (for example: straw and/or tall coarse grass), possibly also containing the slices of soil to which the plant material is attached.
dominio.observaciones: For example, used in thatching or sodding a roof.

dominio.definicion: Small water-worn or pounded stones.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes with an intermixture of sand and/or clay. Used for laying paths and roads.

dominio.definicion: Any igneous rock of dark-green appearance, especially containing chlorite, epidote, and/or hornblende.
dominio.observaciones: Includes nephrites and, in particular, jade.

dominio.definicion: Ground calcareous remains of macroscopic marine animals.
A malleable, magnetic, readily oxidizable metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 26. (Symbol Fe.)
dominio.observaciones: Occurs abundantly in certain ores and in meteorites, and is widely used, chiefly in alloys such as steel.

dominio.definicion: The fluid or semifluid magma or molten rock which flows from a volcano or other fissure in the Earth.
A soft, heavy, malleable, bluish-grey metal that is a chemical element, atomic number 82, occurring in galena and other minerals. (Symbol Pb.)
Fine yellowish-grey loam composed of material transported by the wind.
Timber sawn into rough planks or otherwise partly prepared.
A material for surfacing roads, consisting of broken stone or ironstone slag bound with tar alone, or of tar mixed with pitch or creosote.
dominio.observaciones: Historically, water-bound rather than using tar or pitch.

dominio.definicion: Stony and/or silaceous coral.
A hard grey brittle chemical element, atomic number 25, which is one of the transition metals. (Symbol Mn.)
dominio.observaciones: Used in steels and magnetic alloys.

dominio.definicion: Limestone that has been recrystallized by metamorphism and is capable of taking a polish, especially one that is pure white or has a mottled surface.
White to gray accumulation on lake bottoms caused by precipitation of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) mixed with microscopic fresh water fossil shells and fragments.

Building materials (for example: stone, brick, concrete, hollow-tile, concrete block, gypsum block, or other similar building units or materials and/or a combination of the same) bonded together with mortar to form a structure (for example: a wall, a pier, or a buttress).
A mixture of impure metal sulphides produced during the smelting of sulphide ores (for example: of copper or nickel).
Any of the class of substances that are characteristically lustrous, ductile, fusible, malleable solids and are good conductors of heat and electricity.
dominio.observaciones: For example, gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, tin, and certain alloys (as brass and bronze).

dominio.definicion: Soft wet soil, sand, dust, and/or other earthy matter.
dominio.observaciones: Also, the hard ground produced by the drying of an area of mud.

dominio.definicion: Any of various bivalve molluscs belonging chiefly to the marine superfamily Mytilacea or to the freshwater superfamily Unionacea.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the common edible marine bivalve, Mytilus edulis, which has a dark grey, slightly elongated shell and adheres by a byssus, frequently in large aggregations.

dominio.definicion: Any of numerous liquids with a smooth sticky feel that are immiscible with water (but miscible with organic solvents), flammable, and chemically neutral.
dominio.observaciones: For example, crude oil (or a refined product of this), lubricating oil, or vegetable oil.

dominio.definicion: A deposit or layer of white or grey calcareous matter largely composed of foraminiferan remains, covering large areas of the ocean floor.
Any of various bivalve molluscs of the family Ostreidae, several of which are eaten (especially raw) as a delicacy and may be farmed for food or pearls.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the common European Ostrea edulis, and members of the widespread genus Crassostrea.

dominio.definicion: Material in the form of thin flexible (frequently white) sheets made from the pulp of wood or other fibrous matter which is dried, pressed, and often bleached.
dominio.observaciones: Used for writing, printing, or drawing on, or for wrapping and/or covering.

dominio.definicion: Composed in part, but not completely, by metal.
Small, smooth, rounded stones, that have been worn by the action of water, ice, and/or sand.
Any of a large class of substances which are polymers based on synthetic resins or modified natural polymers.
dominio.observaciones: May be moulded, extruded, or cast while soft or liquid, and then set into a rigid or slightly elastic form, usually by heating or cooling.

dominio.definicion: Mosslike colonies of sessile, polypoid aquatic animals that reproduce by budding.
An unstratified or igneous rock having a homogeneous groundmass containing larger crystals of one or more minerals (frequently feldspar).
dominio.observaciones: For example, a hard rock quarried in ancient Egypt, having crystals of white or red plagioclase feldspar in a fine red groundmass of hornblende or apatite. Loosely, any attractive red or purple stone taking a high polish.

dominio.definicion: Reinforced concrete in which internal stresses have been introduced to reduce potential tensile stress in the concrete resulting from loads.
A light spongy form of volcanic glass, usually of pyroclastic origin and with a high silica content.
dominio.observaciones: Used, for example, as an abrasive (for example: in cleaning, polishing, removing stains and/or dead skin) or as an absorbent for moisture.

dominio.definicion: A trigonal rock-forming mineral consisting of silica, massive or crystallizing in colourless or white hexagonal prisms.
dominio.observaciones: Found widely in igneous and metamorphic rocks. Often coloured by impurities (as amethyst, citrine, cairngorm).

dominio.definicion: Marine protozoa with amoeba-like bodies and radiating filamentous pseudopods.
Any material or combination of materials which spontaneously emits ionizing radiation (for example: nuclear particles and/or gamma rays).
Poured concrete containing steel bars or metal netting to increase its tensile strength.
Stones of any size.
Any of various artificial polymeric substances that are tough and elastic.
dominio.observaciones: Originally an organic substance made from the coagulated latex of various plants, especially Hevea brasiliensis, which in its natural state is thermoplastic.

dominio.definicion: The debris (for example: waste fragments of masonry) of decayed or demolished buildings and/or other structures.
A white or (when impure) reddish-brown mineral crystallizing in the cubic system (sodium chloride, NaCl).
dominio.observaciones: Obtained by mining or by evaporation of seawater and used especially for seasoning and preserving food.

dominio.definicion: Granular material consisting of small eroded fragments of (mainly siliceous) rocks, finer than gravel and larger than a coarse silt grain.
dominio.observaciones: Generally ranging between 0.074 millimetres (No. 200 sieve) and 4.76 millimetres (No. 4 sieve) in size. Often a major constituent of a beach, desert, or the bed of a river or sea. Used for various purposes, as in smoothing stone, founding, or as an ingredient in mortar.

dominio.definicion: Any of various sedimentary rocks composed of sand grains, especially of quartz, cemented together.
dominio.observaciones: Typically red, yellow, brown, grey, or white in colour.

dominio.definicion: A coarse-grained pelitic metamorphic rock that has a structure marked by parallel layers of various minerals and can be split into thin irregular plates.
Rocky or soil-like material resulting from excavating, mining, dredging, and/or processing activities.
Rough masses resembling clinker, formed by the cooling of volcanic ejecta, and of a light aerated texture.
Waste, especially excremental, matter conveyed in sewers.
Calcareous remains of macroscopic marine animals, whole or in fragments.
Small, loose, rounded waterworn pebbles, especially as accumulated on a seashore.
Material consisting of particles whose sizes fall within a specified range (typically 0.002-0.06 millimetres) between those of sand and clay.
A precious metal which is characterized by its lustrous white colour and great malleability and ductility, and is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 47. (Symbol Ag.)
Stony material composed of waste matter or dross separated from metals during smelting or refining.
dominio.observaciones: Also any similar waste product resulting from the fusion of other substances.

dominio.definicion: A muddy or slimy matter or deposit consisting of a thick suspension of fine particles or gel in a liquid, especially one formed as waste in any of various industrial and mechanical processes.
Water solidified by exposure to cold.
dominio.observaciones: For example, snow or ice.

dominio.definicion: The material comprising the thin top layer of much of the Earth's land surface, composed of fragmented rock particles with humus, water, and air.
Accumulated remains of sponges consisting of the small pointed structures of calcite or silica that compose their skeletons.
Any of various primitive sessile aquatic (chiefly marine) animals of the phylum Porifera, which have porous baglike bodies with a skeleton of hard spicules or elastic fibres.
Any of numerous artificially produced alloys of iron containing up to 3 percent of other elements (including less than about 2.2 percent carbon) and having great strength and malleability.
dominio.observaciones: Able to be tempered to many different degrees of hardness. Used for making tools, weapons, and/or machinery.

dominio.definicion: Pieces of rock or mineral substance (other than metal) of definite form and size, usually artificially shaped, and used for some special purpose.
dominio.observaciones: Used, for example, for building, for paving, or in the form of a block, slab, or pillar set up as a memorial and/or a boundary-mark.

dominio.definicion: A white or light-coloured concretionary limestone, usually hard and semi-crystalline, precipitated from water holding calcium carbonate in solution (for example: in hot springs).
dominio.observaciones: May be used for building.

dominio.definicion: A soft porous calcium carbonate rock formed by deposition around mineral springs.
dominio.observaciones: Also any friable porous stone formed of consolidated, often stratified material.

dominio.definicion: A mineral that may be used for the extraction of uranium.
dominio.observaciones: For example, pitchblende, uraninite, carnotite, torbernite, tyuyamunite, autunite, uranophane, and brannerite.

dominio.definicion: Plants collectively, especially those dominating a particular area or habitat.
Loose fragmented solid material ejected from a volcano.
The transparent, colourless, tasteless, odourless, liquid compound of hydrogen and oxygen (formula H2O).
dominio.observaciones: Forms the main constituent of seas, lakes, rivers, and rain, and is put to many domestic and industrial uses.

dominio.definicion: The hard, compact, fibrous substance of which the roots, trunks, and branches of trees and shrubs consist.
dominio.observaciones: Consists largely of secondary xylem, which forms the strengthening and water-transporting tissue of the plant.

dominio.definicion: A hard lustrous bluish-white metallic chemical element, atomic number 30, which is obtained from sphalerite and other ores. (Symbol Zn.)
dominio.observaciones: Used for roofing, galvanizing iron, and making alloys with copper.

dominio.definicion: Granular material consisting of a mixture of small sandy eroded fragments of (mainly siliceous) rocks and small water-worn or pounded stones that are larger than a coarse silt grain.
dominio.observaciones: Generally ranging between 0.074 millimetres (No. 200 sieve) and 7.62 centimetres in size.

dominio.definicion: A layer of loose stone of relatively constant size and shape.
dominio.observaciones: For example, as used to form a foundation for a breakwater.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary salt deposit left after the evaporation of a body of water.
Granular material consisting of a mixture of small sandy eroded fragments of (mainly siliceous) rocks, finer than gravel and larger than a coarse silt grain, and large water- or weather-worn stones.
Granular material consisting of a mixture of small sandy eroded fragments of (mainly siliceous) rocks, finer than gravel, and soft wet soil, dust, and/or other earthy matter.
A plastic composition in which glass reinforcements are imbedded with strength properties greatly superior to those of the base resin.
dominio.observaciones: The reinforcements are usually fibres, rovings, fabrics or mats.

dominio.definicion: Rock formed by alteration of existing rocks by heat, pressure, or other processes in the Earth's crust.
dominio.observaciones: May be foliated or nonfoliated. Common foliated metamorphic rocks include slate, metasandstone, metaconglomerate, phyllite, schist, gneiss, and the 'hybrid rock' (part igneous, part metamorphic) migmatite. Common nonfoliated metamorphic rocks include hornfels, quartzite, marble, and dolomitic marble.

dominio.definicion: Rock formed by solidification of molten lava or magma.
dominio.observaciones: When extrusive igneous rock solidifies near or on the surface of the Earth it is termed volcanic.

dominio.definicion: An igneous rock chemically the same as basalt and gabbro but medium-grained with a usually ophitic texture.
dominio.observaciones: Usually dark coloured and fine or medium textured. Occurs in minor intrusions such as sills and dykes.

dominio.definicion: A substance consisting of a solid colouring matter dissolved in a liquid vehicle (for example: water or oil) that when spread over a surface, dries to leave a thin decorative or protective coating.
Frozen water, a brittle transparent crystalline solid.
A mass of snow flakes (minute hexagonal ice crystals).
dominio.observaciones: Usually as the result of snow falling on the ground.

dominio.definicion: A clayey (usually red) soil or soil horizon characterized by a high proportion of sesquioxides, especially of aluminum and iron, and a low proportion of bases and silica.
dominio.observaciones: Formed by chemical weathering in tropical and subtropical regions, especially one which hardens or has hardened on exposure to air. Also loosely any of various other reddish or iron-rich surface materials in the tropics and sub-tropics.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock consisting of angular, coarse-grained fragments cemented together by a fine-grained matrix (for example: by lime).
A nonmetallic material made from clay and hardened by firing at high temperature.
dominio.observaciones: It contains minute silicate crystals suspended in a glassy cement.

dominio.definicion: A foliated, usually coarse-grained, metamorphic rock in which bands of granular minerals alternate with bands of flaky or prismatic ones.
dominio.observaciones: Formed by the metamorphism of granite and other igneous rocks, and typically consisting of feldspar, quartz, and mica. Usually of a streaked, wavy or banded appearance.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock composed chiefly of calcium carbonate.
dominio.observaciones: Yields lime when calcined and is used as a building material and in the making of cement.

dominio.definicion: A extremely compact, hard, granular rock consisting essentially of quartz.
dominio.observaciones: It is a metamorphosed sandstone in which the siliceous element is often so blended with the quartz grains so as to give the rock a nearly homogenous texture.

dominio.definicion: A thin rectangular tile used as a roofing material and/or for cladding walls.
dominio.observaciones: Often made of wood or bituminous materials.

dominio.definicion: Soft finely stratified rock that splits easily into fragile laminae, consisting of consolidated mud or clay.
A dense, fine-grained, metamorphic rock that develops a characteristic cleavage which may be at any angle with the original bedding plane.
dominio.observaciones: Typically dark grey, blue, or green in colour. Splits readily into smooth parallel-sided flat plates, and used for making tiles for roofing and flooring.

dominio.definicion: A usually square or oblong piece or slice of earth together with the grass growing on it.
Material used in thatching (for example: straw, reeds, and/or palm leaves).
A beam or piece of wood forming or capable of forming part of any structure.
Rock formed by the deposition of sediment.
dominio.observaciones: For example, sandstone, shale, and limestone.

dominio.definicion: Brick made of adobe clay and straw, dried in the sun rather than by oven firing (as are standard bricks).
dominio.observaciones: Larger than standard bricks, adobe bricks require a type of clay that contains between 25 and 45 percent aluminum salts.

dominio.definicion: A timber that has been impregnated with chemicals (for example: cresote oil) to reduce damage from wood rot and/or insects.
dominio.observaciones: Often used for the portions of a structure that are likely to be in ongoing contact with soil and/or water.

dominio.definicion: Predominantly grass with other short growing ground vegetation.

definicion: The slope (rate of upward inclination of the surface from the horizontal) of the surface of a feature (for example: the terrain or a waterbody floor).
descripcion: The (percent) slope is determined as the change in height divided by the horizontal distance over which the change takes place, multiplied by one hundred: ((h2-h1)/d)*100. Generally the slope is determined along the primary alignment of a feature (its established direction of flow or use; for example: a road, a railway, a ridge line, and/or a bridge). In those cases where the primary alignment is essentially horizontal (for example, a beach, a watercourse bank, or a cut) the surface slope is typically determined at right angles to the primary alignment.

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A scaled dimensionless measure denoting one part in every hundred.

definicion: The surface-wave magnitude of the earthquake as reported by the U.S. Geological Survey.
descripcion: A surface-wave is a seismic wave that is constrained to follow the natural wave guide of the Earth's uppermost layers. Its magnitude is quantified using a base-10 logarithmic scale based on the ratio of the amplitude of ground motion to its period, corrected by a factor that is a function of the distance from the point of measurement to the earthquake epicenter.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A dimensionless physical quantity, one which has no unit of measure.

definicion: The type of a control point established by surveying methods based on method of establishment and/or intended use.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a survey control point type.

dominio.definicion: A permanent, stable object containing a marked point of known elevation with respect to a datum used as a reference level for tidal observations or as a control point for levelling.
A point identifying a horizontal position used for locating subordinate surveys or mapping.
A permanent, stable object identifying both horizontal position and elevation benchmark used for locating subordinate surveys or mapping.
A point used by surveyors for determining precise position by astronomical means.
A point identifying a vertical position used for locating subordinate surveys or mapping.
A station in a network of permanently marked 'main' horizontal control points having their geographic positions established to form third order accuracy or better.

A station in a network of horizontal control points of a localized nature (for example: utilized for shoreline plots, sounding marks, and/or stadia work) whose geographic position may be established to a slightly lower order than main horizontal control points.
A station in a network of permanently marked 'main' vertical control points having their geographic positions established to form third order accuracy or better.

A station in a network of vertical control points of a localized nature (for example: utilized for shoreline plots, sounding marks, and/or stadia work) whose geographic position may be established to a slightly lower order than main vertical control points.
A recoverable point on the earth, whose geographic coordinates have been determined by angular methods with geodetic instruments.
dominio.observaciones: A triangulation point is a selected point, which has been marked with a station mark, or it is a conspicuous natural or artificial object.

dominio.definicion: A point whose position has been accurately determined and plotted.
Marker identifying the location of a surveyed boundary line.
A permanent, stable object containing a marked point of known elevation with respect to a datum used as a reference level for tidal observations or as a control point for leveling.

definicion: A general evaluation of the coverage quality of a survey, as a category.
descripcion: See possibly accompanying Attribute: 'Position Quality Category' for additional survey-related information.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a survey coverage category.

dominio.definicion: Surveyed with complete coverage and to established standards.
dominio.observaciones: Survey implies a regular, controlled survey of any date.

dominio.definicion: Surveyed, but not with complete coverage and/or not to established standards.
Survey data either does not exist or is very poor in coverage and/or quality.

definicion: The date interval of a survey.

datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a survey date interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: Formatted in accordance with ISO 8601:2000, 5.5, Time-intervals, as a single data element comprising up to seventeen characters, where the first [YYYY] represents a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, and [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month of the start of the time interval, followed by a solidus '/', followed by the second [YYYY] representing a calendar year, [MM] the ordinal number of a calendar month within the calendar year, and [DD] the ordinal number of a day within the calendar month of the end of the time interval as 'YYYYMMDD/YYYYMMDD' (for example: '19850412/19871007' for 12 April 1985 through 7 October 1987). Either of the dates may be left unspecified by the use of '--------' (for example: '19861201/--------' for 1 December 1986 through an unspecified ending date). Other truncated date representations in accordance with ISO 8601:2000 may be used.

definicion: The nature of the mark established at a survey point.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a survey point mark type.

dominio.definicion: A permanent physical marker identifies the location of the survey point.
dominio.observaciones: Marked survey points may be inscribed metal tablets set in concrete posts, cast metal disks or metal rods driven in the ground.

dominio.definicion: An unmarked survey point which is a recognizable landmark and can be recovered or used as a survey point.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a flagpole or the spire of a church.

dominio.definicion: A temporary survey point that has no associated marker and are therefore is unrecoverable.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the corner of a building or a large rock.

definicion: The type of a survey point based on the purpose for which it is established.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a survey point type.

dominio.definicion: A point used by surveyors for determining precise position by astronomical means.
A point whose vertical position (elevation) above or below an established datum has been determined.
A point whose position (horizontal or vertical) has been determined and is used for purposes of describing and recording land ownership.
dominio.observaciones: A cadastral survey creates, marks, defines, retraces or reestablishes the boundaries and subdivisions of public land.

dominio.definicion: A point whose position has been determined so as to serve as a reference point from which to calculate distances in a photogrammetric survey.
dominio.observaciones: This point is typically the exact point occupied by the camera lens at the moment of exposure.

dominio.definicion: A point having known, precise position (horizontal or vertical) established by geodetic techniques.
dominio.observaciones: The coordinates of a geodetic point are determined mainly by the method of triangulation. Geodetic surveys take the shape and size of the Earth into account and are typically carried out with great precision, often over long distances.

dominio.definicion: A point whose position has been determined for use in measuring the gravitational field for a gravity survey.
A permanently marked point at which a series of measurements of the magnetic field of the Earth have been made and whose (adjusted) gravity is known.
A point at which a theodolite instrument is erected in order to perform a survey.
A permanent, stable object containing a marked point of known elevation with respect to a datum used as a reference level for tidal observations or as a control point for leveling.
A point at which a transit instrument is erected in order to perform a survey.

definicion: The means by which a survey coordinate is developed.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a survey technique.

dominio.definicion: A method of surveying in which an azimuth is derived based on observations of a celestial body.
dominio.observaciones: The horizontal azimuth angle, clockwise from astronomic north, is derived from angular observations of the celestial body.

dominio.definicion: A method of surveying in which the position of a point is defined on the geoid with reference to the planes of the celestial equator and a selected celestial meridian.
dominio.observaciones: The astronomic latitude and longitude are derived from angular observations of celestial bodies.

dominio.definicion: A method of deriving the position of a point by means of mathematical relations and database interpolations.

A method of surveying in which an object or observer is placed at a specified point by using a Doppler Global Navigation Satellite (GNSS) to determine the difference between the actual location and the desired location and then minimizing this difference.

Direct geodetic point positioning at a stationary, solitary station using a 'geodetic quality' dual frequency Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver, a precise ephemerides, satellite clock states, Earth orientation parameters, and solid Earth tide predictions.
dominio.observaciones: The location of the point is tied to a known geodetic reference frame such as the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84) or the International Terrestrial Reference Frame (ITRF). The occupation time at a given survey point is 24 hours.

dominio.definicion: A method of surveying involving the collection of precise carrier phase measurements recorded simultaneously at two or more survey control marks using stand-alone Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) equipment (comprised of a high precision antenna and receiver) and a continually operating reference station.
dominio.observaciones: The frequency carrier phase integer ambiguities of the satellites are more accurately resolved given that the occupation time at a given survey point is 30 to 60 minutes.

dominio.etiqueta: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) Rapid Static
dominio.definicion: A method of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) static surveying in which a base, or static, satellite receiver occupies a point and vectors are measured to a semi-static satellite receiver at another point.
dominio.observaciones: The frequency carrier phase integer ambiguities of the satellites are resolved in a relatively short amount of time, thus this method is not as accurate as 'long-static'. The occupation time at a given survey point is 5 to 15 minutes.

dominio.definicion: A method of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) surveying in which a known GNSS base station and a roving GNSS receiver are used to establish a comminucation link, allowing the surveyor to move to another location and take measurements, without having to relocate the base station.
dominio.observaciones: The differences between the known coordinates at the base station and the values determined from the roving GNSS receiver are referred to as 'corrections' to the signals. These corrections are broadcast to the rover antennas via a communication link and used to determine the vector between the base and the rover; the collected vectors are determined in a post-processing step. The occupation time at a given survey point is 1 to 2 minutes.

dominio.etiqueta: Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) Real-time Kinematic
dominio.definicion: A method of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) surveying that uses a digital communications link to transmit near-instantaneous differential corrections from a known Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) base station(s) to a roving GNSS receiver.
dominio.observaciones: The differences between the known coordinates at the base station and the values determined from the GNSS are referred to as 'corrections' to the signals. These corrections are broadcast to the rover antennas via a communication link in determining the vector between base and rover; the vectors are processed in 'real-time'. The occupation time at a given survey point is 1 to 2 minutes.

dominio.definicion: A method of Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) surveying that uses at least two satellite receivers, one usually occupying a known geodetic station, and based on the theory that satellite orbit errors, atmospheric refractive distortions, and satellite clock errors are assumed the same at both points, thus cancel out.
dominio.observaciones: The accuracy of the vector between the two points depends on the length of occupation time at the survey point. GNSS relative positioning is one of the positioning methods which can provide the most precise relative position between a receiver at a known point and a receiver at a unknown point.

dominio.definicion: A combination of both Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and conventional survey techniques is used to determine the position of a point.
A method of surveying in which a gravimeter is used to measure the local gravity at a specified point in absolute units (gals).
A method of surveying in which an eccentric point, usually located outside the facility housing the absolute gravity station, is surveyed by relative gravity techniques.
A method of surveying where a gravimeter is used to measure the difference in the acceleration of gravity at a specified point and that of a known accurate gravity point.

A method of surveying in which horizontal position is determined by horizontal angular observation from two or more known survey stations to an unknown survey station, no observations being made over the unknown station itself.

The determination of differences of elevation by means of a consecutive series of short horizontal traverses, where the vertical distance along each traverse is determined by direct observation of a graduated rod placed at the end of the traverse and observed with a leveling instrument equipped with a spirit or digital level.
A method of surveying where elevation points are determined by light detection and ranging (LiDAR) tools.
dominio.observaciones: Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) is an optical remote sensing technique that can measure distances to multiple targets, or point clouds, using light. It can be used in both horizontal and vertical positioning.

dominio.definicion: A method of surveying where a location is determined through the use of a 3D Laser Scanner mounted on a vehicle.
dominio.observaciones: Accomplished using either airborne and/or terrestrial LiDAR mounted on a moving vehicle, collecting data on-the-fly.

dominio.definicion: A surveying method to determine the geodetic position of an unknown occupied point via horizontal angular observations from three or more known survey points.
A method of surveying where a location is determined through the use of a 3D Laser Scanner set on the ground.
dominio.observaciones: Static terrestrial three-dimentional Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) used for mapping/modeling.

dominio.definicion: A method of surveying used to extend geodetic control through a series of ground stations located at the vertices of a chain of terrestrial triangles and quadrangles among which position is determined by angular observations on and between triangle apexes.
dominio.observaciones: Distinguished from Trilateration in which distance measurement observations are made of the sides of the triangles.

dominio.definicion: A method of surveying used to extend geodetic control through a series of ground stations located at the vertices of a chain of terrestrial triangles and quadrangles among which position is determimed via electronic distance measurement observations of the sides of the triangles.
dominio.observaciones: Distinguished from Triangulation in which angular observations are made on and between triangle apexes.

definicion: An indication that a feature is suspended overhead.
descripcion: For example, a power transmission line is suspended between pylons and thus one may physically pass under it. Note that the power transmission line is also supported by the pylons and thus if the pylons were removed the power transmission line would fall.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of a marsh based on its morphology and/or dominant vegetation.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a swamp type.

dominio.definicion: A swamp occurring along the banks of permanent or semipermanent streams.
dominio.observaciones: The high water table is maintained by the level of water in the stream. The swamp is seasonally inundated with subsequent sediment deposition.

dominio.definicion: A swamp developed in a topographically defined basin where water derived locally may be augmented by drainage from other parts of the watershed.
