dominio.observaciones: The accumulation of well-decomposed peat is shallow (less than 0.5 metres) at the edge but may reach 2 metres at the centre.

dominio.definicion: A dense thicket of mangrove that is subject to tidal inundation and forming a muddy swamp.

definicion: The condition of a naval mine after being swept.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a swept mine condition.

dominio.definicion: Afloat and adrift.
dominio.observaciones: May be designated in communications as 'FLOAT' followed by the direction of drift (true bearing; 3 numerics), for example: 'FLOAT 110'.

dominio.definicion: Sunk by mine disposal vessel.
dominio.observaciones: May be designated in communications as 'SUNK' followed by DTG (verified time), for example 'SUNK 061715Z0'.

dominio.definicion: Disposed of by mine disposal vessel.
dominio.observaciones: In general, when the intention is to annihilate the mine danger, mines are disposed of by the minehunter or by other means (for example: a diving vessel assisting the hunter). Mine disposal is done by countermining or mine neutralisation. For reasons of the particular tactical objective, rendering safe, recovery, and removal of mines are not included in the general term 'Dispose'. May be designated in communications as 'DISP' followed by DTG (verified time), for example: 'DISP 061732Z8'.

dominio.definicion: Fouled the sweep during mechanical sweeping.
dominio.observaciones: May be designated in communications as 'FOULED'.

dominio.definicion: Exploded during sweeping and hunting operations (a triggered influence mine, not by disposal techniques).
dominio.observaciones: May be designated in communications as 'EXPL' followed by relative bearing RED/GREEN, 3 numerics (000-180) and distance in metres separated by a hyphen (4 numerics).

dominio.definicion: Disposed of by countermining, consisting of the placement of a mine disposal charge close enough to the mine so that sympathetic detonation occurs.
dominio.observaciones: In some cases when a mine is destroyed (countermined) by a remotely operated vehicle (ROV) it may not be known with a degree of certainty whether the mine was actually detonated by the disposal charge. In such cases the minehunter will determine the condition of the mine, using the minehunting sonar, and if required the ROV, taking action to ensure that the mine is effectively countermined. Moored mine sinkers normally remain in place after the mine has been destroyed. However, in some instances the sinkers may be removed and/or taken away. May be designated in communications as 'CMINED' followed by DTG (verified time), for example: 'CMINED 11726Z3'.

dominio.definicion: Disposed of by neutralization, rendering the mine, by external means, permanently incapable of firing on passing of a ship or sweep (although it may remain dangerous to handle).
dominio.observaciones: Neutralisation is accomplished either by disrupting the mine firing mechanism or by separating the firing mechanism from the main explosive charge. It may be achieved by using divers to place a relatively small shaped explosive charge on the mine or by using a vehicle to lay a charge sufficiently close to disrupt the mechanism. Alternatively divers may be used to render the mine safe using EOD procedures. The mine case may remain visually intact. May be designated in communications as 'NEUTR' followed by DTG (verified time), for example: 'NEUTR 270813Z1'.

dominio.definicion: Disposed of by rendering the mine safe as a result of action to make it inoperative by direct interference with its firing system or explosive train.
dominio.observaciones: This may be done underwater, in situ, or after recovery. May be designated in communications as 'RSAFE' followed by DTG (verified time), for example: 'RSAFE 121606Z6'.

dominio.definicion: The mine was recovered in order that a detailed technical evaluation may take place.
dominio.observaciones: It is necessary that the mine suffers as little disruption as is safe and practical. May be designated in communications as 'RECVD' followed by DTG (verified time), for example: 'RECVD 211256Z7'.

dominio.definicion: Removed from the shipping area (initial position) to an area where its detonation would be acceptable.
dominio.observaciones: May be designated in communications as 'RMVD' followed by 3 numerics (true bearing) and distance 4 numerics, separated by a hyphen (indicating metres), for example: 'RMVD 210-1500'.

dominio.definicion: Not dealt with during mine sweeping operations.
dominio.observaciones: May be designated in communications as 'NDEALT'.

definicion: An indication that a periodic behaviour of the feature is synchronized with that of another feature.
descripcion: For example, the members of a set of flashing lights may flash in unison.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

descripcion: TACAN operating channels shall be chosen from ICAO Annex 10 Chapter 3 Table A, of the 352 channels in which the channel numbers, frequencies, and pulse codes are assigned. They are specified by a number followed by a letter.

descripcion: A taxiway shall be identified by a designator comprising a letter, a set of letters, or a combination of a letter or letters followed by a number. The designator is intended to be unique within an appropriate scope (for example: an aerodrome or a military installation) and may be assigned based on a system of abbreviations and/or numbers (for example: 'T1' for Taxiway 1) or based on a naming scheme (for example: 'Alpha', 'Baker' or 'Charlie'), or simply a recognized name (for example: 'Warehouse B' or 'Hanger 11').

definicion: The type of Terminal Arrival Altitude (TAA) area which is contained by an arc defined by the extension of the initial legs and the intermediate segment course based upon the arrangement of an Area Navigation (RNAV) procedure.

definicion: A unique encoded designator for the terminal instrument procedure.
descripcion: The designator is used primarily by automated flight management systems as a primary key to search for, select, portray, and fly while on automatic pilot. This is also used to encode the full identifier into a short string of characters so it may be selected from an on-screen list of available procedures, without the need for the pilot to have to scroll through what at times can be a lengthly list of terminal instrument procedure identifications.

datatype.nombre: Terminal Instrument Procedure Designator Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a terminal instrument procedure designator.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: Six alphanumeric characters where alphabetic characters range from 'A' to 'Z' and numeric characters range from '0' to '9'. In the case of a Standard Instrument Arrival (STAR) or Standard Instrument Departure (SID) procedure the identifier consists of a 5 character component followed by a single character consisting of either a space (' ') or a letter from 'A' to 'Z' or digit from '0' to '9' used to discriminate cases of multiple procedure identifiers at an aerodrome that would otherwise be identical. In the case of a Standard Instrument Arrival (STAR) the identifier consists of the flight management system encoded designator (for example: 'GILMOR SIX ARRIVAL' becomes 'GQE6'). In all cases 'runway' is abbreviated as 'RW' (for example 'RWY 34' becomes 'RW34'). If no encoded designator is provided by the appropriate authority then the full terminal instrument procedure identification is used as the identifier if five or less characters in length (the result being right-padded to 5 characters using the space (' ')), else the full identification is truncated from right-to-left to 5 characters, retaining the suffix character (discriminating cases of multiple otherwise-identical procedure identifiers) as the sixth character if indicated. In the case of an approach procedure the identifier consists of up to 5 characters followed by a single character consisting of a space (' '). The first character is the segment type (for example: 'I' = ILS, 'V' = VOR, 'N' = NDB) followed by the identifier of the primary runway served by the procedure (a two digit identifier with a suffix of 'L' (left), 'R' (right), 'C' (center)) followed by a space (' '). For example: 'ILS Runway 7L' becomes 'I07L  ' (note spaces). In the case of a circling approach, the type of primary navigational aid followed by the circling identification character is used. For example: 'VOR-A' becomes 'VVORA ' (note space).

definicion: The official identification of the terminal instrument procedure as established in accordance with the appropriate naming convention.
descripcion: Examples of the naming convention are specified in Procedures for Air Navigation Services - Aircraft Operations (PANS-OPS) Doc. 8168, Vol. 2, Part 1, Section 4, Chapter 9.

datatype.nombre: Terminal Instrument Procedure Identification Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a terminal instrument procedure identification.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: Twenty-one alphanumeric characters where alphabetic characters range from 'A' to 'Z', numeric characters range from '0' to '9', and the hyphen, dash, or minus sign ('-') is included. The full name is constructed by: (a) eliminating words or abbreviations such as 'departure' and 'arrivals'; (b) eliminating city names and names of airports or heliports; and (c) numbers are converted to integers (for example: 'three' becomes '3').

definicion: The official identification of the flight procedure transition as established in accordance with the appropriate naming convention.

datatype.nombre: Terminal Instrument Procedure Transition Identification Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a transition identification.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: A five character string composed of alpha-numeric characters in the range '0' to '9' and 'A' to 'Z', plus the space character (' ') which may only be used to pad the rightmost portion of the string in the case that the transition identification uses fewer than five characters. For example: 'RW09', 'BF   ' (note spaces), 'TOXEV', 'REXAR', 'YXX01', and 'ALL  ' (note spaces).

dominio.observaciones: Boulders are generally greater than 25 centimetres in diameter; some may be much larger.

An area whose surface is covered partially (between 25 to 55 percent) by boulders.
dominio.observaciones: Boulders are generally greater than 25 centimetres in diameter; some may be much larger.

An area of exposed bedrock that has a irregular surface due to mechanical or weathering effects.

An area whose surface is covered by sand dunes up to 10 metres in height.
An area whose surface is covered by sand dunes greater than 10 metres in height.

A relatively level area whose surface is covered partially (between 20 to 50 percent) by gullies.

A level area created by alluvial action that has stream channels eroded into it.
A relatively level area whose surface is covered mainly (greater than 50 percent) by eroding stream channels.
An area with eroded stream channels greater than 3 metres in depth.

dominio.etiqueta: Steep Rugged Dissected with narrow Gullies
dominio.definicion: An area characterized by high relief and numerous narrow stream channels.

dominio.etiqueta: Karst with numerous Sinkholes and Solution Valleys
dominio.definicion: An area of karst with numerous depressions and valleys caused by the collapse of the underlying limestone, dolomite or gypsum bedrock.
An area of karst with numerous depressions caused by the collapse of the underlying limestone, dolomite or gypsum bedrock.
An area of hummocky karst with large cone-shaped hills and scattered depressions.
An area of hummocky karst with low broad-based mounds and scattered depressions.
The dry bed of an intermittent stream, often with steep sides or located at the bottom of a channel.
A level area of silt and/or sand, free of vegetation and usually salty, lying at the bottom of a desert basin and dry except after rain.
A relatively level area with serpentine depressions and oxbow lakes created by shifting drainage.
An area of tongue-like masses of slow-moving waterlogged soil with steep fronts and gentle upper surfaces interspersed with areas of heaving soil caused by frost action.
An area of small hillocks caused by the freeze-thaw cycle.
An area of formed patterns of rock, soil and/or vegetation caused by frost action.

dominio.definicion: An area of numerous small lakes and ponds.
An ice field containing an appreciable quantity of nearly vertical fissures.
An area with numerous raised shelf-like naturally occurring levelled terrain surfaces.
dominio.observaciones: For example, lava terraces.

dominio.definicion: An area of open-air excavations created by removal of stone by blasting or cutting.
An area in which surface material has been removed in successive parallel strips to expose the minerals, the spoil from each new strip being placed in the previously excavated one.
An area of open-air excavations created by the removal of gravel.
An area of open-air excavations created by the removal of sand.
An area covered by large mounds of spoil produced by mining.

dominio.definicion: An area with numerous stone walls, typically separating fields and/or habitated areas.

dominio.definicion: Loose material transported by a stream or a river and deposited as the river floodplain.

dominio.definicion: A rounded or oval shaped depression.

dominio.definicion: A flat area.
A generally rounded protuberance rising above the level of the surrounding ground.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a costal sand-hill, a mound, a ridge in an ice-field or a more or less elevated piece of ground rising out of a swamp, often densly wooded.

dominio.definicion: A narrow geomorphologic feature as a valley or mountain pass.
A small temporary channel formed on the surface of soil or sand.
A flat area of great extent and elevation.
dominio.observaciones: Usually an extensive land region considerably elevated (more than 150-300 metres) above the adjacent country or sea.

dominio.definicion: An area with steep slopes.
A terraced landform.
An area in which mined materials (for example: coal) are accumulated.
An undulating surface due to folding or primary sedimentary feature.
An area with vertical and/or horizontal movements of the Earth surface due to various influences (for example: geological forces or mining).

An area where removal processes have caused an areal degradation of soil particles (for example: erosion by the action of the wind) or to a linear degradation with deep erosion of different grades (for example: erosion by the action of moving water).
A mix of sand and water forming a soft, shifting mass that becomes unstable when disturbed and is likely to engulf any object resting on its surface.
dominio.observaciones: Quicksand may occur where there are natural springs, riverbanks, beaches, along lake shorelines as well as in tidal flats.

definicion: A description of any unique aspects of the terrain morphology.
descripcion: Used to expand on the use of Attribute: 'Terrain Morphology', especially when the required value is not one of the standard Terrain Morphology values.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is 255 characters in maximum length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: Geographical or legal status of a territory, which is no independent sovereign State nor a regular part of a sovereign State.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a territory special status type.

dominio.definicion: An administrative division established by two or more nations for combined ruling.
A territory that is not subject to a Sovereign State.
dominio.observaciones: For example, Antarctica.

dominio.definicion: A territory which belongs to an internationally acknowledged sovereign State but is in dispute by parts of the population or special groups of interests.
A part of the territory of a sovereign State which is separated from the main territory.
A territory whose status of dependence is internationally acknowledged.
dominio.observaciones: The grade of dependence could be varying, from unhibitated overseas regions without own sovereignty to regions which have voluntary transferred a part of their foreign representation and which could announce their independence at once. Special cases are sovereign States with voluntary association to other sovereign States (for example: the Cook Islands in relation to New Zealand). Such territories get an ISO 3166-1 code in the same manner as independent sovereign States.

dominio.definicion: A partly sovereign territory whose foreign and defence administration is conducted by another sovereign State.
dominio.observaciones: Both protector and protectorate are legal subjects to the law of nations.

dominio.definicion: An area being under control of the United Nations (UN).
A newly conquered territory under the control of an armed force.
A strip of territory in a border area where military activity is precluded.
dominio.observaciones: One of the lines in a DMZ generally serves as a line of separation (for example: armistice control, withdrawal or cease-fire line). For example, two two-kilometre-wide DMZs have existed on either side of the Military Demarcation Line between North and South Korea.

dominio.definicion: A country or a region represented by a State regarding foreign affairs but internally autonomous.
A region subordinated to the central government of a State but holding specific autonomous administrative fields.
An area reserved for specific ethnic groups with or without partial autonomy.
dominio.observaciones: Reservations may allow natives to keep their own culture.

definicion: The tertiary type of material composing a feature, exclusive of the surface.
descripcion: The basis for 'tertiary' may be, for example, compositional dominance or structural organization.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a tertiary structural material type.

dominio.definicion: The powdery residue, composed chiefly of earthy or mineral particles, left after the combustion of any substance.
Large water- or weather-worn stones.
Clay kneaded, moulded, and baked or sun-dried, used as a building material.
White soft earthy limestone consisting almost wholly of calcite and derived chiefly from microscopic salt water fossil shells and fragments.
Residual pieces of combustible matter (for example: coal or wood) that has ceased to flame but has still combustible matter in them.
A member of the subclass Cirripedia, a marine crustacean that is generally sessile as an adult and has limbs modified for filter-feeding.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a barnacle.

dominio.definicion: A stiff tenacious fine-grained earth consisting mainly of hydrated aluminosilicates, which become more plastic when water is added and can be moulded and dried.
dominio.observaciones: Used to make bricks and/or pottery.

dominio.definicion: Water-worn rounded stones, especially of the size used for paving.
A substance or preparation formed by the combination or mixture of various ingredients, especially a compound artificial substance serving the purpose of a natural one.
A heavy-duty building material made from a mixture of broken stone or gravel, sand, cement, and water, that forms a stonelike mass on hardening.
A usually hard calcareous substance secreted by many marine polyps as an external skeleton for support and habitation.
dominio.observaciones: Occurs in both single specimens and extensive accumulations. A similar substance may be produced by other lime-secreting marine organisms.

dominio.definicion: A significant, dense, coral outcrop consisting of corals grown, usually, from a single embryo.
A soft, friable, porous material consisting of fossilized microscopic unicellular alga that have rigid siliceous cell walls.
dominio.observaciones: Used for filters and insulation.

dominio.definicion: A rhizopod of the chiefly marine order Foraminiferida, typically having a calcareous shell with perforations (foramina) through which pseudopodia extend, the fossils forming a major constituent of chalk and many marine oozes.
A member of the genus Fucus, a seaweed with leathery fronds.
dominio.observaciones: For example, bladderwrack.

dominio.definicion: Plant material (for example: straw and/or tall coarse grass), possibly also containing the slices of soil to which the plant material is attached.
dominio.observaciones: For example, used in thatching or sodding a roof.

dominio.definicion: Small water-worn or pounded stones.
dominio.observaciones: Sometimes with an intermixture of sand and/or clay. Used for laying paths and roads.

dominio.definicion: The material comprising the thin top layer of much of the Earth's land surface, composed of fragmented rock particles with humus, water, and air.
The fluid or semifluid magma or molten rock which flows from a volcano or other fissure in the Earth.
Stony and/or silaceous coral.
A hard grey brittle chemical element, atomic number 25, which is one of the transition metals. (Symbol Mn.)
dominio.observaciones: Used in steels and magnetic alloys.

dominio.definicion: White to gray accumulation on lake bottoms caused by precipitation of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) mixed with microscopic fresh water fossil shells and fragments.

Building materials (for example: stone, brick, concrete, hollow-tile, concrete block, gypsum block, or other similar building units or materials and/or a combination of the same) bonded together with mortar to form a structure (for example: a wall, a pier, or a buttress).
Any of the class of substances that are characteristically lustrous, ductile, fusible, malleable solids and are good conductors of heat and electricity.
dominio.observaciones: For example, gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, tin, and certain alloys (as brass and bronze).

dominio.definicion: Soft wet soil, sand, dust, and/or other earthy matter.
dominio.observaciones: Also, the hard ground produced by the drying of an area of mud.

dominio.definicion: Any of various bivalve molluscs belonging chiefly to the marine superfamily Mytilacea or to the freshwater superfamily Unionacea.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the common edible marine bivalve, Mytilus edulis, which has a dark grey, slightly elongated shell and adheres by a byssus, frequently in large aggregations.

dominio.definicion: A deposit or layer of white or grey calcareous matter largely composed of foraminiferan remains, covering large areas of the ocean floor.
Any of various bivalve molluscs of the family Ostreidae, several of which are eaten (especially raw) as a delicacy and may be farmed for food or pearls.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the common European Ostrea edulis, and members of the widespread genus Crassostrea.

dominio.definicion: Composed in part, but not completely, by metal.
Small, smooth, rounded stones, that have been worn by the action of water, ice, and/or sand.
Mosslike colonies of sessile, polypoid aquatic animals that reproduce by budding.
Reinforced concrete in which internal stresses have been introduced to reduce potential tensile stress in the concrete resulting from loads.
A light spongy form of volcanic glass, usually of pyroclastic origin and with a high silica content.
dominio.observaciones: Used, for example, as an abrasive (for example: in cleaning, polishing, removing stains and/or dead skin) or as an absorbent for moisture.

dominio.definicion: A trigonal rock-forming mineral consisting of silica, massive or crystallizing in colourless or white hexagonal prisms.
dominio.observaciones: Found widely in igneous and metamorphic rocks. Often coloured by impurities (as amethyst, citrine, cairngorm).

dominio.definicion: Marine protozoa with amoeba-like bodies and radiating filamentous pseudopods.
Poured concrete containing steel bars or metal netting to increase its tensile strength.
Stones of any size.
Granular material consisting of small eroded fragments of (mainly siliceous) rocks, finer than gravel and larger than a coarse silt grain.
dominio.observaciones: Generally ranging between 0.074 millimetres (No. 200 sieve) and 4.76 millimetres (No. 4 sieve) in size. Often a major constituent of a beach, desert, or the bed of a river or sea. Used for various purposes, as in smoothing stone, founding, or as an ingredient in mortar.

dominio.definicion: A coarse-grained pelitic metamorphic rock that has a structure marked by parallel layers of various minerals and can be split into thin irregular plates.
Rough masses resembling clinker, formed by the cooling of volcanic ejecta, and of a light aerated texture.
Calcareous remains of macroscopic marine animals, whole or in fragments.
Small, loose, rounded waterworn pebbles, especially as accumulated on a seashore.
Material consisting of particles whose sizes fall within a specified range (typically 0.002-0.06 millimetres) between those of sand and clay.
Accumulated remains of sponges consisting of the small pointed structures of calcite or silica that compose their skeletons.
Any of various primitive sessile aquatic (chiefly marine) animals of the phylum Porifera, which have porous baglike bodies with a skeleton of hard spicules or elastic fibres.
Pieces of rock or mineral substance (other than metal) of definite form and size, usually artificially shaped, and used for some special purpose.
dominio.observaciones: Used, for example, for building, for paving, or in the form of a block, slab, or pillar set up as a memorial and/or a boundary-mark.

dominio.definicion: A soft porous calcium carbonate rock formed by deposition around mineral springs.
dominio.observaciones: Also any friable porous stone formed of consolidated, often stratified material.

dominio.definicion: A mineral that may be used for the extraction of uranium.
dominio.observaciones: For example, pitchblende, uraninite, carnotite, torbernite, tyuyamunite, autunite, uranophane, and brannerite.

dominio.definicion: Plants collectively, especially those dominating a particular area or habitat.
Loose fragmented solid material ejected from a volcano.
The transparent, colourless, tasteless, odourless, liquid compound of hydrogen and oxygen (formula H2O).
dominio.observaciones: Forms the main constituent of seas, lakes, rivers, and rain, and is put to many domestic and industrial uses.

dominio.definicion: The hard, compact, fibrous substance of which the roots, trunks, and branches of trees and shrubs consist.
dominio.observaciones: Consists largely of secondary xylem, which forms the strengthening and water-transporting tissue of the plant.

dominio.definicion: A hard lustrous bluish-white metallic chemical element, atomic number 30, which is obtained from sphalerite and other ores. (Symbol Zn.)
dominio.observaciones: Used for roofing, galvanizing iron, and making alloys with copper.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary salt deposit left after the evaporation of a body of water.
A plastic composition in which glass reinforcements are imbedded with strength properties greatly superior to those of the base resin.
dominio.observaciones: The reinforcements are usually fibres, rovings, fabrics or mats.

dominio.definicion: A light silvery ductile and malleable metal, not readily tarnished by air, which is a chemical element, atomic number 13. (Symbol Al.)
A dark, fine-grained igneous rock, often displaying columnar structure and usually composed largely of plagioclase with pyroxene and olivine.
Native consolidated solid rock that has been unaffected by the processes of weathering and underlies the surface of the Earth.
dominio.observaciones: Often overlain by the results of weathering processes, including soil, clay, sand, gravel and related loose materials.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock consisting of angular, coarse-grained fragments cemented together by a fine-grained matrix (for example: by lime).
A nonmetallic material made from clay and hardened by firing at high temperature.
dominio.observaciones: It contains minute silicate crystals suspended in a glassy cement.

dominio.definicion: A malleable and ductile reddish metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 29. (Symbol Cu.)
dominio.observaciones: Used especially for electrical conductors and as the base of alloys.

dominio.definicion: An igneous rock chemically the same as basalt and gabbro but medium-grained with a usually ophitic texture.
dominio.observaciones: Usually dark coloured and fine or medium textured. Occurs in minor intrusions such as sills and dykes.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary rock composed chiefly of a hexagonal carbonate of calcium, magnesium, and usually iron that occurs as translucent crystals of various colours, alone or with calcite.
A thinly-bedded sedimentary deposit consisting of shales and marls alternating with coarser strata such as sandstones and conglomerates.
A foliated, usually coarse-grained, metamorphic rock in which bands of granular minerals alternate with bands of flaky or prismatic ones.
dominio.observaciones: Formed by the metamorphism of granite and other igneous rocks, and typically consisting of feldspar, quartz, and mica. Usually of a streaked, wavy or banded appearance.

dominio.definicion: A precious metal which is characterized by its yellowish colour, resistance to tarnishing and corrosion, and great malleability and ductility, and is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 79 (symbol Au).
Any of a broad class of granular crystalline plutonic rocks, consisting essentially of quartz, orthoclase, feldspar, and mica or hornblende.
dominio.observaciones: Often used for building.

dominio.definicion: Any igneous rock of dark-green appearance, especially containing chlorite, epidote, and/or hornblende.
dominio.observaciones: Includes nephrites and, in particular, jade.

dominio.definicion: A malleable, magnetic, readily oxidizable metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 26. (Symbol Fe.)
dominio.observaciones: Occurs abundantly in certain ores and in meteorites, and is widely used, chiefly in alloys such as steel.

dominio.definicion: A clayey (usually red) soil or soil horizon characterized by a high proportion of sesquioxides, especially of aluminum and iron, and a low proportion of bases and silica.
dominio.observaciones: Formed by chemical weathering in tropical and subtropical regions, especially one which hardens or has hardened on exposure to air. Also loosely any of various other reddish or iron-rich surface materials in the tropics and sub-tropics.

dominio.definicion: A soft, heavy, malleable, bluish-grey metal that is a chemical element, atomic number 82, occurring in galena and other minerals. (Symbol Pb.)
A sedimentary rock composed chiefly of calcium carbonate.
dominio.observaciones: Yields lime when calcined and is used as a building material and in the making of cement.

dominio.definicion: Fine yellowish-grey loam composed of material transported by the wind.
Timber sawn into rough planks or otherwise partly prepared.
Limestone that has been recrystallized by metamorphism and is capable of taking a polish, especially one that is pure white or has a mottled surface.
Any of a large class of substances which are polymers based on synthetic resins or modified natural polymers.
dominio.observaciones: May be moulded, extruded, or cast while soft or liquid, and then set into a rigid or slightly elastic form, usually by heating or cooling.

dominio.definicion: An unstratified or igneous rock having a homogeneous groundmass containing larger crystals of one or more minerals (frequently feldspar).
dominio.observaciones: For example, a hard rock quarried in ancient Egypt, having crystals of white or red plagioclase feldspar in a fine red groundmass of hornblende or apatite. Loosely, any attractive red or purple stone taking a high polish.

dominio.definicion: A extremely compact, hard, granular rock consisting essentially of quartz.
dominio.observaciones: It is a metamorphosed sandstone in which the siliceous element is often so blended with the quartz grains so as to give the rock a nearly homogenous texture.

dominio.definicion: Any material or combination of materials which spontaneously emits ionizing radiation (for example: nuclear particles and/or gamma rays).
Any of various sedimentary rocks composed of sand grains, especially of quartz, cemented together.
dominio.observaciones: Typically red, yellow, brown, grey, or white in colour.

dominio.definicion: Soft finely stratified rock that splits easily into fragile laminae, consisting of consolidated mud or clay.
A precious metal which is characterized by its lustrous white colour and great malleability and ductility, and is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 47. (Symbol Ag.)
A dense, fine-grained, metamorphic rock that develops a characteristic cleavage which may be at any angle with the original bedding plane.
dominio.observaciones: Typically dark grey, blue, or green in colour. Splits readily into smooth parallel-sided flat plates, and used for making tiles for roofing and flooring.

dominio.definicion: Any of numerous artificially produced alloys of iron containing up to 3 percent of other elements (including less than about 2.2 percent carbon) and having great strength and malleability.
dominio.observaciones: Able to be tempered to many different degrees of hardness. Used for making tools, weapons, and/or machinery.

dominio.definicion: A beam or piece of wood forming or capable of forming part of any structure.
A white or light-coloured concretionary limestone, usually hard and semi-crystalline, precipitated from water holding calcium carbonate in solution (for example: in hot springs).
dominio.observaciones: May be used for building.

definicion: The classification of a feature among geographic themes.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a thematic classification.

dominio.definicion: The feature belongs to the 'Aeronautical' theme.
The feature belongs to the 'Vegetation' theme.
The feature belongs to the 'Utilities' theme.
The feature belongs to the 'Population' theme.
The feature belongs to the 'Physiography' theme.
The feature belongs to the 'Industry' theme.
The feature belongs to the 'Ground Transportation' theme.
The feature belongs to the 'Elevation' theme.
The feature belongs to the 'Boundaries' theme.
The feature belongs to the 'Waterbodies' theme.
The feature belongs to the 'Maritime' theme.

definicion: The distance between the two opposite surfaces of an object, usually the distance of smallest measure.
descripcion: The third dimension of an object, distinct from length and width (breadth).

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The class of a thoroughfare based on its importance in the general transportation network.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a thoroughfare class.

dominio.definicion: A component of a national network of arterial, inter-city highways, specifically excluding national motorways.
dominio.observaciones: May be identified in their designations, for example, with a 'US' in the US, a 'B' in Germany and an 'N' in Europe. When referring to designated national systems of motorways such as the US Interstate Highway System or the German Autobahns, preference should be given to instead using enumerant 'National Motorway'.

dominio.definicion: A component of a network of collector highways that feed primary routes.
dominio.observaciones: May be identified in their designations, for example, with an 'R' in France.

dominio.definicion: A component of a national network of limited access motorways.
dominio.observaciones: May be identified in their designations, for example, with an 'I' in the US, an 'M' in the UK, or an 'E' in Europe.

dominio.definicion: A route not otherwise classified as a national motorway, primary route, or secondary route.
dominio.observaciones: Traditionally comprised of farm-to-market routes, country lanes, and larger urban streets.

definicion: The name of a thoroughfare.
descripcion: For example, 'Dolley Madison Boulevard', 'Chain Bridge Road', or 'Meander Lane'. The thoroughfare name may be used to represent the components of a postal address in concert with Attributes: 'Address Number', 'Address Direction Prefix', (optionally) 'Thoroughfare Type', and 'Address Direction Suffix'.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is 80 characters in maximum length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of a roadway based on its design and/or location.
descripcion: A thoroughfare is a public way, unobstructed and forming a route (for example: a road or a path) between two places. The thoroughfare type may be used in proper names and thus to represent the components of a postal address in concert with Attributes: 'Address Number', 'Address Direction Prefix', 'Thoroughfare Name', and 'Address Direction Suffix'.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a thoroughfare type.

dominio.definicion: A roadway that is located outside of a built-up area (for example: a city, town, or village), that has a specially prepared surface that is maintained for use by motor vehicles and is other than a motorway or limited access motorway.
dominio.observaciones: Includes all roadways except motorway, limited access motorway, and street.

dominio.definicion: A broad often landscaped thoroughfare, especially one larger than an ordinary street or avenue.
dominio.observaciones: In general, a broad main urban road.

dominio.definicion: A broad thoroughfare bordered by trees.
A thoroughfare represented as pleasant to drive along or with fine views, especially a private road leading to a house.
dominio.observaciones: More generally used in proper names of thoroughfares in residential areas.

dominio.definicion: A relatively short urban thoroughfare having the shape of a circle.
dominio.observaciones: Usually found in residential areas.

dominio.definicion: A short street ending in the form of a small circular cul-de-sac.
A broad landscaped thoroughfare forming the direct route between one town and another, often divided by planted median strips.
A narrow path, road or street passing between houses, walls, hedges, banks and/or fences.
dominio.observaciones: It usually experiences limited traffic.

dominio.definicion: A roadway that is located within a built-up area (for example: a city, town, or village), that has a specially prepared surface that is maintained for use by motor vehicles and is other than a motorway or limited access motorway.
dominio.observaciones: Includes all roadways within a built-up area except motorway and limited access motorway.

dominio.definicion: A raised level, usually paved area, adjoining a building, for walking or sitting.
dominio.observaciones: More generally used in proper names of thoroughfares in residential areas.

dominio.definicion: A roadway that is specially designed for fast long-distance traffic with unconstrained traffic flow and is subject to special regulations concerning its use.
dominio.observaciones: It may have more than two lanes. A motorway differs from all other types of thoroughfares in that it has no crossroads, no traffic lights, and no pedestrian crossings.

dominio.definicion: A small square or a side-street, especially a cul-de-sac, lined with houses.
dominio.observaciones: More generally used in proper names of thoroughfares in residential areas.

dominio.definicion: An unimproved road.
dominio.observaciones: The surface is usually rough (for example: rutted) and minimally prepared (for example: packed earth or thinly covered with gravel).

dominio.definicion: A roadway that is specially designed for fast long-distance traffic and is subject to special regulations concerning its use that may result in localized constraints on traffic.
dominio.observaciones: A limited access motorway differs from a motorway in that it may have some crossroads, traffic lights, or pedestrian crossings.

dominio.definicion: A thoroughfare junction at which traffic moves in one direction round a central island.
A path worn by the passage of people or animals.
An inclined slip road leading on to or off a main highway.

definicion: The use to which a thoroughfare is put as part of a transportation system.
descripcion: A thoroughfare is a public way, unobstructed and forming a route (for example: a road or a path) between two places.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a thoroughfare use.

dominio.definicion: A thoroughfare whose use is restricted to vehicles (for example: buses) that are part of a public transportation system.
A thoroughfare primarily used to serve private properties (for example: leading to a farm or estate).
A thoroughfare intended for other than general public use (for example: refuse removal or contractor access).
dominio.observaciones: For example, thoroughfares intended for the primary use of: utility personnel, oil and/or logging companies, farmers and/or ranchers, and/or in-holders.

dominio.definicion: A public, high-speed road intended to have restricted access.
dominio.observaciones: Usually passing between and/or around major urban areas.

dominio.definicion: A thoroughfare that passes through a place (for example: an urban area) without requiring vehicles to stop.
A thoroughfare passing round (the centre of) a town, providing an alternative route for through traffic.
A short, usually one-way, road giving access to or exit from a motorway.
Track - a rough path or way formed by use. Path - a way or track laid down for walking or made by continual treading.
A place where roads cross and/or intersect.

definicion: The width of the final approach course at the Landing Threshold Point (LTP).
descripcion: This width, in conjunction with the location of the Flight Path Alignment Point (FPAP) defines the sensitivity of the lateral deviations throughout the approach. The value ranges between 80.00 and143.75 metres, inclusive, in steps of 0.25 metre.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value that is restricted to be non-negative.
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The height above the runway threshold at which the computed glide path crosses the threshold.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of length equal to 0.3048 metres.

definicion: An indication that a ground transportation route (for example: road, cart track or trail) is the most direct way through (both into and then out of) a built-up area or populated place.
descripcion: Routes may branch off of the main through route providing an alternate through route out of the built-up area or populated place. The direct or alternate ways through a built-up area or populated place may consist of the quickest or shortest route. A through route may have devices (for example: traffic lights) to control traffic flow.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type(s) of special power boost fluids available for injecting into the airflow of the aircraft engine to increase power output.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a thrust augmentation fluid type.

dominio.definicion: 100 percent Methanol, reagent grade.
Grade 45/55, 43.8 percent Methanol, 56.2 percent Dematerialised water mixture.
100 percent Dematerialised water.
Anti-Detonation Injection (ADI) fluid for reciprocating engine aircraft.
Water thrust augmentation for jet aircraft.
Water Alcohol injection for thrust augmentation jet aircraft.

definicion: The type of a coast based on its sedimentation and ablation processes and/or its predominant vegetation.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a tidal coast type.

dominio.definicion: A flat coast with tides where tideland develops.
dominio.observaciones: It is an ecological highly diverse, major habitat.

dominio.definicion: A dense thicket of mangrove that is subject to tidal inundation and forming a muddy swamp.

definicion: The tidal current direction at the time of the tide reference level.
descripcion: Typically used together with Attribute: 'Reference Water Level' to specify the tide reference level.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value that is restricted to fall in the range from 0 to 359, inclusive.
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of an angle in two dimensions (the angle between two half-lines terminating at the same point).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of plane angle equal to pi/180, approximately 0.01745532925199433 radians.

definicion: The tidal current direction 1 hour after the tide reference level.
descripcion: Typically used together with Attribute: 'Reference Water Level' to specify the tide reference level from which the time offset is specified.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a tide category.

dominio.definicion: A tide in which the tidal cycle consists of one high water and one low water each tidal day.
The type of tide in which a diurnal wave produces large inequalities in heights and/or durations of successive high and/or low waters.
dominio.observaciones: This term applies to the tides intermediate to those predominantly semidiurnal and those predominantly diurnal.

dominio.definicion: Diurnal tides which become semidiurnal with a considerable decrease in range when the moon's declination is small.
Semi-diurnal tides with noticeable inequality in corresponding extremes.
The tide resulting from the distortion of the normal tide in shallow water with four high waters and four low waters during one day.
A tide in which the tidal cycle consists of two high waters and two low waters each tidal day, with comparatively little diurnal inequality.
A tide with distortional effects resulting from shallow water.

definicion: The type of structure within which a corpse is entombed based on its method of construction, location, and/or occupancy.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a tomb type.

dominio.definicion: A cave serving as a tomb.
dominio.observaciones: May be used to contain a single corpse and then have the opening sealed, or may contain one or more burial niches carved into its walls. The cave may be either man-made (excavated directly into the solid rock) or naturally occurring.

dominio.definicion: A network of underground galleries (for example: caves, grottos, or tunnels) in which burial niches are carved into the walls.
A tomb in the form of an underground chamber or vault located under a religious building (for example: a church).
A tomb constructed as a small building located mostly or completely aboveground.
A building containing a number of sealed tombs.
dominio.observaciones: May also include columbarium niches for cremated remains. Usually each tomb or niche is labeled with a plaque which includes information about the deceased. The term derives from the tomb of Mausolus at Halicarnassus.

dominio.definicion: A mound of earth and stones raised over one or more graves.
dominio.observaciones: A burial mound composed largely or entirely of stones is usually referred to as a 'cairn'.

dominio.definicion: A compartmentalized structure for holding cremated remains.
dominio.observaciones: A columbarium may be enclosed in a building, incorporated into a building, or exist as a freestanding outside structure. Typically, an individual vertical compartment in the columbarium holds an urn of ashes and is covered with a name plaque.

definicion: Tonnage of a sunken or stranded wreck, a hulk, or other vessel.
descripcion: Reference STANAG 3715.

datatype.definicion: An integer domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is an integer. For example, 6 (as in the length of a fathom in feet).
datatype.nota: The realization of this integer datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of the property of a body that causes it to have weight in a gravitational field.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of mass equal to 2,000 pounts (0.9071847 tonne or 907.1847 kilograms).

definicion: The characteristic topmark or daymark shape attached to a maritime aid to navigation to aid identification.
descripcion: May be secured at the top of a buoy or beacon.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a topmark shape.

dominio.definicion: One cone, with its vertex pointing up.
dominio.observaciones: A cone is a solid figure generated by straight lines drawn from a fixed point (the vertex) to a circle in a plane not containing the vertex. The International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) uses one cone, point up, as a lateral mark.

dominio.definicion: One cone, with its vertex pointing down.
dominio.observaciones: A cone is a solid figure generated by straight lines drawn from a fixed point (the vertex) to a circle in a plane not containing the vertex. A single cone pointing down is not used in the International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) system.

dominio.definicion: A sphere.
dominio.observaciones: A sphere is a globular body, the surface of which is at all points equidistant from the centre. The International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) uses a sphere as a safe water topmark.

dominio.definicion: Two spheres, generally vertically disposed one above the other.
dominio.observaciones: A sphere is a globular body, the surface of which is at all points equidistant from the centre. The International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) uses two black balls (spheres) as an isolated danger topmark.

dominio.definicion: A cylinder, vertically oriented.
dominio.observaciones: A cylinder is a solid geometrical figure generated by straight line fixed in direction and describing with one of its' points a closed curve, especially a circle (in which case the figure is a circular cylinder, its ends being parallel circles). The International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) uses a cylinder as a topmark on a lateral mark. In this application, the height of the cylinder is greater than the diameter, resulting in a vertical rectangular topmark when viewed from any direction.

dominio.definicion: A board, usually of rectangular shape, made from timber or metal and used to provide a contrast with the natural background of a daymark.
dominio.observaciones: The actual daymark is often painted on to this board.

dominio.definicion: Having a shape like the capital letter 'X'.
dominio.observaciones: The International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) uses an 'X' shape as a special mark. When so used it should be 3 dimensional in shape, made of at least three crossed bars.

dominio.definicion: A cross with one vertical member and one horizontal member, similar in shape to the character '+'.
A cube standing on one of its vertexes.
dominio.observaciones: A cube is a solid contained by six equal squares; a regular hexahedron.

dominio.definicion: Two cones, one above the other, with their vertices together in the centre.
dominio.observaciones: A cone is a solid figure generated by straight lines drawn from a fixed point (the vertex) to a circle in a plane not containing the vertex. The International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) uses two cones, point to point, as a west cardinal mark.

dominio.definicion: Two cones, one above the other, with their bases together in the centre and their vertices pointing up and down.
dominio.observaciones: A cone is a solid figure generated by straight lines drawn from a fixed point (the vertex) to a circle in a plane not containing the vertex. The International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) uses two cones, base to base, as an east cardinal mark.

dominio.definicion: A plane figure having four equal sides and equal opposite angles (two acute and two obtuse); an oblique equilateral parallelogram.
Two cones, one above the other, with their vertices pointing up.
dominio.observaciones: A cone is a solid figure generated by straight lines drawn from a fixed point (the vertex) to a circle in a plane not containing the vertex. The International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) uses two cones, points up, as a north cardinal mark.

dominio.definicion: Two cones, one above the other, with their vertices pointing down.
dominio.observaciones: A cone is a solid figure generated by straight lines drawn from a fixed point (the vertex) to a circle in a plane not containing the vertex. The International Association of Lighthouse Authorities (IALA) uses two cones, points down, as a south cardinal mark.

dominio.definicion: A broom (bundle of rods or twigs) or a perch (staff) that is pointing up.
A broom (bundle of rods or twigs) or a perch (staff) that is pointing down.
A flag mounted on a short pole.
A sphere (ball) located above a diamond.
dominio.observaciones: A diamond (or rhombus) is a plane figure having four equal sides and equal opposite angles (two acute and two obtuse); an oblique equilateral parallelogram.

dominio.definicion: A plane figure with four right angles and four equal straight sides.
A rectangle where the two longer opposite sides are standing horizontally.
dominio.observaciones: A rectangle is a plane figure with four right angles and four straight sides, opposite sides being parallel and equal in length.

dominio.definicion: A rectangle where the two longer opposite sides are standing vertically.
dominio.observaciones: A rectangle is a plane figure with four right angles and four straight sides, opposite sides being parallel and equal in length.

dominio.definicion: A trapezium that stands on its longer parallel side.
dominio.observaciones: A trapezium is a quadrilateral having one pair of opposite sides parallel.

dominio.definicion: A trapezium that stands on its shorter parallel side.
dominio.observaciones: A trapezium is a quadrilateral having one pair of opposite sides parallel.

dominio.definicion: A triangle with vertex uppermost.
dominio.observaciones: A triangle is a figure having three angles and three sides.

dominio.definicion: A triangle with vertex down.
dominio.observaciones: A triangle is a figure having three angles and three sides.

dominio.definicion: A perfectly round plane figure whose circumference is everywhere equidistant from its centre.
Two upright crosses, generally vertically disposed one above the other.
dominio.observaciones: An upright cross is a cross with one vertical member and one horizontal member, similar in shape to the character '+'.

dominio.definicion: Having a shape like the capital letter 'T'.
A triangle, vertex uppermost, located above a circle.
dominio.observaciones: A triangle is a figure having three angles and three sides.

dominio.definicion: An upright cross located above a circle.
dominio.observaciones: An upright cross is a cross with one vertical member and one horizontal member, similar in shape to the character '+'.

dominio.definicion: A diamond located above a circle.
dominio.observaciones: A diamond (or rhombus) is a plane figure having four equal sides and equal opposite angles (two acute and two obtuse); an oblique equilateral parallelogram.

dominio.definicion: A circle located over a triangle with vertex uppermost.
dominio.observaciones: A triangle is a figure having three angles and three sides.

dominio.definicion: One sphere (ball) located above a cone.
One cone located above one sphere (ball).
One vertically elongated cross (+) or x-shaped object located above a non-filled sphere (ball).
One cylinder, vertically oriented located above a non-filled sphere (ball).
One vertically elongated rhombus located above a filled sphere (ball).

The feature is located at a mountain pass.
The feature is located on a landmass surrounded by water.
The feature is located in a long flat depression, open on one side.
The feature is located on a seacoast.

descripcion: The Touchdown zone is the portion of a runway, beyond the threshold, intended as the first point of contact between landing aircraft and the runway. 1. For rotary-wing and vectored-thrust aircraft, the portion of the helipad or runway used for landing.
