datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity by which events are compared in position and duration.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of time that is 60 minutes in duration, being 3600 seconds.

definicion: The type of a facility, building, or structure that is used for utility provision purposes.
descripcion: For example, services such as gas, electricity, water, or sewers.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a utility facility type.

dominio.definicion: A structure in which electric power is generated, switched, transformed, and/or converted.
The outlet or structure through which reclaimed water or treated effluent is finally discharged to a receiving body of water.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the end of the pipe leading from a sewage treatment plant that delivers the wastewater to the environment, often via a diffuser.

dominio.definicion: A structure where water is channelled from a body of water for use.
dominio.observaciones: For example, to drive a mill, supply a canal, cool a power station, or feed a water purification plant.

dominio.definicion: A structure used in the process of cleaning water to make it suitable for drinking.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a filtration bed.

dominio.definicion: A relatively small building that is separate from but is located near a main building and whose utility use has not been determined.
A facility including one or more buildings and equipment used for power generation.
A building that houses equipment through which a liquid or gas is passed in order to separate the fluid from suspended particulate matter.
A facility for the generation of chilled liquid and/or gas for cooling purposes.
An establishment for storing, purifying, and supplying an area or town with water.

definicion: The type of a vegetated area based on species, biome, physiography and/or structural organization.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vegetation characteristic.

dominio.definicion: A tract covered mainly by grasses that have little or no woody tissue.
dominio.observaciones: For example, pasture, meadow, and steppe.

dominio.definicion: A tract covered mainly by grasses that have little or no woody tissue but including scattered trees.
An area of plants of the large cosmopolitan family Poaceae (formerly Gramineae) that is found principally in tropical regions.
dominio.observaciones: For example, bamboos (Bambuseae).

dominio.definicion: A dense thicket of mangrove that is subject to tidal inundation and forming a muddy swamp.
A generally small collection of trees growing more or less thickly together.
dominio.observaciones: May occur naturally or be deliberately planted for shade, ornamentation, and/or as an orchard (for example: of olives or citrus fruit).

dominio.definicion: A tract of trees whose canopy is not closed (allows sunlight to reach the ground) and often includes undergrowth.
A mixture of herbaceous and low-growing, uncultured plants that may have some woody tissue.
dominio.observaciones: For example, covered by tall grasses, shrubs, and/or bushes. The predominant height is usually less than 2-3 metres.

dominio.definicion: A site in a forest or wood(s) that has been cleared, often for slash and burn agriculture and/or as a result of clear-cutting logging.
dominio.observaciones: May also occur from natural causes such as a forest fire.

dominio.definicion: An area with scattered, usually sparse, treed vegetation.
An area lacking in treed vegetation.
A permanently wet area of land consisting of incompletely decayed organic material and mainly stagnant fresh water.
dominio.observaciones: It is generally too soft to bear the weight of any heavy body.

dominio.definicion: An area of marine plants that grow in long narrow ribbons.
dominio.observaciones: Algae may be moored or floating. For example, sea grass, kelp, or sargasso.

dominio.definicion: An area of any of various grasslike marine algae.
dominio.observaciones: Eel-grass, Zostera marina, is one of the best known sea grasses.

dominio.definicion: An area of plants growing in a marsh, swamp, or other stretch of land that is usually saturated with water.
Plants growing in or inhabiting high mountains (for example: the Alps) above the tree line.
dominio.observaciones: Generally designating any small plant suitable for rockeries.

dominio.definicion: An area used for the cultivation of vegetables, fruit and flowers as well as for the raising of cultivated plants.
An area of open uncultivated ground covered by heather and/or related plants, especially on acid sandy or peaty soil.
An area of dense growth of plants and/or bushes under tall trees.
Plants whose stems do not become woody and persistent (as in a shrub or tree) but remain soft and succulent, and die (completely or down to the root) after flowering.
A tract covered mainly by low-growing, uncultured, woody plants.
dominio.observaciones: For example, brushwood and/or stunted trees. The predominant height may be up to 6-8 metres.

dominio.definicion: A tract covered mainly by short, uncultured, woody plants.
dominio.observaciones: For example, covered by brush, scrub and/or shrubs. The predominant height is usually less than 2-3 metres.

dominio.definicion: A large tract of land covered with trees and undergrowth sometimes mixed with pasture.
A vast, nearly level, treeless arctic region usually with a marshy surface and underlying permafrost.
Any of the vast level grassy usually treeless plains of southeastern Europe and Siberia.
A swampy coniferous forest of high northern latitudes, especially that between the tundra and steppes of Siberia.
An arid and treeless uncultivated sparsely populated tract of land.
An open grassy plain with few or no trees in a tropical or subtropical region.
A dense forest in an area of high rainfall with little seasonal variation, and whose canopy is usually closed (allowing only filtered sunlight to reach the ground).
dominio.observaciones: Especially when located in the tropics, characterized by a rich variety of plant and animal life.

dominio.definicion: A small, poorly drained area dominated by grassy vegetation.

definicion: A subjective evaluation of the concentration of spatial coverage and/or density of vegetation (for example: along a waterbody bank).

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: An indication that an area contains vegetation.
descripcion: For example, a land area is occupied by scattered scrub or covered by grasses, or a waterbody area is occupied by clumps of reeds or covered by water hyacinth.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The predominant species of a tract of vegetation.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vegetation species.

dominio.definicion: A forest tree, Fraxinus excelsior, with grey bark, pinnate foliage, and hard, tough, pale wood.
dominio.observaciones: Also (with specifying word), any of various related or otherwise similar trees; especially any other tree of the genus Fraxinus.

dominio.definicion: A forest tree of the genus Fagus, having thin, smooth bark and glossy oval leaves, and bearing nuts.
dominio.observaciones: Especially the European Fagus sylvatica. Also (usually with specifying word), any of various similar trees, especially (in the southern hemisphere) of the genus Nothofagus.

dominio.definicion: Any of various hardy northern trees or shrubs of the genus Betula (family Betulaceae), having smooth, tough bark and slender branches.
dominio.observaciones: Especially (in Europe) Betula pendula (more fully silver birch) and Betula pubescens (more fully downy birch), and (in North America) Betula papyrifera (more fully paper birch).

dominio.definicion: A tree of the genus Casuarina (family Casuarinaceae) with jointed branches resembling gigantic horsetail plants.
dominio.observaciones: It is native to Australia and parts of Southeast Asia.

dominio.definicion: A tree of the genus Castanea, of the beech family.
dominio.observaciones: Especially that of Castanea sativa (also Spanish chestnut, sweet chestnut). Also (with specifying word), any of various similar trees.

dominio.definicion: A gymnospermous tree or shrub of the order Coniferales, members of which typically bear cones and evergreen needle-like leaves.
dominio.observaciones: For example, the pines, firs, cedars, larches, spruces, and yews.

dominio.definicion: An evergreen oak, Quercus suber, which is native to the Mediterranean and has the distinctive property of producing more cork after some is removed.
dominio.observaciones: Industrially used for various kinds of cork based products.

dominio.definicion: An evergreen coniferous tree of the Eurasian and North American genus Cupressus having flattened shoots with scalelike leaves.
dominio.observaciones: For example, Cupressus sempervirens (also known as Italian cypress), a tall, often fastigiate, tree native to southern Europe and the Middle East, with dark foliage and hard durable wood.

dominio.definicion: Any of various deciduous trees with serrate leaves, of the genus Ulmus and other genera of the family Ulmaceae.
dominio.observaciones: Especially (a) (more fully English elm) the European Ulmaceae procera, once common as a hedge tree in central and southern England; (b) (more fully American elm or white elm) Ulmaceae americana, a tree with pale bark of eastern North America.

dominio.definicion: Any of the genus Eucalyptus of flowering evergreen trees and shrubs, of the myrtle family.
dominio.observaciones: Includes species important as forest trees in Australia and grown elsewhere for their hardwood, oils, gums, and resins, and as ornamentals.

dominio.definicion: Casuarina equisetifolia, the most widespread and well-known member of the family Casuarinaceae.
dominio.observaciones: Known by many names including: Casuarina, ironwood, coast she-oak, horsetail, Australian pine, whistling pine, beefwood, agoho (Philippines), ru (Malaysia), filao (Vietnam, West Africa, West Indies) and nokonoko (Fiji).

dominio.definicion: An evergreen coniferous tree, especially one belonging to the genus Abies of the pine family, characterized by upright cones and flat needles usually arranged in two rows.
dominio.observaciones: Naturally occuring in the temperate zones of the northern hemisphere. Firs consist of more than fifty species.

dominio.definicion: Any plant of the large cosmopolitan family Gramineae (for example: cereals, reeds, and bamboos), members of which typically have erect jointed stems (culms) bearing narrow bladelike leaves and insignificant flowers.
dominio.observaciones: Also, any of various plants resembling the members of Gramineae in appearance.

dominio.definicion: Any of various deciduous shrubs and low trees constituting the genus Corylus, of the birch family, bearing edible nuts enclosed in leafy involucres.
dominio.observaciones: Especially the European hazel, Corylus avellana, and its North American counterpart, Corylus americana.

dominio.definicion: Any of various dwarf shrubs of the family Ericaceae characteristic of heathland or moor.
dominio.observaciones: Especially Erica cinerea (more fully fine-leaved heath) and Erica tetralix (more fully cross-leaved heath), common in dry and in boggy heath respectively.

dominio.definicion: A kind of oak, Quercus ilex, common in Mediterranean countries, with dark evergreen sometimes spiny-toothed leaves.
Any of various large brown seaweeds, chiefly members of the orders Fucales and Laminariales.
dominio.observaciones: Specifically Macrocystis pyrifera of the Pacific coast of America, the largest of the seaweeds. Often burnt for the substances found in the ashes.

dominio.definicion: Any of various deciduous coniferous trees of the genus Larix.
dominio.observaciones: Specifically Larix decidua, native to the Alps and cultivated for its tough durable timber.

dominio.definicion: Any of various tropical trees or shrubs of the genera Rhizophora and Bruguiera (family Rhizophoraceae) with interlacing aerial roots, which form dense thickets in muddy swamps subject to tidal inundation.
dominio.observaciones: For example, Rhizophora mangle (also known as common mangrove or red mangrove). May also be used to describe other tropical trees or shrubs of similar habit and appearance, especially of the genus Avicennia (of the verbena family).

dominio.definicion: A Eurasian tree, Acer campestre (family Aceraceae), with fruit in the form of two winged samaras joined together and palmately lobed leaves (more fully common maple, hedge maple).
dominio.observaciones: Also (with specifying word), any of numerous similar trees of this or other genera.

dominio.definicion: A plant of the class Musci, comprising small bryophytes with scalelike leaves usually spirally arranged and the spore-capsule usually opening by a lid, which grow in crowded masses in bogs, on the surface of the ground, on stones, and on trees.
dominio.observaciones: Also, any of certain algae, lichens, pteridophytes, or flowering plants resembling moss in habit.

dominio.definicion: A palm tree, Nypa fruticans, of mangrove swamps in tropical Asia and Australia, having a creeping rhizome and large feathery leaves.
Any of numerous trees (rarely shrubs) of the genus Quercus, of the beech family, with acorns borne in cupules and frequently with sinuately lobed leaves.
dominio.observaciones: Specifically (more fully common oak, English oak, pedunculate oak) Quercus robur and (more fully durmast oak, sessile oak) Quercus petraea.

dominio.definicion: An evergreen tree, Olea europaea (family Oleaceae), with narrow leaves hoary on the underside and small whitish flowers.
dominio.observaciones: Long cultivated in the Mediterranean region for its fruit and the oil obtained from this. May also be used to describe any of various wild trees or shrubs of the genus Olea; (with specifying word) any of various trees and shrubs allied to the common olive, or resembling it in appearance or in providing oil.

dominio.definicion: Any tree or shrub of the large, chiefly tropical, monocotyledonous family Palmae, typically having an unbranched stem with a crown of very large leaves either palmate or pinnate in shape.
dominio.observaciones: Also (with specifying word), any of various palmlike plants of other families, such as cycads.

dominio.definicion: Any coniferous tree of the genus Pinus, comprising usually large trees with evergreen needle-shaped leaves growing in clusters.
dominio.observaciones: Native to northern temperate regions, and valued especially as a source of timber, tar, and turpentine.

dominio.definicion: Any of various often tall and fast-growing, sometimes narrowly erect, trees of the genus Populus, of the willow family, often with triangular-ovate leaves.
dominio.observaciones: May also be used to describe any of various other trees resembling the poplar: specifically (a) in North America the tulip tree, Liriodendron tulipifera; (b) in Australia either of two trees with leaves like those of many poplars, Homalanthus populifolius, of the spurge family, and (more fully native poplar) Codonocarpus cotinifolius (family Gyrostemonaceae).

dominio.definicion: Posidonia oceanica, an alga-like, vascular, flowering plant endemic to the Mediterranean Sea.
dominio.observaciones: It forms extensive underwater meadows that spread from the shore to the depth of 40 metres. Most often they are found on silty and sandy floors; less often on hard ground. Its rhizomes, which can grow horizontally or vertically, are densely intertwined and constitute a kind of a secondary bottom. This may be several decimetres thick and can sometimes create actual reefs.

dominio.definicion: Any of various tall broad-leaved firm-stemmed grasses of the genera Phragmites and Arundo growing in water or marshy ground, frequently in large stands.
dominio.observaciones: Especially the common reed, Phragmites australis, found in most parts of the world. May also be used, with a specifying word, to describe any of various plants resembling the reed.

dominio.definicion: Any brown alga of the genus Sargassum, the members of which are kept afloat by air-filled bladders and form dense floating masses in warmer parts of the Atlantic.
Coarse marine alga of the genus Laminaria.
dominio.observaciones: For example, oarweed or Laminaria digitata and Laminaria saccharina, two species of seaweed with long feathery fronds, the young stalk and fronds of which are sometimes eaten.

dominio.definicion: Any tree of the genus Juglans (family Juglandaceae), members of which have drooping catkins and aromatic pinnate leaves.
dominio.observaciones: Especially the Eurasian Juglans regia and (more fully black walnut) the North American Juglans nigra. The green fleshy fruit contains an edible kernel in separate halves.

dominio.definicion: A tropical palm tree, Cocos nucifera, that bears a large ovate brown hard-shelled seed having an edible white lining enclosing a white liquid.
dominio.observaciones: Its fruitflesh (Copra) is also processed for the production of oil, fat and dried cocoflakes.

dominio.definicion: Any of numerous, mainly tropical, giant grasses belonging to the genus Bambusa and various related genera.
dominio.observaciones: The mature canes are used for construction and furniture.

dominio.definicion: A free-floating water plant with thick, waxy, rounded, glossy leaves that rise well above the water surface on stalks that grow up to three feet in height.
dominio.observaciones: Water hyacinth growth rate is among the highest of any plant known: hyacinth populations can double in as little as 12 days. In addition to blocking boat traffic and preventing swimming and fishing, water hyacinth infestations also prevent sunlight and oxygen from penetrating the water. Decaying plant matter also reduces oxygen in the water and consequently water hyacinth infestations reduce fisheries, shade out and crowd out immersed plants, and reduce biological diversity.

dominio.definicion: A plant of simple structure that grows chiefly in water, such as the various forms of seaweed.
dominio.observaciones: It ranges in size from a microscopic plant, large numbers of which sometimes cause discoloration of water, to the giant kelp which may extend for more than 185 metres (approximately 600 feet) in length.

dominio.definicion: An African tree (Adansonia digitata) with a short thick stem and a broad crown.
dominio.observaciones: It is capable of storing great quantities of water.

dominio.definicion: A coniferous timber tree of the genus Abies.
dominio.observaciones: Used for veneer, furniture or construction.

dominio.definicion: A tree of the genus Diospyros of the East Indian and African tropic regions.
dominio.observaciones: The wood is noted for its solidity and black colour; it is among the most expensive timbers.

dominio.definicion: A member of the birch family that grows in moist places (Alnus glutinosa).
dominio.observaciones: The light wood is known for being extremely durable under water.

dominio.definicion: The trembling poplar (Populus tremula).
dominio.observaciones: Remarkable for its quivering leaves.

dominio.definicion: A small tree of the northern hemisphere (Carpinus betulus).
dominio.observaciones: Yields tough timber and is cultivated for planting hedges.

dominio.definicion: One of several Norh American trees of the genus Carya.
dominio.observaciones: Related to the walnuts, especially Carya alba, the timber of which is tough and elastic.

dominio.definicion: A tree of the coniferous genus Pinus.
dominio.observaciones: An evergreen with very long needle shaped leaves; used for construction and furniture.

dominio.definicion: A glossy-leaved evergreen shrub (Laurus nobilis), popular in the Mediterranian region.
dominio.observaciones: The leaves are used for spice; the oil of the fruits has medicinal properties.

dominio.definicion: A tree of tropical America (Swietenia mahagoni).
dominio.observaciones: Yields a hard, fine-grained wood, used for building instruments and for woodwork arts.

dominio.definicion: A Californian genus of gigantic conifers.
dominio.observaciones: Has two species; the highest trees in the world.

dominio.definicion: A medium-sized hardwood tree of Western Africa (Aucoumea klaineana).
dominio.observaciones: Often used for furniture.

dominio.definicion: A tree having large spreading branches with broad angular leaves, one of various species of the genus Platanus.
dominio.observaciones: Often grown as avenue-, ornamental- and park-tree.

dominio.definicion: A species of acacia (Acacia tortilis).
dominio.observaciones: Has an umbrella like crown. The mark of Africa.

dominio.definicion: A large East Indian tree (Tectona grandis).
dominio.observaciones: Yields a heavy timber.

dominio.definicion: A genus of coniferous trees or shrubs (Thuja) of the cypress family.
dominio.observaciones: Often cultivated for planting hedges.

dominio.definicion: Any tree or shrub of the genus Salix.
dominio.observaciones: It usually grows near water and is characterized by its long slender branches.

dominio.definicion: An evergreen coniferous tree, such as Abies cedrus.
dominio.observaciones: It has durable and fragrant wood.

dominio.definicion: An alpine coniferous genus (Pinus cembra).
dominio.observaciones: The wood is resinous, durable and is used for panelling and carving.

dominio.definicion: A coniferous of the genus Picea, popular on the northern hemisphere.
dominio.observaciones: Used for construction and trimmed timber.

dominio.definicion: A species of willow, Salix viminalis, growing close to waterbodies or on moist ground.
dominio.observaciones: The pliable shoots of it are used for basket-making.

dominio.definicion: A darkleaved evergreen shrub or tree of the genus Taxus.
dominio.observaciones: All parts of the plant are poisonous.

dominio.definicion: A genus of prickly evergreen shrubs, comprising Juniperus communis. Popular in the northern hemisphere on arid soils.
dominio.observaciones: Used as ornamental plant or for medicinal purposes.

dominio.definicion: Ilex Aquifolium (Holly, or European Holly to distinguish it from related species) is an evergreen tree growing to 10-25 metres tall with smooth grey bark whose leaves are 5-12 centimetres long and 2-6 centimetres broad with three to five sharp spines on each side.
dominio.observaciones: A species of holly native to western and southern Europe, northwest Africa and southwest Asia.

dominio.definicion: A rough prickly shrub of the genus Rubus, with long trailing shoots, especially any member of the aggregate species Rubus fruticosus, with purplish-black fruit, a blackberry-bush.

definicion: The degree of impact of vegetation on trafficability, based on the percent trafficability reduction from a smooth, vegetation-free terrain surface (zero percent reduction).
descripcion: Vegetation reduces trafficability by requiring that either it must be 'overridden' (for example: scrub by a battle tank) or bypassed (for example: orchard trees by an infantryman).

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value that is restricted to be completely contained in the range from 0 to 100, inclusive.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: A dimensionless quantity (a quantity with the dimension of 1).

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A scaled dimensionless measure denoting one part in every hundred.

definicion: The number of vehicles that a feature can accommodate.

datatype.definicion: A count domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a cardinal number or an ordinal number. For example, 4 (as in the number of legs of a cow).
datatype.nota: The realization of this count datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The number of vehicle scales at a weigh station.
descripcion: A weigh station is a building and associated equipment that is used to inspect and weigh motor vehicles. It is located adjacent to a road and used to enforce a variety of motor vehicle safety regulations. Motor vehicles may be weighed by driving them onto a platform.

datatype.definicion: A count domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a cardinal number or an ordinal number. For example, 4 (as in the number of legs of a cow).
datatype.nota: The realization of this count datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of a vehicle based on its use and/or mode of propulsion.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vehicle type.

dominio.definicion: A machine that can be flown in the air.
dominio.observaciones: For example, an aeroplane or a helicopter.

dominio.definicion: A self-propelled motor vehicle.
A flat-bottomed freight-boat that may be either towed or self-propelled (for example: a bulk motor boat).
A vehicle having two wheels turned by pedalling, typically with handlebars at the front and a seat or saddle for the rider.
A small open vessel propelled by oars, engine, or sail.
A large passenger road vehicle running on a fixed route.
A motor vehicle furnished with beds and other domestic equipment.
A trailer that is used as a dwelling, has no permanent foundation, and is designed to be easily moved.
A two-wheeled motor-driven road vehicle without pedal propulsion.
A large seagoing vessel propelled by sail or engine.

definicion: Half the length of a segment on the vertical axis (perpendicular to the horizontal plane of WGS-84 ellipsoid), which represents the maximum acceptable magnitude of error introduced by the navigation system, and yet still be usable for precision approach operations.
descripcion: The value ranges between 0.0 and 50.8 metres, inclusive, in steps of 0.2 metre.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value that is restricted to be non-negative.
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The reference water level from which the safe vertical clearance is measured, if the clearance is measured from a body of water.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vertical clearance reference.

dominio.definicion: The average height of all high waters at a location over a 19-year period.
The average height of the high waters of spring tides.
The average height of higher high waters at a location over a 19-year period.
The average height of the sea at a tide station measured from a fixed predetermined reference level.
The average height of higher high water at spring tides at a location.
The highest water level observed at a location.
A tidal surface datum approximating the level of the mean of the higher high water at spring tides.

definicion: Information pertaining to ensuring safe vertical clearance for vessels passing under potential overhead obstacles (for example: a bridge).
descripcion: For example, may state the local sounding datum or reference water level from which overhead clearance is specified on charts.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is 132 characters in maximum length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The vertical clearance of an object in closed condition (for example: a closed lifting bridge) measured from the horizontal plane towards the object overhead.

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The vertical clearance of an object in opened condition (for example: an open lifting bridge) measured from the horizontal plane towards the object overhead.

datatype.definicion: A real-interval domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: The safe vertical clearance of an object measured from the horizontal plane toward the object overhead.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "length", defined as the length of the path travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.

definicion: A reference surface with respect to which elevations and/or depths are specified.
descripcion: The values of elevation (or sometimes equivalently, height) and depth are determined along the direction of the reference surface normal.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vertical datum.

dominio.definicion: The oblate ellipsoidal figure of the Earth defined by the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984.
The geopotential surface defined by the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 EGM96 Earth Gravity Model that is closely associated with the mean ocean surface.
A continuous surface over the oceans (or its hypothetical extension under the land masses) defined by the mean of sea level surfaces approximated and observed over 19 years.
A fixed reference for elevations derived from a general adjustment of the first-order terrestrial levelling nets of the United States, Canada, and Mexico.
dominio.observaciones: In the adjustment, only the height of the primary tidal bench mark, referenced to the International Great Lakes Datum of 1985 local mean sea level height value, at Pointe-au-Pere, Quebec, on the Gulf of St. Lawrence was held fixed, thus providing minimum constraint.

dominio.definicion: A fixed reference for elevations derived from a general adjustment in 1929 of the first-order leveling nets of both the United States and Canada.
dominio.observaciones: In the adjustment, mean sea level was held fixed as observed at 21 tide stations in the United States and 5 in Canada.

dominio.definicion: A continuous surface over dry land and non-tidal waters (for example: lakes).
dominio.observaciones: In the case of non-tidal waters it is necessary to specify hydrologic conditions in order to ensure a precise reference surface specification. Over extensive areas it is often defined by a digital elevation model (for example: a matrix of elevation values or a Triangulated Irregular Network (TIN)). Over tidal waters (for example: oceans) it is usually considered to be extended to cover the remainder of the world based on a Mean Sea Level (MSL) surface.

dominio.definicion: The geopotential surface defined by the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 EGM08 Earth Gravity Model that is closely associated with the mean ocean surface.

definicion: The set of reference points or a mathematical model of the Earth's surface (a datum) against which vertical position measurements are made as basis for measuring elevations.
descripcion: For example, 'AMSTERDAM GAUGE', 'NEWLYN', 'WGS84', 'MSL', 'AGL', etc. A datum is a mathematical model (for example: ellipsoid) or reference point, of the earth from a geometric, geodetic, and gravitational point of view built on the scientific and technological knowledge available at the moment.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that contains only non-lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The reference system for determining a vertical distance.
descripcion: Two series of values exist: 1. real distance from either GND, MSL, or the WGS-84 ellipsoid; 2. pressure distance.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vertical distance reference.

dominio.definicion: The vertical distance measured relative to the ground.
The vertical distance measured relative to mean sea level.
dominio.observaciones: Also known as altitude.

dominio.definicion: The vertical distance measured relative to the WGS-84 Ellipsoid.
The vertical distance measured relative to mean sea level using standard atmospheric pressure.
dominio.observaciones: The altimeter setting is set to standard atmosphere.

definicion: The altitude, height or flight level of the bottom of the airspace, air route, or holding pattern.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of length equal to 0.3048 metres.

definicion: A unique identification code that identifies a feature that is a vertical obstruction to low-level flight.
descripcion: Although parts of the identifier include digits it can also consist of non-numeric characters.

datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a vertical obstruction identifier.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: An eleven character code consisting of four blocks of information as follows: Positions 1-2, the FIPS 10-4 two-character Country Code; Positions 3-6, a World Aeronautical Chart (WAC) Identifier; Positions 7-10, a Unique Obstruction Identification consisting of a four-digit (0001-9999) number; Position 11, an alphanumeric Producer Code.

definicion: The numerical value of an altitude that may be assigned by Air Traffic Control (ATC) when different from the relevant published value.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of length equal to 0.3048 metres.

definicion: The relationship between the feature and the underlying ground (terrain) or waterbody bottom.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vertical relative location.

dominio.definicion: Located on the waterbody bottom.
Buried below the waterbody bottom.
Buried below the ground (terrain) surface.
Located on the ground (terrain) or the surface of the waterbody.
Located above the ground (terrain) or the surface of the waterbody.
Located above the waterbody bottom but below the waterbody surface.
Located at all times below the waterbody surface and may be located above, on, or below the waterbody bottom.

definicion: The type of dataset and associated process that was used to define the digital representation of the vertical coordinate values of the feature or data set.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vertical source category.

dominio.definicion: Determined by interpolation of DTED Level 1 (3 arc second) data.
Determined by interpolation of DTED Level 2 (1 arc second) data.
No elevation values are present; the data set is two-dimensional.
Determined from analysis of reflective surface data (for example: first return LiDAR or IFSAR).
Determined by analysis of stereoscopic imagery.
Determined by interpolation of Triangulated Irregular Network (TIN) data.
Determined by interpolation of SRTM Level 1 (3 arc second) data.
dominio.observaciones: The initial release of Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) data included data void areas that have subsequently been in-filled by a variety of techniques to result in a seamless model. The quality of the resulting elevation surface will vary in these void-areas from their surrounding regions.

dominio.definicion: Determined by interpolation of SRTM Level 2 (1 arc second) data.
dominio.observaciones: The initial release of Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) data included data void areas that have subsequently been in-filled by a variety of techniques to result in a seamless model. The quality of the resulting elevation surface will vary in these void-areas from their surrounding regions.

definicion: The altitude, height or flight level of the top of the airspace, air route, or holding pattern.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of a linear extent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A conventional unit of measurement of length equal to 0.3048 metres.

definicion: The method by which a vessel was boarded.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vessel boarding method.

dominio.definicion: Walked up the gangway.
Used a grappling-hook, an iron-clawed instrument intended to be thrown with a rope attached in order to get a firm hold on an object (for example: a wall or an enemy ship vessel).
Jumped aboard from an adjacent object (for example: a pier or another vessel) without use of other equipment.
Climbed a tow-line.

definicion: The part of a vessel at which boarding was accomplished.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vessel boarding point.

dominio.definicion: At or near or toward the center of a vessel.
A narrow walkway extending outward from both sides of a pilothouse to the full width of a vessel.
dominio.observaciones: Officers use bridge wings when docking or maneuvering in locks and narrow waterways.

dominio.definicion: The room containing the vessel's engines.
An overhang consisting of the fan-shaped part of the deck extending aft of the sternpost of a vessel.
That part of the vessel built around the sternpost, from the counter up to the taffrail.

definicion: An indication that a vessel draft correction has been applied.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of a vessel or vessel-like object based on size, shape, design, function and/or condition.
descripcion: May be used to characterize vessels that are functional, disused, hulks, or wrecked (reference STANAG 3715), as well as objects that may appear similar to a vessel from a distance.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a vessel type.

dominio.definicion: A wreck-like anomaly is present on the sea floor, however the specific wreck type has not been determined.
A machine that can be flown in the air (for example: an aeroplane or helicopter).
A vessel functioning in a subsidiary and/or supplementary capacity.
dominio.observaciones: In naval terms, not a fighting ship.

dominio.definicion: A warship of the most heavily armed and armoured class, of sufficient size to take part in a main attack.
dominio.observaciones: Generally having at least 10 inches of armour and carrying a main battery of 12 inch guns or larger.

dominio.definicion: A usually flat bottomed boat, used principally in harbours and inland waterways though is often seagoing, for the transport of goods or sometimes passengers and usually propelled by towing.
A floating object moored to the bottom in a particular (charted) place, as an navigation or for other specific purposes.
A large watertight chamber open at the bottom, from which the water is kept out by air pressure, used in laying foundations under water.
A warship designed to serve as a base for aircraft.
The goods (load) previously carried by a vessel.
A vessel used for the detection and pursuit of submarines.
A vessel employed in sailing along a coast, trading from port to port, especially of the same country.
A high-speed warship less heavily armed than a battleship.
Ship debris (for example: plates, miscellaneous metal) are present however the specific wreck type has not been determined.
A vessel or floating structure equipped with machinery for excavating ditches or canals, deepening channels and harbours, and removing solid matter from the bottom of a water area.
A floating offshore vessel or platform supporting the complete apparatus and structure required for drilling an oil or gas well.
Any chemical compound, mixture, and/or device the primary or common purpose of which is to function by explosion, that is with substantially instantaneous release of gas and/or heat.
dominio.observaciones: Usually of military origin, either lost at sea or intentionally dumped.

dominio.definicion: A vessel engaged in harvesting fish or other products from the sea for commercial gain.
An artificial reef constructed by dumping assorted junk in an area which may be of very small extent or may stretch a considerable distance along a depth contour.
dominio.observaciones: Often established by private interests, usually sport fishermen, to simulate natural reefs and wrecks that attract fish.

dominio.definicion: A vessel for transporting passengers, vehicles, and/or goods across a stretch of water, especially as a regular service.
A general-purpose warship with mixed armament, usually lighter than, or, in the US and some other navies, heavier than a destroyer.
dominio.observaciones: Generally between a corvette and a destroyer in size and designed for convoy escort work.

dominio.definicion: A small vessel of shallow draught (fitted for) carrying relatively heavy guns.
A ship fitted out exclusively for the treatment and transport of the sick and wounded.
A flat-bottomed type of sailing vessel used in the China seas, with a square prow, prominent stem, full stern, suspended rudder, and lugsails.
A cargo carrying system using specially built ships and lighters.
dominio.observaciones: Cargoes are loaded into LASH lighters which are towed to a LASH ship where they are embarked. At their destination the LASH lighters are disembarked and towed away to their unloading berths. Special berths or anchorages are sometimes designated for LASH ships.

dominio.definicion: Any of several types of naval assault landing craft especially designed for putting troops and equipment directly ashore.
A ship designed for transporting liquefied petroleum gas (primarily propane).
A naval vessel intended to ferry infantry that could not beach directly, but instead carries a number of smaller assault landing craft that can ferry infantry to a beach.
dominio.observaciones: During World War II, often converted cross channel ferries and other similar ships of the same size.

dominio.definicion: The largest naval vessels designed to put their bows directly onto a beach, open their bow doors and lower a ramp supporting vehicle entry and/or exit.
dominio.observaciones: Typically about 5000 tons and capable of landing a squadron of tanks or a large number of other vehicles.

dominio.definicion: A distinctively marked vessel anchored or moored at a charted point, to serve as an aid to navigation.
A ship equipped to lay or clear away floating and submarine mines.
A type of small auxiliary ship built for the US Navy during World War II, built to lay and maintain steel anti-torpedo or anti-submarine nets.
A vessel designed to carry (large) quantities of cargo, such as grain, that is not in the form of separate packages.
Any obstruction that hinders or prevents maritime movement, particularly anything that endangers or prevents passage of a vessel.
dominio.observaciones: Usually an isolated danger to navigation such as a sunken rock or pinnacle.

dominio.definicion: A cargo vessel having accommodations for limited numbers of passengers.
dominio.observaciones: For example, ubiquitous twelve-passenger freighters once common on the seas in which the transport of passengers is secondary to the carriage of freight.

dominio.definicion: A vessel which moves systematically around an area for the purposes of watching, repressing, protecting, and/or inspecting.
Any high tower or spire-shaped pillar of rock or coral, alone or cresting a summit.
dominio.observaciones: It may or may not be a hazard to surface navigation.

dominio.definicion: A ship (especially a passenger ferry) onto which vehicles are driven directly at the start of the voyage and off at the end.
A vessel propelled by means of a sail or sails extended on rigging to catch the wind.
A lighter comprising part of cargo carrying system using specially built ships.
dominio.observaciones: Cargoes are loaded into LASH lighters which are towed to a LASH ship where they are embarked. At their destination the LASH lighters are disembarked and towed away to their unloading berths. Special berths or anchorages are sometimes designated for LASH ships.

dominio.definicion: A vessel, especially a warship, capable of operating under water and usually equipped with torpedoes, missiles, and a periscope.
A ship or vessel specially equipped for carrying out hydrographic and/or oceanographic surveys.
A ship fitted with tanks for transporting oil or other fluids in bulk.
An obsolete vessel providing a mark to shot at for practice.
A small, fast and lightly armed warship for carrying or discharging torpedoes.
A ship used to carry soldiers and/or supplies.
A small stoutly built powerful boat used to tow larger vessels.
A vessel that fishes by dragging an open-mouthed bag-net along the sea-bed.
A container ship capable of transporting over 7,000 Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit (TEU).
dominio.observaciones: The TEU number is the number of standard 20-foot containers measuring 20 x 8.0 x 8.5 feet (6.1 x 2.4 x 2.6 metres) that a vessel can carry.

dominio.definicion: A light sailing vessel, especially equipped for racing or a larger, usually power driven vessel equipped for cruising.
A vessel driven by water in the form of gas or vapour.
A craft or structure for transport by water, driven by an engine.
A craft or structure for transport by water, driven by two engines.
A vessel using a form of electric drive in which turbine-driven generators supply electric power to motors coupled to the propeller.
A vessel driven by a rotary motor in which a wheel or drum with curved vanes is driven by expanding hot air admitted to it and allowed to escape.
A vessel operated by a merchant marine organisation, engaged in the transport of goods for payment.
A vessel used by a countries armed forces, sometimes engaged in the pursuit of warfare.
A vessel that operates close to the shore.
A type of merchant vessel built in the US by rapid mass-production methods during the war of 1939-45.
A ship engaged in trade with the Indian subcontinent.
A single-masted fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel, usually employed for coasting or fishing.
A small powerful boat for towing larger boats and ships that can operate in ocean conditions.
A vessel carrying provisions and/or equipment.
A boat, usually flat-bottomed, for transferring goods from a ship to a wharf or another ship.
A ship or boat used to attend a larger one, especially to supply goods and provisions, convey orders, and/or carry passengers to and from shore.
A fishing vessel that drags its trawl from the rear of the vessel.
A barge upon which is mounted a mechanism for hoisting materials by a boom hung from a central post.
A machine for moving heavy objects, usually by suspending them from a projecting arm or beam, mounted on a floating platform.
A vessel that carries coal.
A small one-masted fore-and-aft rigged vessel with mainsail and jib.
A two-masted sailing ship with a square-rigged foremast and a fore-and-aft-rigged mainmast.
A two-masted, fore-and-aft rigged sailing vessel in which the mizzen-mast is shorter than the mainmast and stepped forward of the rudder post.
dominio.observaciones: Formerly used especially for coastal trading.

dominio.definicion: A light pilot or patrol vessel.
dominio.observaciones: Also used to describe a sailing-yacht with one mainsail and two foresails; originally a small fore-and-aft rigged boat with one mast, more than one head-sail, and a running bowsprit, formerly used especially as a fast auxiliary.

dominio.definicion: A small seagoing fore-and-aft rigged vessel, originally with two masts, later often with three or four, the foremast being equal to or smaller than the other masts.
A small square sterned ocean-going sailing vessel without head rails.
dominio.observaciones: Specifically, such a ship with the aftermost mast fore-and-aft rigged and the other masts square-rigged.

dominio.definicion: A vessel carrying letters and parcels.
A vehicle or craft supported by a cushion of air ejected downwards against the surface (of land or sea).
A vessel with no means of self-propulsion on which vehicles are driven directly on at the start of the voyage and off at the end of it.
A power-driven vessel equipped with a cabin and living accommodation.
A boat with two hulls side by side.
A small motor boat carried on a cruising yacht.
dominio.observaciones: Also, a similar boat, usually partly open, used as a pleasure-boat.

dominio.definicion: A boat used for pleasure or amusement.
A high-speed motor boat.
A small open boat, propelled by oars, sails or an outboard motor.
A ship's small boat for use in emergency.
A vessel used for the purpose of saving people from danger.
A boat used by a pilot to meet an incoming ship.
Generally, a vessel used to convey passengers to another vessel for embarkation.
dominio.observaciones: Specifically, used by a military force to enter a ship for the purposes of providing information or inspection of the ship, its crew or contents.

dominio.definicion: A ship specially built or adapted for breaking a channel through ice.
A vessel used in the business of raising sunken or wrecked ships or their contents.
A vessel engaged in visiting undiscovered or uninvestigated territory, especially to get scientific information.
A vessel engaged in the business of conducting investigation into the sea and its environs to increase the sum of knowledge.
An unrigged hull of a wrecked or condemned ship.
A vessel from long ago used by an armed force.
An aircraft deriving both lift and propulsive power from horizontally revolving, usually engine-driven, blades or rotors and capable of ascending and descending vertically.
A vessel used by a military or naval force to guard a coastline and specified area of water and to police the regulations, safety, order and effective operation of marine traffic in its jurisdiction.
Any of a class of battleships (originally superior to all their predecessors) whose main armament was entirely big guns of the same calibre.
A heavy-gunned warship of higher speed and lighter armour than a battleship.
A high-speed warship less heavily armed than a battleship.
A large naval cruiser whose principal armament usually consists of 8 guns.
A large naval cruiser whose principal armament usually consists of 6 guns.
A vessel from long ago used by an armed force.
A small vessel used for military purposes.
A vessel carrying weapons.
A vessel accompanying another vessel for security or protection.
A ship moored or grounded in order to block a channel.
A floating breakwater used to create a man-made harbour.
A floating platform, for the landing of passengers and goods.
A concrete caisson used to create a man-made harbour.
A man-made obstacle that bars advance or access to submarines.
A type of cargo ship produced in large numbers by American shipyards during World War II to replace losses caused by German submarines.
A sailing boat with three hulls.
A fishing vessel equipped with a trawl net with its mouth held apart by a beam.
In general, a vessel engaged in the transport of goods or passengers for payment.
dominio.observaciones: Specifically, a boat that takes the catch from a fishing fleet to market.

dominio.definicion: A vessel designed to carry goods stored in (large) containers.
An escort vessel smaller than a frigate used especially for protecting convoys against submarines in the war of 1939-45.
A fast warship of a type designed to protect other ships (for example: by attacking submarines) with guns and torpedoes.
A vessel (for example: a fishing vessel) used by the UK Royal Navy, especially in wartime, for patrolling, conveying stores, and other duties.
dominio.observaciones: Generally, a vessel engaged in fishing with a drift-net.

dominio.definicion: A fishing ship with facilities for immediate processing of the catch.
A ship for transporting freight.
A boat equipped with a device consisting of planes for lifting its hull out of the water to increase its speed.
A ship belonging to a line of passenger ships.
A ship or aircraft equipped to lay explosive mines.
A ship for clearing away floating and submarine mines.
A vessel propelled through the use of wheels having paddle-boards fitted radially which press backwards against the water.
A boat designed for use on rivers.

dominio.definicion: An armoured surface vessel that is no larger than a destroyer.
dominio.observaciones: A destroyer is a fast warship of a type designed to protect other ships (for example: by attacking submarines) with guns and torpedoes.

dominio.definicion: Any of a class of naval ships designed specifically to conduct Amphibious Warfare by the landing of infantry troops on a beachhead.
A permanently moored floating structure (for example: an old ship) that is used for accommodation.

dominio.definicion: A vessel designed and used to lay underwater cables for telecommunications or electrical power.
A specialized ship with a crane for lifting heavy loads.
A specialized watercraft with pumps and nozzles designed for fighting shoreline and shipboard fires.
A specialized vessel designed and utilized primarily for launching, operating, supporting, and landing helicopters.
A boat or a boat-like building fitted for residential use, for anchorage, and/or for leisurely cruising.
A ship used to train or support the training of students in a maritime profession.
dominio.observaciones: Two types of vessels are generally recognized as Training Ships:  those used for training at sea and hulks used to house classrooms.

dominio.definicion: Any vehicle operating on the surface of the water that does not require on-board presence of human operators.

dominio.definicion: A boat engaged in harvesting fish or other products from the sea for commercial gain.

dominio.definicion: A 'T'-shaped VASIS consisting of light units arranged on one side of the runway in the form of two wing bars with a bisecting longitudinal line of lights.

definicion: The relative size of an explosive eruption, based on ejecta volume, rate, height, duration and related factors.
descripcion: The volcanic explosivity index correlates with the magnitude and/or intensity and/or destructiveness and/or (less frequently) dispersive power, violence, and energy release rate of the volcanic eruption. The VEI scale ranges from 0 to 8, where 0 denotes an eruption with a minimum of plume formation.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain category denoting a volcanic explosivity index.

dominio.definicion: A non-explosive eruption whose plume is less than 100 metres in height and whose ejecta volume is less than 10,000 cubic metres.
dominio.observaciones: It is of the Hawaiian-type and this type of eruption typically occurs daily around the world. Hawaiian-type eruptions may occur along fissures or fractures that serve as linear vents, such as during the eruption of Mauna Loa Volcano in Hawaii in 1950, or they may occur at a central vent such as during the 1959 eruption in Kilauea Iki Crater of Kilauea Volcano, Hawaii. In fissure-type eruptions, molten, incandescent lava spurts from a fissure on the volcano's rift zone and feeds lava streams that flow downslope. In central-vent eruptions, a fountain of fiery lava spurts to a height of several hundred feet or more. Such lava may collect in old pit craters to form lava lakes, or form cones, or feed radiating flows.

dominio.definicion: A gentle, effusive eruption whose plume rises 100 to 1000 metres and whose ejecta volume exceeds 10,000 cubic metres.
dominio.observaciones: It may be either of the Hawaiian- or Strombolian-type and this type of eruption typically occurs daily around the world. Hawaiian-type eruptions may occur along fissures or fractures that serve as linear vents, such as during the eruption of Mauna Loa Volcano in Hawaii in 1950, or they may occur at a central vent such as during the 1959 eruption in Kilauea Iki Crater of Kilauea Volcano, Hawaii. In fissure-type eruptions, molten, incandescent lava spurts from a fissure on the volcano's rift zone and feeds lava streams that flow downslope. In central-vent eruptions, a fountain of fiery lava spurts to a height of several hundred feet or more. Such lava may collect in old pit craters to form lava lakes, or form cones, or feed radiating flows. In Strombolian-type eruptions (for example: observed during the 1965 activity of Irazu Volcano in Costa Rica) huge clots of molten lava burst from the summit crater to form luminous arcs through the sky. Collecting on the flanks of the cone, lava clots combine to stream down the slopes in fiery rivulets.

dominio.definicion: An explosive eruption whose plume rises 1 to 5 kilometres and whose ejecta volume exceeds 1,000,000 cubic metres.
dominio.observaciones: It may be either of the Strombolian- or Vulcanian-type and this type of eruption typically occurs weekly around the world; the Galeras volcano (Columbia) is a typical example. In Strombolian-type eruptions (for example: observed during the 1965 activity of Irazu Volcano in Costa Rica) huge clots of molten lava burst from the summit crater to form luminous arcs through the sky. Collecting on the flanks of the cone, lava clots combine to stream down the slopes in fiery rivulets. In Vulcanian-type eruptions (for example: observed during the 1947 activity of Paricutin Volcano in Mexico), a dense cloud of ash-laden gas explodes from the crater and rises high above the peak. Steaming ash forms a whitish cloud near the upper level of the cone.

dominio.definicion: A severe, explosive eruption whose plume rises 3 to 15 kilometres and whose ejecta volume exceeds 10,000,000 cubic metres.
dominio.observaciones: It may be either of the Vulcanian- or Pelean-type and this type of eruption typically occurs yearly around the world. In Vulcanian-type eruptions (for example: observed during the 1947 activity of Paricutin Volcano in Mexico), a dense cloud of ash-laden gas explodes from the crater and rises high above the peak. Steaming ash forms a whitish cloud near the upper level of the cone. In Pelean-type eruptions (for example: the 1968 activity of Mayan Volcano in the Philippines), a large quantity of gas, dust, ash, and incandescent lava fragments are blown out of a central crater, fall back, and form tongue-like, glowing avalanches that move down-slope at velocities as great as 100 miles per hour. Such eruptive activity can cause great destruction and loss of life if it occurs in populated areas, as demonstrated by the devastation of St. Pierre during the 1902 eruption of Mount Pelee on Martinique, West Indies.

dominio.definicion: A cataclysmic eruption whose plume rises 10 to 25 kilometres and whose ejecta volume exceeds 0.1 cubic kilometres.
dominio.observaciones: It may be either of the Pelean- or Plinian-type and this type of eruption typically occurs every ten or more years around the world. In Pelean-type eruptions (for example: the 1968 activity of Mayan Volcano in the Philippines), a large quantity of gas, dust, ash, and incandescent lava fragments are blown out of a central crater, fall back, and form tongue-like, glowing avalanches that move down-slope at velocities as great as 100 miles per hour. Such eruptive activity can cause great destruction and loss of life if it occurs in populated areas, as demonstrated by the devastation of St. Pierre during the 1902 eruption of Mount Pelee on Martinique, West Indies. In Plinian-type eruptions (also known as 'Vesuvian eruptions', being marked by their similarity to the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 as described in a letter written by Pliny the Younger), columns of gas and volcanic ash extend high into the stratosphere. The key characteristics are ejection of large amount of pumice and very powerful continuous gas blast eruptions.

dominio.definicion: A paroxysmal eruption whose plume rises more than 25 kilometres and whose ejecta volume exceeds 1 cubic kilometre.
dominio.observaciones: It is of the Plinian-type and this type of eruption typically occurs every fifty or more years around the world. In Plinian-type eruptions (also known as 'Vesuvian eruptions', being marked by their similarity to the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 as described in a letter written by Pliny the Younger), columns of gas and volcanic ash extend high into the stratosphere. The key characteristics are ejection of large amount of pumice and very powerful continuous gas blast eruptions. The eruption in 1963 of the Agung volcano in Bali was of this type.

dominio.definicion: A colossal eruption whose plume rises more than 25 kilometres and whose ejecta volume exceeds 10 cubic kilometres.
dominio.observaciones: It is of the Plinian-type and this type of eruption typically occurs every hundred or more years around the world. In Plinian-type eruptions (also known as 'Vesuvian eruptions', being marked by their similarity to the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 as described in a letter written by Pliny the Younger), columns of gas and volcanic ash extend high into the stratosphere. The key characteristics are ejection of large amount of pumice and very powerful continuous gas blast eruptions. The eruption in 1783 of the Laki volcano in Iceland was of this type.

dominio.definicion: A colossal eruption whose plume rises more than 25 kilometres and whose ejecta volume exceeds 100 cubic kilometres.
dominio.observaciones: It is of the Plinian-type and this type of eruption typically occurs every thousand or more years around the world. In Plinian-type eruptions (also known as 'Vesuvian eruptions', being marked by their similarity to the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 as described in a letter written by Pliny the Younger), columns of gas and volcanic ash extend high into the stratosphere. The key characteristics are ejection of large amount of pumice and very powerful continuous gas blast eruptions. The eruption in 1815 of the Tambora volcano in Indonesia was of this type.

dominio.definicion: A colossal eruption whose plume rises more than 25 kilometres and whose ejecta volume exceeds 1,000 cubic kilometres.
dominio.observaciones: It is of the Plinian-type and this type of eruption typically occurs every ten thousand or more years around the world. In Plinian-type eruptions (also known as 'Vesuvian eruptions', being marked by their similarity to the eruption of Mount Vesuvius in AD 79 as described in a letter written by Pliny the Younger), columns of gas and volcanic ash extend high into the stratosphere. The key characteristics are ejection of large amount of pumice and very powerful continuous gas blast eruptions. The eruption 26,500 years ago (the Oruanui eruption) of the Taupo volcano in New Zealand was of this type.

definicion: The type of lava based on its characteristics.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a volcanic lava composition.

dominio.definicion: Lava that form lava spines, lava domes or 'coulees' (which are thick, short lavas) and are associated with pyroclastic (fragmental) deposits.
dominio.observaciones: Most felsic lava flows are extremely viscous, and typically fragment as they extrude, producing blocky autobreccias. Unusually hot (exceeding 950 degrees Celsius) rhyolite lavas, however, may flow for distances of many tens of kilometres, such as in the Snake River Plain of the northwestern United States.

dominio.definicion: Lava that is lower in aluminum and silica, and usually somewhat richer in magnesium and iron. Intermediate lavas form andesite domes and block lavas, and may occur on steep composite volcanoes, such as in the Andes.
dominio.observaciones: Poorer in aluminium and silica than felsic lavas, and also commonly hotter (in the range of 750 to 950 degrees Celsius), they tend to be less viscous.

dominio.definicion: Lava that is high in iron and magnesium, and has relatively lower aluminum and silica, which taken together reduces the degree of polymerization within the melt.
dominio.observaciones: Owing to the higher temperatures, viscosities can be relatively low, although still thousands of times more viscous than water.

dominio.definicion: Lavas such as komatiite and highly magnesian magmas which form boninite take the composition and temperatures of eruptions to the extreme.
dominio.observaciones: Komatiites contain over 18 percent magnesium oxide, and are thought to have erupted at temperatures of 1600 degrees Celsius. At this temperature there is no polymerization of the mineral compounds, creating a highly mobile liquid with viscosity as low as that of water.

definicion: The type of a volcanic phenomenon based on its cause and/or form.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a volcanic phenomena type.

dominio.definicion: Large, circular, basin-shaped volcanic depression created by destruction of the upper part of the volcanic cone by an great eruption. Diameter > 1000 m.
A small vent in a volcanic area that discharges vapor (greater than 130 degrees Centigrade) that turn into steam.
A type of hot spring that intermittently eject jets of hot water and steam issuing from the earth, usally as a result of vulcanic activity.
An accumulation of pyroclastic material (ash, lapilli, rock fragments) around a volcanic vent that is generated when ascending magma react with ground-water.
dominio.observaciones: Hydroclastic volcanoes are tuff ring and cones and maar.

dominio.definicion: Mud-flow composed mainly of volcanic ash lubricated by water causing the volcanic ash to flow under gravitational movement:.
The molten material extruded from a volcano or by a fissure eruption on the surface of the earth where it cools and solidifies.
The exhalation of cabron dioxide gas in an area of late-stage volcanic activity; also, the small opening from which the gas is emitted.
Volcanic exhalation of sulphurous gases within a caldera (100 - 250 degrees Centigrade).
A spring whose water temperature is appreciably higher than the local mean annual atmospheric temperature.
An eruption that takes place from an elongated fissure, rather from a central vent.
Exhalation of gas associated to vocanic activity.
dominio.observaciones: The most important volcanic gases are H2O, CO2, SO2, H2, H2S and CO.

dominio.definicion: A conical hill formed by the accumulation of cinders and other pyroclasts, normally of basaltic or andesitic composition.
Mound of volcanic rock that forms as a (viscous) lava flows onto the surface and amasses over a vent.
An accumulation of pyroclastic material (ash, lapilli, rock fragments) around a volcanic vent that is generated when ascending magma react with ground-water.
dominio.observaciones: Tuff cones are characterized by higher profiles than tuff rings and maars.

definicion: The classification by shape of a volcano.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a volcano shape.

dominio.definicion: Cone-shaped mountain or peak composed of layers of lava.
Cone formed round the mouth of a volcano by debris cast up during eruption.
Broad, gently sloping, and resembling a flattened dome or shield, generally formed by overlapping and interfingering basaltic lava flows.
Crater of great size whose breadth greatly exceeds that of the vent(s) within it.
Large, conical, and composed of alternating layers of lava and pyroclastic materials.

dominio.definicion: A wall consisting of a closely planted line of bushes or small trees, forming a boundary.

dominio.definicion: One of the pair of walls, usually masonry, that contain a lock basin and support the lock gates.

dominio.definicion: An opening gate used to control flood water.
dominio.observaciones: Usually extends across a channel and when required, is closed to control flood waters from the sea.

dominio.definicion: A steel structure used for closing the entrance of locks and wet or dry docks.
The massive hinged doors at each end of a lock.
An opening gate in a dyke.
A gate used only in a state of emergency (for example: to control or cause flooding).
A sliding gate or other contrivance for changing the level of a body of water by controlling the flow into or out of it.

definicion: The 'hardness' of a sample of water as determined by the combined mass of calcium carbonate and magnesium carbonate per volume of solution.
descripcion: Calcium and magnesium enter water mainly through the weathering of rocks. 'Hard' water has a high mineral content (in contrast with 'soft' water).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a water level effect.

dominio.definicion: Partially covered and partially dry at high water.
Not covered at high water under average meteorological conditions.
dominio.aliases: Does Not Cover, Above Water Surface

dominio.definicion: Remains covered by water at all times under average meteorological conditions.
An area projecting from the bottom of a body of water (for example: a reef) that periodically extends above and is submerged below the surface.
Flush with, or washed by the waves at low water under average meteorological conditions.
An area periodically covered by flood water, excluding tidal waters.
Resting or moving on the waterbody surface without sinking.
Flush with, or washed by the waves at chart datum under average meteorological conditions.

definicion: The potability of water based on the type of treatment required before it is safe for human consumption.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a water potability.

dominio.definicion: Suitable for consumption by humans.
Capable of being relatively easily treated to become potable.
dominio.observaciones: For example, treatable using simple filtration and/or disinfection.

dominio.definicion: Incapable of being easily treated to become potable.
dominio.observaciones: For example, requiring distillation or reverse osmosis treatment.

dominio.definicion: Unsuitable for, or not intended for, consumption by humans.

definicion: The class of a protected water gathering ground or reservoir.
descripcion: The protected (restricted use) terrain incorporates facilities for the collection of water and is so designated in order to protect the water on and beneath the terrain from being contaminated.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a water protection class.

dominio.definicion: For groundwater this is the area closest to the capture location (for example: source or well); any landuse is forbidden in this area. For reservoirs this is the area of the waterbody plus the shore area.

For groundwater this is the area within which water can reach (flow to) the capture location (for example: source or well) within 50 days. For reservoirs this area restricts any harmful actions in the area around the waterbody.

For groundwater this is the area within which water can reach (flow to) the capture location (for example: source or well) in total. For reservoirs this area restricts actions of chemical or nuclear actions.
If the Protection Area Class III is larger than 2 kilometres then the Zone III A is not bigger than 1 kilometre and consists only of Zones I and II.
If the Protection Area Class III is larger than 2 kilometres then the Zone III B consists of Zone III without Zones III A, II and I.

definicion: The type of a water race based on its structure and/or intended purpose.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a water race type.

dominio.definicion: An open artificial watercourse or passageway for water, having a gate or valve to regulate its flow.
dominio.observaciones: May be employed in mine ore washing operations or for irrigation. Sluices are usually located on the ground.

dominio.definicion: An open artificial watercourse normally inclined and having no gate, which conveys water for the purposes of material transport including water, hydraulic mining operations, or the study of water and sediment movement.
dominio.observaciones: Flumes are used in hydraulic or placer mining and in the logging industry. Unlike a sluice, a flume will not be controlled by a gate. A flume may be either on the ground or elevated above the ground surface.

dominio.definicion: An artificial channel that feeds water to a point of industrial application (for example: a millwheel or turbine) before use.
An artificial channel for conveying water away from a point of industrial application (for example: a millwheel or turbine) after use.

definicion: The reason for the importance of an area to the supply of drinking water.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a water supply importance.

dominio.definicion: It includes facilities of the public utilities for the provision and/or maintenance of the water supply.
A region where a water providing facility collects its resource (water).
Regeneration of the groundwater and increase of its volume in useable aquifers.
An area especially protected by law that provides medicinally useful water.
An area especially protected by law that is important to water collection and a secure water supply.

definicion: The average depth of the zone of soil saturation except where bounded by an impermeable body in which no water table exists.
