definicion: The type of a water disturbance caused by the interaction of any combination of waves, currents, eddies, tidal streams, wind, shoals, and obstructions.
descripcion: May be used as a means of subtyping Feature: 'Water Turbulence'.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a water turbulence type.

dominio.definicion: Waves breaking gradually over a considerable distance.
Waves tending to curl over and break with a crash.
Waves peak up, but then instead of spilling or plunging they surge up on the beach face.
A circular movement of water usually formed, where currents pass obstructions between two adjacent currents flowing counter to each other, or along the edge of a permanent current.
Short, breaking waves occurring when a strong current passes over a shoal or other submarine obstruction or meets a contrary current or wind.
Small waves formed on the surface of water by the meeting of opposing tidal currents.
A turbulent, potentially dangerous rotating movement of water in a waterbody.
dominio.observaciones: The waterbody may be inland (for example: a river) or not (for example: a sea).

dominio.definicion: Waves breaking, usually caused by a shallowing of the water body.
dominio.observaciones: Roughly classified into the three types of: spilling, plunging, and surging. The French word 'brisant' is used for the obstacle causing the breaking of the wave.

dominio.definicion: Wind driven waves from differing directions, resulting in waves that are irregular, unpredictable and that may be difficult to navigate.
dominio.observaciones: Confused sea conditions occur as a result of major shifts in wind direction that occur quickly, generally after major fronts or hurricanes.

definicion: The type of available water based on its composition.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a water type.

dominio.definicion: Water with a pH above 7.0.
Water which has natural mineral salts or gases (carbon dioxide) and contains at least 250 milligrams per litre of dissolved salts and minerals.
Water containing greater than 15,000 to less than or equal 30,000 milligrams per litre of total dissolved solids (TDS).
Containing less than 1,500 milligrams per litre of dissolved salts or minerals.
dominio.observaciones: Chloride is less than or equal to 600 milligrams per litre and sulphates are less than or equal to 300 milligrams per litre.

dominio.definicion: Water containing dissolved salts and minerals greater than or equal to 1,500 to less than or equal to 15,000 milligrams per litre.
dominio.observaciones: Brackish water may result from mixing of seawater with fresh water, as in estuaries, or it may occur naturally, as in brackish fossil aquifers.

dominio.definicion: Water containing greater than 30,000 to less than or equal 40,000 milligrams per litre of total dissolved solids (TDS).
Water containing greater than 40,000 milligrams per litre of total dissolved solids (TDS).
dominio.observaciones: Saltier than full strength seawater.

definicion: The use(s) for which water is withdrawn or consumed from a source.
descripcion: Uses include, for example: domestic purposes, industrial processing, and irrigation.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a water use.

dominio.definicion: Water applied to lands specifically to assist in the growing of crops and pastures.
Water for motels, hotels, restaurants, office buildings, and other commercial facilities.
dominio.observaciones: Excludes specifically industrial purposes.

dominio.definicion: Water used for household gardening and/or watering of grounds plantings (for example: shrubs and lawns).
dominio.observaciones: May also include additional exterior domestic purposes (for example: washing of vehicles).

dominio.definicion: Water used for industrial purposes such as fabrication, processing, washing, and cooling.
dominio.observaciones: For example, used by industries as steel, chemical and allied products, paper and allied products, mining, and petroleum refining.

dominio.definicion: Water use by facilities that meet a social purpose (for example: charity or imprisonment) and/or to serve the general social welfare (for example: health care or education).
Water used for watering livestock, feeding lots, dairy operations, fish farming, and other on-farm agricultural purposes excepting irrigation.
Water used for street cleaning, firefighting and other municipal purposes.
dominio.observaciones: May also include additional domestic or commercial uses.

dominio.definicion: Water used to either directly generate hydroelectric power or for the purpose of cooling at a thermal power station (one that utilizes combustion of hydrocarbons).
Water used to maintain vegetative growth in recreational lands such as parks and golf courses, or in support of other recreational uses (for example: swimming pools).
Water used for household purposes, such as drinking, food preparation, bathing, and washing clothes and dishes.

definicion: A narrative or other textual description of the screening, casing, and/or finishing of a water well.
descripcion: A well screen is system of mesh screening or holes designed to allow water to enter a well or borehole without undue loss of flow while excluding sand, silt, and other geologic material. A well casing is a tubular structure placed in the drilled hole to maintain the physical opening from the underground water source to the surface, and also to insulate the passage of water from either loss or pollution in the intervening strata. The casing extends above the surface and protects against surface contaminants entering the water supply by its height and some form of covering.

The bottom consists of equally distributed solid rock (bedrock) and unconsolidated material.
The bottom consists predominantly of solid rock (bedrock).
The bottom is covered by sand and gravel.
The bottom is equally covered by sandy and silty material.
The bottom covered predominantly by sand and gravel.
The bottom is covered by silt, clay and mud.

The bottom is covered predominantly by silt, clay and mud.

definicion: The shape and/or configuration of a waterbody as a whole or in a localized area.
descripcion: Generally used to describe relatively large bodies of water, for example those that are characterized by tidal conditions, swells, and/or high heavy wave action, whether containing fresh or salt water.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a waterbody morphology.

dominio.definicion: A natural or artificial passage or channel through shoals or steep banks, or across a line of banks lying between two channels.
An elevation over which the depth of water is relatively shallow, but normally sufficient for safe surface navigation.
dominio.observaciones: Typically located on a shelf (continental or insular).

dominio.definicion: An obsolete term which was generally restricted to depths greater than 6,000 metres.
An indentation in the coastline.
A depression in the sea floor of variable extent.
A large flat area of mud or sand attached to the shore and alternately covered and uncovered by the tide.
A long narrow, characteristically very deep and asymmetrical depression of the sea floor, with relatively steep sides, commonly between abyssal hills and continental margins.
dominio.observaciones: Trenches are commonly associated with subduction zones, the trench then paralleling a volcanic arc.

dominio.definicion: A level tract of land, as the bed of a dry lake or an area frequently uncovered at low tide.
A rock lying at or near the sea surface that may constitute a hazard to surface navigation.
A rocky formation continuous with and fringing the shore.
A relatively narrow, deep depression with steep sides, the bottom of which generally has a continuous slope.
dominio.observaciones: Developed characteristically on some continental slopes.

dominio.definicion: A navigable narrow part of a bay, strait, or river.
An offshore hazard to surface navigation that is composed of unconsolidated material.
A relatively small isolated elevation of a rounded shape.
A long, narrow elevation with steep sides often separating ocean basins.
A large isolated elevation, greater than 1000 metres in relief above the sea floor, characteristically of conical form.
Any high tower or spire-shaped pillar or rock or coral, alone or cresting a summit.
dominio.observaciones: It may extend above the surface of the water. If completely submerged it may or may not be a hazard to surface navigation.

dominio.definicion: An extensive, flat, gently sloping or nearly level region at abyssal depths.
A flat or nearly flat area of considerable extent, dropping off abruptly on one or more sides.
A subordinate elevation, ridge or rise projecting outward from a larger feature.
A zone adjacent to a continent (or around an island) and extending from the low water line to a depth at which there is usually a marked increase of slope towards oceanic depths.
A long depression of the sea floor characteristically flat bottomed and steep sided and normally shallower than a trench.
A broad pass, resembling in shape a riding saddle, in a ridge or between contiguous seamounts.
A tract, on occasion extensive, of often low (100-500 metre) elevations on the deep sea floor.
A gently dipping featureless surface, underlain primarily by sediment, at the base of any steeper slope.
A gentle slope with a generally smooth surface on the sea floor, characteristically found around groups of islands or seamounts.
A region adjacent to a continent, normally occupied by or bordering a shelf, that is highly irregular with depths well in excess of those typical of a shelf.
The zone, generally consisting of shelf, slope and rise, separating the continent from the abyssal plain or deep sea floor.
A gentle slope rising from the oceanic depths towards the foot of a continental slope.
An elongated and comparatively steep slope separating or gently sloping areas.
A relatively smooth, fan-like, depositional feature normally sloping away from the outer termination of a canyon or canyon system.
An extensive linear zone of irregular topography of the sea floor, characterized by steep-sided or asymmetrical ridges, troughs or escarpments.
A narrow break in a ridge or a rise.
A seamount having a comparatively smooth flat top.
A small isolated elevation of the sea floor.
A local depression, often steep sided, of the sea floor.
A depositional embankment bordering a canyon, valley or deep-sea channel.
The axial depression of the mid-oceanic ridge system.
An annular depression that may not be continuous, located at the base of many seamounts, islands and other isolated elevations.
A large and complex grouping of ridges and seamounts.
A prominent elevation either pointed or of a very limited extent across the summit.
A region identifiable by a group of similar physiographic features whose characteristics are markedly in contrast with surrounding areas.
A broad elevation that rises gently and generally smoothly from the sea floor.
dominio.observaciones: May occasionally be used to refer to the linked major mid-oceanic mountain systems of global extent.

dominio.definicion: A continuously sloping, elongated narrow depression commonly found in fans or abyssal plains and customarily bordered by levees on one or both sides.
Several seamounts in linear or arcuate alignment.
A narrow zone at the seaward margin of a shelf along which is a marked increase of slope.
A sea floor barrier of relatively shallow depth restricting water movement between basins.
The slope seaward from the shelf edge to the upper edge of a continental rise or the point where there is a general reduction in slope.
A relatively flat horizontal or gently inclined surface, sometimes long and narrow, that is bounded by a steeper ascending slope on one side and by a steeper descending slope on the opposite side.
A relatively shallow, wide depression, the bottom of which usually has a continuous gradient.
dominio.observaciones: This term is generally not used for features that have canyon-like characteristics for a significant portion of their extent.

dominio.definicion: An artificial water course used for navigation.
A large body of water entirely surrounded by land.
A relatively large natural stream of water.
A straight section of a river, especially a navigable river between two bends or an arm of the sea extending into the land.
A bowl-shaped cavity in the seabed, especially one made by the explosion of a mine, shell, or bomb.
A funnel-shaped stream mouth or embayment where fresh water mixes with sea water under tidal influences.
Sea area close to the shore below low tide.
dominio.observaciones: Not to be confused with the term 'nearshore', which begins above the low water mark.

dominio.definicion: A narrow, raised embankment along a beach formed by the deposit of material by waves and marks the limit of high tides.
A break or shear in the earth's crust with an observable displacement between the two sides of the break, and parallel to the end of the break.
Highly reflective patch of seabed found by side scan, no contact found using MM sonar.
An anomaly of the magnetic field of the earth, extending over a relatively small area, due to local magnetic influences.
Undulating surface feature of varying shape produced in unconsolidated sediments by wave or current action.
A trough or corrugation formed in the foreshore or in the bottom, immediately offshore, formed by waves or tidal currents.
A large mobile wave-like sediment feature in shallow water and composed of sand.
An opening or aperture on the floor of the sea.
The natural issue of fresh water from the bottom of the sea at one or more locations.
dominio.observaciones: These fresh water emission(s) may affect buoyancy and/or anchorages within the area.

dominio.definicion: An opening or aperture on the floor of the sea, specifically extruding volcanic material, giving rise to a source of heat.
Small depression on the seabed.
A major spur-like protrusion of the continental slope extending to the deep seafloor.
dominio.observaciones: Characteristically, the crest deepens seaward.

dominio.definicion: A low bulge around the southeastern end of the island of Hawaii.
An area of subdued corrugations off Baja California.
An open body of water forming a slight recession in a coastline.
A small terrace.
An entire mountain system including the subordinate ranges, interior plateaus, and basins.
The deepest part of a stream, bay, lagoon, or strait, through which the main current flows.
A small coastal indentation, smaller than a bay.
A long, narrow, steep-walled, deep-water arm of the sea at high latitudes, usually along mountainous coasts.
A small level or nearly level area.
A branch of a canyon or valley.
A closed, linear, narrow, shallow depression.
A small valley-like feature.
A large recess in the coastline, larger than a bay.
A narrow waterway extending into the land, or connecting a bay or lagoon with a larger body of water.
An isolated, extensive, flat-topped elevation on a shelf, with relatively steep sides.
A low, isolated, rounded hill.
One of the major divisions of the vast expanse of salt water covering part of the Earth.
A flat or gently sloping underwater surface that may extend seaward from the shore, and is often seaward of the shelfbreak.
A flat, gently sloping or nearly level region.
A small canyon.
A gentle slope connecting areas of different elevations.
A series of associated ridges or seamounts.
A long arm of the sea either forming a channel between the mainland and an island or islands, or connecting two larger bodies of water.
A large body of salt water more or less confined by continuous land or chains of islands forming a subdivision of an ocean.
A valley on a shelf, generally the shoreward extension of a canyon.
A relatively narrow waterway, usually narrower and less extensive than a sound, connecting two larger bodies of water.
An elongate (tongue-like) extension of a flat sea floor into an adjacent higher feature.
A collapsed or partially-collapsed seamount, commonly of annular shape.
A regional geologic structure dominated by generally subparallel fault-block mountains separated by broad alluvium-filled basins.
As a feature of a trench, the deeper landward trench wall is found closer to the bottom of the trench running along the landward trench slope.
An area where there exists a change in the geometry of a body of rock due to folding, faulting, shearing, or compression.
An elevated and generally planar region along a shelf surrounding an island.
A delta-shaped sedimentary unit lying on a trench floor on the regional slope adjacent to a continental margin.
A deep valley-like incision into the continental slope, thought to be eroded by turbidity currents.
A shallower descent along a regional slope adjacent to a continental margin, usually associated with a subduction zone.
A relatively elongated and comparatively steep slope separating more gently sloping areas.
A relatively flat shelf adjacent to a continent and similar topographically to, but deeper than, a continental shelf.
A ridge that extends through all of the oceans, with a total length of 80,000 kilometres and an average depth of about 2500 metres.
dominio.observaciones: It occurs in the middle part of the oceans (except in the North Pacific where it is confined to the far eastern region). The mid-ocean ridge essentially represents a broad undersea cordillera or mountain range that rises to its highest elevation at the axis and slopes away on either flank.

dominio.definicion: A planar region within a regional slope along a continental margin or the flanks of a subduction zone.

Abyssal hills that are emphasized by the hilly- and/or seamount-covered deep ocean provinces that are covered only by pelagic deposits and locally derived material eroded from adjacent hills and/or seamounts.
An upper/shallower descending margin from a platform.
A surface characterized by a close succession of parallel or nearly parallel ridges and valleys, and resulting from the differential erosion of highly folded strata of varying resistances.
A complex physiography of generally adjacent and linear ridges and valleys.
dominio.observaciones: The genesis of this morphology is initial expression due to rising magna and the creation of a seafloor spreading zone.

dominio.definicion: A valley that has developed along a rift.
dominio.observaciones: It is 1 to 2 kilometres deep, a few tens of kilometres wide, and lies along the axis of the ridge.

dominio.definicion: A sedimentary basin located along the slope portion of a continental margin.
A type of sediment slide where the downward slipping mass of rock or unconsolidated material of any size moves as a single unit or as several related units.
A floor of a trench as contrasted with the adjacent walls of the trench.
The slope of the overriding plate where two plates collide, one plate bends downward and a trench is formed.

definicion: An indication that an object is an overhead obstruction over a navigable waterbody.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The type of trough-like depression that is normally occupied by a watercourse.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a watercourse channel type.

dominio.definicion: A permanent or relocated watercourse that has been diverted, dredged, straightened and/or dyked.
A watercourse divided into an intricate network of interlacing channels.
dominio.observaciones: Generally shallow, the smaller channels are continually shifting and are separated by bar deposits.

dominio.definicion: A deep, narrow, V-shaped channel with steep rocky sides.
A dry, intermittent, or ephemeral drainage course marked by deposits of alluvial material that are not confined to a specific channel.
dominio.observaciones: The channels are commonly shallow and braided, can cover a wide area being nearly level with the surrounding floodplain, and are separated by flat, low lying segments.

dominio.definicion: A pronounced meander or horseshoe-shaped loop in a watercourse.
A branch of a watercourse that divides from and rejoins the watercourse further along.
A watercourse that has not been channelized or relocated.
dominio.observaciones: Follows a normal meandering channel with variations in channel bed morphology.

dominio.definicion: A surface watercourse that disappears into an underground channel, or dries up in an arid area.

definicion: The type of a watercourse based on its shape and/or configuration.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a watercourse morphology.

dominio.definicion: An area where a watercourse enters a larger body of water (for example: a lagoon, a lake or a bay).
A small, and comparatively still, deep part of a larger body of water (for example: a stream or a harbour), or a small body of standing water.
A point where a watercourse noticeably changes direction.
A place where two or more watercourses join or flow together.
A channel formed as a result of a watercourse cutting through a meander neck.
A straight section of a navigable watercourse or channel between two bends.
A diverging branch flowing out of a main watercourse and rejoining it downstream.
A watercourse that has been substantially ditched, dyked and/or straightened.
A watercourse branch which flows away from the main channel, as in a delta or irrigation canal.
The source and upper part of a watercourse, including the upper drainage basin.
A former watercourse or distributary no longer carrying flowing water, but still evident due to lakes, wetland, topographic and/or vegetation patterns.
A pronounced meander or horseshoe-shaped loop in a watercourse.
A crescent-shaped lake commonly found adjacent to meandering watercourses.
A lake formed by the collection of water in the crater of an inactive volcano.

definicion: The type of the sink of a watercourse.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a watercourse sink type.

dominio.definicion: Gradually dissipates due to a lowering of the water table.
Disappears suddenly into the ground and partially or completely ceases flowing on the surface.
Disappears into a sinkhole (a closed depression caused by a collapse of soil or overlying formation above fractured or cavernous bedrock).
Disappears into holes in the ground other than a sinkhole.

definicion: The classification of an inland waterway based on the length, width, draft, and tonnage of supported ship types and pushed convoys, class I being defined as the lowest level (classes I to IV, according to the European inland waterways classification).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a waterway classification.

dominio.definicion: Penische': A river of regional importance located west of the Elbe River that can used by boats that are a maximum of 38.5 metres in length, 5.05 metres in width and a draught of a maximum of 1.8 to 2.2 metres. The tonnage should be at most between 250 and 400 tonnes.

Kempenaar': A river of regional importance located west of the Elbe River that can used by boats that are a maximum of 50 to 55 metres in length, 6.6 metres in width and a draught of a maximum of 2.5 metres. The tonnage should be at most between 400 and 650 tonnes.

Gustav Koenigs': A river of regional importance located west of the Elbe River that can used by boats that are a maximum of 67 to 80 metres in length, 8.2 metres in width and a draught of a maximum of 2.5 metres. The tonnage should be at most between 650 and 1000 tonnes.

Johann Welker': A river of international importance that can used by boats that are a maximum of 80 to 85 metres in length, 9.5 metres in width and a draught of maximum 2.5 metres. The tonnage should be at most between 1000 and 1500 tonnes. It is usable for pushboats with one push-lighter with a total length of a maximum of 85 metres, a width of maximum 9.5 metres, a draught of 2.5 to 2.8 metres and a total tonnage of 1250 to 1450 tonnes.

Grosses Rheinschiff': A river of international importance that can used by boats that are a maximum of 95 to 110 metres in length, 11.4 metres in width and a draught of max 2.4 to 2.8 metres. The tonnage should be at most between 1500 and 3000 tonnes. It is usable for pushboats with one push-lighter with a total length of a maximum of 95 to 110 metres, a width of maximum 11.4 metres, a draught of 2.5 to 4.5 metres and a total tonnage of 1600 to 3000 tonnes.

A river of international importance that can used by boats that are a maximum 95 to 110 metres in length, 11.4 metres in width and a draught of maximum 2.4 to 2.8 metres. The tonnage should be at most between 1500 and 3000 tonnes. It is usable for pushboats with two push-lighters in a row with a total length of a maximum of 172 to 185 metres, a width of maximum 11.4 metres, a draught of 2.5 to 4.5 metres and a total tonnage of 3200 to 6000 tonnes.

A river of international importance that can used by boats that are a maximum of 95 to 110 metres in length, 11.4 metres width and a draught of maximum 2.4 to 2.8 metres. The tonnage should be at most between 1500 and 3000 tonnes. It is usable for pushboats with two push-lighters side by side with a total length of maximum 95 to 110 metres, a width of maximum 22.8 metres, a draught of 2.5 to 4.5 metres and a total tonnage of 3200 to 6000 tonnes.

A river of international importance that can used by boats that are a maximum of 140 metres in length, 15 metres width and a draught of maximum 3.9 metres. The tonnage should be at most between 1500 and 3000 tonnes. It is usable for pushboats with four push-lighters, two side by side and two in a row with a total length of a maximum of 185 to 195 metres, a width of maximim 22.8 metres, a draught of 2.5 to 4.5 metres and a total tonnage of 6400 to 12000 tonnes.

A river of international importance that can used by boats that are a maximum of 140 metres in length, 15 metres width and a draught of maximum 3.9 metres. The tonnage should be at most between 1500 and 3000 tonnes. It is usable for pushboats with six push-lighters, two side by side and three in a row or three side by side and two in a row with a total length of a maximum 270 to 280 metres, a width of maximum 22.8 metres or a total length of maximum 195 to 200 metres and a width of maximum 33.0 to 34.2 metres, a draught of 2.5 to 4.5 metres and a total tonnage of 9600 to 18000 tonnes.

A river of international importance that can used by boats that are a maximum of 140 metres in length, 15 metres width and a draught of maximum 3.9 metres. The tonnage should be at most between 1500 and 3000 tonnes. It is usable for pushboats with nine push-lighters, three side by side and three in a row with a total length of maximum 285 metres, a width of maximum 33 to 34.2 metres, a draught of 2.5 to 4.5 m and a total tonnage of 14500 to 27000 tonnes. On some waterways pushboats with more than nine push-lighters can be used. The limits for length and width should then be adjusted.

Gross Finow': A river of regional importance located east of the Elbe River that can used by boats that are a maximum of 41 metres in length, 4.7 metres in width and a draught of a maximum of 1.4 metres. The tonnage should be at most 180 tonnes.

BM - 500': A river of regional importance located east of the Elbe River that can used by boats that are a maximum of 57 metres in length, 7.5 to 9.0 metres in width and a draught of a maximum of 1.6 metres. The tonnage should be at most 500 to 630 tonnes.

A river of regional importance located east of the Elbe River that can used by boats that are a maximum of 67 to 70 metres in length, 8.2 to 9.0 metres in width and a draught of a maximum of 1.6 to 2.0 metres. The tonnage should be at most 470 to 700 tonnes.

definicion: The status of maintenance of a waterway based on the existance of a plan and schedule for its upkeep.
descripcion: For a man-made channel, the schedule for resurvey or dredging to ensure charted depths are accurate and the waterway is safe for navigation.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a waterway maintenance status.

dominio.definicion: No plan (and thus no schedule) exists for maintenance of the waterway.
No schedule exists for regular waterway maintenance, thus published information may be out of date.
Regular waterway maintenance ensures that published information is correct and reliable.

definicion: An indication of whether the way-point is considered named or un-named.
descripcion: One distinguishing factor between a named way-point and an un-named way-point is whether or not an aircraft can use the way-point as a location reference to air traffic control.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a way-point class.

dominio.definicion: A way-point that does not have an official five character identifier.
dominio.observaciones: Unnamed way-points are required within the airspace structure for various reasons (for example: marking boundaries along a route), but are generally not reported to air traffic control during navigation.

dominio.definicion: A way-point with an official five character identifier.
dominio.observaciones: Named way-points are required within the airspace structure and are used as a primary means of navigation and reporting to air traffic control while travelling along a published navigation route.

definicion: A characteristic describing the aircraft's flight path when navigating by or over a waypoint.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a way-point type.

dominio.definicion: A waypoint which requires turn anticipation to allow tangential interception of the next segment of a route or procedure.
A waypoint at which a turn is initiated in order to join the next segment of a route or procedure.

definicion: The intended use of a way-point within the defined limits of an airspace.
descripcion: For example, a free-flight way-point or a special use airspace entry or exit point.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a way-point usage.

dominio.definicion: A way-point which exists within the airspace structure as a stand-alone point.
dominio.observaciones: The way-point is not attached to any published routeing.

dominio.definicion: A way-point which is specifically designed for use within designated Area Navigation (RNAV) airspace.
A way-point which exists within a sectioned part of high altitude airspace, specifically designed for navigation using a reference system within the aircraft.
dominio.observaciones: This is commonly termed within the aviation community as the 'free flight airspace', navigating solely by Navigation Reference System (NRS) way-points, with no published air traffic routes.

dominio.definicion: A way-point which is specifically designed for use within either the high altitude air traffic control assigned airspace or the high altitude special use airspace structures.

definicion: The type of weapons storage based on its shape, usage and/or construction

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a weapon storage type.

dominio.definicion: An underground, vertical cylindrical container for the storage and launching of intercontinental ballistic missiles
Protective case used to aid in the safe movement of missiles or components
Storage base or support for missiles or components

definicion: The category of a weapon system.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a weapon system category.

dominio.definicion: A large cannon like weapons, transportable and usually operated by more than one person.
A mixture of anti-aircraft, anti-shipping and other field artillery equipment.
A gun is a muzzle or breech-loaded projectile-firing weapon.
A device that emits light or electromagnetic radiation through a process of optical amplification based on the stimulated emission of photons.
A self propelled guided weapon system.
A self propelled non guided weapon system.

definicion: The type of a weapons range based on its intended use(s).

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a weapons range type.

dominio.definicion: Suitable for training with and testing pistols, rifles, machine guns, and other small calibre weapons.
Suitable for training with and testing the large-caliber high-velocity main gun of a battle tank, as well as other weapons found on armoured vehicles.
dominio.observaciones: The main gun is usually capable of firing kinetic energy penetrators, high explosive anti-tank rounds, and in some cases guided missiles. Such practice may include maneuver as well as discharge of weapons.

dominio.definicion: Suitable for training with and testing large-calibre field artillery weapons (for example: a howitzer or a cannon).
Suitable for training with and testing grenades.
dominio.observaciones: A grenade is a small explosive or chemical bomb detonated by a fuse and which may be thrown by hand or launched from a special device attached to a rifle or carbine.

dominio.definicion: An area allocated for breaking up of structures and/or equipment (for example: destruction of arms by international agreement) by explosive blasting.
An area allocated for bombardment during the live firing of weapons.

definicion: The type of weather conditions under which a feature is usable.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a weather restriction type.

dominio.definicion: Suitable for use regardless of the weather.
dominio.observaciones: For example, in the case of a road the following characteristics might apply: (1) With reasonable maintenance, passable throughout the year to a volume of traffic never appreciably less than its maximum capacity. (2) Normally having a waterproof surface and only slightly affected by rain, frost, thaw, or heat. (3) Never closed because of weather effects other than snow or flood blockage.

dominio.definicion: Suitable for use other than during the winter season, when it is closed.
dominio.observaciones: For example, in the case of a road regular plowing, salting, and/or sanding may not take place during the winter season.

dominio.definicion: Suitable for use under fair weather conditions only.
dominio.observaciones: For example, in the case of a road the following characteristics might apply: (1) Passable only in fair and dry weather. (2) So seriously affected by adverse conditions that the road may remain closed for long periods. (3) Improvement of such a road can only be achieved by construction or realignment.

dominio.definicion: Suitable for use in all weather conditions, however may have some reductions in usability due to weather.
dominio.observaciones: For example, in the case of a road the following characteristics might apply: (1) With reasonable maintenance, passable throughout the year but at times the volume of traffic is considerably less than maximum capacity. (2) Normally not having a waterproof surface and considerably affected by rain, frost, thaw, or heat. (3) Closed for short periods of up to one day at a time by adverse weather conditions during which heavy use of the road would probably lead to collapse.

dominio.definicion: Suitable for use under winter season conditions only.
dominio.observaciones: For example, in the case of a road it may cross a waterbody and therefore is nonoperational until a sufficiently thick layer of ice has formed.

definicion: The maximum weight that can be supported by a surface.

datatype.definicion: A real domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number. For example, 98.6 (as in the normal human body temperature in degrees Fahrenheit).
datatype.nota: The realization of this real datatype is implementation-dependent.

cantidadFisica.definicion: The quantity of the property of a body that causes it to have weight in a gravitational field.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: The base unit in SI for the physical quantity "mass", defined as equal to the mass of the international prototype of the kilogram.

definicion: The cause of a weight bearing restriction on a land transporation route.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a weight restriction reason.

dominio.definicion: The existence of a bridge below the route.
The existence of a tunnel below the route.
The existence of a bad road surface.
The existence of a culvert below the route.

definicion: The type(s) of equipment attached to or adjacent to a wellbore.
descripcion: A wellbore is the openhole or uncased portion of a well.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a well equipment.

dominio.definicion: The assembly of fittings, valves, and controls located at the surface and connected to the flow lines, tubing, and casing of the well so as to control the flow from the reservoir.
dominio.observaciones: It also serves as a facility for installing casing hangers as well as christmas trees and other production control devices.

dominio.definicion: An assembly of valves, spools, pressure gauges and chokes fitted to the wellhead of a completed well to control production.
dominio.observaciones: The christmas tree also incorporates facilities to enable safe access for well intervention operations such as slickline, electric wireline or coiled tubing. Its function is to both prevent the release of petroleum or gas from a well into the environment and also to direct and control the flow of formation fluids from the well. When the well is ready to produce petroleum or natural gas, valves are opened and the release of the formation fluids is allowed through a pipeline leading (eventually) to a refinery.

dominio.definicion: An arrangement of piping or valves designed to control, distribute and often monitor fluid flow.
dominio.observaciones: For smaller subsea fields, for example, the wellhead and christmas tree are installed directly on the seabed, with production from several wells co-mingled at a subsea manifold. Subsea manifolds are often linked by pipelines and umbilical control lines back to a nearby platform, where engineers can control and monitor the petroleum and natural gas production.

dominio.definicion: A subsea structure covering the equipment (for example: a wellhead or a manifold) in order to protect against trawl gear damage.
dominio.observaciones: The structure may be designed to allow trawl gear to pass over it without snagging or stopping the vessel (termed 'overtrawl'), or to either deflect or to deliberately snag fishing gear but allow easy retrieval (termed 'fisher friendly').

dominio.definicion: A downhole pump and supporting equipment used to ensure flowing production of fluids at the desired or necessary rate.
dominio.observaciones: Pumps are required when the formation pressure is insufficient. Most petroleum wells are eventually put on pumps as pressure declines during production. The exceptions are in strong waterdrive reservoirs or in settings where pressure maintenance by gas or water injection is sufficient to maintain a high reservoir pressure.

dominio.definicion: An artificial-lift pumping system using a surface power source to drive a downhole pump assembly.
dominio.observaciones: A beam and crank assembly creates reciprocating motion in a sucker-rod string that connects to the downhole pump assembly. The pump contains a plunger and valve assembly to convert the reciprocating motion to vertical fluid movement.

dominio.definicion: A cylindrical or spherical vessel used to separate petroleum, natural gas and water from the total fluid stream produced by a well.
dominio.observaciones: Gravity segregation is the main force that accomplishes the separation, thus the heaviest fluid settles to the bottom and the lightest fluid rises to the top. The objective is to maximize the hydrocarbon liquid recovery and to provide maximum stabilization to the resultant phases (liquid and gas) leaving the final separator.

dominio.definicion: A tank in which the petroleum is stored after treatment (for example: to remove water).
A vessel used to treat oil-water emulsions so that the oil can be accepted by the pipeline or transport.
dominio.observaciones: Treater mechanisms break down the emulsion using either heat, gravity segregation, chemical additives and/or electric current.

dominio.definicion: A well lacking wellbore-attached equipment (for example: a wellhead, a christmas tree and a pipeline connection) and therefore no longer in production.
dominio.observaciones: The well may remain capable of production and be temporarily capped, or it may be permanently abandoned and sealed (for example: by pumping a grout mixture into the wellbore).

definicion: The type of a well, generally based on method of construction.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a well type.

dominio.definicion: A well whose wall is faced, generally with masonry, to prevent collapse.
dominio.observaciones: Usually circular with a stone border and a structure built above it for lowering and raising a bucket.

dominio.definicion: Created by a perpendicular boring into a confined aquifer, the water rising spontaneously above the water-table (strictly, to the surface).
Created by either digging or drilling.
Created through a (generally manual) process of digging to tap shallow groundwater.
dominio.observaciones: The resulting bore is wide, typically several feet or more in diameter.

dominio.definicion: Created by specialized equipment using methods specific to the nature of the strata penetrated (for example: drilled, driven, bored, and/or jetted).
dominio.observaciones: Generally employed to tap deep groundwater reservoirs. The resulting bore is narrow, typically only a few inches in diameter.

definicion: The type(s) of material that are pumped down a wellbore.
descripcion: Steam, carbon dioxide, water, and other substances can be injected into an oil-producing stratum in order to maintain reservoir pressure, heat the oil or lower its viscosity, thus allowing it to flow to a producing well nearby. Waste water may be injected into the ground between impermeable layers of rocks to avoid polluting fresh water supplies, or carbon dioxide similarly sequestered.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain category denoting a wellbore injection material.

dominio.definicion: Air-based compressed gas mixtures (often enhanced with oxygen or ozone) used to support fireflooding (an in-situ combustion method for producing heavy oil).
dominio.observaciones: Note that air is not suitable for reservoir pressure because it tends to cause deterioration of the oil, thus carbon dioxide or natural gas is normally used for pressure restoration.

dominio.definicion: Compressed gaseous, or liquefied, carbon dioxide injected into underground formations.
dominio.observaciones: Underground injection of carbon dioxide for purposes such as enhanced oil recovery (EOR) and enhanced gas recovery (EGR) is a long-standing practice. Carbon dioxide injection for geologic sequestration involves different technical issues and potentially much larger volumes of carbon dioxide and larger scale projects than for EOR and EGR.

dominio.definicion: A special chemical solution used to improve oil recovery, remove formation damage, clean blocked perforations or formation layers, reduce or inhibit corrosion, upgrade crude oil, or address crude oil flow-assurance issues.
dominio.observaciones: Chemical injections can be administered either continuously or in batches, typically in injection wells, although at times in production wells.

dominio.definicion: A fluid consisting of water, fine particles derived from the coal, and chemicals used in coal washing, that is produced when coal is prepared for market.
dominio.observaciones: Coal washing reduces the amount of non-combustible materials (including sulphur) from the coal. In addition to containing chemicals used during washing, coal slurry contains heavy metals naturally present in coal, such as arsenic, mercury, chromium, cadmium, boron, selenium and nickel.

dominio.definicion: A surfactant-type chemical solution used to improve oil recovery, clean blocked perforations or formation layers, or address crude oil flow-assurance issues.

A method of thermal recovery in which a flame front is generated in the reservoir by igniting a fire at the sandface of an injection well followed by continuous injection of air or other gas mixture with high oxygen content to maintain the flame front.
dominio.observaciones: As the fire burns, it moves through the reservoir toward production wells. Heat from the fire reduces oil viscosity and helps vaporize reservoir water to steam. The steam, hot water, combustion gas and a bank of distilled solvent all act to drive oil in front of the fire toward production wells.

dominio.definicion: A mixture of light hydrocarbons that are gases at atmospheric temperature and pressure, but held in the liquid state by pressure to facilitate storage, transport and handling.
dominio.observaciones: Commercial liquefied gas consists essentially of either propane or butane, or mixtures thereof. It is often stored in metal cylinders (bottled gas) and used as fuel for tractors, trucks, and buses, and as a domestic cooking or heating fuel in rural areas.

dominio.definicion: Any of a number of liquids that may be used to enhance oil recovery (for example: chemicals, detergents, liquefied carbon dioxide, sea water) or stored for later retrieval (for example: light crude, liquefied petroleum gas, water).
Natural gas injected into an underground formation, typically one already containing both natural gas and crude oil, to maintain or restore reservoir pressure.
dominio.observaciones: Other reasons for gas injection are gas-lift operations, cycling in gas-condensate reservoirs or for storing gas in an underground reservoir.

dominio.definicion: A complex mixture of naturally occurring hydrocarbon compounds found in rock.
dominio.observaciones: Petroleum can range from solid to gas, but the term is generally used to refer to liquid crude oil. Impurities such as sulphur, oxygen and nitrogen are common in petroleum. There is considerable variation in color, gravity, odor, sulphur content and viscosity in petroleum from different areas.

dominio.definicion: The injection of generally small volumes of various treating fluids into a underground formation under pressure.
The injection of superheated steam in order to extract viscous crude oil; an enhanced oil recovery (EOR) method that is the main type of thermal stimulation of oil reservoirs.
dominio.observaciones: Steam may be either cyclically injected, followed by a 'soak' and then recovery from a single well, or injected into a well separate from the production well.

dominio.definicion: The injection of superheated fluids in order to extract viscous crude oil.
dominio.observaciones: For example: steam.

dominio.definicion: Water injected into an underground formation to pressurize and displace hydrocarbons towards producing wells.
dominio.observaciones: Water-injection wells are common offshore, where filtered and treated seawater is injected into a lower water-bearing section of the reservoir. Injection water is also used in water-storage operations in offshore and remote locations with economic and environmental constraints.

definicion: The operational status of a wellbore.
descripcion: For example: active, shut-in, or plugged.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain category denoting a wellbore status.

dominio.definicion: The well has ceased production (for example: because there is insufficient hydrocarbon potential to complete the well, or production operations have drained the reservoir) or the borehole ceased serving its intended function (for example: injection operations are no longer necessary) and all recoverable equipment has been salvaged.
The well is in operation for its intended purpose (for example: natural gas recovery or waste disposal) or the borehole is serving its intended function.
The wellhead is not immediately accessible from the surface, being covered by a significant amount of overburden.
The wellbore is being drilled.
The wellbore has not encountered hydrocarbons in economically producible quantities.
dominio.observaciones: Most wells contain salt water in some zones. In addition, the wellbore usually encounters small amounts of crude oil and natural gas. Whether the well is a 'duster' depends on many factors of the economic equation, including proximity to transport and processing infrastructures, local market conditions, expected completion costs, tax and investment recovery conditions of the jurisdiction and projected oil and gas prices during the productive life of the well.

dominio.definicion: The mineral rights lease governing the operation of the well has expired.
The well or borehole is planned but drilling has not yet commenced.
The well has permanently ceased production or the borehole ceased serving its intended function and has been plugged.
dominio.observaciones: Different regulatory bodies have differing requirements for plugging operations, typically requiring that cement plugs be placed and tested across any open hydrocarbon-bearing formations, across all casing shoes, across freshwater aquifers, and perhaps several other areas near the surface, including the top 6 to 15 metres (20 to 50 feet) of the wellbore.

dominio.definicion: Unproductive drilling operations continued to a greater depth than that at which a potentially productive formation was found, and the well was subsequently completed in the shallower formation with the length of the well bore from the deepest depth at which the well is completed to the maximum depth drilled plugged to ensure against cross-strata fluid migration.
The well or borehole has been closed off, the well being shut so that it does not produce a fluid product of any kind, or the borehole is no longer serving its intended function.
The well has been capped off temporarily.

The well has temporarily ceased production or the borehole ceased serving its intended function, some or all recoverable equipment has been salvaged, but the site has been left in a state to readily enable the future resumption of operations.
The well has not entered full production, being used only for the extraction of limited quantities.
The well has not yet been 'completed' by the addition of downhole pipe and equipment required to enable safe and efficient production.

definicion: The type of a wetland on its hydrologic character, morphology and/or dominant vegetation.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a wetland type.

dominio.definicion: A soft, poorly drained wetland that is characterized by the growth of only non-woody plants (for example: grasses) and often forms a transition region between a waterbody and land.
dominio.observaciones: It is subject to frequent or tidal inundations, but not considered to be continually under water. It lacks trees.

dominio.definicion: A marsh occurring in a uniformly shallow marsh depression or swale, having a gradual gradient from the edge to the deepest portion.
dominio.observaciones: Water levels fluctuate rapidly and the marsh edge may be poorly defined.

dominio.definicion: A marsh occupying the contact zone between high and low water marks bordering semipermanent or permanent lakes.
dominio.observaciones: The marsh, usually found along protected shorelines, behind barrier beaches in lagoons, on islands, or in embayments, is subject to flooding by a rise in lake levels, wind waves, or surface runoff.

dominio.definicion: A marsh occupying shorelines, bars, stream beds, or islands in continuously flowing watercourses.
dominio.observaciones: The marsh is subject to prolonged annual flooding and is commonly covered by thick layers of sediments.

dominio.definicion: A seasonally flooded, poorly drained wetland with more woody plants than a marsh and better drainage than a bog.
dominio.observaciones: It is covered with water all or most of the year, and accumulating dead vegetation does not rapidly decay. It can exist on flat-lying areas created by certain geomorphic environments. The vegetation mainly consists of hydrophytic trees and/or scrubs whose roots are adapted to wet conditions, with an open to very dense canopy closure.

dominio.definicion: A swamp occurring along the banks of permanent or semipermanent streams.
dominio.observaciones: The high water table is maintained by the level of water in the stream. The swamp is seasonally inundated with subsequent sediment deposition.

dominio.definicion: A swamp developed in a topographically defined basin where water derived locally may be augmented by drainage from other parts of the watershed.
dominio.observaciones: The accumulation of well-decomposed peat is shallow (less than 0.5 metres) at the edge but may reach 2 metres at the centre.

dominio.definicion: A dense thicket of mangrove that is subject to tidal inundation and forming a muddy swamp.
An area subject to seasonal or regular overflooding by a running water.
A zone, characterized by wetland cultivaton of rice, subject to available water.
A boggy area without ground-water contact in regions rich in precipitation.
dominio.observaciones: Predominantly covered with moss.

dominio.definicion: A boggy area saturated up to the surface with fertile ground water.
dominio.observaciones: Predominantly covered with reed, rush. Developing in depressions or as a filling up-status of a lake.

dominio.definicion: A permanently wet area of land consisting of incompletely decayed organic material and mainly stagnant fresh water.
dominio.observaciones: It is generally too soft to bear the weight of any heavy body.

definicion: An indication that wide berth should be given to a marine feature by nearby vessels.
descripcion: For example, the surrounding area may constitute an underwater hazard due to submerged equipment or should not be disturbed due to ongoing scientific investigation.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The dimension of a feature taken perpendicular to its primary alignment of use and generally in the horizontal plane.
descripcion: The primary alignment of a feature is its established direction of flow or use (for example: a road, a power line right-of-way, a river, rapid, and/or a bridge). A feature-specific rule may apply. In the case of a bridge, the width is the distance perpendicular to the bridge centre-line and generally in the horizontal plane. In the case of a dam, the width is the distance perpendicular to (across the) the dam crest. If no such direction of flow or use exists then (1) if the feature is irregular in shape its width is taken perpendicular to the direction of its greatest horizontal dimension (see Attribute: 'Greatest Horizontal Extent'), else (2) if the feature is regular in shape then a shape-specific rule may apply: for a rectangular feature, the length of the shorter axis; for a round feature, the diameter.

datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is a real number interval.
datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

campos.definicion: The lower-value of a real-interval, the first member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.

The upper-value of a real-interval, the second member of a pair of real numbers that represent all of the numbers between the two and possibly including one and/or the other depending on the interval closure.
The closure conditions of the two endpoints of the real number interval.

definicion: The type visual indicator located at the aerodrome showing the wind direction.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a wind direction indicator type.

dominio.definicion: A conical textile tube designed to indicate wind direction and relative wind speed.
A device designed like an arrow whose small end points into the wind.
A weather vane shaped like the letter 'T' or like an aeroplane, located on an aerodrome or landing area to show the wind direction to flying aircraft.

definicion: An indication that a feature, for example a wind turbine, has no wings attached.
descripcion: This may occure because of maintenance purposes or because of the type of construction.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The fraction of canopy cover within a defined area during the winter season.
descripcion: The canopy is formed by the upper branches of the trees in a forest forming a more or less continuous layer.

datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

unidadRecomendada.definicion: A scaled dimensionless measure denoting one part in every hundred.

definicion: The type of a wireless telecommunication service based on the mechanism(s) of transmission and/or the nature of the communication(s) supported.
descripcion: For example, radio broadcast or mobile phone service.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a wireless telecommunication type.

dominio.definicion: A radio apparatus functioning similar to a telephone but operating by means of radio waves transmitted between the instruments in full duplex mode over a cellular network of base stations.

A system for transmitting digital and analog signals (for example: long-distance telephone calls and the relay of television programs) between two locations on a line of sight radio path using directional antennas to form a fixed radio connection.
dominio.observaciones: Long daisy-chained series of such links may be used to form transcontinental telephone and/or television communication systems.

dominio.definicion: A radio apparatus functioning similar to a telephone but operating by means of radio waves transmitted between the instruments in full duplex mode.
dominio.observaciones: The radiotelephone equivalent of land dial phone service, operating through a system of relatively widely separated base stations or satellites. Mobile phone systems were the predecessors of modern cellular phone technology. When first introduced, mobile phone systems suffered from few useable channels, heavy congestion, and very high operating costs.

dominio.definicion: A broadcast system for transmitting radio-frequency electromagnetic waves as a means of communication.
dominio.observaciones: Most often used for broadcasting a variety of entertainment (for example: music and news) shows interspersed with commercial messages.

dominio.definicion: A radio apparatus functioning similar to a telephone but operating by means of radio waves transmitted between the instruments and usually only in simplex (either single or dual-frequency) mode.
dominio.observaciones: For example, a 'walkie-talkie'. The user presses a special switch on the transmitter when they wish to speak. A special code-word such as the phrase 'over' may be used to signal that the speaker has finished transmitting. Radio telephones have been largely superseded by digital mobile phones however they are still widely used in specialized applications, for example police communications, emergency services, taxi services, and private mobile radio networks (PMR).

dominio.definicion: A radio apparatus functioning similar to a telegraph but operating by means of radio waves transmitted between the instruments.
dominio.observaciones: Messages are sent using a code such as the 'dot-dash' Morse code.

dominio.definicion: A system for reproducing on a screen visual images transmitted (usually with sound) by radio signals.

definicion: The fraction of land within a defined area that is covered by woody vegetation, excluding undergrowth.

datatype.nota: The realization of this complex datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: An identifier that is used to determine the World Aeronautical Chart (WAC) number of the region in which a given geographic point is included.

datatype.nombre: World Aeronautical Chart Identifier Structured Text
datatype.definicion: A structured text value specifying a World Aeronautical Chart (WAC) identifier.
datatype.nota: The realization of this structuredText datatype is implementation-dependent.
datatype.estructura: A four-character alphanumeric code consisting of either a 4-digit numeric value in the range 0000 through 1851, or one of the two-character values: '1A','1B', '1C', '1D', '1E', or '1F'.

definicion: An indication that a port is in the World Port Index.

datatype.definicion: A Boolean domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is { TRUE, FALSE }, representing the true and false values in a two-valued logic system.
datatype.nota: The realization of this boolean datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The unique identifier element in the NGA World Port Index (Publication 150).
descripcion: The World Port Index lists all of the major shipping ports in the world, giving all the information (for example: latitude and longitude, facilities information, tidal data, and customs information) that a ship captain might need to prepare for a visit.

datatype.definicion: A key domain value that contains only non-lexical characters and is 5 characters in maximum length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this key datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The registered name of a wrecked or sunken vessel.

datatype.definicion: A text domain value that may contain lexical characters and is unconstrained in length.
datatype.nota: The realization of this text datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: A unique number identifying a source-receiver combination during the collection of transmission loss data, as determined by the Acoustic Station Inventory System (ASIS).
descripcion: Reference STANAG 3715.

datatype.definicion: An index domain value.
datatype.descripcion: The domain of values is an integer that is used for identification. For example, 44762 (as in the number assigned to a prison inmate).
datatype.nota: The realization of this index datatype is implementation-dependent.

definicion: The portion of a wreck or hulk that is persistently showing above the water surface.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a wreck or hulk exposure.

dominio.definicion: Any portion of the hull is showing.
Only the masts are showing.
Only the funnels are showing.
Any portion of the superstructure is showing.
A portion of the masts and funnel are showing.

definicion: The status of a maritime wreck based on configuration and hazardousness to navigation.

datatype.definicion: A coded domain value denoting a wreck status.

dominio.definicion: A submerged wreck that is not considered dangerous to surface navigation.
dominio.observaciones: Non-dangerous wrecks generally have more than 30 metres (16.4 fathoms) clearance. The IHO Chart Specifications, however, specifically use 20 metres (10.94 fathoms) to determine the non-dangerousness of a wreck (reference: MP-004 422.5 and 422.6).

dominio.definicion: A wreck submerged at such a depth as to be considered dangerous to surface navigation.
dominio.observaciones: Dangerous wrecks generally have less than 30 metres (16.4 fathoms) clearance. The IHO Chart Specifications, however, specifically use 20 metres (10.94 fathoms) to determine the dangerousness of a wreck (reference: MP-004 422.5 and 422.6).

dominio.definicion: Wreck remains are distributed on the bottom, resulting in a foul ground that is safe for surface navigation but should be avoided for anchoring, taking the ground or ground fishing.
A wreck for which only the mast(s) is visible at the sounding datum indicated.
A wreck for which any portion of the hull or superstructure is visible at the sounding datum indicated.
